families.name: ETS class I (ETS1/ERG/FLI1)
families.def: GGA(A/T) core, ACCGGAAGT. ETS1/2, ERG, FLI1, FEV, ETV1/4/5, ETV6/7, ERF, ETV3, ELK1/3/4, GABPA, SPDEF.
families.short: ETS proteins are a family of 28 human transcription factors that each bind DNA through a single ~85-residue winged helix-turn-helix domain and read a nine-base site whose informative part is the four-base core GGA(A/T). The class I members - ETS1 and ETS2, ERG, FLI1, FEV, the PEA3 proteins ETV1/4/5, the ternary complex factors ELK1/3/4, the repressors ERF and ETV3, and GABPA - select essentially the same sequence, ACCGGAAGT, so a match names the class rather than a protein. These sites sit just upstream of a large fraction of human promoters and, in enhancers, next to RUNX, GATA, PAX and SRF sites. Class I also contains every ETS gene recurrently rearranged in cancer: ERG in prostate cancer, FLI1 and ERG in Ewing sarcoma, ETV1 and ETV4 in both.
families.long:
## The factors

The human genome contains 28 ETS genes. All encode one copy of the ETS domain: about 85 residues
folded as a winged helix-turn-helix, three alpha-helices packed on a four-stranded antiparallel
beta-sheet, that binds DNA as a monomer. Profiling the DNA-binding preference of every human and
mouse ETS protein split the family into four classes, and class I is by far the largest: the ETS
subfamily (ETS1, ETS2), the ERG subfamily (ERG, FLI1, FEV), the PEA3 proteins (ETV1, ETV4,
ETV5), the ternary complex factors (ELK1, ELK3, ELK4), the repressors ERF and ETV3, and GABPA.
GABPA is the structural exception: it functions only in complex with the ankyrin-repeat subunit
GABPB, which it recruits using the ETS domain plus a carboxy-terminal extension. Several class I
proteins carry autoinhibitory segments flanking the ETS domain that are relieved by partner
binding. Expression ranges from near-ubiquitous (GABPA, ELK1, ERF, ETV3) through
lymphoid-enriched (ETS1), endothelial and hematopoietic (ERG, FLI1), to narrowly restricted
(FEV). SPDEF is grouped here in this atlas, but biochemically it is the sole class IV factor and
prefers a GGAT core.

## The motif

The site is nine base pairs, ACCGGAAGT, and nearly all of its information is in the GGA(A/T)
core. Two invariant arginines in recognition helix H3 hydrogen-bond the two core guanines; a
conserved tyrosine (Tyr395 in ETS1) supports the interface; a lysine in the wing contacts DNA 5'
of the core and a lysine in the H2-H3 turn contacts the opposite strand 3' of it. The core is
read base by base, the flanks indirectly, through sequence-dependent backbone geometry. The
flanks separate subfamilies, and separate them weakly: class I prefers A three bases 5' of the core and disfavors C there, the ELF/EHF group
prefers C at that position (CCCGGAAGT), SPI1/SPIB/SPIC use a purine-rich 5' flank (AGAGGAAGTG),
and SPDEF alone prefers GGAT. Quantitatively, different ETS proteins vary only about ten-fold in
affinity for the same consensus, whereas one protein's affinity across variant sites spans five-
to eighty-fold; sequence therefore grades site quality much better than it identifies a
paralogue, and no class I member is separable from another by motif alone. The CCGG contains a
CpG, and methylating it blocks binding. Tandem arrangements are a distinct case: GGAA
microsatellites of four or more consecutive repeats are the response elements of the EWS-FLI1
fusion, and some models grouped here (JASPAR MA0149.1, archetype AC0561) are GGAA repeats rather
than single sites.

## Where it acts

ETS occupancy follows two logics. At promoters it is largely redundant: a strong CCGGAAGT sits
20-40 bp upstream of the transcription start site in CpG-island housekeeping promoters - roughly
a quarter of human promoters carry an ETS site near the start site - and different ETS proteins
bind interchangeably, with most GABPA-occupied promoters in Jurkat cells also occupied by ETS1.
These sites lie in hypomethylated CpG islands, so the CpG in the core stays unmethylated. At
distal, DNase-sensitive enhancers, occupancy is factor-specific, the sequence departs from
consensus, and specificity comes from composite elements: ETS1 with RUNX1 at AGGA(A/T)GTGG, which
binds more than 30-fold cooperatively and marks over a thousand ETS1-specific regions in T cells;
ETS with GATA in hemogenic endothelium, where FLI1, GATA2 and SCL cross-regulate through
neighboring sites; ETS1 with PAX5 at the mb-1 promoter, where Gln22 of the PAX5 paired domain
hydrogen-bonds Tyr395 of ETS1; the ternary complex factors with SRF at serum response elements;
and ERG with the androgen receptor in prostate cancer, where the two share about 44% of sites.
The ETS-IRF composite element (EICE) belongs to the SPI1 subfamily and is described there.

## Biology and disease

Class I factors run housekeeping transcription, growth-factor responses and lineage programs.
Gabpa-null mouse embryos die before implantation, consistent with GABPA's occupancy of
housekeeping promoters. Ets1 loss impairs T-cell and natural killer cell development. ERG and
FLI1 are required for endothelial and hematopoietic specification. The clinical weight of the
class is oncogenic rearrangement: TMPRSS2-ERG and related fusions place ERG, ETV1, ETV4 or ETV5
under androgen control in roughly half of prostate cancers, and EWSR1-FLI1 or EWSR1-ERG defines
Ewing sarcoma, where the fusion's prion-like EWSR1 domain converts GGAA microsatellites into de
novo enhancers.

## Reading a hit

Treat a single match as weak evidence. The four-base GGAA core is expected about 12 million times
per strand in a 3.1-Gb genome and the full nine-mer ACCGGAAGT on the order of 10,000 times per
strand by base-composition arithmetic; CCGG-containing words are rarer than that because the
genome is CpG-depleted, but the site is still common enough that isolated hits mean little
without context: conservation, accessibility, a nearby partner site, or a promoter position close
to the start site. A hit identifies an ETS site, not an ETS protein: ETS1, ERG, FLI1, ELK1
and GABPA are not distinguishable from sequence. ChIP-derived models carry partner signal:
HOCOMOCO's ChIP-based ETS1 model (ETS1.H14CORE.1.P.B) has consensus ACAGGAAGTGG, whose trailing
GTGG is the RUNX1 half-site of the ETS1-RUNX1 composite, and several other ChIP-derived ETS
models converge on CAGGAAG rather than the in vitro CCGGAAGT. Half of the JASPAR entries grouped
here (16 of 32) are CAP-SELEX heterodimer models such as ERF::SREBF2 or ETV5::FIGLA, where much
of the matrix is the partner's site, not an ETS site. Finally, consensus strings are stored on
either strand: GABPA's JASPAR model reads CACTTCCTGT, the reverse complement of ACAGGAAGTG.
families.caveats:
A hit tells you the family, not the member: all class I ETS proteins select the
same nine-mer in vitro and differ only in weak flanking preferences, so a "FLI1 site" and an
"ERG site" are the same sequence. The core is short and frequent, so a match outside an
accessible, conserved or composite context is expected by chance. Sixteen of the 32 JASPAR models
here are CAP-SELEX heterodimers whose matrices are partly a bHLH, FOX, HOX or SREBF site; four
models here are GGAA repeats rather than single sites and will hit any GGAA microsatellite; and the
ChIP-derived HOCOMOCO models (evidence letter P) include RUNX-extended and CAGGAAG variants that
reflect partners and indirect binding rather than intrinsic ETS specificity. SPDEF is placed in
this family here but reads GGAT and is biochemically its own class.

families.name: AP-1 (FOS/JUN)
families.def: TRE/AP-1 site TGA(C/G)TCA. FOS, FOSB, FOSL1/2, JUN, JUNB, JUND, BATF, BATF2/3, JDP2, ATF3, and FOS::JUN heterodimers.
families.short: AP-1 is the collective name for dimers of the JUN proteins (JUN, JUNB, JUND) with the FOS proteins (FOS, FOSB, FOSL1, FOSL2), together with the related basic region-leucine zipper partners ATF3, JDP2 and BATF/BATF2/BATF3. They bind the seven-base TPA response element TGA(C/G)TCA, two TGAC half-sites read one per subunit, and also the one-base-longer cyclic-AMP response element TGACGTCA. FOS and JUN were among the first proto-oncogenes described, and AP-1 activity rises within minutes of growth-factor, cytokine, ultraviolet or oxidative stimulation. The site is one of the most frequently occupied sequences in accessible chromatin, concentrated in distal enhancers, where AP-1 binding helps keep regions open for other factors. Because every member reads the same seven bases, a match names the family rather than the protein.
families.long:
## The factors

AP-1 is a dimer pool rather than a single protein. The JUN subfamily (JUN, JUNB, JUND) and the FOS subfamily (FOS, FOSB, FOSL1/FRA-1, FOSL2/FRA-2) are basic region-leucine zipper (bZIP) factors: a roughly 60-residue module in which a basic region lies along the DNA major groove and an adjacent leucine-rich heptad repeat forms a parallel two-stranded coiled coil with the partner subunit. Fos proteins barely homodimerize and need a Jun partner; Jun homodimerizes weakly and prefers Fos, a bias the c-Fos-c-Jun crystal structure traced to an asymmetric network of interhelical electrostatic contacts in the zipper. Three further groups join the same pool and read the same site: ATF3, JDP2, and the immune bZIPs BATF, BATF2 and BATF3. JUN, JUND, FOSL1, FOSL2 and ATF3 are broadly expressed; FOS and FOSB are immediate-early genes whose transcription rises within minutes of stimulation; BATF and BATF3 are largely confined to lymphoid and dendritic lineages. Measuring DNA specificity for 102 bZIP dimers showed that about 72% of heterodimer motifs are simply the partners' half-sites joined, which is why this pool behaves as one motif.

## The motif

The classical site is the 7 bp TPA response element (TRE), TGA(C/G)TCA, written TGASTCA. It is two TGAC half-sites in opposed orientations sharing a central base, one read by each subunit. TGACTCA and TGAGTCA are exact reverse complements, so these are not two variants but one site seen from either strand. The 8 bp cyclic-AMP response element (CRE), TGACGTCA, is the same half-site pair with one extra base between them, and Jun-, ATF3-, JDP2- and BATF-containing dimers bind it as well. Information sits almost entirely on TGA and TCA; the central base and the flanks are weakly constrained, although an A or T immediately outside each half-site is common, giving the ATGACTCAT of many models. In the crystal structure the coiled coil is flexibly joined to the basic regions and the heterodimer does not occupy the asymmetric TGAGTCA in a unique orientation, which is the structural reason no base distinguishes the Fos half from the Jun half. The 77 models gathered here bear this out: the JASPAR dimer matrices FOS::JUN, FOSL2::JUNB, FOSL2::JUND and BATF::JUN each have a same-family neighbour at 0.99 similarity or better. The consensus derived from these models is ATGACTCA, but the highest-information members - BATF3, BATF2, FOS, JUNB, JDP2 and ATF3 - are the 8 bp ATGACGTCAT. That split follows evidence type rather than biology: in vitro selection recovers the CRE as the higher-affinity site for these dimers, whereas ChIP-derived models recover the 7 bp TRE, which is what cells actually occupy. BATF models carry a second element, a TTTC placed two or three bases from the TRE: the AP-1-IRF composite element (AICE) through which BATF dimers recruit IRF4 or IRF8.

## Where it acts

AP-1 sites are enriched at distal enhancers rather than in CpG-island promoters, and AP-1-like footprints are among the most frequently recovered classes in genome-wide DNase I footprint maps. The site is genuinely common: a 7-mer of this composition is expected roughly 4 x 10^5 times in 3.1 Gb of human sequence, so most matches are not functional. AP-1 occupancy is better described as collaborative than instructive: AP-1 binding raises local accessibility and licenses glucocorticoid receptor binding at shared elements, and AP-1 motifs are among the sequences that lineage-determining factors use to prime enhancers in macrophages and B cells. Named composites include the AICE with IRF4 and IRF8, the NFAT-AP-1 composite of the IL2 and CSF2 enhancers, and glucocorticoid receptor tethering sites.

## Biology and disease

AP-1 converts short-lived signals - growth factors, cytokines, ultraviolet light, oxidative stress - into transcription, and its targets span proliferation, differentiation, apoptosis, wound repair and bone remodeling. Mice lacking c-fos are osteopetrotic because osteoclasts fail to form, and have hematopoietic defects; c-jun-null embryos die in mid-gestation with hepatic failure. Batf3-null mice lack CD8-alpha-positive (cDC1) dendritic cells and prime cytotoxic T cells poorly. In cancer AP-1 acts in both directions depending on tissue and member: JUN is amplified in dedifferentiated liposarcoma, FOS and FOSB are recurrently rearranged in epithelioid hemangioma, and FOSL1 is elevated in many epithelial tumors, while JUNB and JUND can be growth-suppressive.

## Reading a hit

A TGASTCA match identifies the family, not the member: nothing in the sequence separates FOS from FOSB or FOSL1/2, or JUN from JUNB or JUND, and the ATF3, JDP2 and BATF models are equally close. At seven informative bases a single occurrence in a promoter is not evidence of regulation; ask instead whether it falls in accessible chromatin in your cell type. The site is also hard to separate from its siblings. If your match is TGACGTCA, the CREB/ATF family is at least as likely, and ATF6/CREB3 if the 3-prime flank is GTGG. If GC extensions flank the core, as in TGCTGACTCAGCA, read MAF; if only the 3-prime side is GC, as in TGACTCAGC, read NFE2/BACH. ChIP-derived AP-1 models are also prone to indirect recovery: a JUN-like motif is one of a handful repeatedly enriched in ChIP-seq datasets for unrelated factors, accounting for up to 45% of peaks in some sets. One CIS-BP entry labelled ATF3 in this family (M07822) is a CACGTG E-box whose nearest neighbours are USF motifs; treat it as out of place here.
families.caveats: An AP-1 match is one of the safest family calls in this atlas and one of the least informative member calls. All 13 proteins share the motif, so a hit licenses "an AP-1-family dimer could bind here" and nothing more; it does not say which subunits, whether the site is occupied, or whether occupancy activates or represses. The 7 bp core occurs a few hundred thousand times in the genome, so require accessibility, conservation or allelic evidence before calling a site functional. Half of the models here come from ChIP-seq, and AP-1 motifs are a well-documented contaminant of ChIP-seq peaks for unrelated factors, so an AP-1 motif under someone else's peak is not evidence that the two proteins interact.

families.name: Anterior HOX (HOX1-8)
families.def: TAAT core with PBX/MEIS cooperativity; paralogue groups 1-8: HOXA1-A7, HOXB1-B8, HOXC4-C8, HOXD1-D8.
families.short: The 39 human HOX genes sit in four clusters and specify position along the head-to-tail axis. This family covers paralogue groups 1 to 8 - the anterior and central HOX proteins - with 75 motifs for 27 gene symbols. Their homeodomains read the generic TAAT core, written TAATTA for groups 1-3 and shifting to TAATGA or TAATGG for groups 4-8. On their own these proteins are essentially interchangeable in vitro: no matrix separates HOXA5 from HOXB5 or HOXC6. Real sequence discrimination appears only in complex with the TALE cofactors PBX and MEIS, which build a bipartite site, ATGATTNATNN, whose HOX half-site shifts stepwise along the cluster.
families.long:
## The factors

HOXA1-A7, HOXB1-B8, HOXC4-C8 and HOXD1-D8 make up this family, together with unassigned HOXA/HOXB/HOXC/HOXD archetypes: 27 symbols, 75 motifs. Each protein is a single homeodomain with short flanking regions, expressed in a spatially restricted, colinear pattern - genes at the 3' end of a cluster are expressed earliest and most anteriorly - and controlled in part by retinoic acid. Immediately N-terminal to the homeodomain most of them carry a hexapeptide motif (IYPWMK and variants) that docks into a pocket of the TALE-class cofactor PBX1-4 (extradenticle in Drosophila); MEIS1-3 and PKNOX1/2 form the second TALE arm. Anterior HOX proteins bind cooperatively with PBX in a hexapeptide-dependent manner, shown for HOXB4, HOXB6 and HOXB7 but not for HOXA10, and grafting the HOXB7 hexapeptide onto HOXA10 confers cooperativity.

## The motif

The invariant feature is the four-base core 5'-TAAT-3'. When the DNA preferences of four Drosophila HOM proteins were compared directly, Ultrabithorax, Antennapedia and Deformed all preferred TAAT while Abdominal-B preferred TTAT, and Ubx and Antp were indistinguishable outside the core; the residues responsible lie in the homeodomain N-terminal arm, not at position 50 (all HOX proteins have glutamine there).

Within this family the bases 3' of the core drift with cluster position. JASPAR and HOCOMOCO in vitro models give CTAATTAC for groups 1-3 (HOXA1, HOXA2, HOXB1, HOXB2, HOXD1, HOXD3), TTAATGA for groups 4-5 (HOXA4, HOXB4, HOXC4, HOXD4, HOXA5) and TAATGG/TAATTG for groups 6-8 (HOXA6, HOXA7, HOXB8, HOXD8). The family medoid is HOXA6 (HOCOMOCO HXA6.H14CORE.0.SM.B) and its trimmed consensus is TAATGA, which is why the data consensus for the family reads TAATGA rather than the TAATTA usually quoted for anterior HOX; both are the same 6-bp window with a different 3' base, and cohesion across the family is 0.87.

The cofactor site is where specificity actually lives. Binding-site selection with PBX-HOX heterodimers returned the bipartite sequence 5'-ATGATTNATNN-3', with PBX contacting ATGAT and HOX the more variable TNATNN half; across HOXB1 to HOXB9 and HOXA10 the HOX half-site core shifts stepwise from TTAT to TGAT in an order that matches gene position in the cluster. Crystal structures explain both halves: the HoxB1-Pbx1-DNA complex at 2.35 A shows the hexapeptide bound in a pocket created by the three-residue TALE insertion, and the HoxA9-Pbx1 structure shows that N-terminal arm residues determine sequence preference indirectly, without contacting bases. SELEX-seq on all eight Drosophila Hox proteins with Exd showed the same principle quantitatively: latent specificity differences emerge only in the complex, group into three classes that follow colinearity, and correspond to differences in minor-groove shape, the same readout mechanism worked out structurally for Sex combs reduced.

## Where it acts

Anterior HOX sites are in embryonic distal enhancers, not CpG-island promoters, and in vivo occupancy tracks accessible, PBX/MEIS-marked regions. Counting matters: TAATTA is expected on the order of two million times in 3.1 Gb, while the ATGATTNAT composite is expected a few hundred thousand times - still common, but two orders of magnitude more specific. Two ChIP-derived models in this family make the point directly: HOXB4 and HOXB7 ChIP-seq models read TGATTGATG, the PBX-HOX composite, while HT-SELEX models for the same two proteins read TTAATGA. Archetype analysis of DNase footprints likewise puts a HOXB/PBX composite (TTGATTAAT) in this family.

## Biology and disease

Anterior HOX genes set segmental identity in the hindbrain, branchial arches and axial skeleton. Hoxa2 loss in mouse produces a homeotic transformation of the second branchial arch toward first-arch identity. In humans, homozygous HOXA1 loss of function causes brainstem malformation with inner-ear, cardiovascular and cognitive involvement, and a HOXB1 founder mutation causes hereditary congenital facial palsy, reproducing the Hoxb1 null mouse phenotype. Anterior HOX genes are also downstream of retinoic acid signaling in the hindbrain, and PBX1 itself is oncogenic as the E2A-PBX1 fusion in acute lymphoblastic leukemia.

## Reading a hit

A bare TAAT or TAATTA hit is close to meaningless. It does not identify a HOX protein, does not distinguish anterior HOX from the large Q50 homeodomain family that reads the same core, and occurs so often that genome-wide scans return millions of matches. The only sequence configuration with real discriminating power is the PBX composite ATGATTNATNN, and even that identifies a class, not a paralogue. Evidence quality is good for the in vitro claim - 19 of 23 HOCOMOCO models here have HT-SELEX support - but ChIP-derived HOX motifs should be assumed to be cofactor composites or, worse, unrelated: in a direct comparison the most enriched motif in HOXA2 ChIP-seq peaks was not bound by HOXA2 in vitro at all. Three flagged members are informative rather than wrong: a HOXB2::ELK1 model is a measured heterodimer site dominated by its ETS half, two footprint archetypes labelled HOXC/HOXD and HOXC/HOXA are posterior-type (TTTTATTG), and an archetype labelled HOXB/BARHL is plain TAATTA.
families.caveats: Treat a match as "anterior/central HOX-type TAAT site" at best. The 27 gene symbols here are not separable by matrix, and the core is shared with the ~200-member Q50 homeodomain class, so a TAATTA hit does not even establish that a HOX protein is involved. Expect millions of genome-wide matches; require the PBX composite ATGATTNATNN, expression data and accessibility before treating a site as HOX-bound. ChIP-derived models for these factors are suspect: the two ChIP-only HOCOMOCO models in this family are PBX-HOX composites rather than HOX sites, and published comparisons show the top motif in HOXA2 peaks is not one HOXA2 binds in vitro. Three CIS-BP entries come from mouse orthologues.

families.name: Posterior HOX (HOX9-13, AbdB-like)
families.def: TTTTATKR / TTAT core preferred by paralogue groups 9-13: HOXA9-A13, HOXB9, HOXB13, HOXC9-C13, HOXD9-D13.
families.short: HOX paralogue groups 9 to 13 - the Abdominal-B-like or posterior HOX proteins - read a different core from the rest of the homeodomain superfamily. Where most homeodomains require TAAT, these prefer TTAT, and their in vitro sites extend to TTTTACGAC (equivalently GTCGTAAAA on the opposite strand). This family collects 63 motifs for the 16 posterior HOX genes: HOXA9-A13, HOXB9, HOXB13, HOXC9-C13 and HOXD9-D13. The longer, AT-rich site makes these motifs considerably rarer and more informative than a bare TAAT hit, but the 16 paralogues remain indistinguishable from each other. Groups 9-10 partner with PBX, groups 11-13 with MEIS instead.
families.long:
## The factors

Sixteen genes, 63 motifs: HOXA9, HOXA10, HOXA11, HOXA13, HOXB9, HOXB13, HOXC9-C13 and HOXD9-D13. These are the 5' genes of each HOX cluster, expressed latest and most posteriorly under colinearity, and they pattern the posterior trunk, the limb autopod and the urogenital tract; HOXA9 and HOXA10 are also central to hematopoietic progenitor regulation.

Cofactor usage splits the group. Paralogues 9 and 10 still form cooperative complexes with the TALE protein PBX1, although HOXA10 lacks a canonical hexapeptide and uses a tryptophan-containing motif instead. Paralogues 11, 12 and 13 do not bind PBX1a and instead heterodimerize with MEIS1, which was identified as a common retroviral integration site in myeloid leukemias where Hoxa9 is co-activated; the heterodimer occupies a composite target with a MEIS1 half-site (TGACAG) adjacent to an Abd-B-like HOX site (TTTTACGAC), and HOXA9 additionally forms trimeric complexes with PBX2 and MEIS1 in myeloid cells.

## The motif

The defining difference is the core. In a direct comparison of four Drosophila HOM proteins, Abdominal-B bound a site with an unusual TTAT core while Ultrabithorax, Antennapedia and Deformed all preferred TAAT; the responsible residues lie in the homeodomain N-terminal arm, and the same arm differences are conserved in the vertebrate Abd-B-like proteins. Concretely, posterior HOX homeodomains begin GRKKRVPYTK or TRKKRCPYTK where anterior ones begin GKRARTAYTR or RKRGRQTYTR. Position 50 is glutamine throughout, so this split is not a position-50 effect; the HoxA9-Pbx1 crystal structure showed directly that these arm residues set specificity without contacting bases, through DNA conformation, and that the posterior hexapeptide adopts a different conformation from the anterior one.

In vitro models across the family converge tightly. HOCOMOCO HT-SELEX and methyl-HT-SELEX models for HOXD9, HOXA10, HOXA11, HOXC9-C12 and HOXD10-D12 read TTTTACGAC, with the group-13 genes (HOXA13, HOXB13, HOXC13, HOXD13) shifting the last base to give TTTACGAG. CIS-BP and JASPAR models for several of the same genes report the variant TTTTATTGC/TTTTATTGG, and the family medoid is HOXC9 (HOCOMOCO HXC9.H14CORE.1.S.C) at TTTATGAC. A degenerate rendering of the same core is often written TTTTATKR, including in this atlas's own family definition; it describes the 5'-TTTAT-3' core with the 3' bases left ambiguous and is not a separate site. Cohesion is 0.89, the highest of the homeodomain families here, and no member is flagged as belonging elsewhere.

Paralogues are not separable. Nothing in these matrices distinguishes HOXA9 from HOXD9, and the only within-family distinction with support is group 13 versus groups 9-12. ChIP-derived models look different from the in vitro ones because they capture the cofactor composite: HOXA9, HOXC9 and HOXC10 ChIP models read TGATTTATGG, that is, the PBX half-site ATGAT followed by a posterior TTAT half-site, consistent with the finding that within the PBX composite the HOX half-site core shifts stepwise from TTAT to TGAT along the cluster.

## Where it acts

Posterior HOX sites are in distal developmental enhancers, prominently in the limb autopod regulatory landscape 5' of HOXD and in hematopoietic progenitor enhancers. Unlike TAATTA, the site is genuinely rare: at human base composition the 9-mer TTTTACGAC is expected only a few tens of thousands of times in 3.1 Gb, so a strong full-length match is worth taking seriously. Co-occurring motifs are the informative context - MEIS (TGACAG) for groups 11-13 and PBX (ATGAT) for groups 9-10 - and in leukemia HOXA9 sites overlap extensively with MEIS1 occupancy.

## Biology and disease

Human posterior HOX mutations produce distinctive limb and urogenital phenotypes. HOXD13 polyalanine expansion causes synpolydactyly; HOXA13 mutation causes hand-foot-genital syndrome; HOXA11 mutation causes amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia with radioulnar synostosis. HOXB13 carries the recurrent germline G84E variant that raises prostate cancer risk. In leukemia, the NUP98-HOXA9 fusion arising from t(7;11)(p15;p15) drives myeloid transformation, and deregulation of the HOXA9/MEIS1 axis is the shared downstream program of MLL-rearranged and NPM1-mutant acute myeloid leukemia, making it an active therapeutic target.

## Reading a hit

A full TTTTACGAC or TTTTATTG match is one of the more informative homeodomain hits available, because the site is long and rare. What it does not do is name a protein: all 16 posterior HOX genes share it, and a hit should be reported as a posterior/Abd-B-like HOX site. Two further practical points. First, matches truncated to TTTAT are no more specific than a generic AT-rich homeodomain hit and should not be counted. Second, five of the 30 HOCOMOCO models in this family are ChIP-only and four more combine ChIP with SELEX; the ChIP-derived versions are PBX-HOX composites (TGATTTATGG) rather than HOX monomer sites, so scanning with them tests for the composite element, not for the HOX protein. One JASPAR entry here, HOXD12::ELK1, is a measured heterodimer motif whose information is dominated by the ETS half-site and will match ETS-driven promoters.
families.caveats: Better than most homeodomain families, but still a class-level call. All 16 posterior HOX paralogues share one motif, so report a hit as "Abd-B-like/posterior HOX", never as HOXA9 or HOXD13. The strength of the call depends on match length: the full 9-mer TTTTACGAC is expected only tens of thousands of times genome-wide and is meaningful, whereas a TTTAT-only match is an ordinary AT-rich homeodomain hit. Five of 30 HOCOMOCO models are ChIP-only and read the PBX-HOX composite TGATTTATGG rather than the monomer site; scanning with these tests for the composite element. The HOXD12::ELK1 entry is a heterodimer motif dominated by its ETS half.

families.name: TALE homeodomain (PBX/MEIS/TGIF)
families.def: TGATTGAT and TGACAG. PBX1-4, MEIS1-3, PKNOX1/2, TGIF1/2, TGIF2LX/2LY; PBX-HOX composite sites.
families.short: TALE homeodomain factors - PBX1-4, MEIS1-3, PKNOX1/2 (PREP1/2) and TGIF1/2 with the TGIF2LX/TGIF2LY retrogenes - carry a homeodomain with three extra residues inserted between helices 1 and 2, the Three Amino acid Loop Extension that names the class. That insertion creates a pocket that docks the hexapeptide of HOX proteins, which is how these factors turn otherwise generic HOX binding into specific composite sites. Two cores dominate the family: MEIS, PKNOX and TGIF read TGACAG, usually as the palindrome TGACAGCTGTCA, while PBX proteins read TGAT and assemble PBX-HOX elements (TGATTNAT) and PBX-MEIS elements (TGATTGACAG). These composite sites are the reason HOX and TALE factors have any DNA-level specificity at all.
families.long:
## The factors

The TALE superclass takes its name from a three-residue insertion between helices 1 and 2 of the homeodomain, recognized in 1997 in the MEIS, PBC, KNOX, Iroquois and TGIF groups. The human members here are the PBC class (PBX1-4), the MEIS class (MEIS1-3 and the more distantly related PKNOX1/PKNOX2, also called PREP1 and PREP2), and the TGIF class (TGIF1, TGIF2 and the X- and Y-linked retrogenes TGIF2LX and TGIF2LY). The Iroquois branch is treated separately in this atlas as HD_IRX. Beyond the homeodomain, PBX proteins carry PBC-A and PBC-B domains, and MEIS/PKNOX proteins carry the homologous MEIS/HR domains, through which the two groups heterodimerize with each other. PBX and MEIS/PKNOX are broadly expressed; TGIF1 and TGIF2 are widely expressed transcriptional repressors that also serve as Smad corepressors, linking the family to TGF-beta and NODAL signaling.

## The motif

The extra three residues do two things. They lengthen the loop so that PBX can accommodate an additional fourth helix and, critically, they form part of a hydrophobic pocket that binds the hexapeptide (YPWM-like) motif found N-terminal to the homeodomain in most HOX proteins. A bare homeodomain reads only a 4-6 bp TAAT-type core, so HOX proteins on their own are nearly indistinguishable. Docking through the TALE pocket assembles a bipartite element: the HOXB1-PBX1 and HOXA9-PBX1 cocrystals show PBX occupying a TGAT half-site and the HOX partner an adjacent TNAT half-site, giving the composite TGATTNATNN, with the identity of the central bases set by the HOX paralogue. MEIS, PKNOX and TGIF read a different core, TGACAG, and in vitro they bind it overwhelmingly as the head-to-head palindrome TGACAGCTGTCA - the highest-information models in this family, up to 22 bits in JASPAR and CIS-BP, reported for TGIF1, TGIF2, PKNOX2, MEIS2 and MEIS3 alike. PBX-MEIS heterodimers instead give the asymmetric composite TGATTGACAG, seen in the ChIP-derived HOCOMOCO models for PBX1, PBX2, PBX3 and PKNOX1. Pooled, the family consensus is TGACAGCt with cohesion 0.74; the TGACAG and TGAT branches are readily distinguished from one another, but within each branch the paralogues are not.

## Where it acts

PBX and MEIS/PKNOX sites are found in developmental enhancers, especially in and around the HOX clusters and in hindbrain and limb enhancers, where the composite elements confer the segment specificity that bare HOX motifs cannot. Genome-wide, PKNOX1/PREP1 and MEIS1 occupy largely independent site sets: PREP1 associates with promoters and housekeeping genes, MEIS1 with promoter-remote developmental regions, and HOX-type sequences co-occur with MEIS1 but not PREP1 binding sites, while PBX1 cooperates with both. Composite element names worth searching for are the PBX-HOX or hexapeptide element and the PBX-MEIS/PREP element; TGIF palindromes additionally co-occur with SMAD sites, reflecting TGIF's role as a Smad corepressor. Because TGACAG is only 6 bp and TGAT only 4, matches to the half-sites are extremely common; the 12-bp TGACAGCTGTCA palindrome, by contrast, is expected only in the low thousands per genome.

## Biology and disease

PBX1 loss in mouse disrupts skeletal patterning and chondrocyte differentiation, and PBX1 haploinsufficiency in humans causes syndromic congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract. MEIS1 is the top locus in genome-wide association studies of restless legs syndrome. In cancer the family is best known for two mechanisms: the t(1;19) fusion E2A-PBX1 in pre-B acute lymphoblastic leukemia, and the collaboration of MEIS1 with HOXA9, where Hoxa9 transforms primary bone marrow cells specifically with Meis1a rather than Pbx1b - a pairing that underlies MLL-rearranged leukemia. Heterozygous TGIF1 mutations cause holoprosencephaly, linking NODAL signaling to human neural axis determination.

## Reading a hit

A TGACAGCTGTCA palindrome is strong evidence for a TALE factor but says nothing about which one: TGIF1, TGIF2, TGIF2LX, TGIF2LY, PKNOX1, PKNOX2, MEIS2 and MEIS3 all have essentially this model. A bare TGACAG or TGAT is too short to act on. The most useful reading is compositional: a TGATTNAT composite points to a PBX-HOX pair, and TGATTGACAG to a PBX-MEIS/PREP pair, and those are the hits worth following up. Note that several PBX and PKNOX models in HOCOMOCO are ChIP-only (P grade), so their TGATTGGC and TGATTGACAG variants may partly reflect the partner's contribution rather than PBX alone; one low-information CIS-BP entry in this family (CTAATTAa) has nearest neighbours in the K50 homeodomain group and is best ignored.
families.caveats: Within each branch the paralogues are interchangeable: the TGACAGCTGTCA palindrome is shared by TGIF1/2, TGIF2LX/2LY, PKNOX1/2 and MEIS1-3, and PBX1-4 share TGAT. Treat a hit as "TALE, MEIS/TGIF type" or "TALE, PBX type", not as a named protein. Half-site matches (TGACAG, TGAT) occur far too often to interpret. Several PBX and PKNOX models are ChIP-derived only (HOCOMOCO P grade) and their composite forms may carry a partner's half-site, which is informative but is not evidence that PBX alone binds it. One low-information CIS-BP member resolves to a K50 homeodomain site.

families.name: T-box
families.def: AGGTGTGA half-site, palindromic in TBXT. TBX1-6, TBX10, TBX15, TBX18-21, TBXT/T, TBR1, EOMES, MGA.
families.short: T-box sites are read by the seventeen human T-box proteins - TBXT (Brachyury), TBX1 to TBX6, TBX10, TBX15, TBX18 to TBX22, TBR1, EOMES and MGA - through a ~180-residue T domain that inserts a helix deep into a widened minor groove, a recognition mode found in no other family. The unit of binding is an eight-base half-site, AGGTGTGA, written TCACACCT in the other orientation. Brachyury binds a palindromic pair of half-sites as a dimer; several paralogues occupy single half-sites or tandem repeats instead. These factors specify the notochord, heart, limbs, pharyngeal apparatus and T-helper-1 lineage, and mutations in individual genes cause distinct human malformation syndromes - but the paralogues are essentially indistinguishable from sequence.
families.long:
## The factors

The human genome carries seventeen T-box genes, conventionally grouped into five subfamilies: TBXT (T/Brachyury); the TBX1 subfamily (TBX1, TBX10, TBX15, TBX18, TBX20, TBX22); the TBX2 subfamily (TBX2, TBX3, TBX4, TBX5); the TBX6 subfamily (TBX6 and MGA); and the TBR1 subfamily (TBR1, EOMES, TBX21). All share the T domain, about 180 residues of immunoglobulin-like beta-sandwich. The Brachyury T domain-DNA structure showed an unusual recognition mode: a C-terminal helix buries itself in an enlarged minor groove without bending the DNA, and specificity comes from hydrophobic packing and a main-chain carbonyl contact to a guanine as well as conventional major-groove contacts. Expression is mostly narrow and developmental - TBXT in nascent mesoderm and notochord, TBX5 and TBX20 in heart and forelimb, TBX1 in pharyngeal mesoderm, TBR1 and EOMES in cortical neurons and, for EOMES and TBX21, in lymphocytes. One member is a hybrid: MGA combines a T domain with a bHLH-zipper region that heterodimerises with MAX and binds E-boxes, so MGA reads two unrelated motifs. The family splits into activators (TBX5, TBX20, TBX21, EOMES, TBXT) and repressors (TBX2, TBX3) that use the same element.

## The motif

The core unit is the eight-base half-site AGGTGTGA, equivalently TCACACCT on the opposite strand; both orientations are standard and both appear in these databases, a frequent source of confusion when comparing consensus strings. Binding-site selection with Brachyury first defined it; the protein bound as a monomer in that assay. Geometry is where the paralogues differ, insofar as they differ at all. The Brachyury structure used a 24-bp palindrome and found a dimer whose two monomers contact each other, whereas the human TBX3 structure on a palindromic duplex found the two sites recognised independently, with no stabilising monomer-monomer interface - different quaternary arrangements within one fold. The data reflect this: the TBXT and TBX19 models here are inverted palindromes (TCACACCTAGGTGTGA), several models are everted pairs (AGGTGTGAAATTCACA), TBX20 models are direct tandem repeats (AGGTGTGAAGGTGTGA), and the majority are plain single half-sites. Beyond geometry, the paralogues are not separable. Across four databases, the primary models for TBX1, TBX2, TBX3, TBX4, TBX5, TBX6, TBX15, TBX18, TBX20, TBX21, TBR1, EOMES, MGA and TBXT are all AGGTGTGA or AGGTGTGAA - character-for-character identical in many cases - and the family's cohesion of 0.86 across 60 motifs is high given how many distinct proteins are involved. High-throughput SELEX reached the same conclusion: homodimer orientation and spacing preferences often carry more information than the core consensus. Treat spacing and orientation, not base identity, as the only thing that might discriminate members, and treat even that as weak. One provenance note: the CIS-BP TBX10 motif is transferred from the mouse protein at 89% DNA-binding-domain identity rather than measured on the human protein.

## Where it acts

T-box sites are predominantly enhancer elements and are not CpG-island features. Occupancy is highly cell-type restricted because expression is: a TBX5 site in a cardiomyocyte and a TBR1 site in a cortical neuron may be the same sequence. In the heart, T-box sites co-occur with GATA4, NKX2-5, MEF2 and SRF sites, and TBX5-GATA4-NKX2-5 co-binding is the best-studied combinatorial arrangement in cardiac enhancers. In lymphocytes, TBX21 sites sit alongside STAT, RUNX and ETS sites at the IFNG locus. The only named heterodimeric element in these collections is MGA::EVX1, a T-box half-site adjacent to a homeodomain TAAT core, which is a composite of two different proteins rather than a T-box variant.

## Biology and disease

Brachyury is required for posterior mesoderm and notochord; homozygous mutants fail axial development. The paralogues map neatly onto human malformation syndromes: TBX5 mutations cause Holt-Oram syndrome, with septal defects and radial-ray limb malformations; TBX3 mutations cause ulnar-mammary syndrome; loss of Tbx1 in mice reproduces the DiGeorge/22q11.2 deletion phenotype; TBX20 mutations cause diverse cardiac pathology including septation and valve defects and cardiomyopathy; TBX19 (TPIT) mutations cause isolated ACTH deficiency; TBX22 mutations cause cleft palate with ankyloglossia; TBX6 variants contribute to congenital scoliosis. TBX21 (T-bet) was isolated as the T-box factor that drives interferon-gamma and commits naive CD4 T cells to the Th1 lineage, and can redirect polarised Th2 cells. In cancer, germline duplication of the TBXT locus confers strong susceptibility to familial chordoma, a notochord-derived tumour in which TBXT is also the near-universal lineage dependency; TBX2 and TBX3 are amplified or overexpressed in breast and other carcinomas, where they repress CDKN2A.

## Reading a hit

Assume a T-box hit names the family and nothing more. Models for fourteen or more paralogues are identical, so which protein is responsible must be inferred from expression, not from sequence. An eight-base half-site is also short - AGGTGTGA occurs on the order of tens of thousands of times per genome - so an isolated half-site match is weak. Matches gain weight when the geometry is present: an inverted pair (AGGTGTGA...TCACACCT), an everted pair, or a tandem repeat within a few base pairs is much more likely to be real than a lone half-site. Check provenance before trusting a specific label: the CIS-BP TBX10 model is inherited from mouse, and the Vierstra archetype names (AC0487:TBX/T, AC0490:TBX/EOMES, AC0491:TBX/MGA) list the factor groups whose motifs clustered together, not distinguishable specificities. Two ChIP-derived entries in this family, TBX20.H14CORE.0.P.C and TBX5.H14CORE.1.P.B, read GTGNTGACAG, contain no recognisable T-box core, and have their nearest neighbours outside the family (label agreement 0.1); they are better read as reflecting co-occupancy with another factor than as T-box recognition, and should not be used for scanning.
families.caveats: This family has the paralogue problem in its most extreme form: the primary models for fourteen or more T-box proteins are AGGTGTGA or AGGTGTGAA, identical in many cases, so a hit identifies T-box and nothing finer - the responsible protein follows from which paralogue is expressed. An eight-base half-site is common by chance, so weight matches by geometry: inverted, everted or tandem pairs are far more credible than a single half-site. Two ChIP-derived models here (TBX20.H14CORE.0.P.C, TBX5.H14CORE.1.P.B) read GTGNTGACAG with no T-box core and neighbours outside the family; treat them as co-occupancy signal. The CIS-BP TBX10 motif is transferred from mouse.

families.name: Other BTB-ZF (ZBTB)
families.def: BTB-domain zinc fingers without a dedicated entry: ZBTB1-6, ZBTB11-49 and relatives. BCL6/BCL6B, HIC1/HIC2, ZBTB17, ZBTB18, ZBTB33, ZBTB7A/B/C and ZBTB48 are covered separately.
families.short: BTB-ZF proteins, also called POZ-ZF, pair an N-terminal BTB/POZ domain, a dimerization module, with a short C2H2 zinc-finger array. This entry collects the 28 less-studied members: ZBTB1 to ZBTB6, ZBTB8A and ZBTB8B, ZBTB11, 12, 14, 16, 20, 22, 24, 26, 32, 37, 40 to 45, 47 and 49, plus myoneurin (MYNN) and ZNF131. The distinctive BTB-ZFs with well-mapped sites, among them BCL6, HIC1/2, ZBTB7A/B, MIZ1, ZBTB18, Kaiso and TZAP, are split into their own entries. It is not a single motif: 60 matrices, cohesion 0.42, median length 10 bp. Several members do read inverted-repeat sites, as obligate dimerization predicts, but the half-sites differ from protein to protein.
families.long:
## The factors

The BTB domain (broad-complex, tramtrack, bric-a-brac), also called POZ (poxvirus and zinc finger), is a protein-protein interaction module with a highly conserved core fold. It was first visualized in the PLZF/ZBTB16 crystal structure (Ahmad et al. 1998), and the PLZF BTB homodimer remains the reference model; surveys of 17 eukaryotic genomes place BTB-ZF among several BTB families and show a large vertebrate expansion (Stogios et al. 2005). BTB-ZF factors are predominantly transcriptional repressors, with prominent roles in haematopoietic development and malignancy (Kelly and Daniel 2006; de Greef et al. 2011). Their C2H2 arrays are short compared with KRAB zinc fingers, typically two to six fingers, which limits how much sequence one monomer can read and is part of why dimerization matters. Twenty-eight gene symbols appear here. Members with distinctive, better-mapped sites are described elsewhere in this atlas: BCL6 and BCL6B, HIC1 and HIC2, ZBTB7A and ZBTB7B, ZBTB17/MIZ1, ZBTB18, ZBTB33/Kaiso, PATZ1 (grouped with MAZ) and ZBTB48/TZAP (grouped with the telobox factors). What remains is deliberately the residue: a few members with good data, a majority with almost none.

## The motif

There is no family consensus; cohesion is 0.42. Median consensus length is 10 bp and median information content 12.7 bits, short and weak beside the KRAB zinc-finger entries; only 2 matrices reach 20 bp and only 7 exceed 20 bits. The clearest structural signature is the dyad an obligate BTB homodimer predicts. ZBTB32 (also TZFP, FAZF) gives TGTACAGTAATACTGTACA at 28.9 bits, an inverted repeat of TGTACAGTA; its half-site ACTGTA is also the entire HOCOMOCO model for ZBTB16/PLZF at 9.4 bits, so at half-site resolution those two are indistinguishable. ZBTB22 gives TCACTATTATAGTGA, a near-perfect inverted repeat of TCACTAT, reproduced independently in CIS-BP and the Vierstra archetype AC0356. ZBTB43 gives GTGCCATANNNNCAGCAC, two half-sites separated by four unconstrained positions. ZBTB20 (CTATACGTT) and ZBTB45 (CACCTATAG, or CTATAGGTG on the other strand) both centre on CTATA and score about 0.96 against each other, so they are not separable. ZBTB14 (ZF5/ZFP161) is GC-rich and appears variously as TGCGCGTGCACGTG, GCGCGTGCGCGCG and CCGCGCAC; its CIS-BP model's nearest neighbour is an E2F matrix at 0.96 and its JASPAR model matches a non-family motif at 1.00, so ZBTB14 hits cannot be separated from the general GC-box and E2F pool. MYNN gives GACTTTTATTTT identically in CIS-BP, HOCOMOCO and the archetype AC0431, one of the few internally consistent models here. ZBTB40 has the best-supported model in the family: AAMAAAACTTTATTGA, 22.7 bits, grade A with ChIP, SELEX and integrative evidence. Two members contradict themselves across databases: ZBTB26 appears as TTCTGGA, as a CG repeat, and as TTYAAAANTTTTCTAGAA; ZBTB49 as TTTCGCCTGGCACGTCA and as GTGACCAGCCAGGCMAAAATGG. Neither should be treated as settled.

## Where it acts

Promoters and promoter-proximal regions, mostly; short, moderately informative motifs are typical of factors recruited into promoter complexes rather than of long-range specificity. Genome-wide maps exist for few members. ZBTB11 is found at nuclear respiratory factor 2 (NRF-2/GABP) target promoters, where it facilitates GABP recruitment to genes for respiratory complex I and the mitoribosome (Wilson et al. 2020). ZBTB24 is required for DNA methylation of juxtacentromeric repeat sequences (de Greef et al. 2011). ZBTB16/PLZF occupies an extensive transcription-factor poising network in juvenile spermatogonial stem cells (Yi et al. 2025). For most other members the HOCOMOCO model is the only positional information available.

## Biology and disease

Human phenotypes are established for three members. ZBTB24 mutations cause immunodeficiency, centromeric instability and facial anomalies syndrome type 2, which shares hypomethylation of juxtacentromeric repeats with DNMT3B-mutant ICF1 and involves B cell development (de Greef et al. 2011). ZBTB20 mutations cause Primrose syndrome (Cordeddu et al. 2014), and Zbtb20 haploinsufficiency reproduces the intellectual disability and autism-like behaviour in mice (Hindermann et al. 2026). ZBTB11 mutations cause hereditary intellectual disability; the pathogenic substitutions destabilize the protein, lowering its dosage and producing a severe respiratory complex I assembly defect, impaired respiration and cell death (Wilson et al. 2020). Beyond disease genetics, ZBTB16/PLZF controls juvenile spermatogonial stem cell development (Yi et al. 2025), and myoneurin regulates BMP signalling by competing with PPM1A for SMAD binding (Yang et al. 2022) — several of these proteins act mainly through protein-protein rather than protein-DNA interactions.

## Reading a hit

Because the BTB domain dimerizes, look for the dyad: an inverted repeat of the half-site, with the spacing of the reference matrix. A half-site alone is weak evidence, and half-sites are shared between members, ACTGTA between ZBTB32 and PLZF and CTATA between ZBTB20 and ZBTB45. At a median of 10 bp and 12.7 bits, most of these motifs occur hundreds of thousands of times in the human genome, so a single match without conservation, accessibility or ChIP support supports nothing. Eleven of 60 matrices have their nearest neighbour in another family: three resemble HSF motifs (two ZBTB26 models and the archetype AC0687), two the ZBTB7 motif (ZBTB11 and ZBTB2), two HAND/TWIST (ZBTB42 and AC0074), and one each E2F (ZBTB14), Kaiso/ZBTB33 (AC0312), ZBTB18 (ZBTB42) and HIC (ZBTB43). The ZBTB11 case is instructive: its JASPAR motif CACTTCCGG contains CCGGAAG, the GABP/ETS core, and ZBTB11 is known to recruit GABP to promoters, so the most parsimonious reading is that this matrix records GABP's specificity captured through co-binding rather than ZBTB11's own. Finally, the CIS-BP models for ZBTB1 (CCCGCA) and ZBTB3 (CACTGC) are transferred from mouse orthologues; the domains are 100% identical, so the transfer is sound, but at 6.5 to 6.8 bits they are too weak to scan with.
families.caveats: This is a domain family with several unrelated motifs, not one motif: 28 proteins, 60 matrices, cohesion 0.42, no consensus. The matrices are short (median 10 bp, 12.7 bits), so most match hundreds of thousands of genomic positions and a lone hit means little. Because BTB is a dimerization domain, require the dyad rather than a half-site, and note that half-sites are shared: ACTGTA between ZBTB32 and PLZF, CTATA between ZBTB20 and ZBTB45. Eleven matrices most closely resemble another family's motif, and ZBTB11's is most plausibly GABP's, captured through co-binding. The ZBTB26 and ZBTB49 models contradict each other across databases, and the mouse-derived ZBTB1 and ZBTB3 models carry under 7 bits.

families.name: NKX
families.def: TAAGTG / CACTTAA. NKX1-1/1-2, NKX2-1 to 2-8, NKX3-1/3-2, NKX6-1 to 6-3, plus NKX-like archetypes.
families.short: NKX proteins are homeodomain transcription factors related to Drosophila tinman and vnd, and they are the main exception to the rule that homeodomains read a TAAT core. NKX2-1 (TTF-1), NKX2-2 to NKX2-8, NKX3-1 and NKX3-2 prefer TAAGTG (read as CACTTA on the other strand), a specificity recognized as unusual when TTF-1 was first cloned. The family collects 51 motifs for 16 genes, including NKX1-1/1-2, NKX6-1 to NKX6-3 and NANOG. It is the least cohesive homeodomain family in this atlas because the NKX6 proteins in fact read a conventional TAAT core rather than TAAGTG, so the label covers two different sites.
families.long:
## The factors

NKX genes are the vertebrate NK-class homeobox genes, orthologues of Drosophila tinman (heart) and vnd/NK-2 (ventral nervous system). Sixteen symbols and 51 motifs are grouped here: NKX1-1 and NKX1-2; NKX2-1 (also called TTF-1 or TITF1), NKX2-2, NKX2-3, NKX2-4, NKX2-5, NKX2-6 and NKX2-8; NKX3-1 and NKX3-2; NKX6-1, NKX6-2 and NKX6-3; plus NANOG and unassigned NKX archetypes. Each is restricted to a small number of lineages: NKX2-1 to thyroid and lung, NKX2-5 to heart, NKX2-2 and NKX6-1 to pancreatic endocrine progenitors and ventral neural tube, NKX3-1 to prostate epithelium, NKX3-2 (BAPX1) to axial skeleton, NANOG to pluripotent cells. All bind DNA as monomeric homeodomains; none of them needs a dedicated DNA-binding partner, although NKX2-5 and GATA4 co-activate shared targets.

## The motif

The consensus is TAAGTG. Randomized-site selection with the NKX2-5 homeodomain gave high-affinity sites of the form 5'-TNNAGTG-3' and only intermediate or weak binding to 5'-C(A/T)TTAATTN-3', the conventional TAAT-type site, which is the cleanest demonstration that NKX proteins prefer a different core. The TTF-1/NKX2-1 site is often written CAAGTG, which is the same sequence read the other way.

The structural reason is not position 50. Every NKX homeodomain has glutamine there, the residue that in other families specifies TAATTA; the NMR structure of the vnd/NK-2 homeodomain on DNA confirms Gln50 together with the canonical Asn51 hydrogen bond and minor-groove contacts from Lys3 and Arg5. What differs is elsewhere in the recognition helix, notably position 54, which is tyrosine in NKX2-1, NKX2-5 and NKX3-1 but methionine or alanine in TAATTA-reading homeodomains. This is why the position-50 rule, which explains TAATTA versus TAATCC, does not explain TAAGTG.

The family is internally split, and this is its most important practical feature. NKX2-x and NKX3-x models are TAAGTG: NKX3-2 (the medoid, HOCOMOCO NKX32.H14CORE.0.PSM.A) TAAGTG, NKX3-1 TTAAGTGG, NKX2-3 TTAAGTG, NKX2-8 TTAAGTG, NKX2-1 and NKX2-2 TTGAGTG. The NKX6 models are not: NKX6-1 and NKX6-2 give TTAATTA and NKX6-3 gives ATTAATGAC, ordinary TAAT-core sites. NANOG models are TAATGG-like. Family cohesion is accordingly 0.74, the lowest of the homeodomain families here, and NKX6-2's CIS-BP model is flagged as resembling anterior HOX - correctly, since TAATTA is what it is. Within each subgroup the paralogues are indistinguishable: no matrix separates NKX2-1 from NKX2-4, or NKX3-1 from NKX3-2. Several models here are dimeric or extended, such as NKX3-2 TTAAGTGGCACTTAA (two half-sites in inverted orientation) and NKX6-1 ATTAATGGGHWTTTAAT.

## Where it acts

Sites sit in lineage-specific enhancers and in promoters of tissue-defining genes: TTF-1 was purified on thyroid-specific gene promoters, NKX2-5 acts on cardiac structural gene enhancers, and NKX6-1 acts downstream of NKX2-2 in beta-cell formation. TAAGTG is a common hexamer, expected on the order of two million times in 3.1 Gb at human base composition, so genome-wide match counts are large and uninformative; accessibility and expression do the work. NKX2-5 sites frequently co-occur with GATA and TBX motifs in cardiac enhancers, NKX6-1 with PDX1 and other pancreatic homeodomain sites.

## Biology and disease

Heterozygous NKX2-5 mutations cause atrial septal defect with progressive atrioventricular conduction block, and Nkx2-5 null mouse embryos arrest at the heart-tube stage. NKX2-1 haploinsufficiency causes brain-lung-thyroid syndrome (choreoathetosis, congenital hypothyroidism, pulmonary disease), while the NKX2-1 locus at 14q13 is focally amplified in lung adenocarcinoma. NKX3-1 is a prostate tumor suppressor whose expression is lost early in prostate carcinogenesis. NKX6-1 is required for pancreatic beta-cell formation, NKX3-2 for axial skeletal development, and NANOG for maintenance of pluripotency in the epiblast and in embryonic stem cells.

## Reading a hit

A TAAGTG match indicates an NKX2/NKX3-type site and no particular gene. A TAAT-type match labelled NKX6 is a generic homeodomain site and should be read as such. This family also carries the clearest indirect-binding problems in the homeodomain set: 6 of its 17 HOCOMOCO models are ChIP-only, and two of them are flagged as matching other families entirely. The NANOG ChIP-derived model reads CCTTTGTNATGCAAA - the octamer ATGCAAAT, which is the POU/OCT4 motif, exactly what indirect capture of a co-occupied partner looks like for a factor that shares enhancers with OCT4 and SOX2. An NKX2-5 ChIP model reads GTGHTGACAG and matches the TBX family. Six CIS-BP entries in this family are transferred from mouse orthologues, one of them (NKX2-6) inferred at 93% DNA-binding-domain identity rather than measured. Prefer the HT-SELEX-derived models when testing whether a sequence is an NKX site.
families.caveats: Treat a TAAGTG hit as "an NKX2/NKX3-type site", not as a named factor; paralogues within each subgroup are indistinguishable. The family label spans two different motifs - NKX2 and NKX3 proteins read TAAGTG, but NKX6-1/6-2/6-3 read an ordinary TAAT core - which is why cohesion is only 0.74 and why one NKX6-2 model is flagged as HOX-like. ChIP-only evidence is a real risk here: 6 of 17 HOCOMOCO models are ChIP-derived, and two are flagged as belonging elsewhere, including a NANOG model that is actually the OCT4 octamer. Six CIS-BP motifs are inherited from mouse proteins. Expect roughly two million genome-wide matches, so require accessibility and expression.

families.name: PAX paired domain
families.def: Paired-domain site GTCACGC(A/T)TGA; PAX1/9, PAX2/5/8, PAX3/7, PAX4/6 (with and without the homeodomain half-site).
families.short: The paired domain is a bipartite DNA-binding domain, unique to the nine human PAX proteins, that reads an unusually long site: a GTCACGC(A/T)TGA core set inside a footprint of roughly 15 to 20 base pairs. Two helix-turn-helix subdomains, PAI and RED, grip adjacent stretches of the double helix, so the recognition surface is far larger than that of a single homeodomain. PAX3, PAX4, PAX6 and PAX7 additionally carry a complete homeodomain that contributes an independent TAAT half site, making their composite elements longer still. PAX sites are therefore among the most information-rich transcription factor motifs in the genome. These factors specify the eye, thyroid, kidney, pancreatic beta cells, B lymphocytes and muscle progenitors, and paired-domain mutations cause aniridia, Waardenburg syndrome and renal-coloboma syndrome.
families.long:
## The factors

Nine human genes, PAX1 to PAX9, each encode a paired domain of about 128 residues. They fall into four
subgroups by what else they contain: PAX1 and PAX9 (paired domain plus octapeptide), PAX2, PAX5 and PAX8
(plus octapeptide and a vestigial partial homeodomain), PAX3 and PAX7 (plus octapeptide and a complete
homeodomain), and PAX4 and PAX6 (paired domain plus complete homeodomain). The paired domain binds DNA as
a monomer; no dimerisation is required. It is built from two independently folding helix-turn-helix units,
the N-terminal PAI subdomain and the C-terminal RED subdomain, joined by a linker that tracks the minor
groove. Expression is tissue-restricted rather than ubiquitous: PAX5 in B lymphocytes, PAX8 in thyroid and
kidney, PAX6 in eye, pancreas and central nervous system, PAX3 and PAX7 in neural crest and muscle
satellite cells, PAX4 in pancreatic beta cells.

## The motif

The core paired-domain site is GTCACGC(A/T)TGA, about 11 bp, sitting inside a 15 to 20 bp contacted
region. Crystal structures of a *Drosophila* Prd paired domain at 2.5 A and of the human PAX6 paired
domain at higher resolution showed how the information is distributed: the PAI helix 3 inserts into the
major groove and reads the 5' GTCAC half, the beta-hairpin and N-terminal beta-turn make extensive
minor-groove contacts, and the RED subdomain reaches the 3' end of the site. Most of the affinity and most
of the specificity lie in the 5' GTCACGC; RED contributes additional 3' contacts and is dispensable at
some sites. Alternative splicing of PAX6 exon 5a inserts 14 residues into PAI, inactivates it, and
switches the protein to a RED-dominated specificity, so one gene encodes two different sequence
preferences. The homeodomain of PAX3, PAX4, PAX6 and PAX7 adds a separate TAAT half site and dimerises
cooperatively on palindromic P3-type elements, TAAT-N2/3-ATTA. All three shapes appear in the assembled
data: paired-domain models such as CGTCACGCATGACTGC for PAX9, pure homeodomain palindromes such as
TAATCGATTA for PAX3 and PAX7, and a composite CGTCACGCTWATTA that fuses both in 14 bp. Paralogues within
a subgroup are not separable: PAX1 and PAX9, and PAX2, PAX5 and PAX8, have motifs matching each other at
0.96 or better.

## Where it acts

PAX proteins work at both promoters and distal enhancers, and their long sites make named composite
elements unusually tractable. The best characterised is the B-cell-specific mb-1 (CD79A) promoter, where
PAX5 bound to its paired-domain site recruits ETS-family proteins into a ternary complex on an adjacent
GGAA core; the PAX5 half of that element is degenerate on its own and depends on the partner. PAX6 acts at
lens crystallin promoters and at pancreatic and retinal enhancers. In alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma the
PAX3-FOXO1 fusion occupies myogenic enhancers through the retained paired domain plus homeodomain.
Because the full site is long, genome-wide occurrence by chance is low relative to 6 to 8 bp motifs, and
occupancy is strongly cell-type restricted; the same sequence is largely unoccupied in tissues that do not
express the relevant PAX gene.

## Biology and disease

Heterozygous PAX6 loss causes aniridia and a spectrum of anterior-segment eye malformations, and the
mouse *Small eye* mutant is the orthologous allele. PAX3 mutations cause Waardenburg syndrome types 1 and
3; PAX2 mutations cause renal-coloboma syndrome; PAX8 mutations cause congenital hypothyroidism from
thyroid dysgenesis. Mice lacking Pax5 arrest B-cell development at the pro-B stage and show posterior
midbrain patterning defects. In cancer, t(2;13) and t(1;13) translocations fuse PAX3 or PAX7 to FOXO1 in
alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma; PAX5 is recurrently altered in B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukaemia; PAX8 is
used diagnostically in thyroid, renal and ovarian tumours.

## Reading a hit

A full GTCACGC(A/T)TGA match is one of the more trustworthy motif hits available, because 11 informative
positions are rare by chance. It tells you the subgroup, not the protein: nothing in the sequence
separates PAX2 from PAX5 or PAX8. Short matches are much weaker evidence. The homeodomain-only models are
generic paired-like homeodomain sites: the JASPAR PAX4 entry MA0068.2 is CTAATTAG and its nearest
neighbours across all four databases are PRD-like homeobox motifs, not PAX motifs, and a CIS-BP PAX3 entry
is a bare TAATTG whose neighbours are Q50 homeodomain motifs. Several Vierstra footprint archetypes
labelled PAX carry no paired-domain information at all (GTGCACAC, TCCCCGGGC, CCACCCS, GTTT); these name
the factor group whose footprints clustered, and the cluster can be driven by co-occurring factors. This
is the least cohesive family in the set, at 0.57.
families.caveats: Trust long paired-domain matches; distrust short ones. The family pools three different motif shapes, paired domain, homeodomain half site, and composite, and only the first is PAX-diagnostic. Within the PAX1/PAX9 and PAX2/PAX5/PAX8 subgroups the motifs are interchangeable, so a hit names a subgroup at best. Homeodomain-only models labelled PAX4 or PAX3 are indistinguishable from PRD-like and Q50 homeodomain sites and are flagged in the underlying data as probably belonging elsewhere. Several PAX-labelled footprint archetypes contain no recognisable paired-domain sequence and should not be used to call PAX occupancy. Occupancy is strongly restricted to tissues that express the gene.

families.name: SCAN-domain zinc fingers (ZSCAN/ZKSCAN)
families.def: SCAN-domain C2H2 factors: ZSCAN and ZKSCAN genes, ZNF24-like SCAN factors.
families.short: The larger, thinner-documented half of the human SCAN-domain zinc fingers: 26 labels including ZSCAN1, 2, 5, 9, 12, 16, 23, 25, 26, 30 and 31, ZKSCAN2, 4, 5, 7 and 8, and the older names ZNF165, ZNF174, ZNF232, ZNF396, ZNF444 and ZNF449. Each combines an N-terminal SCAN domain, an approximately 80-residue leucine-rich module that dimerizes, with a tandem C2H2 finger array; the ZKSCAN members also carry a KRAB domain. This is not a single motif. The 48 matrices here form roughly twenty per-protein groups that do not resemble one another, ranging from ZSCAN16's TGTTAACAGAGCCTC to ZNF444's poly-C run. Functional data exist for only a handful of members.
families.long:
## The factors

The SCAN domain is a conserved, leucine-rich module of about 80 to 84 residues found near the N terminus of a subfamily of C2H2 zinc fingers. It contains three predicted helices and mediates self-association or selective association with other SCAN-bearing proteins (Williams et al. 1999). The one high-resolution structure, an NMR structure of the MZF1 SCAN domain, is a domain-swapped dimer of five-helix monomers with helix 3 at the core of the interface and a dissociation constant near 600 nM; more than 60 human C2H2 zinc-finger genes carry the domain (Peterson et al. 2006). SCAN genes sit in clusters, often tandem arrays, carry 3 to 14 fingers, and some combine SCAN with KRAB or SANT domains and generate alternative isoforms (Edelstein and Collins 2005). Nomenclature has churned: ZNF165, ZNF174, ZNF232, ZNF396, ZNF444 and ZNF449 predate the ZSCAN/ZKSCAN scheme and are the same class of protein. The ZKSCAN members can recruit TRIM28 through their KRAB domain. The atlas places the seven SCAN factors with the best-mapped sites in a separate ZNF24 entry; the members with thinner data are collected here.

## The motif

There is no family consensus; cohesion is 0.39. The 48 matrices have a median consensus length of 14 bp and median information content 16.1 bits, with 15 above 20 bits and a maximum of 32.4 bits (ZSCAN2, AGGTTAGACTTCAGGAAGGACTTCC). Within-family similarity looks high (median 0.95, only 2 of 35 below 0.7), but that is an artefact of redundancy: the close neighbour is almost always the same protein measured again in another database, as for ZNF449 (AGCCCAACC, its reverse complement GGTTGGGCT, and the archetype AC0534) or ZSCAN5C (TTTGTTGACTCAC and TGTGAGTCAATAAA). Between proteins the motifs are unrelated: ZSCAN16 TGTTAACAGAGCCTC at 31 bits with methyl-SELEX support and an agreeing archetype AC0298; ZSCAN23 CATGTGCTAATTACA; ZSCAN31 GCATAACTGCCCTGC; ZSCAN9 TGATTCTTATCTTATCC, a direct TTATC repeat; ZNF174 GGCGAGTGATCGGC, whose CIS-BP model GNCGATCACTTGCC is the same sequence on the opposite strand; ZSCAN5/ZSCAN5A GTCCCCCCCAAA; ZKSCAN5 TCACCTCC; ZNF444 CCCCCTCCCCC. Because the SCAN domain dimerizes, dyadic sites would be a reasonable expectation, and a few models are compatible with one, but most are not obvious inverted repeats and no member has been tested for half-site organization. Do not assume a dyad. Several models are low-complexity rather than specific: the CIS-BP entry for ZSCAN16 (M08377) is a pure (AT)n tract, ZNF444's is a poly-C run flagged as matching the ZNF281 motif, and ZKSCAN2's is a poly-A run whose nearest neighbour outside this family scores 1.00.

## Where it acts

Little systematic mapping has been published. The matrices themselves split into two groups with different expected genomic distributions: the GC- and CT-rich models (ZNF444, ZKSCAN5, ZSCAN25, ZNF165) will fall in promoters and CpG islands, where they are hard to separate from the general GC-box pool, while the longer AT-containing models (ZSCAN2, ZSCAN23, ZKSCAN8, ZNF232) will fall mostly in repeat-rich non-coding sequence. The genes themselves cluster in tandem arrays, several on chromosome 19 (Edelstein and Collins 2005). Systematic surveys of poorly characterized human transcription factors find that roughly half bind conventional promoters and enhancers while the other half bind repeat-rich closed chromatin at protein-specific sites (Razavi et al. 2026); most ZSCAN members have not been placed in either group. For ZNF165 the best evidence is that it acts with SMAD3 at TGF-beta target genes rather than autonomously (Gibbs et al. 2020), which matters for how its motif should be read.

## Biology and disease

The functional literature is thin and uneven. ZNF165 is a cancer-testis antigen that elicits antibody responses in hepatocellular carcinoma patients (Dong et al. 2004) and acts as a SMAD3 cofactor coordinating oncogenic TGF-beta signalling in triple-negative breast cancer, where it is required for tumour cell growth (Gibbs et al. 2020). For most other members, published work is limited to expression surveys and to the systematic screens that generated the motifs in the first place (Najafabadi et al. 2015; Schmitges et al. 2016; Jolma et al. 2026). The KRAB-bearing ZKSCAN members are expected to repress through TRIM28, but this has been shown for very few of them. Absence of a phenotype in this entry reflects absence of study, not a demonstrated lack of function; these are among the proteins the Codebook effort was designed to address.

## Reading a hit

Read a hit as belonging to one named protein: there is no ZSCAN motif. Check the evidence code first. Of the 19 HOCOMOCO models here, 8 are ChIP-only (code P) and the rest carry some in vitro support, with grades splitting 4 A, 7 B and 8 C. Discard the low-complexity matrices for scanning: an (AT)n, poly-C or poly-A model will match millions of positions and carries no factor-specific information. Five matrices have their nearest neighbour in a different family: three are the ZSCAN4/ZNF24 motif (both ZSCAN1 models and the archetype AC0530), one is the ZNF281 poly-C motif (ZNF444), and one is a homeodomain TAATT site (the CIS-BP model for ZSCAN31) — so cross-check before naming a factor. One model, the CIS-BP entry for ZSCAN26, is transferred from the mouse orthologue at 0.89 DNA-binding-domain identity and carries under 10 bits; it should not be used. Finally, because SCAN factors heterodimerize with one another, an occupied site may have been contacted by a partner's fingers rather than by those of the protein whose name is on the motif.
families.caveats: This entry is a structural class, not a motif: 26 proteins, 48 matrices, cohesion 0.39, and no consensus. A hit names one protein at best. Several matrices are low-complexity — an (AT)n tract for ZSCAN16 in CIS-BP, poly-C for ZNF444, poly-A for ZKSCAN2 — and should not be scanned at all. Eight of 19 HOCOMOCO models are ChIP-only, so the enriched sequence may be a partner's; ZNF165 in particular works as a SMAD3 cofactor. The CIS-BP ZSCAN26 model is a mouse transfer carrying under 10 bits. Because SCAN domains heterodimerize, occupancy may reflect a partner's fingers rather than the named protein's.

families.name: IRF
families.def: ISRE/AICE, AANTGAAA repeats. IRF1-9; composite EICE (with SPI1) and AICE (with BATF).
families.short: The nine human interferon regulatory factors, IRF1 through IRF9, bind DNA with an N-terminal winged helix-turn-helix domain studded with five conserved tryptophans. Each domain reads only a short AANTGAAA half-site, so functional elements are tandem repeats of it: the interferon-stimulated response element (ISRE), written RNGAAANNGAAACT or, on the other strand, AGTTTCNNTTTC. The same half-site also appears in two named composites - the EICE with PU.1 or SPIB, and the AICE with BATF-JUN - which is how IRF4 and IRF8, weak DNA binders on their own, reach their targets. IRFs drive the type I and type II interferon responses, myeloid and lymphoid development, and plasma cell differentiation; IRF6 is the non-immune outlier, acting in epithelium, where mutations cause orofacial clefting.
families.long:
## The factors

Nine IRF genes exist in humans, IRF1 to IRF9 (an IRF10 is present in birds and fish but not in
mammals). Each encodes an N-terminal DNA-binding domain of roughly 115 residues characterized by a
cluster of five conserved tryptophans - the "tryptophan cluster" that defines the family - folded as
a variant helix-turn-helix. Most members also carry a C-terminal IRF-association domain that
mediates homodimers, IRF-IRF heterodimers, and complexes with non-IRF partners: STAT2 for IRF9,
BATF-JUN for IRF4 and IRF8, PU.1 and SPIB for IRF4 and IRF8. Functionally the family splits along
lines that sequence does not see. IRF1 and IRF2 are broadly expressed and act as an
interferon-inducible activator/repressor pair on the same sites. IRF3 is constitutive and
cytoplasmic until phosphorylated on virus sensing, whereupon it dimerizes and drives type I
interferon genes; IRF7 amplifies that response and is highly expressed in plasmacytoid dendritic
cells. IRF9 is the constitutive DNA-binding subunit of ISGF3. IRF4 and IRF8 are lymphoid and myeloid,
with low intrinsic DNA affinity; IRF5 acts in myeloid cells and B cells. IRF6 is the outlier -
epithelial, expressed in skin and oral periderm, with no established role in interferon signaling.

## The motif

The unit is a short half-site, AANTGAAA, of which only about four bases (the GAAA) are read
strongly. The crystal structure of the IRF1 domain on the PRD I element of the interferon-beta
promoter showed why: the recognition helix lies obliquely in the major groove, contacts a short GAAA
core through three of the five conserved tryptophans, and bends the DNA toward the protein. Because
so little sequence is read per domain, affinity and specificity come from repetition, and the IRF2
structure showed cooperative binding to a tandem GAAA repeat driven by DNA distortion. The canonical
element is therefore the ISRE, written RNGAAANNGAAACT; the data consensus for this family,
CGAAACCGAAACT, is the same element read on the opposite strand, whose reverse complement
AGTTTCGGTTTCG is the familiar AGTTTCNNTTTC form. Two composites reuse the same half-site with a
different partner. The EICE, GGAAGTGAAAC, is a PU.1 or SPIB site fused to an IRF half-site; the
AICE joins an IRF half-site to an AP-1 site, either as AICE1 (TTTCNNNNTGASTCA, four bases of spacer)
or AICE2 (GAAATGASTCA, directly abutting). Paralogue resolution from sequence is close to zero: the
in vitro models for all nine IRFs are near-identical GAAA repeats, and what separates them in vivo is
which partner they cooperate with, not which bases they read.

## Where it acts

ISREs sit predominantly in promoters of interferon-stimulated genes, usually within a few hundred
base pairs of the transcription start site, and in virus-inducible enhancers such as the
interferon-beta enhanceosome, where PRD I and PRD III are IRF elements. In lymphoid and myeloid
cells, IRF4 and IRF8 occupancy is overwhelmingly composite: EICEs at immunoglobulin light-chain
enhancers, where DNA-bound and Ser148-phosphorylated PU.1 raises IRF4 affinity 20- to 40-fold, and
AICEs with BATF-JUN in T cells and dendritic cells. AICE affinity grades the response to signal
strength: high-affinity AICEs remain occupied under weak T-cell receptor stimulation while
low-affinity ones only under strong stimulation. ISGF3, the STAT1-STAT2-IRF9 trimer, accounts for
most ISRE occupancy in a type I interferon response, with the STAT1-STAT2 pair on the 5' GGAA and
IRF9 on the second repeat. IRF6 works instead in epithelial enhancers of the periderm and keratinocyte programs.

## Biology and disease

IRFs are the transcriptional output of innate immune sensing and are also lineage regulators.
Human IRF8 mutations cause dendritic cell immunodeficiency, with biallelic loss abolishing monocytes
and dendritic cells. IRF4 is required for plasma cell
differentiation, and multiple myeloma lines die when IRF4 is depleted whether or not IRF4 itself is
mutated. A common IRF5 haplotype that alters splicing and expression is a reproducible risk factor
for systemic lupus erythematosus. IRF6 mutations cause Van der Woude syndrome (cleft lip or palate
with lower lip pits) and popliteal pterygium syndrome, the clearest case of an IRF acting outside
immunity.

## Reading a hit

A single AANTGAAA half-site is not evidence of anything: with roughly six specified bases it is
expected on the order of a million times per strand in a 3.1-Gb genome. Require the tandem repeat,
or a composite. The most common misreading is confusion with STAT. A STAT homodimer site (GAS) is an
inverted repeat, TTCNNNGAA, with the two half-sites facing each other; an ISRE is a direct repeat,
GAAANNGAAAC, with both half-sites in the same orientation - and its reverse-complement spelling
AGTTTCNNTTTC superficially resembles a GAS. The two families genuinely overlap in biology as well,
because ISGF3 contains STAT1 and STAT2, so ISRE-shaped matrices appear under both labels; one
footprint archetype grouped in this family is named AC0672:IRF/STAT precisely because the clustering
could not separate them. Evidence for this family is comparatively good - most HOCOMOCO models here
carry in vitro HT-SELEX or methyl-HT-SELEX support, and most JASPAR profiles here are SELEX-derived - but two
ChIP-derived entries have absorbed a partner's site. HOCOMOCO's ChIP-based IRF8 model
(IRF8.H14CORE.0.P.B, consensus AGDGGAAGTGAAAGT) contains GGAAGTGAAA, an EICE whose 5' half is a PU.1
site, not an IRF site; and one CIS-BP model here (M07978, TGHGGAAATGARTCA) is AICE2-shaped, an IRF
half-site abutting an AP-1 heptamer, and its best match across the databases lies outside the IRF
family. In
myeloid or B-lineage data, check for an adjacent GGAA or TGASTCA before concluding that an IRF acted
alone.
families.caveats:
A hit identifies an IRF-type element, not an IRF protein: all nine paralogues select
near-identical GAAA repeats in vitro, and their specificity in cells comes from partners (PU.1/SPIB
at an EICE, BATF-JUN at an AICE, STAT2 in ISGF3), not from the bases they read. A lone AANTGAAA
half-site is far too short to be meaningful; insist on a tandem repeat or a composite. Expect
cross-talk with the STAT family in both directions, since ISGF3 contains STAT1 and STAT2 and reads
the ISRE - one footprint archetype here is named IRF/STAT. Most models in this family have in vitro
support, but the ChIP-derived IRF8 model contains an embedded PU.1 half-site and one CIS-BP model in
this family is actually an AICE, half AP-1. Neither should be read as intrinsic IRF specificity.
