families.name: E2F / DP
families.def: TTTSSCGC. E2F1-8, TFDP1/2.
families.short: E2F factors are the transcriptional output of the retinoblastoma (RB) pathway and set the G1/S transition. Eight human genes, E2F1-E2F8, encode a winged-helix DNA-binding domain. E2F1-E2F6 bind DNA only as heterodimers with a DP subunit (TFDP1 or TFDP2); E2F7 and E2F8 carry two tandem winged-helix domains and work without DP. All of them read essentially the same GC-rich eight-base element, written TTTSSCGC and just as often rendered on the other strand as GCGGGAAA. E2F1-E2F3 are activators released when CDKs phosphorylate RB; E2F4-E2F8 repress, E2F4 as part of the DREAM complex that also reads the adjacent CHR element. Sites sit in CpG-island promoters of replication and cell-cycle genes, and the RB-E2F axis is disabled in most human cancers.
families.long:
## The factors

Humans have eight E2F genes and two dimerization partners, TFDP1 and TFDP2 (DP1 and DP2).
E2F1-E2F6 each contribute one winged-helix domain and must heterodimerize with a DP subunit,
which contributes a second winged helix, so the functional unit is a pseudo-symmetric clamp
built from two different proteins. The crystal structure of the E2F4-DP2 DNA-binding regions
on DNA showed both recognition helices inserted into the major groove of one short GC-rich
site. E2F7 and E2F8 are the exceptions: each carries two winged-helix domains in a single
polypeptide, binds as a homodimer or as an E2F7-E2F8 heterodimer, and needs no DP partner.
Function splits along the same lines as pocket-protein binding. E2F1, E2F2 and E2F3a are
activators held inactive by RB; E2F4 and E2F5 are repressors that partner p107 and p130
(RBL1, RBL2); E2F6 lacks the pocket-protein-binding region and represses as part of a
Bmi1-containing polycomb complex; E2F7 and E2F8 are atypical repressors. E2F1-E2F3 peak at
G1/S, whereas E2F4 is abundant in quiescent cells and accounts for most of the E2F signal in
chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP) experiments, largely through the DREAM complex.

## The motif

The literature consensus is TTTSSCGC (S = G or C), eight positions. Because the element is
close to self-complementary at its center, databases write it on either strand: TTTCCCGC,
TTTGGCGC, GCGGGAAA and GGCGGGAA are all the same site. The data consensus here, GGCGGGAA, is
the reverse complement of TTCCCGCC and does not contradict the literature form. In vitro
models from HT-SELEX are longer and palindromic, TTTTGGCGCCAAAA or TTTTGGCGGGAAA, which
reflects two overlapping half-sites and the two-subunit clamp; ChIP-derived models collapse to
the shorter, GC-skewed GGCGGGAA. The information is concentrated in the central GCGC or GCGG,
where the two recognition helices make direct base contacts, and falls off through the flanking
T-rich or A-rich tract. Because the core is GC-rich and contains CGCG or GGCGGG, E2F models
overlap the sequence space of the KLF/SP GC-box (GGGGCGGGG) and of other GC-repeat binders;
the Vierstra archetype AC0552:E2F/ZBTB is effectively a GCGCGCGC repeat whose nearest
neighbours in these data lie outside the family. Across 37 motifs from four databases the
family is cohesive (0.82) and no paralogue is separable: E2F1 through E2F8 and TFDP1 all
converge on one model, and E2F7/E2F8 differ only in showing the doubled form expected from
their tandem domains.

## Where it acts

E2F sites are promoter elements, not typical distal enhancer elements. They cluster within a
couple of hundred base pairs of the transcription start site in CpG islands, upstream of
replication genes (CDC6, the MCM2-7 genes, PCNA, POLA1), nucleotide metabolism genes (TYMS,
RRM2) and the E2F genes themselves. Genome-wide, E2F1, E2F4 and E2F6 occupy largely the same
promoters, which is one reason ChIP data do not separate the paralogues, and a large fraction
of occupied regions contain no canonical consensus at all. The best-characterized composite
element is the CDE/CHR module: a GC-rich cell cycle-dependent element (CDE) separated by about
four base pairs from a cell cycle genes homology region (CHR, TTYGAA), found in G2/M promoters
such as CDC25C, CDK1, CCNB2 and PLK1. The CHR is bound by LIN54 inside the DREAM/MuvB complex
and the CDE by an E2F-family protein; the two are functionally coupled, and both are needed for
p53-p21-DREAM repression. E2F sites also sit next to NF-Y CCAAT boxes and SP1 GC-boxes.

## Biology and disease

Loss of E2F1 in mice produces tumors as well as thymic hyperplasia, combined loss of E2F1-E2F3
blocks proliferation, and E2f7/E2f8 double-knockout embryos die with widespread apoptosis and
polyploidy. In human cancer the pathway upstream of E2F is disrupted far more often than E2F
itself: RB1 deletion, CDKN2A loss, CCND1 amplification and CDK4/CDK6 activation all converge on
releasing activator E2Fs, and CDK4/6 inhibitors work by restoring RB-mediated E2F repression.
Adenovirus E1A, HPV E7 and SV40 large T each dissociate E2F from pocket proteins, and HPV E7
specifically deregulates CDE/CHR-controlled genes. Deregulated E2F1 can also drive apoptosis,
which is why E2F activity is not simply pro-proliferative.

## Reading a hit

A single E2F match is weak evidence. The element is eight GC-rich bases with little flanking
information, so it occurs frequently by chance and is especially common in CpG-island promoters,
where base composition alone inflates matches. The match tells you nothing about which member
is bound: all eight E2Fs and both DP proteins share one model, and in a proliferating cell
several are present at once. It also does not tell you whether the site activates or represses,
since activator and repressor E2Fs use the same sequence. Confirm you are not looking at a
KLF/SP GC-box or a generic GC repeat. If the hit is in a G2/M promoter, look for a CHR about
four base pairs downstream, which is stronger evidence than the E2F match alone.
families.caveats: Trust an E2F hit as evidence for "an E2F-family site" and nothing narrower. The 8-bp GC-rich core gives frequent chance matches, especially inside CpG islands, and it overlaps KLF/SP GC-boxes, MAZ and other GC-repeat models. No paralogue is distinguishable from sequence, and neither activator nor repressor identity is readable. HOCOMOCO ChIP-only models (evidence letter P) are shorter and GC-skewed relative to the HT-SELEX and methyl-HT-SELEX models (S, M), which show the longer palindrome; the discrepancy is a difference in method, not in the factor. Roughly a third to a half of genomic E2F occupancy in ChIP experiments falls on regions without a canonical consensus, so absence of a match does not exclude binding.

families.name: MAF (MARE)
families.def: Maf recognition element TGCTGAC(G)TCAGCA; large MAFs (MAF, MAFA/B, NRL) and small MAFs (MAFF/G/K).
families.short: Maf proteins are basic region-leucine zipper factors that recognise an unusually long site, the Maf recognition element or MARE: 13 base pairs as TGCTGACTCAGCA, or 14 as TGCTGACGTCAGCA. The MARE is an AP-1 or CRE core with GC extensions added on both sides, and those extensions are read by two residues, an arginine and an asparagine, that are unique to the Maf basic region. The large Mafs - MAF, MAFA, MAFB and NRL - have transactivation domains; the small Mafs - MAFF, MAFG and MAFK - do not, so their homodimers repress and they serve instead as the obligate DNA-binding partners of the CNC and BACH proteins. Family members control lens, pancreatic beta cell, rod photoreceptor and erythroid programs, and are mutated or translocated in retinitis pigmentosa, insulinomatosis, carpotarsal osteolysis and myeloma.
families.long:
## The factors

Two subgroups share this element. The large Mafs - MAF (c-Maf), MAFA, MAFB and NRL - have an N-terminal transactivation domain in addition to the bZIP module, and an extended homology region adjacent to the basic region that contributes to DNA contact. The small Mafs - MAFF, MAFG and MAFK - are bZIP and little else; they have no activation domain, so small Maf homodimers act as repressors. Their more important role is as partners: the cap-n-collar (CNC) factors NFE2, NFE2L1, NFE2L2 and NFE2L3, and the BTB-bZIP repressors BACH1 and BACH2, cannot bind DNA as monomers, and require a small Maf to form a functional heterodimer. No functional difference is established among MAFF, MAFG and MAFK at the bZIP level. Expression differs a great deal: MAFG and MAFK are broadly expressed, MAFF is stress-inducible, MAFA is largely confined to pancreatic beta cells and lens, MAFB to macrophages, kidney podocytes and hindbrain, and NRL to rod photoreceptors. Maf proteins also heterodimerize with FOS and JUN, and those mixed dimers have binding specificities distinct from either homodimer.

## The motif

The MARE is 13 or 14 bases. Selection with v-Maf recovered two forms at roughly equal efficiency: the T-MARE, TGCTGACTCAGCA, and the C-MARE, TGCTGACGTCAGCA. Strip the flanks from either and you are left with exactly the AP-1 TRE or the CREB/ATF CRE; the Maf-specific information is entirely in the GC pairs added at each end. The crystal structure of MafG on DNA showed how those extensions are read: two well-conserved basic-region residues, Arg57 and Asn61, adopt unusual side-chain orientations and contact the extended GC bases directly, while Maf-specific residues in the N-terminal and basic regions stabilize the complex through backbone phosphate contacts. This is why the MARE is long and why no other bZIP family reads it. Because only one subunit of a heterodimer is a Maf, CNC-Maf and BACH-Maf heterodimers read a half-MARE: GC-extended on the Maf side, AP-1-like on the other side. That element is the antioxidant response element, treated here as the NFE2/BACH family. The 34 models collected for MAF show the split plainly. Full-length models carry both flanks (HOCOMOCO MAFG, MAFK, MAFA and MAFB read AATGCTGACTCAGCA-like sequences), while many others are truncated to one flank, which is why the consensus derived from these models is only the 7 bp TGCTGAC rather than the full 13-mer. Two heterodimer matrices assigned here, JASPAR MAF::NFE2 and MAFG::NFE2L1, read ATGACTCAGCA - GC on one side only - and nine of their ten nearest neighbours across the four databases carry labels from outside this family. Within the family, members are not distinguishable: MAFF, MAFG and MAFK are interchangeable, and the large Mafs differ from them mainly in affinity for degenerate sites. Even the heterodimer distinction is narrow: Nrf2-MafG and MafG homodimers bind the consensus MARE equally well and differ only on suboptimal sequences, traced to Ala502 of Nrf2, where Mafs have tyrosine.

## Where it acts

MAREs sit in tissue-specific enhancers and promoters: the alpha-A-crystallin and other crystallin genes in lens, insulin and beta-cell identity genes, rhodopsin and the rod gene set through NRL, and the HS2 enhancer of the beta-globin locus, whose NF-E2 site is a tandem MARE. Through CNC-small Maf heterodimers the same family of elements controls the cytoprotective and proteasome gene batteries. Half-MAREs outnumber full MAREs by a wide margin in real genomes, so most Maf-family occupancy in ChIP data reflects heterodimers rather than Maf homodimers. Because small Mafs are obligate partners, their genomic distribution largely follows that of the CNC and BACH proteins.

## Biology and disease

NRL determines rod photoreceptor fate: Nrl-null mice make cones in place of rods, and dominant NRL mutations cause autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa. A MAFA missense change causes familial insulinomatosis and diabetes in the same pedigrees. Mutations clustering in the N-terminal transactivation domain of MAFB cause multicentric carpotarsal osteolysis. MAF itself is dysregulated by translocation to immunoglobulin loci in a subset of multiple myeloma. Small Maf compound knockouts in mice reproduce aspects of CNC and BACH loss, as expected when the obligate partner is removed rather than the signal-responsive subunit.

## Reading a hit

The useful rule is to count the flanks. If your match carries GC extensions on both sides of a TGAC(G)TCA core, a Maf homodimer or large-Maf dimer is the best explanation and AP-1 is not, even though the AP-1 site is literally inside it. If the GC extension is on one side only, you are looking at a CNC-Maf or BACH-Maf half-MARE, that is, the NFE2/BACH family; two matrices assigned to MAF here are exactly that, so the MAF / NFE2-BACH boundary is a labelling convention rather than a separation in sequence space. If there is no GC extension at all, read AP-1 or CREB/ATF instead. Short models are a trap: several HOCOMOCO and CIS-BP entries here are truncated to TGCTGAC, TGCTGA or GTCAGCA, and a 6 or 7 base match of that kind will occur tens of thousands of times genome-wide. No member call is available - not MAFF versus MAFG versus MAFK, not MAF versus MAFA versus MAFB versus NRL, and not whether a Maf is the activating subunit at all. The original selection paper already warned that some sites reported in the literature as TREs are in fact Maf sites; the converse error, calling a MARE an AP-1 site, is the one a motif scanner will make for you.
families.caveats: The full 13 to 14 base MARE is one of the most specific bZIP calls available, because the GC extensions are read by residues no other bZIP family has. Everything short of that is ambiguous. A bare core is AP-1 or CRE; a one-sided GC extension is an antioxidant response element and belongs to NFE2/BACH, where two matrices filed under MAF in fact sit. Several models here are truncated to six or seven bases and should not be used for genome-wide scanning. No member can be inferred: the three small Mafs are interchangeable, the four large Mafs nearly so, and a hit does not say whether the partner subunit is another Maf, a CNC factor or a BACH repressor - which is the difference between activation and repression.

families.name: K50 homeodomain (OTX/PITX/CRX-type, TAATCC)
families.def: TAATCC/TAATCY specificity from lysine at homeodomain position 50. The true K50 set: OTX1/2, CRX, DMBX1, PITX1-3, GSC, GSC2. Paired-like factors that carry Q50 and read TAATTA are grouped with HD_Q50 instead, whatever their gene family.
families.short: A small group of homeodomains carries lysine instead of glutamine at position 50 of the domain, and that single substitution changes the two base pairs read 3' of the invariant TAAT core from TA to CC. The result is TAATCC, the bicoid-type site. In human the true K50 set is nine genes: OTX1, OTX2, CRX and DMBX1, PITX1, PITX2 and PITX3, and GSC and GSC2. They are tightly consistent - 34 motifs, all converging on TAATCC, with cooperative dimers on TAATCCGATTA - and unusually well supported in vitro. Paired-like factors that share their gene families but carry glutamine at position 50, such as RAX, VSX2, PHOX2B and NOBOX, read TAATTA and are covered by HD_Q50 instead.
families.long:
## The factors

The homeodomain is a 60-residue three-helix module whose recognition helix sits in the major groove while a flexible N-terminal arm reads the adjacent minor groove. Bicoid, the Drosophila anterior morphogen, is the founding member of the K50 class, defined by lysine at position 50 - the last residue of the recognition helix - and unique among homeodomains in also carrying arginine at position 54, which it needs for RNA binding.

In human the class is small and well defined: OTX1, OTX2, CRX and DMBX1 (the OTX group), PITX1, PITX2 and PITX3, and GSC and GSC2. These nine genes contribute 34 motifs across JASPAR, HOCOMOCO, CIS-BP and the footprint archetypes. The only other member is ANHX, a divergent homeobox gene that has alanine rather than lysine at position 50 and whose two reported motifs (TTGACAAG) are not K50 sites at all.

Membership here follows measured specificity, not gene family. Many proteins classified as paired-like alongside OTX, PITX and GSC - VSX1/2, RAX/RAX2, PHOX2A/2B, NOBOX, MIXL1, VENTX, PROP1, DRGX, BSX, OTP and SEBOX - carry glutamine at position 50 and their motifs are TAATTA-type; they are grouped with the Q50 homeodomains in HD_Q50. Expression of the K50 proteins is narrow and lineage-defining: CRX and OTX2 in photoreceptors and retina, OTX1/OTX2 in forebrain and eye, PITX1-3 in pituitary, anterior eye segment and hindlimb, GSC and GSC2 in craniofacial mesenchyme and mesendoderm, DMBX1 in midbrain.

## The motif

The consensus is TAATCC (equivalently GGATTA on the opposite strand). Every homeodomain recognizes the 5'-TAAT-3' core through a hydrogen bond from the invariant Asn51 to its second adenine plus minor-groove contacts from N-terminal arm arginines; residue 50 discriminates the two base pairs immediately 3' of it. Site selection with six different residues at position 50 gave six distinct specificities differing at exactly those positions, through water-mediated hydrogen bonds and van der Waals contacts; lysine contacts the C:G pairs that glutamine cannot. Swapping residue 50 in Bicoid converts it into an Antennapedia-class TAATTA binder; the reverse swap in Paired confers Bicoid specificity. Solution structures of the native Bicoid homeodomain on TAATCC and of PITX2 on DNA show the K50, N51 and R54 side chains remaining mobile within the interface, and the PITX2 structure rationalizes the homeodomain substitutions that cause Axenfeld-Rieger syndrome.

Only about six base pairs carry information, so monomeric models are short: all nine genes give 5-7 bp TAATCC/GGATTA matrices, and the family medoid is the footprint archetype AC0061 (PITX/OTX) at exactly TAATCC. This is a tight family: cohesion 0.90, data consensus exactly TAATCC, no member flagged as resembling another family.

The longer models are dimeric. Paired-like homeodomains bind cooperatively on palindromes whose half-sites are three base pairs apart (the P3 site, TAATNNNATTA), and residue 50 sets the central bases, so the K50 version is TAATCGGATTA or TAATCCGATTA. That is exactly what the OTX1, OTX2 and OTX archetype models show; the PITX1 and PITX3 models instead carry two GGATTA half-sites. Residue-level rules for cooperativity across the 36 human paired-like factors have recently been derived, and blindness-causing CRX homeodomain mutations have been shown to alter cooperative dimerization rather than monomeric affinity.

Within the family, individual paralogues are not separable: no matrix distinguishes OTX2 from CRX, or PITX1 from PITX2 from PITX3. K50 versus Q50 is the only specificity distinction that sequence supports.

## Where it acts

These sites concentrate in tissue-specific distal enhancers and in promoters of terminal differentiation genes. The best-mapped case is photoreceptors, where CRX occupies thousands of sites at rod and cone gene promoters and enhancers, typically with NRL and NR2E3 motifs nearby. TAATCC is common in absolute terms - roughly two million expected copies in 3.1 Gb at human base composition - so location and cell type do the discriminating, not the 6-mer. The dimeric TAATCCGATTA is about a thousand-fold rarer, with a few thousand expected copies, and is correspondingly more informative.

## Biology and disease

This small family carries a striking dominant disease load. CRX mutations cause cone-rod dystrophy and Leber congenital amaurosis; heterozygous OTX2 mutations cause microphthalmia and anophthalmia; PITX2 mutations cause Axenfeld-Rieger syndrome; PITX1 mutation causes asymmetric lower-limb malformation; GSC mutation causes SAMS syndrome (short stature, auditory canal atresia, mandibular hypoplasia and skeletal abnormalities). Many of these substitutions fall inside the homeodomain and alter DNA binding or dimerization directly, which is why the in vitro motifs and cooperativity rules have clinical relevance.

## Reading a hit

A TAATCC match is one of the better-behaved homeodomain calls, but it is still a class-level call: it says a K50 homeodomain could bind, not whether OTX2, CRX, PITX2 or GSC bound it, and in retina at least two of those are usually present. Evidence quality here is uniformly good - all 12 HOCOMOCO models have HT-SELEX or methyl-HT-SELEX support, none is ChIP-only, none of the 34 motifs is a cross-species transfer, and no member is flagged as belonging to a different family. Two things to watch. The ANHX entries read TTGACAAG and should not be scanned as K50 sites. And one CIS-BP CRX model carries only 2.3 bits of information, with consensus TAAT, so it will match almost any AT-rich sequence; prefer the JASPAR or HOCOMOCO CRX models. Finally, if your hit is TAATTA rather than TAATCC, you are looking at the Q50 family - which includes paired-like proteins whose names (RAX, VSX2, PHOX2B, NOBOX, PROP1) might otherwise lead you to expect a K50 site.
families.caveats: A TAATCC match identifies a K50-type homeodomain site, not a protein: OTX1/2, CRX, DMBX1, PITX1-3 and GSC/GSC2 share one motif. Expect roughly two million matches genome-wide, so condition on expression and accessibility; the dimeric TAATCCGATTA is about a thousand-fold rarer and far more informative. Evidence is unusually clean for a homeodomain family - all 12 HOCOMOCO models have in vitro SELEX support, none is ChIP-only, nothing is a cross-species transfer and nothing is flagged as belonging elsewhere. Two exceptions: the ANHX motifs (TTGACAAG) are not K50 sites, and one CIS-BP CRX model carries only 2.3 bits. A TAATTA hit belongs to HD_Q50, which holds the paired-like factors that carry Q50.

families.name: CREB / ATF (CRE)
families.def: Cyclic-AMP response element TGACGTCA and its half-site. CREB1, CREM, ATF1, ATF2, ATF4, ATF7, CREB5.
families.short: The CREB/ATF group contains the basic region-leucine zipper factors CREB1, CREM, ATF1, ATF2, ATF7, ATF4 and CREB5. They bind the cyclic-AMP response element, the eight-base palindrome TGACGTCA, and its five-base half-site TGACG. The element was defined in the somatostatin promoter as the sequence through which cAMP raises transcription, and CREB1 phosphorylated on Ser133 recruits the coactivators CBP and p300 to it. Unlike the closely related AP-1 site, the CRE carries a central CpG, so its occupancy is sensitive to DNA methylation, and CRE-containing promoters are concentrated in CpG islands. Genome-wide, CREB occupies a few thousand promoters with a profile that is similar across tissues. All members read the same palindrome, so a match identifies the group rather than a single factor.
families.long:
## The factors

Three subgroups share this element. The CREB subgroup - CREB1, CREM and ATF1 - carries a kinase-inducible domain; phosphorylation of CREB1 Ser133 by protein kinase A, calcium/calmodulin kinases and others creates the surface that binds the CBP and p300 KIX domain. CREM is expressed as many isoforms, including activators and the repressor ICER, and a testis-specific form required for spermiogenesis. The ATF2 subgroup - ATF2, ATF7 and CREB5 - is activated instead by the stress-responsive kinases JNK and p38. ATF4 is an outlier: it is regulated translationally, through an upstream open reading frame that is bypassed when eIF2-alpha is phosphorylated during the integrated stress response, and its preferred site is not the plain CRE. All are bZIP proteins, dimerizing through a leucine zipper and reading DNA with a basic region in the major groove. The group was defined as an "extensive family of leucine zipper proteins able to selectively form DNA-binding heterodimers", and cross-family dimers with Jun were reported soon afterwards, which is why the CREB/ATF and AP-1 families cannot be cleanly separated at the protein level either.

## The motif

The CRE is the 8 bp palindrome TGACGTCA: two TGAC half-sites related by a two-fold axis, one per subunit. The crystal structure of a CREB bZIP bound to the somatostatin CRE showed the basis for its selective dimerization and a divalent-cation-enhanced mode of DNA binding. Half-site CREs (TGACG, or CGTCA on the other strand) are functional and far more common in promoters than the full palindrome; they bind with lower affinity and with measurably different kinetics, which is one reason CREB occupancy and CREB-dependent induction are not the same thing. The feature that distinguishes the CRE from the AP-1 TRE is a single inserted base, giving a central CpG. That CpG is methylatable, and methylation of TGACGTCA abolishes CREB binding and cAMP-dependent activation; genome-wide CREB occupancy tracks both the presence of a consensus CRE and its methylation state. ATF4 is the exception within the family: its selected site is the C/EBP-ATF response element, read as TGATGCAAT or TTGCATCA, one CRE half joined to one C/EBP half. The ATF4 models here (JASPAR MA0833.3, HOCOMOCO ATF4 ChIP and HT-SELEX models) therefore sit closer to C/EBP than to CREB, and their label agreement with the rest of the family is low by construction rather than by error. CREB1, CREM, ATF1, ATF2, ATF7 and CREB5 are not distinguishable from sequence; JASPAR ATF7 MA0834.2 and the CIS-BP ATF7 model are 0.99 similar, and both are within 0.98 of CREB5 and ATF2 models.

## Where it acts

Unlike AP-1, this family is promoter- and CpG-island-biased. Serial analysis of chromatin occupancy in rat PC12 cells recovered 6,302 CREB loci, of which 40% lay within 2 kb of an annotated transcription start site, 49% within 1 kb of a CpG island and 72% within 1 kb of a candidate CRE. In human tissues CREB occupied roughly 4,000 promoter sites, with very similar profiles across tissues, yet only a small fraction of those genes responded to a cAMP agonist, because induction additionally requires CBP recruitment. Half-CRE sites often sit beside other promoter elements rather than in enhancer clusters. Named composite contexts include the CRE-TATA arrangement of the somatostatin promoter, tandem half-CREs in cAMP-inducible promoters, and the amino-acid response elements at which ATF4 acts on ATF3, TRIB3, ASNS and DDIT3.

## Biology and disease

This family is the main route from cAMP and calcium signaling to transcription: gluconeogenic and lipid programs in liver, circadian Per1 induction, activity-dependent transcription and long-term synaptic plasticity in neurons, and hormone-responsive programs in endocrine tissue. ICER provides negative feedback by competing for the same element without activating. ATF2 and ATF7 transmit stress-kinase signaling and have roles in DNA-damage responses. ATF4 is the effector arm of the integrated stress response: it raises amino-acid transporter and aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase expression during amino-acid limitation, and together with CHOP it increases protein synthesis during prolonged ER stress to the point of cell death. Loss-of-function phenotypes are generally mild for individual members and severe for combinations, the expected signature of a shared element.

## Reading a hit

A full TGACGTCA is a reasonably specific family call, but not a member call: CREB1, CREM, ATF1, ATF2, ATF7 and CREB5 give the same matrix. A half-site (TGACG) is much weaker evidence and occurs far too often to interpret alone. The CpG matters twice: the 8-mer is rarer than the AP-1 TRE partly because the genome is depleted of CpG, and a match in a methylated region may never be occupied, so pair the hit with methylation or accessibility data where you have it. Boundaries with siblings are real. TGACTCA without the central G is AP-1; TGACGTGG, or CCACGTCA read the other way, is ATF6/CREB3; TTACGTAA is PAR bZIP. If your match is the ATF4-style TGATGCAAT, it is a C/EBP-ATF composite and the C/EBP family is an equally good explanation. Seven of the 13 HOCOMOCO models here carry in vitro evidence, and four of those - ATF2, ATF7, CREB1 and CREM - are grade-A models combining ChIP with both HT-SELEX and methyl-SELEX, which is strong support that these proteins bind this sequence directly.
families.caveats: A full palindromic CRE is one of the better-supported motifs in this collection, with grade-A HOCOMOCO models backed by both ChIP and in vitro selection. What it cannot do is name a factor: six of the seven members are interchangeable at the sequence level, and Jun-family proteins bind the same palindrome, so a CRE hit is genuinely ambiguous between this family and AP-1. Treat the 5 bp half-site as a weak signal. Methylation makes matters worse in one direction and better in another: a methylated CRE is unlikely to be CREB-bound, but is a candidate C/EBP-alpha site. ATF4 models in this family are C/EBP-ATF composites and should not be read as ordinary CREs.

families.name: GATA
families.def: WGATAA. GATA1-6, TRPS1; composite GATA-E-box with TAL1.
families.short: GATA factors are zinc-finger transcription factors that bind the six-base core WGATAA (usually AGATAA or TGATAA) through a single C4-type zinc finger plus a basic tail. Humans have six canonical members, GATA1-6, in two expression groups: GATA1/2/3 in blood, lymphocytes and mammary epithelium, GATA4/5/6 in heart, gut and gonad. The atypical protein TRPS1 carries one GATA-type finger and binds the same core as a repressor. Sites are short and very common, and are often read in pairs or next to an E-box occupied by TAL1. GATA binding sites underlie globin gene switching, cardiac septation and T-helper-2 commitment, and the factors are mutated in congenital heart disease, HDR syndrome and breast cancer.
families.long:
## The factors

Six canonical human GATA proteins (GATA1-6) share a pair of C4-type zinc fingers. Only the
C-terminal finger, with its adjacent basic tail, is required for sequence-specific binding; the
N-terminal finger stabilizes binding to certain palindromic and double sites and is the docking
surface for the cofactors ZFPM1/ZFPM2 (FOG1/FOG2). GATA proteins bind DNA as monomers, not as
obligate dimers, although two molecules can occupy adjacent sites on the same or opposite faces
of the helix. Expression splits the family in two: GATA1 (erythroid, megakaryocytic, mast,
eosinophil), GATA2 (hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells, endothelium) and GATA3
(T lymphocytes, mammary luminal epithelium, kidney, parathyroid, inner ear) versus GATA4, GATA5
and GATA6 (heart, endoderm-derived gut, lung, liver, gonad, pancreas). TRPS1 is an outlier: it
has a single GATA-type finger, binds the same core, and represses rather than activates. ZGLP1
is annotated as GATA-like but its measured specificity in these databases (ATGATCGAT) is not the
GATA core, and it clusters here only weakly.

## The motif

The literature consensus is WGATAA, sometimes written (A/T)GATA(A/G) to include the less common
3' G. The NMR structure of the chicken GATA-1 finger-plus-tail bound to DNA showed that the core
module contacts GAT in the major groove while the basic C-terminal tail wraps into the minor
groove to read the 3' AA and the 5' W; this is why the invariant information sits on GATA and
falls off sharply outside it. Only about 6 bp carry real information, so a GATA PWM is one of the
least specific vertebrate models in routine use. Many database entries are written on the reverse
strand as TTATCT or CTTATCT, which is the same site; the data consensus here, AGATAAg, is simply
the forward-strand form of the same six-base core. Extended versions exist. Tandem sites in the
arrangement GATAA-N(n)-TTATC are common in real regulatory elements and give the double-GATA
archetype seen in footprint clustering. The GATA-E-box composite element places WGATAA 8-10 bp
from a CAGNTG E-box and is bound by the TAL1/E47/LMO2/LDB1/GATA1 pentameric complex; JASPAR
models this as a GATA1::TAL1 dimer motif. No experiment distinguishes GATA1 from GATA2 from
GATA6 by sequence: their in vitro and ChIP-derived models are effectively the same matrix.

## Where it acts

GATA sites are enhancer elements far more than promoter elements, and they are not associated
with CpG islands. Because WGATAA occurs roughly once every few kilobases by chance, the human
genome contains on the order of a million matches and only a small fraction are occupied in any
cell type. Occupancy is set by chromatin: GATA1 and GATA2 mark erythroid enhancers, GATA3 marks
luminal breast and Th2 enhancers, GATA4 and GATA6 mark cardiac and gut enhancers, and the same
sequence is invisible in the wrong lineage. GATA2 and GATA1 exchange at many of the same sites
during erythroid maturation, the so-called GATA switch. Frequent neighbors are the E-box of TAL1,
KLF1 CACCC boxes, RUNX1, SP1, FOXA1 and estrogen receptor (in breast), and NKX2-5, TBX5 and MEF2
(in heart). GATA3 and GATA4 both behave as chromatin-opening factors at a subset of their sites.

## Biology and disease

Gata1-null mouse embryonic stem cells arrest at the proerythroblast stage and die of apoptosis,
and a megakaryocyte-selective knockdown causes thrombocytopenia. In humans, GATA1 exon 2
mutations producing the short GATA1s isoform cause transient abnormal myelopoiesis and Down
syndrome-associated acute megakaryoblastic leukemia; other GATA1 mutations cause X-linked
dyserythropoietic anemia and thrombocytopenia. GATA2 haploinsufficiency causes MonoMAC syndrome
and familial MDS/AML. GATA3 is required for and sufficient to drive Th2 cytokine expression in
CD4 T cells; heterozygous mutations cause HDR syndrome (hypoparathyroidism, deafness, renal
dysplasia), and GATA3 is one of the most frequently mutated genes in luminal breast cancer.
GATA4 mutations cause septal defects and interact genetically with TBX5. TRPS1 loss causes
tricho-rhino-phalangeal syndrome; TRPS1 immunostaining is now used as a breast-carcinoma marker.

## Reading a hit

A WGATAA match tells you the family and nothing about the member. Treat any claim that a site is
"the GATA1 site" rather than "a GATA site" as an inference from expression or ChIP data, not from
sequence. Because the informative core is six bases, isolated matches in a random background are
expected and carry almost no evidence by themselves; a hit becomes interesting when it is
conserved, sits in open chromatin of a tissue that expresses a GATA factor, or is doubled or
paired with an E-box. Two specific confusions are worth knowing. AT-rich homeodomain sites
(TAAT-containing) and the reverse-complement TTATCT can score on loose GATA models, and vice
versa. And the CIS-BP human TRPS1 motif is not measured on human TRPS1: it is transferred from a
Drosophila protein at 63% DNA-binding-domain identity, so the model's fine structure should not
be read as TRPS1-specific even though TRPS1 genuinely binds GATA cores. HOCOMOCO GATA models
graded A are backed by both ChIP-seq and in vitro SELEX (evidence codes PSM), which is stronger
support than ChIP alone.
families.caveats: The core is only 6 bp, so chance matches are abundant and a single hit is weak evidence. All six canonical paralogues share one matrix; sequence cannot assign a member, and neither can ChIP-seq in a cell expressing several of them. Reverse-strand renderings (CTTATCT) and AT-rich homeodomain sites are the two commonest misreadings. The CIS-BP TRPS1 model is inferred from a Drosophila protein, and the HOCOMOCO ZGLP1 model does not match the GATA core despite ZGLP1's GATA-like domain annotation. Vierstra archetypes labelled GATA/TAL describe a composite element, not a claim that GATA and TAL1 motifs are separable.

families.name: RFX
families.def: X-box GTTRCC(A/T)3GGYAAC. RFX1-8.
families.short: RFX proteins recognize the X-box, a pseudo-palindrome built from two GTTRCC-like half-sites separated by zero to three bases. The DNA-binding domain is a 76-residue winged helix that reads bases with its beta-hairpin wing rather than with the usual recognition helix, and two domains bind one X-box cooperatively. Humans have eight members, RFX1-RFX8. RFX1-3 form homodimers and heterodimers and drive ciliary gene programs; RFX5 works in a complex with RFXAP and RFXANK to switch on MHC class II genes; RFX6 is restricted to pancreatic islet and enteroendocrine cells. The full 13-14 bp palindrome is one of the most information-rich motifs in vertebrate collections, which makes RFX hits unusually trustworthy.
families.long:
## The factors

The human RFX family has eight genes. All share a highly conserved 76-residue DNA-binding domain
(DBD); most also carry dimerization domains (B, C and DIM regions) that RFX1, RFX2 and RFX3 use
to form homodimers and heterodimers with each other. RFX1-3 are the ciliogenic branch and are
broadly expressed, with RFX2 and RFX3 concentrated in tissues that build motile cilia. RFX4 is
largely brain- and testis-restricted and produces isoforms lacking parts of the dimerization
region. RFX5 does not dimerize with other RFX proteins; it functions in the RFX (also called
RFXANK-RFXAP-RFX5) complex that, together with the coactivator CIITA, drives MHC class I and
class II transcription. RFX6 is restricted to pancreatic islet and gut enteroendocrine cells and
works downstream of NEUROG3. RFX7 is broadly expressed and acts downstream of p53. RFX8 is
poorly characterized in humans, and the CIS-BP human RFX8 entry is not a human measurement at
all: it is transferred from a louse (Pediculus humanus) protein at 55% DBD identity.

## The motif

The literature consensus, from the RFX1 crystal structure, is 5'-GTNRCC(N0-3)RGYAAC-3'. In
practice vertebrate RFX models converge on the tighter form GTTGCCATGGCAAC, which is what the
motif data in this family reports (GTTGCCATGG). The two forms are not in conflict: the databases
are dominated by high-affinity selection experiments that pick GTTGCC as the half-site and a
2-3 bp spacer, while the literature consensus is written loosely enough to cover the weaker,
variably spaced sites found in real promoters. The structural explanation is unusual. RFX1 is a
winged-helix (helix-turn-helix) protein, but instead of inserting a recognition helix into the
major groove it uses a beta-hairpin wing to make the base-specific contacts; two DBDs bind
cooperatively on opposite half-sites of a symmetrical X-box. This is why the informative positions
are the GTT/AAC ends and the CC/GG pair inside them, and why the central spacer bases are almost
free. Half-sites alone are real sites: RFX5, RFX6 and RFX7 models in these databases are
essentially single half-sites (GTTGC, GTTGCTA, GTTGCCAGG) with 7-12 bits, whereas RFX1-4 models
reach 20-23 bits. Paralogues within RFX1-4 are not separable by sequence. RFX5 and RFX7 can
sometimes be distinguished from RFX1-3 by the *absence* of a strong second half-site, but that is
an occupancy difference, not a specificity difference.

## Where it acts

X-boxes are promoter-proximal more often than not, typically within a few hundred bases of the
transcription start site of ciliary genes (IFT and BBS genes, dynein subunits, ciliary membrane
proteins) and of MHC class II genes, where the X box sits next to the X2 box and about 15-20 bp
from the Y box. The Y box is a CCAAT element bound by NF-Y, and RFX5 and NF-Y bind the class II
promoter cooperatively; this is the best-characterized composite element containing an X-box. In
motile ciliated epithelium RFX2 and RFX3 co-occupy promoters with FOXJ1, the forkhead factor that
specifies motile cilia, and in Drosophila the equivalent partnership is Rfx with Fd3F. RFX6 in
islets co-occupies enhancers with NEUROD1, PDX1 and NKX2-2. X-box counts are modest for a
vertebrate motif precisely because the full palindrome is long: genome-wide scans typically
recover a few thousand strong matches, most of them at ciliary and immune loci.

## Biology and disease

Loss of the RFX complex causes MHC class II deficiency (bare lymphocyte syndrome, complementation
groups C, D and E): RFX5, RFXAP or RFXANK mutations remove X-box binding, class II expression
fails, and patients present with combined immunodeficiency. The original RF-X activity was
defined by its absence in such patients' cells. RFX1-3 are the transcriptional core of
ciliogenesis across animals, and the X-box-driven ciliary program is old enough to predate
metazoans. Rfx3 mutant mice have laterality defects, hydrocephalus and impaired nodal cilia;
combined Rfx1/2/3 loss ablates motile ciliogenesis. RFX6 loss of function causes Mitchell-Riley
syndrome (neonatal diabetes with intestinal atresia); heterozygous truncating RFX6 variants cause
maturity-onset diabetes of the young with reduced penetrance, and Rfx6 is also required to
maintain adult beta-cell identity. RFX7 is recurrently mutated in lymphoid cancers and mediates
part of the p53 response, controlling genes including DDIT4 and PDCD4. An estrogen-receptor-RFX4
fusion has been reported in breast tumors.

## Reading a hit

A full 13-14 bp X-box match is strong evidence, and among vertebrate motifs it is one of the few
where a single high-scoring hit is worth acting on: the palindrome carries about 20 bits, so
chance occurrences in the human genome are rare. What a hit does not tell you is which RFX
protein. RFX1, RFX2, RFX3 and RFX4 are indistinguishable from sequence, and the practical
question is which of them is expressed in your cell type. Half-site-only matches (GTTGC plus a
purine) are a different matter: at 7-9 bits they occur by chance constantly, and they are the form
in which RFX5, RFX6 and RFX7 models are represented here, so hits on those models deserve much
more skepticism than hits on RFX1-4. Two provenance problems affect this family in CIS-BP: the
RFX8 motif comes from a louse protein at 55% DBD identity and the RFX6 motif from guinea pig at
71%, so neither is a human measurement. One HOCOMOCO RFX3 secondary model (evidence code S,
grade B) does not resemble an X-box at all and should not be used.
families.caveats: Trust full-palindrome X-box hits; treat half-site hits (GTTGC alone) as near-worthless on their own, because they carry under 9 bits. Nothing in the sequence separates RFX1, RFX2, RFX3 and RFX4, so assign a member from expression, not from the match. The RFX5 model reflects a three-protein complex, not RFX5 alone. In CIS-BP the human RFX8 motif is transferred from a louse protein (55% DBD identity) and the RFX6 motif from guinea pig (71%); neither was measured on the human protein. One HOCOMOCO RFX3 secondary model is not X-box-like and looks unreliable.

families.name: MYC / MAX / MXD
families.def: Canonical E-box CACGTG. MYC, MYCN, MAX, MXI1, MXD1-4, MNT, MGA, MLX, MLXIP, MLXIPL.
families.short: MYC, MYCN and their obligate partner MAX bind the canonical E-box CACGTG as bHLH-LZ heterodimers, and the same site is bound by MAX homodimers and by the MAX-associated repressors MXD1-4, MXI1, MNT and MGA, which recruit Sin3-HDAC complexes. The related MLX branch (MondoA, ChREBP) reads an E-box with T/A flanks. The motif is a 6-bp palindrome, two CAC half-sites read by a histidine-glutamate-arginine triad in each basic region. MYC-MAX occupancy is concentrated in CpG-island promoters of already-active genes, which is why MYC is central to the growth program and why it is one of the most frequently activated oncogenes in human cancer. No member of the network can be told from another by sequence alone.
families.long:
## The factors

This family is the MYC/MAX/MXD network: three MYC paralogues (MYC, MYCN, MYCL), their obligate partner MAX, the MAX-binding repressors MXD1-MXD4 (MAD1, MXI1, MAD3, MAD4), MNT and MGA, and the MAX-like hub MLX with its partners MLXIP (MondoA) and MLXIPL (ChREBP). All carry a basic helix-loop-helix leucine zipper (bHLH-LZ) domain: two helices joined by a loop, with the zipper extending helix 2 into a parallel coiled coil that sets dimer choice. MYC proteins do not homodimerize appreciably and reach DNA essentially only as MYC-MAX heterodimers; MAX homodimerizes and is the common partner for MXD proteins, MNT and MGA, which carry a Sin3-interaction domain and convert the same site from activation to repression. MGA is unusual in combining the bHLH-LZ with a separate T-box DNA-binding domain. MLX heterodimerizes with MondoA and ChREBP, which are nutrient sensors rather than growth effectors. MAX, MNT and MLX are broadly expressed; MYC tracks proliferation, MYCN is largely neural and embryonic, MYCL is restricted. The atlas assigns 30 motifs here (9 JASPAR, 12 HOCOMOCO, 8 CIS-BP, 1 Vierstra archetype) across nine symbols with motifs of their own: MAX, MYC, MYCN, MXI1, MXD4, MNT, MLX, MLXIP, MLXIPL. Family cohesion is 0.90 and the medoid is MAX (MA0058.4).

## The motif

The canonical site is the 6-bp palindrome CACGTG, one CAC half-site per monomer. The Max-DNA co-crystal showed how it is read: a histidine, a glutamate and an arginine in the basic region contact the CAC triplet, the glutamate hydrogen-bonding the cytosine and adenine and the arginine the guanine on the opposite strand, with the central CG contacted only through the backbone and water. The Myc-Max and Mad-Max structures showed the same contacts, so MYC-MAX, MAX-MAX and MXD-MAX read one motif. Single substitutions in the basic region can switch preference between CACGTG and neighbouring E-boxes, which is why closely related bHLH proteins differ far more in flanks than in core. Information beyond the core sits mainly at the two flanking positions: MYC and MYCN favour C and G immediately outside (CCACGTGG), whereas the MLX branch favours T and A (ATCACGTGAT), the same preference that defines USF and MITF/TFE. Flanking effects are largely a DNA-shape effect rather than direct base contact. The family also tolerates lower-affinity variants - CATGTG, CACGCG, CATGCG - and one HOCOMOCO MAX model is a CATGTG class-A-like variant while another is a CACGTG dimer with a 3-bp gap. ChREBP does not work through a bare E-box at all: its functional element, the carbohydrate response element, is two E-box-like half-sites separated by five base pairs. No member of this family is distinguishable from any other by sequence.

## Where it acts

MYC-MAX occupancy is overwhelmingly promoter-proximal, in CpG islands and nucleosome-depleted, already-active regions rather than distal enhancers; genome-wide mapping in B cells and in fibroblasts found thousands of bound regions strongly enriched for CpG islands, with only a fraction containing a canonical E-box. A 6-bp palindrome is expected roughly once every 4 kb, several hundred thousand times in a 3-Gb genome; CpG depletion in mammalian DNA lowers the real CACGTG count, but it remains orders of magnitude above the number of sites any single factor occupies. Occupancy therefore tracks promoter accessibility and MYC dose. As MYC levels rise it spreads from high-affinity promoters into weaker and more distal sites, the behaviour described as promoter invasion or, in the amplifier model, as general amplification of already-expressed genes.

## Biology and disease

MYC-MAX output is the growth program: ribosome biogenesis, nucleotide and glucose metabolism, and cell-cycle entry, opposed at the same sites by MXD-MAX, MNT-MAX and MGA-MAX repression. The MLX branch is metabolic: MondoA responds to glucose-6-phosphate, and ChREBP drives hepatic lipogenic genes in response to glucose. MYC is among the most frequently activated oncogenes in human cancer, by IGH translocation in Burkitt lymphoma, by amplification in many carcinomas, and by MYCN amplification in high-risk neuroblastoma. Whether high MYC changes which genes are expressed or mainly how much is a genuine and unsettled disagreement: amplification models argue for near-uniform scaling of active genes, while selective-regulation studies report distinct activated and repressed target sets and tumour-specific profiles.

## Reading a hit

A CACGTG match tells you the sequence is a canonical E-box, not that MYC binds it. USF1/2, MITF/TFE3/TFEB, CLOCK-BMAL1, HIF-ARNT, SREBP and BHLHE40/41 all read the same core; flanks shift the odds but do not resolve the factor. Within this family, MYC, MYCN, MAX, MXI1, MXD4 and MNT share one motif, so a hit identifies the network, not the member - which matters because activators and repressors are both in it. MYC ChIP-derived models are additionally biased toward active CpG-island promoters, and a large share of MYC peaks have no E-box at all, so ChIP-only models partly encode promoter context. Prefer in vitro-supported HOCOMOCO models (S/M evidence) when the question is "does this protein bind this sequence".
families.caveats: CACGTG is short, palindromic and shared across the bHLH class, so a single hit is weak evidence for anything specific. It cannot distinguish MYC from MAX, MXD, MNT or MLX, nor this family from USF, MITF/TFE, CLOCK-BMAL1, HIF-ARNT or SREBP. MYC ChIP-seq peaks are dominated by open, active CpG-island promoters and many contain no E-box, so ChIP-derived MYC models partly capture promoter context rather than intrinsic specificity. The CIS-BP MLXIP model is transferred from the mouse protein at 82% DNA-binding-domain identity, and one secondary HOCOMOCO MYCN model (aCGCGCgc) is not an E-box at all. Treat a hit as 'canonical E-box' and require expression, chromatin and direct binding data to name a factor.

families.name: NFAT
families.def: GGAAA core; NFATC1-4 (Rel-homology) and NFAT5/TonEBP.
aka: nuclear factor of activated T cells
families.short: NFAT sites are read by five proteins with a Rel-homology DNA-binding domain: the calcineurin-regulated NFATC1, NFATC2, NFATC3 and NFATC4, plus the structurally distinct, calcium-independent NFAT5 (TonEBP). Unlike NF-kB, the calcineurin-dependent NFATs bind as monomers to a short GGAAA core, usually written TGGAAA and only about six informative bases long. Because that is too little information to specify a site on its own, NFATs typically work in composite elements, most famously the NFAT-AP1 element of the interleukin-2 promoter, where NFAT and a Fos-Jun dimer touch each other on adjacent DNA. NFAT activity is controlled by dephosphorylation and nuclear import, which is why cyclosporin A and tacrolimus, which inhibit calcineurin, are immunosuppressive.
families.long:
## The factors

Five human proteins carry an NFAT DNA-binding domain. NFATC1 (NFAT2), NFATC2 (NFAT1), NFATC3 (NFAT4) and NFATC4 (NFAT3) share a Rel-homology region related to that of NF-kB, preceded by a long regulatory domain packed with serine-rich motifs and SP boxes. In a resting cell that domain is heavily phosphorylated and the protein is cytoplasmic; a sustained rise in cytosolic calcium activates the phosphatase calcineurin, which dephosphorylates it and exposes a nuclear localisation signal. Nuclear export kinases such as GSK3, CK1 and DYRK reverse this, so NFAT shuttles continuously and its nuclear concentration tracks calcium in near-real time. NFATC1 and NFATC2 dominate in lymphocytes, NFATC3 in thymocytes, NFATC4 in heart, skeletal muscle and brain. NFAT5 (TonEBP) is the outlier: it keeps the Rel-homology fold but lacks the calcineurin-docking regulatory domain, is activated by hypertonicity rather than calcium, and binds DNA as an obligate homodimer that completely encircles the double helix. That structural work also made the family's relationship to NF-kB explicit, since DNA-bound NFAT5 adopts an NF-kB-like arrangement.

## The motif

The core is GGAAA, normally written with its 5' T as TGGAAA, and the databases converge on a very short model: the representative in vitro-supported HOCOMOCO entry is ATGGAAAAT, of whose nine positions about six carry real information. The Rel-homology domain contacts the GGAA bases through basic residues in the equivalent of NF-kB's L1 loop, but a monomer covers only one half-site's worth of DNA, so total specificity is low - TGGAAA occurs roughly every 2 kb in random sequence. Two features add length in practice. First, many NFAT models in these databases are two half-sites in opposed orientation (for example TTTCCATGGAAA, or TTTCCNNTAACGGAAAA), reflecting genuine NFAT dimers on pseudo-palindromic, kB-like sites; the HIV-1 LTR tandem kB element is the structural example. Second, the classic arrangement is the NFAT-AP1 composite element of the interleukin-2 distal antigen-receptor response element, where NFAT and Fos-Jun bind adjacent sites and form a continuous protein-DNA interface across 15 bp. That partnership leaves a visible mark on the motif collections: the ChIP-derived NFATC1 and NFATC2 models here read TGGAAAAANTGAGTCA - the NFAT core spliced to a canonical AP-1 site, which is a property of the element, not of the protein. NFAT5 differs slightly, preferring a TonE-like TGGAAANNYNY, but not enough to separate it from NFATC1-4 by score. Within NFATC1-4 there is no usable discrimination at all: family cohesion is 0.87 and several members' models are effectively identical.

## Where it acts

NFAT sites are enhancer elements far more often than promoter elements, and they are not CpG-island features. Occupancy is strongly cell-type restricted because it depends both on calcium signalling and on chromatin a lineage factor has already opened; in T cells the relevant regions are co-occupied by AP-1, and frequently by RUNX1, ETS1, GATA3 or TBX21 depending on the subset. Composite elements with recognised names include the interleukin-2 ARRE-2 (NFAT-AP1) and the tandem kB/NFAT element of the HIV-1 long terminal repeat, which NFAT and NF-kB can each occupy. Cooperation with AP-1 is not optional for much of the programme: NFAT mutants that cannot recruit Fos and Jun activate a different, largely non-overlapping set of genes.

## Biology and disease

The calcineurin-NFAT axis is the main transcriptional output of antigen-receptor signalling, driving interleukin-2, interleukin-4, interferon-gamma, CD40LG and FASLG in T cells, and contributing to the anergy programme when NFAT acts without AP-1. Beyond immunity, NFATC1 is required for osteoclast differentiation downstream of RANK and for heart valve development, and NFATC3 and NFATC4 contribute to cardiac hypertrophy. The pathway is a first-line drug target: cyclosporin A and tacrolimus block calcineurin and are standard immunosuppressants in transplantation, and their renal and neurological toxicity reflects how broadly the pathway is used. NFAT5-null mice show that the lymphoid microenvironment is osmotically stressful, with impaired lymphocyte function and renal medullary defects, and NFAT5 drives osmolyte-transporter genes under hypertonic conditions.

## Reading a hit

A bare TGGAAA match is weak evidence. With six informative positions the site occurs hundreds of thousands of times in the human genome, so one match carries essentially no information unless supported by clustering, conservation, or an adjacent partner site. Look for composites: a TGGAAA within about 15 bp of a TGASTCA is far more convincing than either alone, and tandem or inverted GGAAA repeats indicate the dimeric mode. A hit cannot distinguish NFATC1 from NFATC2, NFATC3 or NFATC4, and only marginally separates NFAT5, so report it as NFAT-family. Check the evidence code before trusting a model: HOCOMOCO entries with S or M in the fourth field come from HT-SELEX or methyl-HT-SELEX and are statements about the protein, whereas the ChIP-only NFATC1 and NFATC2 models here are demonstrably contaminated by the composite element's AP-1 site - scan with those and you are scoring AP-1 as much as NFAT. Note also that the Vierstra archetype AC0682 is labelled NFATC/ZNF because unrelated zinc-finger motifs clustered with it, not because those factors share a specificity.
families.caveats: This is a short, low-information motif and that dominates everything else. Six informative bases make chance matches overwhelmingly more common than real sites, so an isolated TGGAAA should not be reported as an NFAT site; require a composite (usually AP-1 within about 15 bp), a tandem or inverted pair, or independent occupancy data. No model separates NFATC1-4, and NFAT5 only weakly, so a hit is family-level. Several ChIP-derived NFATC1 and NFATC2 models in these databases include the AP-1 TGAGTCA alongside the NFAT core: that is the partner's motif riding along, and it inflates apparent specificity. Finally, occupancy requires calcium signalling, so matches in an unstimulated cell are mostly inactive.

families.name: Divergent forkhead sites (FOXP dimeric / FHL)
families.def: Forkhead factors whose preferred site is not the canonical RYAAAYA: FOXP1-4 dimeric TGTTTAC repeats, and the alternate FHL/GACGC site used by FOXN1/N4 and bispecifically by FOXN2/N3, FOXJ2/J3.
families.short: This entry collects the forkhead factors whose preferred site is not the ordinary RYAAAYA element. Two things are going on. FOXN1 and FOXN4 read a completely unrelated five-base sequence, GACGC, called the forkhead-like or FHL motif, using the same recognition helix in a shifted register; FOXN2, FOXN3, FOXJ2 and FOXJ3 are bispecific and bind both FHL and canonical sites. Separately, the FOXP proteins (FOXP1-4) are the only forkheads that can form a domain-swapped dimer, and their highest-information models are a head-to-head pair of forkhead half-sites rather than a single one. The factors matter clinically: FOXN1 loss causes human athymic immunodeficiency, FOXP2 a speech disorder, and FOXP3 the autoimmune syndrome IPEX.
families.long:
## The factors

Seven of the human forkhead proteins sit here. FOXN1 is restricted to thymic epithelium and skin
keratinocytes; FOXN4 to retinal and spinal neural progenitors; FOXN2, FOXN3, FOXJ2 and FOXJ3 are
broadly expressed. FOXP1, FOXP2 and FOXP4 are expressed in brain, lung, heart and lymphocytes,
and FOXP3 almost only in regulatory T cells. All carry the same ~100-residue winged-helix domain
as the rest of the family - three alpha-helices on a small beta-sheet, with wing 1 and wing 2
gripping the backbone - so nothing about the fold predicts their unusual specificity. What
distinguishes the FOXP subfamily structurally is a single substitution: a proline conserved in
other FOX proteins is an alanine in FOXP1-4, which allows the domain to swap helices with a
second copy of itself. In the FOXP2 and FOXP3 crystal structures the swapped dimer is real, and
in the FOXP3 ternary complex with NFAT1 on the interleukin-2 promoter it bridges two separate
DNA duplexes rather than two half-sites on one. IPEX-causing FOXP3 mutations map either to the
DNA-binding surface or to this dimer interface, and interface mutants bind DNA normally but
cannot suppress T cell activation.

## The motif

There is no single consensus for this family, which is why one is not given. The FHL site is
GACGC, five bases with no resemblance to RYAAAYA. The FOXN1 co-crystal structure at 1.6 A shows
why the same protein can read either: the recognition helix sits in the major groove in both
cases, but the FKH and FHL sequences are contacted in two distinct modes with partially
different registers, using a mixture of direct and water-mediated hydrogen bonds, and a single
alternative side-chain rotamer in the recognition helix is a major determinant of which mode is
used. The FoxN3 structures make the same point from the other side: FoxN3 adopts essentially one
conformation on both sites and uses the same amino acids to touch different bases, while the DNA
shape differs between the two complexes. Bispecificity of this kind has arisen repeatedly and
independently in forkhead evolution and is generally not explained by changes in the known
specificity-determining residues. The FOXP side of the family looks different again. Most FOXP
models here are ordinary canonical sites (JASPAR FOXP1, FOXP2, FOXP3, FOXP4 all GTAAACA;
HOCOMOCO FOXP1 TGTTTACT), but the highest-information models, CIS-BP FOXP3 (25.6 bits) and
Vierstra AC0285 (24.8 bits), are ATTTGTCATACAAAT: two RYAAAYA half-sites in their ACAAAT flavor,
facing each other, with a three-base spacer. Whether that arrangement is bound by the domain-
swapped dimer or by two independent monomers is not settled by the available structures, which
show the swapped dimer holding two different DNA molecules.

## Where it acts

Because GACGC is only five bases, it is expected several million times in the genome and carries
almost no positional information on its own; FOXN1 needs its C-terminal region for high-affinity
binding, and its affinity drops on DNA containing 5-methylcytosine, so methylation state and
flanking sequence matter more here than for canonical forkhead sites. FOXN1 acts at thymic
epithelial enhancers controlling the genes that make the thymus permissive for T cell
development, and at hair keratin genes in skin. FOXP1 and FOXP2 occupy large numbers of distal
sites in brain and lymphoid cells, often with co-repressors of the NuRD and CtBP families rather
than with a named composite element; FOXP3 works in a multiprotein complex on T cell enhancers
together with NFAT, RUNX1 and ETS factors, which is how the IL2 promoter site was solved. JASPAR
contains a CAP-SELEX composite, FOXJ2::ELF1, in which most of the information is the ETS GGAA
core.

## Biology and disease

FOXN1 null mice and rats are the classical nude strains: no thymus, no hair. Human FOXN1
mutations produce the same picture - congenital alopecia, nail dystrophy and severe T cell
deficiency - and the human nude phenotype was the first clinical description of this. FOXP2 was
identified through a family with a severe developmental speech and language disorder segregating
with a forkhead-domain mutation. FOXP3 mutations cause IPEX (immune dysregulation,
polyendocrinopathy, enteropathy, X-linked), and FOXP3 is the lineage-defining factor of
regulatory T cells. FOXP1 haploinsufficiency causes intellectual disability with autistic
features, and FOXP1 is recurrently translocated and overexpressed in diffuse large B-cell
lymphoma and MALT lymphoma. FOXN3 and FOXJ3 have weaker phenotypes; FOXN4 is required for
retinal amacrine and horizontal cell production.

## Reading a hit

A GACGC match alone means very little: five bases, no degeneracy assumed, and no way to tell
FOXN1 from FOXN4 or from a bispecific FOXN2/FOXN3 or FOXJ2/FOXJ3. Use it only in combination
with expression evidence or with a longer model that includes the flanks. A canonical RYAAAYA
match cannot be assigned to this family at all, since FOXP1-4, FOXJ2, FOXJ3, FOXN2 and FOXN3 all
also read the ordinary site and are indistinguishable there from the 40-odd other forkheads. The
dimeric ATTTGTCATACAAAT model is specific enough to be worth something, but it appears in only
two of the 29 models here and is labelled FOXP3 in one database and simply "FOXP" in the other.
HOCOMOCO contains no FOXN model at all; the two CIS-BP FOXN entries (FOXN1, 3.3 bits; FOXN4, 5.2
bits) are inferred from mouse proteins at 99% and 95% DNA-binding-domain identity. Treat
FOXJ2::ELF1 as an ETS motif: its nearest neighbors across all four databases are ETV-family
motifs, not forkhead ones.
families.caveats: Moderate confidence in the family as a concept, low confidence in member assignment. The FHL site GACGC is too short to be informative alone and is not distinguishable between FOXN1, FOXN4 and the bispecific FOXN2/FOXN3, FOXJ2/FOXJ3 proteins. Most FOXP and FOXJ models in these databases are ordinary RYAAAYA sites, so a hit on them says "forkhead", not "divergent forkhead". Only two models capture the FOXP head-to-head arrangement. The FOXN1 and FOXN4 CIS-BP models are inferred from mouse orthologs, and HOCOMOCO has no FOXN entry. The JASPAR FOXJ2::ELF1 composite is dominated by its ETS half and its nearest neighbors are ETS motifs.

families.name: GLI
families.def: GACCACCCA. GLI1-3, GLI4, GLIS1-3, ZIC-adjacent sites.
families.short: GLI factors are five-fingered C2H2 zinc-finger proteins that read the nine-base site GACCACCCA and form the transcriptional output of the Hedgehog pathway. Humans have three canonical members: GLI1, an activator that is itself a Hedgehog target gene, and GLI2 and GLI3, which are made as full-length activators but are partially degraded into N-terminal repressors when Hedgehog signaling is off. The related GLIS1, GLIS2 and GLIS3 proteins read a close variant, GACCCCCCAC. Binding is monomeric and the informative bases are concentrated at the 3' end of the site, which fingers four and five contact directly. GLI sites control limb and neural-tube patterning, and pathway mutations cause polydactyly syndromes, basal cell carcinoma and SHH-subgroup medulloblastoma.
families.long:
## The factors

Three canonical human GLI proteins, GLI1, GLI2 and GLI3, are the vertebrate counterparts of
Drosophila Cubitus interruptus. Each carries five tandem C2H2 zinc fingers and binds DNA as a
monomer. GLI2 and GLI3 are bifunctional: an N-terminal repressor domain and a C-terminal
activation domain flank the finger array, and limited proteolysis removes the activation domain to
leave a repressor. GLI1 lacks the N-terminal repressor region and is a dedicated activator; because
GLI1 transcription is itself induced by Hedgehog signaling, GLI1 mRNA is widely used as a pathway
readout. GLI2 and GLI3 are broadly expressed during development, whereas GLI1 accumulates only
where the pathway is active.

The GLIS subfamily, GLIS1, GLIS2 and GLIS3, is the nearest relative: Kruppel-like proteins with
five fingers whose DNA-binding domains are close enough to GLI that their motifs cluster together,
but whose expression is largely non-overlapping (GLIS3 in thyroid, pancreatic islets and kidney,
GLIS2 in kidney, GLIS1 in a restricted set of tissues and in oocytes). A fourth entry, GLI4
(ZNF767P), is annotated as a family member but the matrices assigned to it in these databases do
not resemble a GLI site; treat it separately.

## The motif

The consensus GACCACCCA was defined by selecting genomic fragments bound by recombinant GLI: the
protein protected 23-24 bases at each site, and all recovered sites contained the same nine-base
core. The crystal structure of the five GLI fingers on a high-affinity site explains the shape of
the information content. Finger one makes no DNA contact; fingers two through five wrap into the
major groove without the strictly periodic geometry of Zif268; and fingers four and five make
extensive base contacts across a conserved nine-base-pair stretch whose conformation is
intermediate between B- and A-form DNA. The consequence is that the 3' half of the site
(reverse-strand TGGGTGGTC) carries most of the specificity while the 5' flank is tolerant.

Systematic affinity measurements of every single substitution show a wide dynamic range, and
reporter assays with natural promoters show that many low-affinity variants still drive strong
activation at moderate GLI concentrations. So "non-consensus" GLI sites are functional, and a
strict consensus search under-counts real elements. The GLIS paralogues prefer GACCCCCCAC, with the
central ACC replaced by CCC; the databases keep GLI and GLIS as separate matrices, but their
cross-similarity is high enough that only strong matches can be assigned to one subfamily. The data
consensus here, GACCACCCACgdcG, is the same core with a weakly informative 3' extension.

## Where it acts

GLI binding is mostly at distal enhancers rather than core promoters, and GLI sites are not a
CpG-island feature. ChIP of GLI activators in Hedgehog-responsive mouse neural tissue recovers on
the order of a thousand high-confidence regions, enriched at known pathway components (Ptch1, Gli1,
Hhip) and at patterning genes (Foxa2, Nkx2-2), with the motif recovered de novo. Because the
informative core is nine bases with degenerate flanks, exact matches occur tens of thousands of
times in the human genome and the great majority are never occupied. Occupancy tracks pathway
activity and chromatin: the same sequence is silent in tissue where GLI2 and GLI3 are not
stabilized. Frequent neighbors in Hedgehog-responsive enhancers include SOX2, FOXA2 and NKX
factors, and ZIC proteins, which bind an overlapping sequence and can physically associate with GLI
zinc fingers.

## Biology and disease

Hedgehog ligand binding to PTCH1 relieves inhibition of SMO, which blocks the phosphorylation of
GLI2 and GLI3 by PKA, GSK3 and CK1 and thereby blocks their processing. In the unstimulated state
GLI3 is converted into a truncated repressor, GLI3R; in the developing limb this produces a graded
anterior-to-posterior distribution of repressor that patterns the digits. SUFU sequesters GLI
proteins and opposes the pathway.

Gli2-null mice lack a floor plate and show reduced Shh responses; Gli1-null mice are viable and
only reveal defects in combination with a Gli2 mutation, consistent with GLI2 being the principal
activator and GLI1 an amplifier. Truncating GLI3 mutations cause Greig cephalopolysyndactyly
syndrome, while frameshifts in the middle third of the gene, which leave a repressor-like product,
cause Pallister-Hall syndrome. GLI1 was originally cloned as an amplified, highly expressed gene in
a human glioma, and Hedgehog-driven tumors (basal cell carcinoma, SHH-subgroup medulloblastoma)
signal through GLI even when the initiating lesion is in PTCH1 or SMO. On the GLIS side, biallelic
GLIS3 loss causes neonatal diabetes with congenital hypothyroidism, GLIS2 (NPHP7) loss causes
nephronophthisis, and GLIS1 improves the efficiency of somatic-cell reprogramming.

## Reading a hit

A GACCACCCA match identifies the GLI/GLIS class and nothing finer. GLI1, GLI2 and GLI3 have
effectively the same matrix, so no sequence argument distinguishes them; assignment to a member
comes from expression or ChIP data. More importantly, a hit does not tell you the sign of the
output, because GLI3R binds the same site as GLI2 full-length activator. With nine informative
bases the site is common enough to occur by chance in any few-kilobase window, so an isolated match
is weak evidence; conservation, open chromatin in a Hedgehog-responsive tissue, and proximity to
other pathway targets all help. Conversely, the functional importance of low-affinity variants
means absence of a consensus match does not exclude GLI regulation. In HOCOMOCO, the GLI2 and GLI3
models carry in vitro support (HT-SELEX and methyl-SELEX, grade A), whereas the GLI1 model is
ChIP-only at grade C; the GLI4 entries are ChIP-only and do not look like a GLI site at all.
families.caveats: A hit tells you "GLI/GLIS", never which paralogue and never whether the factor present is an activator or the GLI3 repressor. The nine-base core occurs frequently by chance, so isolated matches carry little weight without conservation or Hedgehog-responsive chromatin. GLI and GLIS matrices differ at only one or two central positions, so weak matches cannot be assigned to a subfamily. Low-affinity, non-consensus sites are demonstrably functional, so consensus searching both over-calls inert sites and misses real ones. The GLI4/ZNF767P matrices in these databases are ChIP-derived and unlike the GLI site; the Vierstra archetype carrying that motif is named GLI but groups poorly with the rest of the family.

families.name: PRDM
families.def: PR/SET-domain zinc fingers. PRDM1/BLIMP1 (AAAG(T/C)GAAAG), PRDM4-6, PRDM9 (recombination hotspots), PRDM10/13/14/15/16.
families.short: PRDM proteins are zinc-finger transcription factors defined by an N-terminal PR domain, a variant of the SET methyltransferase fold, followed by a tandem array of C2H2 zinc fingers that does the DNA binding. The family is heterogeneous and does not share one motif: each member's finger array reads its own sequence, and those sequences are unrelated to one another. The best-characterized members are PRDM1/BLIMP1, which binds an interferon-regulatory-factor-like AAAGTGAAAG site and drives plasma-cell differentiation; PRDM9, whose rapidly evolving finger array selects meiotic recombination hotspots and underlies a mouse hybrid-sterility phenotype; PRDM14, in naive pluripotency; and PRDM16, in brown adipocyte and craniofacial development. A hit labelled PRDM should be interpreted per member, never as a family-level call.
families.long:
## The factors

The PRDM proteins take their name from the PR domain, a diverged SET domain of about 130 residues,
followed by a variable number of C2H2 zinc fingers. Humans have roughly 19 PRDM genes. This family
groups the ones for which a motif has actually been measured: PRDM1, PRDM4, PRDM5, PRDM6, PRDM9,
PRDM10, PRDM13, PRDM14, PRDM15 and PRDM16. MECOM (historically PRDM3) is kept as a separate family
here because its two zinc-finger clusters behave differently from a single array.

Only some PR domains are catalytically active. PRDM9 is a genuine histone H3 lysine-4
trimethyltransferase, first described in mouse as Meisetz, and that activity is required for meiotic
prophase. For most other members the PR domain has no demonstrated methyltransferase activity and acts
as a protein-interaction surface; PRDM1/BLIMP1, for instance, works by recruiting histone deacetylase
and methyltransferase cofactors rather than by modifying histones itself. Expression is mostly
restricted. PRDM1 appears in plasma cells, effector T cells, keratinocytes, primordial germ cells and
placenta; PRDM9 essentially only in meiotic germ cells; PRDM14 in embryonic stem cells and germ cells;
PRDM16 in brown and beige adipocytes, craniofacial mesenchyme and hematopoietic stem cells. Few PRDMs
are broadly expressed, so the plausible member behind a hit is usually decided by cell type rather than
by sequence.

## The motif

There is no family consensus, and the data in this atlas show that plainly: member motifs range from the
GTTTCAAG core of PRDM4, through the IRF-like AAAGTGAAAG of PRDM1, to GGTCTCTAAC for PRDM14 and G-rich
models for PRDM9 and PRDM16. Cohesion across the family is low, about 0.5, and the medoid motif
(ACTTTCACT, the PRDM1 site on the reverse strand) is simply the most central member, not a shared
element.

PRDM1/BLIMP1 is the clearest case. Its zinc fingers read an approximately 10-bp site built on a GAAAG
core; the optimal selected sequence is close to AAAGTGAAAG, which overlaps a subset of
interferon-stimulated response elements, so BLIMP1 and IRF1/IRF2 compete for the same DNA with
comparable affinities. In vivo, several motif variants are needed to capture BLIMP1 occupancy, and
binding is sensitive to CpG methylation. The reverse-complement rendering ACTTTCACTTT is the same site
and is what several database entries display.

PRDM9 is different in kind. Its DNA-binding module is a minisatellite-encoded tandem array of roughly a
dozen C2H2 fingers, one of the fastest-evolving coding sequences in mammals, polymorphic within humans
and between mouse strains. Human hotspots are enriched for a degenerate 13-mer, CCNCCNTNNCCNC, which
the common human A allele recognizes; crystal structures of the human PRDM9 finger array on DNA explain
the base contacts, and the C allele reads a different sequence. Because the array differs between
alleles, no single PRDM9 matrix is correct for all individuals, and the JASPAR and CIS-BP PRDM9 models
are approximations of one allele's preference at best.

## Where it acts

PRDM1 sites sit in promoters of genes it represses, including IRF-dependent immune programs, in both
CpG-poor and CpG-island promoters, with the methylation-sensitive variants biased to the latter. PRDM9
sites are the defining feature of meiotic double-strand-break hotspots: tens of thousands of them,
typically 1-2 kb wide, mostly outside promoters, and in mouse directed away from functional elements
such as transcription start sites. PRDM14 and PRDM15 sites are concentrated at enhancers and promoters
of pluripotency and signaling genes in stem cells. PRDM16 sites are found at brown-fat enhancers, where
PRDM16 acts less as an autonomous sequence reader than as a partner of adipogenic factors, which matters
for interpreting its ChIP-derived motif.

## Biology and disease

PRDM1 knockout blocks plasma-cell formation and specification of primordial germ cells; in humans PRDM1
is inactivated by mutation and deletion in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, where it behaves as a tumor
suppressor. PRDM9-null mice are sterile with arrested meiosis; PRDM9 allele identity changes hotspot
usage in human families; and one PRDM9 allele is the mouse hybrid-sterility gene, with sterility
reversible by swapping the finger array. PRDM14 loss destabilizes naive pluripotency and PRDM15 loss
does the same through WNT and MAPK-ERK targets. PRDM16 loss impairs brown-fat identity and causes
cardiomyopathy in 1p36 deletion syndrome; PRDM5 loss-of-function causes brittle cornea syndrome; PRDM6
variants cause nonsyndromic patent ductus arteriosus. PRDM10 and PRDM16 also appear as fusion partners
in soft-tissue tumors and leukemia.

## Reading a hit

Treat a PRDM hit as a hit on one named member. Sequence cannot tell you which PRDM bound, because the
members do not share a motif and the family label spans unrelated sites. Check which member the
underlying matrix is labelled with, then whether that member is expressed in your cell type. For PRDM1
the site is short and IRF-like, so an IRF or ISRE explanation is at least as likely as BLIMP1 unless
BLIMP1 is present. For PRDM9 a match is meaningless outside meiotic germ cells, and allele-dependent
even there. Several PRDM entries rest on ChIP-only evidence, where the motif may belong to a partner:
the HOCOMOCO PRDM13 model matches a SNAI-type CAGGTG E-box and the PRDM16 model resembles an EBF site,
and both are flagged as inconsistent with their labels by their nearest neighbours across databases.
families.caveats: This family has no shared motif, so a family-level hit means little; only the member-specific matrix matters. Cohesion across members is about 0.5, and two entries contradict their labels: the HOCOMOCO PRDM13 model (GCAGGTGG) is a SNAI-type E-box and the PRDM16 model (TCCCCTGGGA) resembles an EBF site, both from ChIP-only data where an indirect or partner motif is the simpler explanation. PRDM1 evidence is strong and includes in vitro selection, but the site overlaps IRF elements, so IRF1, IRF2 or an ISRE is a competing interpretation. PRDM9 matrices describe one allele of a polymorphic finger array and are interpretable only in meiotic germ cells. Short G-rich PRDM models match frequently by chance.
