families.name: MYB / MYB-like
families.def: MBS YAACKG. MYB, MYBL1, MYBL2; plus Myb/SANT archetypes (SNAPC4, MYPOP, TERF1/2 telobox).
families.short: MYB factors bind the Myb binding site (MBS), a six-base element written YAACKG, through two or three imperfect ~52-residue repeats that each fold into a helix-turn-helix-like unit. Humans have three true MYB proteins: MYB (c-Myb), MYBL1 (A-Myb) and MYBL2 (B-Myb). Only repeats R2 and R3 are required for sequence-specific binding, and their recognition helices sit side by side in one major groove. MYB proteins control hematopoietic progenitor expansion, spermatogenesis and, for MYBL2, mitotic gene expression through the MuvB complex. MYB is duplicated in T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia and fused to NFIB in adenoid cystic carcinoma. This family key also collects Myb/SANT-fold archetypes whose proteins are not MYB factors and do not bind the MBS, which is the main source of confusion here.
families.long:
## The factors

Three human genes encode true MYB transcription factors: MYB (c-Myb), MYBL1 (A-Myb) and MYBL2
(B-Myb); HOCOMOCO labels them MYB, MYBA and MYBB, and the Vierstra archetypes use the group
name MYBL. Their DNA-binding domain is built from three imperfect repeats of about 52 residues,
R1, R2 and R3, each containing three regularly spaced tryptophans and folding into a
helix-turn-helix-related unit. R1 is dispensable: R2 and R3 alone give specific binding, which is
why plant and fungal homologues are usually R2R3 proteins. MYB is expressed in immature
hematopoietic cells, colonic crypt epithelium and some neural progenitors; MYBL1 is highest in
testis and germinal-center B cells; MYBL2 is a cell-cycle gene, rising in S phase and peaking at
G2/M. This atlas key is deliberately broader than the three MYB proteins, because the Myb/SANT
fold is reused by proteins that are not MYB factors. In the current data those extras are DMTF1
(DMP1, a cyclin D-binding Myb-like protein), MYPOP (a Myb-related protein that partners profilin)
and TTF1 (the RNA polymerase I transcription termination factor, not the thyroid factor NKX2-1,
which is unfortunately also called TTF-1). TERF1 and TERF2, whose telobox is a Myb-like repeat,
are held in a separate TELOBOX family here; SNAPC4, which uses Myb repeats to bind the snRNA
proximal sequence element, has no motif in these databases. The SANT domain itself, found in
chromatin remodelers and corepressors, has the Myb fold but is thought to read histone tails
rather than DNA sequence.

## The motif

The literature consensus for the MBS is YAACKG, six bases, usually quoted as PyAAC(G/T)G. The
invariant part is AAC followed by G or T then G; the identity comes from the recognition helix of
R3 inserting into the major groove with R2 packed alongside, so the two repeats read one
continuous site and the cavity in R2 rearranges on binding. Database renderings differ mainly by
strand and by doubling. JASPAR MYB (MA0100.4) and the corresponding CIS-BP model give CAACTG,
which is YAACKG with Y=C and K=T; the HOCOMOCO ChIP model GGCAGTTG is the same site read on the
other strand. The data consensus for the family as a whole, CCGTTA, is the reverse complement of
TAACGG, again the same core. In vitro selection on MYBL1 and MYBL2 returns longer, near-palindromic
models such as AACCGTTAACGG and CCGTTAAACSG: these are two MBS half-sites in inverted orientation
and reflect how the isolated domains bind selected DNA, not a different specificity. Within the
three MYB proteins nothing is separable by sequence. The non-MYB members are separable, and they
are not MBS models: DMTF1's high-quality integrative model is CCCGGATG, MYPOP's is GCGCAA, and
TTF1's is the rDNA Sal box terminator, recognizable by its internal GACCAG. Their nearest
neighbours across the four databases fall outside this family, and the family's cohesion (0.72
over 22 motifs) is lower than for a single-specificity family for exactly that reason.

## Where it acts

MYB sites are short and occur in both promoters and enhancers. In hematopoietic cells c-Myb
occupies thousands of sites and cooperates with CEBP factors, RUNX1, GATA2 and the coactivators
CBP/p300; classic targets include MYC, KIT, CCNB1 and, in T cells, TCR genes. MYBL2 behaves
differently: it is recruited to mitotic promoters mainly as a subunit of the MYB-MuvB (MMB)
complex, which hands over from the repressive DREAM complex at G1/S, and MuvB's own sequence
anchor is the CHR element read by LIN54, not the MBS. Consequently much of the MYBL2 signal in
chromatin immunoprecipitation sits on CHR-containing promoters where the underlying sequence is
not a Myb site at all. TTF1 sites are confined to the rDNA repeat, where the Sal box terminates
Pol I transcription, so its motif is genomically almost absent outside the rDNA and its
nucleolar-organizer copies.

## Biology and disease

Mice lacking c-Myb die around embryonic day 15 with a failure of fetal hepatic hematopoiesis, the
sharpest demonstration that MYB is needed for progenitor expansion rather than for lineage
identity. Mybl1-null male mice are sterile with a meiotic arrest, and Mybl2 loss is lethal at the
blastocyst stage. In cancer, MYB is more often amplified, translocated or driven by a new enhancer
than mutated: tandem duplication of MYB occurs in T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia, and a
recurrent MYB-NFIB fusion defines most adenoid cystic carcinomas of salivary gland and breast.
MYBL2 overexpression is a component of proliferation signatures in many tumors and is largely a
readout of cell-cycle activity.

## Reading a hit

A YAACKG match is six informative bases and will occur by chance roughly every few hundred base
pairs on either strand, so a single hit is close to meaningless without other evidence. The three
MYB proteins cannot be separated from sequence, so a hit means "a MYB-family site" at best, and
expression context is what narrows it: MYB in immature hematopoietic cells, MYBL1 in testis and
germinal centers, MYBL2 in cycling cells. The bigger hazard in this key is the label. Several
members are Myb/SANT-fold proteins that do not bind the MBS, and a match scored against the
DMTF1, MYPOP or TTF1 models is a match to an unrelated sequence that happens to share the family
key. For MYBL2, treat ChIP-derived enrichment with care: recruitment through MuvB to CHR
elements means a B-Myb peak often marks a LIN54 site rather than a Myb site.
families.caveats: Two problems compound here. First, the MBS is six bases, so chance matches are abundant and the three MYB paralogues are indistinguishable by sequence. Second, this key is a fold class, not a single specificity: DMTF1 (CCCGGATG), MYPOP (GCGCAA) and TTF1 (the rDNA Sal box) are Myb/SANT-fold proteins whose motifs are unrelated to the MBS, and the CIS-BP MYPOP model is transferred from mouse. The family cohesion of 0.72 reflects this mixture. For MYBL2, ChIP-derived signal is frequently recruitment through the MuvB complex onto LIN54's CHR element rather than direct MBS binding, so a B-Myb peak is not evidence of a Myb site.

families.name: NFE2 / NRF / BACH (ARE)
families.def: Antioxidant/electrophile response element TGACTCAGC. NFE2, NFE2L1/L2/L3, BACH1, BACH2.
families.short: This family covers the cap-n-collar (CNC) basic region-leucine zipper activators NFE2, NFE2L1 (NRF1) and NFE2L2 (NRF2) together with the BTB-bZIP repressors BACH1 and BACH2. None of them binds DNA alone: each must heterodimerize with a small Maf protein (MAFF, MAFG or MAFK). The resulting element is the antioxidant or electrophile response element, TGACTCAGCA, an AP-1-like TGAC half-site read by the CNC or BACH subunit joined to a GC-extended half read by the small Maf. It is therefore a one-sided version of the Maf recognition element. NRF2 drives the cytoprotective gene battery and is constitutively activated by KEAP1 loss in several cancers; NFE2 is required for platelet formation; BACH1 is a heme sensor and BACH2 a lymphocyte regulator. Members cannot be distinguished from sequence.
families.long:
## The factors

The CNC subfamily takes its name from the Drosophila cap-n-collar protein and comprises NFE2 (p45), NFE2L1 (NRF1), NFE2L2 (NRF2) and NFE2L3 (NRF3). The BTB-bZIP proteins BACH1 and BACH2 read the same element but carry a BTB domain and act as repressors. A defining property of both sets is that they cannot bind DNA as monomers or as homodimers: every functional complex is a heterodimer with one of the small Maf proteins, which supply half of the DNA contact. Regulation differs by member. NRF2 is continuously ubiquitinated through a KEAP1-CUL3 complex and degraded; electrophiles and oxidants modify reactive KEAP1 cysteines, NRF2 escapes degradation and accumulates in the nucleus. BACH1 is a heme sensor: heme binding releases Bach1 from MAREs and promotes its nuclear export, handing the same sites to CNC activators. Expression is uneven. NFE2 is restricted to erythroid and megakaryocytic cells, NFE2L1 and NFE2L2 are broad, BACH1 is broad, and BACH2 is concentrated in B and T lymphocytes. NFE2L3 has no motif model in any of the four source collections and so appears nowhere in this atlas. One naming hazard: NFE2L1 is routinely called NRF1, but an unrelated factor, nuclear respiratory factor 1 (gene symbol NRF1), shares that abbreviation and binds a GC-rich palindrome unrelated to this element.

## The motif

The element was originally defined functionally, as the core required for antioxidant-inducible transcription of rat glutathione S-transferase Ya and NAD(P)H:quinone reductase: 5'-(A/G)TGACNNNGC-3'. In the sequences that actually occur, the variable middle is almost always TCA, giving the 10 or 11 base consensus TGACTCAGCA, sometimes written with the 5-prime A as ATGACTCAGCA. Read the other way round it is TGCTGAGTCAT, the consensus derived from the 21 models collected here: the same element on the opposite strand, with models differing in how much flank they retain. The small Maf subunit reads the GC extension through Arg57 and Asn61 of the Maf basic region, the same residues that read both flanks of a full MARE. The CNC subunit reads the other half, and the residue that makes the difference is Ala502 of NRF2, which sits where Maf proteins have a tyrosine; replacing it with tyrosine makes NRF2-MafG bind like a MafG homodimer and shifts its target gene set. So the ARE is a MARE with one flank removed, and a single residue in the CNC partner explains why. Common variants include an AT-rich 3-prime extension (GCATTT or GCANTTT) present in many small-Maf-partnered models, and a truncated TGACTCAT form that is simply the AP-1 TRE and carries no Maf-side information at all. JASPAR BACH1 MA1633.2 and the CIS-BP NFE2L1 model are of this second kind, which is why their nearest neighbours fall outside the family. No member is distinguishable: NFE2, NFE2L1, NFE2L2, BACH1 and BACH2 give one motif, and the small Maf partner is likewise unidentifiable.

## Where it acts

AREs occur at promoters and enhancers of the cytoprotective battery: NQO1, GCLC and GCLM, HMOX1, TXN, GPX2, SLC7A11, glutathione S-transferases, and proteasome subunit genes. ChIP-seq of Nrf2 in Keap1-null mouse embryonic fibroblasts, integrated with expression data, defined 645 basal and 654 inducible direct targets with 244 in common, so the responsive set is a few hundred genes rather than thousands. The erythroid NF-E2 site of the beta-globin HS2 enhancer is a tandem ARE and MARE. The same elements are occupied competitively: a BACH-small Maf dimer keeps them repressed until heme or an electrophile replaces the repressor with an activator, so occupancy and output are decoupled. Co-occurrence with AP-1 sites is common because the core is shared.

## Biology and disease

NRF2 is the main transcriptional response to electrophiles and oxidants, and the pathway protects against chemical carcinogenesis, emphysema and inflammatory injury in mouse models. The same pathway is subverted in tumours: KEAP1 mutations and NFE2L2 mutations in the KEAP1-binding Neh2 domain constitutively activate NRF2 in non-small-cell lung cancer and elsewhere, where it supports growth and confers chemotherapy and radiation resistance. NFE2/p45-null mice fail to produce platelets despite intact thrombopoietin signaling, and somatic NFE2 mutations occur in myeloproliferative neoplasms. BACH2 haploinsufficiency causes a human immunodeficiency with defective B and T cell function, a phenotype linked to loss of a super-enhancer-driven expression level.

## Reading a hit

Every model in this family is, by construction, a heterodimer motif: the CNC and BACH proteins cannot bind DNA alone, so roughly half the information in any NRF2 or BACH1 matrix belongs to a small Maf. A ChIP-derived NRF2 motif is therefore not evidence that NRF2 contacts those GC bases. The practical test is the 3-prime GC. TGACTCAGC is an ARE; TGACTCA alone is an AP-1 TRE and cannot be assigned here; GC on both sides is a full MARE and belongs to MAF. Because the families are nested this way, a 7 or 8 base match is not separable among AP-1, NFE2/BACH and MAF. Two entries in this collection carry motifs that do not belong: CIS-BP M08184, labelled BACH1, is a CACGTG E-box whose nearest neighbours are USF motifs, and JASPAR BACH2 MA1470.2 is a long CRE-like AANCATGACGTCATGNTT that matches outside the family. Six of the eight HOCOMOCO models here are ChIP-only (evidence P, grade B); only the NFE2 and BACH2 models add in vitro support. Finally, a hit says nothing about direction: the same element is bound by BACH1 or BACH2 to repress and by NRF2 or NFE2 to activate, and sequence cannot tell you which is present.
families.caveats: Read every matrix in this family as a heterodimer motif, because the CNC and BACH proteins do not bind DNA without a small Maf; half of the information is the partner's. The family is nested between two siblings: remove the 3-prime GC and you have an AP-1 TRE, add GC on the 5-prime side and you have a full MARE, so short matches cannot be assigned. Member identity is unavailable, and so is direction, since activators (NFE2, NRF1, NRF2) and repressors (BACH1, BACH2) compete for the same sites. Two entries here carry motifs that belong elsewhere, one an E-box and one a long CRE. NFE2L3 has no model in any source database, and NFE2L1 shares the abbreviation NRF1 with an unrelated factor.

families.name: Steroid receptors (GR/MR/PR/AR)
families.def: Inverted repeat of AGAACA (ARE/GRE) spaced by 3 bp. NR3C1/GR, NR3C2/MR, PGR, AR.
families.short: The steroid receptors - glucocorticoid receptor (GR/NR3C1), mineralocorticoid receptor (MR/NR3C2), progesterone receptor (PGR) and androgen receptor (AR) - are hormone-activated transcription factors that bind DNA as homodimers on a 15 bp inverted repeat: two copies of the hexamer AGAACA facing each other across a 3 bp spacer, written AGAACAnnnTGTTCT. All four receptors read essentially the same element, so a match identifies the steroid-receptor group and not a particular receptor. Which receptor occupies a site in a given cell is decided by hormone availability, receptor expression, pioneer factors such as FOXA1 and pre-existing chromatin accessibility, not by sequence. These elements carry the transcriptional response to cortisol, aldosterone, progesterone and androgens, and they are the DNA end of drugs from dexamethasone to the antiandrogens used in prostate cancer.
families.long:
## The factors

Four receptors share this element: GR (NR3C1), MR (NR3C2), PGR and AR, the oxosteroid branch of the nuclear receptor superfamily. Each has an N-terminal activation region, a C4 double-zinc-finger DNA-binding domain (DBD), a flexible hinge and a C-terminal ligand-binding domain that binds cortisol, aldosterone, progesterone or dihydrotestosterone respectively. DNA binding is by a homodimer: the first zinc finger contributes the recognition helix that enters the major groove of one half-site, and a loop in the second zinc finger (the D-box) forms the interface between the two subunits. GR and MR are expressed in most tissues; PGR is largely restricted to uterus, breast, ovary and parts of the brain, AR to prostate, seminal vesicle, muscle, skin and bone. The four collections here contribute 21 models, labelled AR, NR3C1, NR3C2 and PGR.

## The motif

The response element is an inverted repeat of a hexamer with a 3 bp spacer, abbreviated IR3: AGAACA nnn TGTTCT, 15 bp and almost exactly palindromic. Information is concentrated in the two hexamers; the three spacer bases are weakly constrained but not free, and selection in a receptor-competitive setting showed that spacer and flanking positions are chosen asymmetrically and contribute to receptor preference rather than to raw affinity (Nelson et al. 1999). The crystal structure of the GR DBD dimer on DNA established how the recognition helix reads the half-site (Luisi et al. 1991). Which hexamer a receptor reads is set by three residues in the first zinc finger: swapping them converts GR specificity to that of the estrogen receptor, which reads AGGTCA instead, while five residues in the stem of the second finger set the tolerated half-site spacing (Umesono and Evans 1989).

The models here have a systematically degenerate 5' half-site. The GR and MR matrices from JASPAR and HOCOMOCO read AG(A/T)ACAnnnTGTTCC, often written in the literature as GGTACAnnnTGTTCT, which is why the family's data consensus is AGWACAtnaTGTtCc rather than the symmetrical form quoted above; both describe the same element, one from selected high-affinity sites and one from averaged genomic occupancy. AR has one partly private variant: some natural androgen-selective elements are direct rather than inverted repeats of the hexamer with a 3 bp gap (ADR3), and the AR DBD binds them head-to-head using an extended dimer interface (Shaffer et al. 2004; Denayer et al. 2010). In practice this discriminates weakly. Single base changes inside the hexamer alter GR conformation and activity, not only affinity, so the element behaves as a sequence-specific allosteric ligand (Meijsing et al. 2009; Weikum et al. 2017). Several HOCOMOCO models here are single half-sites (TGTTC, AGAACA, GWACA) carrying 4-8 bits; alone they have almost no specificity.

## Where it acts

Steroid receptor sites are overwhelmingly distal enhancers rather than promoters, and are strongly cell-type restricted. Up to 95% of de novo GR binding after hormone falls in chromatin that was already accessible, so the cistrome is largely pre-specified by cell identity, with sequence a secondary contribution (John et al. 2011). AR occupancy depends on tissue-specific pioneer factors: FOXA1 both opens AR sites and masks others, and its depletion redistributes AR binding wholesale (Sahu et al. 2011; Pihlajamaa et al. 2014). Composite arrangements are common - a GRE next to AP-1, NF-kB, STAT5 or FOX sites, and in liver next to CEBP and HNF4 motifs. GR also represses genes from a distinct negative element (nGRE) that is not an IR3 and is bound by two non-dimerizing monomers (Hudson et al. 2013), and can act without touching DNA by tethering to AP-1 and NF-kB.

## Biology and disease

These elements carry the metabolic and anti-inflammatory programs of cortisol, salt and water handling by aldosterone, the uterine and mammary response to progesterone, and male sexual development and prostate growth. GR-null mice die perinatally from failure of lung maturation. Loss-of-function NR3C1 variants cause generalized glucocorticoid resistance; NR3C2 loss causes pseudohypoaldosteronism type 1, and an NR3C2 gain-of-function variant causes early-onset hypertension. AR loss-of-function causes androgen insensitivity syndrome, and CAG-repeat expansion in AR causes spinal and bulbar muscular atrophy. In cancer, AR amplification, point mutation and the AR-V7 splice variant drive castration-resistant prostate cancer, PGR status is a standard breast cancer biomarker, and glucocorticoids acting through GR remain part of lymphoid leukemia regimens.

## Reading a hit

A match says a steroid receptor could bind, not which one. The full-length GR, MR, PGR and AR matrices in this collection mostly sit within 0.89-1.00 of each other, so sequence cannot assign the receptor; ligand, receptor expression, cell type and cofactors can. Because roughly 10-12 of the 15 positions carry information, exact consensus IR3s are rare (order 10^2 per haploid genome) but sites within one or two mismatches number in the tens of thousands, far more than are occupied in any one cell type, so intersect hits with accessibility data. Check the evidence code on HOCOMOCO models: in vitro entries (S, M, SM) support direct binding, while ChIP-only entries (P) can absorb neighbouring signal - ANDR.H14CORE.2.P.B here is a single half-ARE fused to an AT-rich element and matches other families better than its own. A GR or AR ChIP peak with no IR3 is not necessarily a failure: tethering to AP-1 and NF-kB is a documented mode of action.
families.caveats: Trust a good IR3 hit as evidence for the family, not for a receptor: the GR, MR, PGR and AR matrices here are near-identical, and even AR's direct-repeat preference separates them only weakly. Because the element tolerates mismatches, near-consensus sites occur tens of thousands of times genome-wide while only a fraction are ever bound, so a scan hit without accessibility, hormone treatment or ChIP support is weak evidence. Half-site-only models (TGTTC, AGAACA) should not be scanned genome-wide. ChIP-derived models can include a partner's signal, and these receptors also regulate genes by tethering to other factors, so motif presence is neither necessary nor sufficient.

families.name: COUP-TF (NR2F)
families.def: DR1 AGGTCAAAGGTCA. NR2F1/2/6.
aka: chicken ovalbumin upstream promoter transcription factor
families.short: COUP-TFI (NR2F1), COUP-TFII (NR2F2) and EAR2 (NR2F6) are orphan nuclear receptors that bind DNA as homodimers, most often on a DR1: two AGGTCA half-sites in the same orientation separated by one base pair. Their distinguishing property is not a private consensus but promiscuity - the same dimer accommodates direct repeats with several spacings, plus inverted and everted arrangements of the same hexamer - which is how COUP-TFs compete with vitamin D, thyroid hormone and retinoic acid receptors for shared elements and repress them. The three paralogues share one motif and are also not separable from RXR homodimers, HNF4/TR2-TR4 or ERR sites. COUP-TFII specifies venous identity and is required for angiogenesis; NR2F1 mutations cause an optic atrophy and intellectual disability syndrome.
families.long:
## The factors

Three paralogues: NR2F1 (COUP-TFI, EAR3), NR2F2 (COUP-TFII, ARP1) and NR2F6 (EAR2). COUP-TF was purified as a factor binding upstream of the chicken ovalbumin gene and cloned as a member of the steroid receptor superfamily (Wang et al. 1989); NR2F1 and NR2F2 are among the most conserved nuclear receptors known (Lin et al. 2011). Each has a C4 double-zinc-finger DNA-binding domain (DBD) with a C-terminal extension and a ligand-binding domain; they bind as homodimers and can heterodimerize with RXR. The ligand-free COUP-TFII ligand-binding domain, solved at 1.48 A, is in an autorepressed conformation, with helix alpha10 folded into the ligand pocket and the activation function-2 helix occupying the coactivator groove; retinoic acid at concentrations above physiological levels releases this, so COUP-TFII is ligand-regulatable but has no established endogenous ligand (Kruse et al. 2008). NR2F1 is expressed in brain, eye, inner ear and neural crest derivatives, NR2F2 in mesenchyme, venous endothelium and reproductive tract, NR2F6 broadly including lymphocytes. Twenty-one models fall in this family (JASPAR 7, HOCOMOCO 8, CIS-BP 3, Vierstra 3).

## The motif

The core arrangement is a DR1: AGGTCA-n-AGGTCA, 13 bp, seen in the data as AGGTCAAAGGTCA (JASPAR NR2F1 MA1537.2, HOCOMOCO COT1.H14CORE.1.PSM.A). The family's data consensus is the shorter AaAGGTCA, an extended single half-site, because many models here are half-sites with a 5' A or AA rather than full dimeric elements.

A counting convention trips people up constantly and is worth stating plainly. The original characterisation described COUP-TF elements as direct repeats of GGTCA with a 2 bp spacing; modern usage calls the identical element a DR1, a direct repeat of AGGTCA with a 1 bp spacing. The two descriptions differ only in whether the half-site is defined as a 5-mer or a 6-mer. Compare like with like before concluding that two sources disagree.

The real signature of this family is tolerance of geometry. Aligning natural COUP-TF elements showed that besides the predominant direct repeat, functional sites vary in both orientation and spacing of the GGTCA motif; the functional DNA-binding form is a dimer needing two half-sites, and the dimer undergoes a substantial structural adaptation to accommodate these variants. The consequence is that COUP-TF can occupy the response elements of the vitamin D, thyroid hormone and retinoic acid receptors and down-regulate their hormonal induction (Cooney et al. 1992). The models in this collection reproduce that range: DR1 (NR2F1 MA1537.2), DR2 (NR2F6 MA0728.1, gAGGTCAAaAGGTCA), IR1 (NR2F1 MA1538.1 and NR2F6 MA1539.1, aAGGTCAnTGACCTt), IR2 (NR2F6.H14CORE.3.SM.B, AAGGTCAatGacC) and bare half-sites (AGGTCA, AAGGTCA).

Nothing here separates the paralogues: NR2F1, NR2F2 and NR2F6 models are 0.96-0.99 similar to each other. Worse, they are barely separable from other families - members' best match outside this family runs 0.89-0.98, and two of the three Vierstra archetypes assigned here are labelled NR2F/RXRG and NR2F/RXRA because COUP-TF and RXR footprints cluster together. Protein-binding microarrays did detect a polarity preference within the DR1 for COUP-TFII, as for HNF4A and RXRA homodimers (Fang et al. 2012), but that is a quantitative preference, not a discriminator you can apply to a single hit.

## Where it acts

Mostly distal enhancers in mesenchyme and endothelium, with NR2F2 marking venous rather than arterial endothelium. Functionally many COUP-TF sites are repressive, and the mechanism documented in detail is competition: occupying a DR element that another receptor needs (Cooney et al. 1992). COUP-TF motifs co-occur with SOX, FOX and GATA sites in neural and cardiovascular enhancers, and because the element is a plain DR1 they overlap physically with RXR-heterodimer and HNF4 elements in the same regions.

## Biology and disease

Nr2f2-null mouse embryos die around E10.5 with defective angiogenesis and heart development (Pereira et al. 1999). Deleting COUP-TFII in endothelium makes veins acquire arterial characteristics, including neuropilin 1 and Notch pathway markers, while ectopic expression fuses veins and arteries - COUP-TFII maintains vein identity by repressing Notch signalling (You et al. 2005). In tumour models COUP-TFII promotes growth and metastasis by supporting tumour angiogenesis (Qin et al. 2010). In humans, heterozygous NR2F1 point mutations and deletions cause Bosch-Boonstra-Schaaf optic atrophy syndrome, combining optic atrophy or hypoplasia with developmental delay and intellectual disability (Bosch et al. 2014), and rare NR2F2 variants cause congenital heart defects, notably atrioventricular septal defects (Al Turki et al. 2014).

## Reading a hit

A DR1 hit licenses very little. It does not name the paralogue, and it does not even name the family: RXR homodimers, PPAR:RXR, HNF4A and the TR2/TR4 heterodimer all use DR1, and their matrices in this atlas sit within 0.89-0.98 of the models here. Report the geometry you actually see - spacing and orientation - and state the counting convention you used, because a DR1 under one convention is a 2 bp-spaced repeat under another. Given about 11 informative positions in a 13 bp element, near-consensus DR1s occur tens of thousands of times per haploid genome, far more than any COUP-TF cistrome. Half-site-only models (eight of the twenty-one here read AGGTCA, gGGTCa, AAGGTCA or AaAGGTCA) should not be scanned genome-wide. Evidence codes help a little: NR2F1 and NR2F6 have grade A HOCOMOCO models with combined ChIP, HT-SELEX and methyl-SELEX support (PSM), so direct binding is not in doubt; what a hit cannot tell you is which NR2F protein, or whether a different DR1-binding receptor was there instead.
families.caveats: This is one of the least discriminating motifs in the atlas. NR2F1, NR2F2 and NR2F6 models are 0.96-0.99 similar to each other, and their best matches outside the family run 0.89-0.98 - RXR homodimers, PPAR:RXR, HNF4A and TR2/TR4 all bind the same DR1. Two of the three Vierstra archetypes here are named NR2F/RXRG and NR2F/RXRA for that reason. Eight of the twenty-one models are single half-sites. COUP-TF also binds DR, IR and everted arrangements with several spacings, so geometry constrains the candidates less than it does for most nuclear receptor families. Treat a hit as evidence that some DR1-binding nuclear receptor could bind, and use expression and chromatin data to go further.

families.name: NFI (CTF/NF-1)
families.def: Palindromic TTGGC(N5)GCCAA. NFIA, NFIB, NFIC, NFIX.
families.short: Nuclear factor I proteins bind a 15-bp palindrome, TTGGC followed by five variable bases and GCCAA. Four human genes, NFIA, NFIB, NFIC and NFIX, encode DNA-binding domains that are about 85% identical, so they bind as homodimers or heterodimers in any combination and cannot be told apart from sequence. The domain adopts a SMAD MH1-like fold with a bound zinc ion, which is why the family is classified with SMAD rather than with any CCAAT-box factor. The full palindrome is highly informative, but NFI also occupies single TTGGC half-sites. NFI factors keep stem cell populations in glia, retina, skin and muscle on track, and are mutated in human overgrowth and brain malformation syndromes.
families.long:
## The factors

Four human genes, NFIA, NFIB, NFIC and NFIX, each produce several splice isoforms. The
N-terminal region carries both the DNA-binding and the dimerization functions; the C-terminal
regions differ and carry the transactivation or repression activity. Because the DNA-binding
domains are roughly 85% identical, all six pairwise heterodimers form in addition to the four
homodimers, and the effective factor in a cell is usually a mixture. A crystal and solution study
of NFI-X bound to its consensus palindrome showed a MH1-like fold with a structural Zn2+ site, an
obligate dimeric assembly, and the base contacts that set specificity; the authors present it as
prototypic for the whole family given the DBD identity. This places NFI in the same structural
class as the SMADs, which is why TFClass and the archetype labels used here call the group
"SMAD/NF-1". Expression is broad but graded: NFIA and NFIB dominate in developing CNS and glia,
NFIX in neural stem cells, muscle and hematopoiesis, NFIC in tooth and kidney. NFI was originally
purified as a host factor required for adenovirus type 2 DNA replication, and independently as
"CTF" (CCAAT box transcription factor) and as the chicken "TGGCA protein"; all three are the same
family.

## The motif

The consensus is the 15-bp palindrome TTGGC(N5)GCCAA, equivalently written TGGC(N5)GCCA. Each
monomer reads one TTGGC half-site, so the information sits almost entirely on the two half-sites;
the five central bases are a spacer and contribute little. Spacing is the strict part. Early
binding studies varying the gap showed that NFI tolerates very little change in spacer length,
which is what you expect from a rigid dimer whose two DNA-contacting elements are fixed distances
apart; the JASPAR and HOCOMOCO full-site models accordingly run 14-17 columns with the spacer
degenerate. Full-site models reach 15-26 bits, among the most informative in these collections.
Half-site models also exist and are legitimate: NFI binds single TTGGC/TGCCAA sites with lower
affinity, and several database entries for all four paralogues are 5-7 bp half-sites carrying only
8-12 bits. No paralogue is distinguishable from any other by sequence. The name "CCAAT box
transcription factor" is a historical trap: the NFI half-site GCCAA contains the letters of a
CCAAT box read on one strand, and NFI was long listed among CCAAT-binding proteins, but NFI and
NF-Y are unrelated proteins with different folds and different optimal sites. If a scan returns
both, they are separate hypotheses, not confirmations of each other.

## Where it acts

NFI sites are found at promoters and at enhancers, and NFI proteins are enriched at distal
regulatory elements in stem and progenitor populations. NFI binding is closely tied to chromatin
accessibility: in skin stem cells NFI factors occupy super-enhancers and provide access for
lineage factors while suppressing alternative fates, and in retinal progenitors NFI factors
control mitotic exit and late-born cell specification. NFI also binds nucleosomal DNA more
readily than many factors, consistent with a role early in opening elements. Recurring partners
include FOXA1 in prostate, the glucocorticoid and progesterone receptors at the MMTV promoter
(where NFI and the receptor compete for overlapping DNA), SOX factors in glia, and MYOD in
muscle. Because the full palindrome is long, genome-wide scans recover a manageable number of
strong matches, but half-site matches are effectively everywhere.

## Biology and disease

Mouse knockouts give distinct phenotypes despite the shared motif: Nfia loss causes corpus
callosum agenesis and hydrocephalus, Nfib loss impairs lung maturation and forebrain
development, Nfic loss blocks tooth root formation, and Nfix loss affects brain, muscle and
hematopoiesis. The human syndromes mirror them. NFIA haploinsufficiency causes a CNS malformation
syndrome with corpus callosum hypoplasia, macrocephaly and urinary tract defects. NFIX variants
cause two different disorders depending on whether the transcript escapes nonsense-mediated
decay: missense or deletion alleles affecting the DNA-binding/dimerization domain cause Malan
(Sotos-like) overgrowth syndrome, while alleles producing stable truncated protein cause
Marshall-Smith syndrome. NFIB is amplified and drives progression and metastasis in small cell
lung cancer, and NFIB works with CARM1 in that setting; NFIB fusions also occur in adenoid cystic
carcinoma via MYB-NFIB translocation.

## Reading a hit

A full TTGGC(N5)GCCAA match is good evidence that some NFI dimer can bind, and it is specific
enough that chance matches are uncommon. It is no evidence at all about which paralogue, and
because heterodimers are the rule, "which paralogue" may not even be a well-posed question in a
cell expressing three of them; assign from expression data. Half-site hits are a different
proposition: TTGGC or TGCCAA alone carries under 12 bits and will occur by chance many times in
any window you look at, so half-site models should be treated as weak. Two confusions are worth
flagging. First, the GCCAA half-site overlaps the letters of a CCAAT box, and NFI's old name CTF
invites the false inference that an NFI hit is an NF-Y hit; the true NF-Y site is CCAAT read in a
different context and the proteins are unrelated. Second, NFI's MH1-like fold means archetype and
class labels place it with SMAD, which can look like a mislabeling but is structurally correct.
HOCOMOCO NFI models graded A generally rest on both ChIP-seq and in vitro selection (evidence
codes PS or PSM), so the full-site matrices here are well supported.
families.caveats: The four paralogues share one matrix and freely heterodimerize, so a hit identifies NFI, never NFIA versus NFIB versus NFIC versus NFIX. Full-palindrome matches are trustworthy; half-site models (TTGGC or GCCAA alone, under 12 bits) are not, and several database entries for this family are half-sites. Spacer length matters more than spacer sequence, so a match with a shifted gap is probably not a site. Do not equate the GCCAA half-site with the CCAAT box of NF-Y despite NFI's historical name CTF; the two proteins are unrelated. The SMAD/NF-1 class label reflects the shared MH1-like fold and is not an error.

families.name: MBD and CxxC readers
families.def: Methyl-CpG and unmethylated-CpG readers. MECP2, MBD1-3, CXXC1/4/5, KDM2A/B, TET1/3, DNMT1, KMT2A/B.
families.short: This family puts two opposite kinds of reader in one place. MBD proteins - MECP2, MBD1, MBD3 - bind CpG that is methylated. ZF-CxxC proteins - CXXC1/CFP1, CXXC4, CXXC5, KDM2A, KDM2B, FBXL19, TET1, TET3, DNMT1, KMT2A, KMT2B - bind CpG that is not. Neither group has a sequence-specific site in any useful sense. The single most important thing to know about this page is that its motifs are essentially measurements of CpG density: the family consensus is literally CG, eight of the twenty-one models carry two to four bits of information, and the representative model is a two-base-pair CG. Treat a MECP2 motif in particular with real scepticism.
families.long:
## The factors

Two unrelated protein modules are collected here because they do the same job from opposite directions. The methyl-CpG binding domain was defined in 1998 as the shared feature of a small mammalian family - MeCP2 plus MBD1, MBD2, MBD3 and MBD4 - that binds DNA containing methylated CpG; MeCP2 then recruits a Sin3A and histone deacetylase complex, which was the first mechanistic link from DNA methylation to repressive chromatin. The zinc-finger CxxC domain does the reverse: it binds CpG only when the cytosine is unmethylated, and it appears in a striking list of chromatin enzymes - CXXC1 (CFP1), CXXC4 and CXXC5, the H3K36 demethylases KDM2A and KDM2B, FBXL19, the 5-methylcytosine dioxygenases TET1 and TET3, the maintenance methyltransferase DNMT1, and the H3K4 methyltransferases KMT2A and KMT2B. In every case the domain is a targeting device attached to a catalytic or scaffolding protein, not a transcription factor in its own right.

Because methylation is almost entirely restricted to CpG in mammalian somatic cells, and because CpG islands are by definition the unmethylated CpG-dense regions, the two groups partition the same dinucleotide between them according to its modification state rather than according to its sequence context.

## The motif

There is no motif in the ordinary sense, and the atlas data say so plainly. The family consensus is CG. The representative model, CIS-BP M01919 for CXXC1, is a two-base-pair CG carrying 4.0 bits. Eight models - those for CXXC1, CXXC5, KMT2A, KDM2A, KDM2B, FBXL19, TET1 and DNMT1 - are CG or CGG at 1.5 to 4.5 bits. The MECP2 model in CIS-BP, M00806, is the dinucleotide Ac at 1.8 bits. The slightly longer models add at most one or two informative flanking positions: TACG for FBXL19, TaCGc for KDM2A, TaCGT for CXXC4, GCGch for MBD1, CCGCcG for CXXC1 in HOCOMOCO. Structural work on human CXXC domains shows exactly this - the CpG is read directly and the domains differ modestly in which bases they tolerate immediately around it - so the flanking preferences in these models are real but small.

The long models are a different problem. HOCOMOCO's KMT2A model, CcCcGCCgCCGCCGCCGCCgCC, and its KMT2B model, GCGGCGGC, are ChIP-derived (evidence code P, grade B) CGG-repeat and GC-rich patterns; the MBD3 model, GGAGCgcaGsngGsgggrgvg, is likewise ChIP-only. These describe the base composition of CpG-island promoters, which is where the proteins sit, not a site the proteins select. The Vierstra archetype for MECP2, cCCGGag, and for MBD1, gGgCCGGag, are footprint archetypes over the same GC-rich compartment. Only TET3's tACGTaagGggggg has grade A multi-assay support, and it is dominated by an ACGT core plus a G-tract.

One statistic deserves attention. The short CG models have high label agreement, 0.5 to 0.8, meaning their nearest neighbours in other databases really do carry family labels - but their bestOther scores are also 0.85 to 0.95, meaning they are nearly identical to models in unrelated families. When both numbers are high for a two-bit model, the model is not discriminating anything.

## Where it acts

CpG islands, and methylated CpG everywhere else. CFP1/CXXC1 occupancy tracks unmethylated CpG islands and shapes their chromatin, and KDM2A is recruited to CpG islands by its CxxC domain to remove H3K36 methylation there. TET1 acts genome-wide on 5-methylcytosine and 5-hydroxymethylcytosine, with CpG islands and their shores prominent. MeCP2, by contrast, is not localised in the usual sense at all: in neurons it is present at levels approaching those of the histone octamer and tracks methylated CpG across the whole genome, and it represses the rate of transcriptional initiation of long, highly methylated genes rather than acting at discrete sites.

## Biology and disease

MECP2 is the Rett syndrome gene - mutations in the X-linked gene cause the classic neurodevelopmental disorder in girls, and duplication of the locus causes a distinct syndrome in boys. This is a very well-understood gene with a very poorly defined binding motif, and the contrast is instructive. KMT2A rearrangement defines a major class of acute leukaemia; DNMT1 mutations cause hereditary sensory neuropathy with dementia; TET2, a relative of the TET1/TET3 proteins filed here, is one of the most commonly mutated genes in myeloid malignancy. In none of these cases does a motif model contribute to interpretation.

## Reading a hit

Do not treat a match in this family as a binding site. If you must use these models, read them as a CpG-density statistic and check whether your region is a CpG island. Then ask which direction of methylation sensitivity matters: a CXXC protein requires the CpG to be unmethylated, an MBD protein requires it to be methylated, and the motif model cannot tell you which state your sequence is in - you need methylation data for that. Be most sceptical of MECP2. Its CIS-BP model is 1.8 bits, its Vierstra archetype is a generic GC-rich footprint, and the biology says MeCP2 coats methylated CpG genome-wide rather than occupying motifs. A MECP2 motif hit is not a MeCP2 site. The same applies to the ChIP-derived KMT2A, KMT2B and MBD3 models, which report the composition of CpG-island promoters.
families.caveats: These are not sequence-specific motifs. The family consensus is CG, the representative model is a two-base CG, and eight of twenty-one models carry under 4.5 bits; they measure CpG density, not a site. Methylation state, which is what actually determines binding and which is opposite for the MBD and CxxC halves of the family, is invisible to a sequence scan. The long KMT2A, KMT2B and MBD3 models are ChIP-only (grade B) and describe the GC-rich composition of CpG-island promoters. MECP2 deserves particular scepticism: its CIS-BP model is 1.8 bits, and MeCP2 binds methylated CpG genome-wide at near-nucleosomal abundance rather than at discrete sites. Two CIS-BP models are cross-species transfers.

families.name: SIX
families.def: MEF3 element, read as TGATAC / GTATCA (the two strands of one extended site). SIX1/2/4 and SIX3/6 select the same core in vitro and differ in cofactor use rather than in sequence.
families.short: The six human SIX genes encode homeodomain proteins with an additional SIX domain that recruits the EYA family of transcriptional coactivators. Their shared DNA core is TGATAC (GTATCA on the other strand), usually embedded in a longer element written GTAACCTGATAC, which on the opposite strand contains the MEF3 site TCAGGTT first defined in the myogenin promoter. SIX1, SIX2 and SIX4 partner with EYA proteins and activate transcription; SIX3 and SIX6 instead recruit Groucho/TLE corepressors and repress. The family builds muscle, kidney, inner ear and eye: SIX1 mutations cause branchio-oto-renal syndrome, SIX3 mutations cause holoprosencephaly, and SIX1 with EYA is re-activated in several carcinomas.
families.long:
## The factors

Six human genes - SIX1, SIX2, SIX3, SIX4, SIX5 and SIX6 - encode the vertebrate relatives of *Drosophila* sine oculis. Each protein carries a homeodomain preceded by a roughly 110-residue SIX domain, which is the family's second functional module: it does not bind DNA but provides the interaction surface for the EYA coactivators, and the crystal structure of the human SIX1 SIX domain bound to the EYA2 ED domain shows how that interface is organized. The family splits on cofactor use rather than on sequence. SIX1, SIX2 and SIX4 bind EYA1-4; EYA has intrinsic protein tyrosine phosphatase activity and its recruitment converts a SIX-DACH complex from repressing to activating, so the same site can give opposite outputs depending on which partner is present. SIX3 and SIX6 do not bind EYA and instead recruit Groucho-related corepressors through an eh1-like motif in the SIX domain, acting as repressors. SIX1 and SIX4 are expressed in somites, muscle satellite cells, kidney and otic placode; SIX2 in nephron progenitors; SIX3 and SIX6 in the anterior neural plate, retina and hypothalamus. SIX5 is a family member with no motif model in any of the four collections used here.

## The motif

All SIX models in these databases converge on a GATAC core. The HT-SELEX and methyl-SELEX models - SIX1.H14CORE.1.SM.B, SIX2.H14CORE.2.SM.B, SIX3.H14CORE.0.SM.B, SIX6.H14CORE.0.SM.B and two CIS-BP models - reduce to tGATAC, 6-9 bits. The ChIP-derived and longer JASPAR models extend it: SIX1 and SIX2 give tGaAAcyTGAtac, JASPAR SIX1 gives GtAACCTGA, JASPAR SIX2 TGAAACCTGAt, SIX4 TGtAAccTGAcACC, and the Vierstra archetype AC0459 GtAACcTGAta. Read the long version on the opposite strand and the classical name appears: GTAACCTGATAC is GTATCAGGTTAC reversed, and TCAGGTT is the MEF3 motif identified in the myogenin promoter as the site through which Six1 and Six4 activate myogenin during somitogenesis. So the family has one site described under two names and two strand conventions; the pooled consensus here, GtaACgcGATACc, is the long form. Two caveats about the split written into this family's definition. First, SIX3 and SIX6 are sometimes described as preferring a TAAT-type site rather than the MEF3 site, but in these four databases their in vitro models give the same TGATAC core as SIX1/2/4, and the JASPAR Six3 model (AtaGGGTATCA) is the GTATCA form - so the SIX1/2/4 versus SIX3/6 division is a cofactor distinction, not one you can make from sequence. Second, one CIS-BP member of this family reads GAgTTGTAGT and has nearest neighbours among the ETS factors; it should not be used as a SIX motif.

## Where it acts

SIX sites occur in tissue-specific enhancers and promoters: the myogenin promoter MEF3 element, nephron progenitor enhancers for SIX2, otic and branchial arch enhancers for SIX1, and forebrain and retinal enhancers for SIX3 and SIX6. The functional unit is usually a SIX site plus its cofactor complex rather than a cluster of different motifs, which is why composite element names are rare for this family. Because the core is only 6 bp, exact TGATAC matches number on the order of 10^6 genome-wide and carry almost no information alone; the 11-13 bp extended form is far more discriminating. Note that the short models will also match GATA-like sequence by coincidence - one Vierstra archetype in this family is labelled SIX/GATA for that reason.

## Biology and disease

Heterozygous SIX1 mutations cause branchio-oto-renal syndrome by disrupting EYA1-SIX1-DNA complexes, and Six1 or Six4 loss in mouse impairs myogenesis and kidney and inner ear development. SIX2 is required to maintain nephron progenitors. Mutations in the SIX3 homeodomain cause holoprosencephaly, and Six3 represses Wnt signaling in the anterior neuroectoderm, which is required for forebrain formation; SIX6 lies in a chromosome 14 cluster and is associated with eye malformation and, in common variation, with optic disc and glaucoma phenotypes. The SIX1-EYA complex is re-expressed in breast, ovarian and other carcinomas, where it promotes migration and metastasis, and is being pursued as a drug target.

## Reading a hit

A bare TGATAC hit is close to meaningless: 6 bp, high genomic frequency, and shared by every SIX paralogue. Insist on the extended GTAACCTGATAC / MEF3 form before calling a site. Even then the hit identifies the family and not the member, and it does not tell you the output, because SIX1/2/4 with EYA activate while SIX3/6 with Groucho repress at what looks like the same sequence. The SIX1, SIX2 and SIX4 models graded P in HOCOMOCO come from ChIP alone and their 5' extension may reflect co-bound partners; the SM-graded models are the in vitro evidence and are the short GATAC form.
families.caveats: The GATAC core is only 6 bp and is shared by all SIX paralogues, so short matches are uninformative and will also pick up GATA-like sequence - one Vierstra archetype here is labelled SIX/GATA. Use the extended 11-13 bp MEF3 form. A hit cannot distinguish SIX1, SIX2, SIX3, SIX4 or SIX6, and cannot predict activation versus repression, since that depends on whether EYA or Groucho is recruited. SIX5 has no model here at all. One CIS-BP member of the family reads an ETS-like sequence (GAGTTGTAGT) and is flagged as belonging elsewhere; the longer SIX1/2/4 models are ChIP-derived and may include partner contributions.

families.name: SMAD
families.def: SBE GTCT/AGAC and GC-rich SMAD motifs. SMAD1-5, SMAD9.
families.consensus: GTCT / AGAC (palindrome GTCTAGAC); also the 5-bp GC motif GGC(GC/CG)
families.short: SMAD proteins are the intracellular effectors of TGF-beta family signaling. Their MH1 domain inserts a beta-hairpin into the major groove and reads just four bases, GTCT or its reverse complement AGAC, often written as the CAGAC box or as the 8-bp palindrome GTCTAGAC. SMAD3, SMAD4 and the BMP-activated SMAD1/5/9 also bind a separate 5-bp GC-rich element, GGCGC or GGCCG. Both elements are far too short to be informative alone, and genome-wide SMAD occupancy is set mainly by whichever lineage-determining factor is present, so most SMAD ChIP peaks are better explained by a partner's motif than by an SBE. This is a family where a motif hit needs corroboration more than almost any other.
families.long:
## The factors

Eight human SMADs fall into three groups. The receptor-regulated R-SMADs are SMAD2 and SMAD3
(phosphorylated by TGF-beta and activin receptors) and SMAD1, SMAD5 and SMAD9/SMAD8
(phosphorylated by BMP receptors). SMAD4 is the shared co-SMAD. SMAD6 and SMAD7 are inhibitory
and are not sequence-specific activators. DNA contact is made by the N-terminal MH1 domain, a
compact domain with a bound zinc ion whose 11-residue beta-hairpin inserts into the major groove;
the C-terminal MH2 domain mediates trimerization, so the functional unit on DNA is normally a
trimer of two R-SMADs plus SMAD4, giving two or three DNA-contacting hairpins. One paralogue is a
special case: wild-type SMAD2 carries a 30-residue insert encoded by exon 3 immediately before the
hairpin that blocks direct DNA binding. Full-length SMAD2 reaches DNA through partners, most
clearly the forkhead protein FOXH1/FAST1; the naturally occurring SMAD2 delta-exon-3 splice form
does bind DNA, like SMAD3.

## The motif

The classical Smad-binding element is 4 bp, GTCT, read on the other strand as AGAC and usually
quoted with a flanking base as CAGAC ("CAGA box") or CAGACA. Zawel and colleagues showed that
SMAD3 and SMAD4 both recognize an identical 8-bp palindrome, GTCTAGAC, and the Smad3 MH1 crystal
structure explained why: the hairpin reads GTCT and two hairpins from a trimer can occupy the two
halves of the palindrome. Real promoters usually contain tandem CAGA repeats rather than a perfect
palindrome; the TGF-beta response element of the PAI-1/SERPINE1 promoter is the canonical example.
Separately, SMADs bind a 5-bp GC-rich element with consensus GGC(GC) or GGC(CG). This was first
described as a BMP-responsive element for SMAD1/5, but structural work showed that SMAD3 and SMAD4
bind the same 5GC motifs, and that these motifs occur in clusters in SMAD-bound regions
genome-wide. So the family has two chemically distinct consensus sequences, not one; a database
entry showing GTCTAGAC and one showing a GC-rich string can both be correct. The data for this
family reflects that split, and its cohesion (0.76) is the lowest in this batch. The CAGAC-type
and 5GC-type models do not interconvert, and paralogues are not separable from sequence within
either type. The CIS-BP SMAD9 entry is a GC-rich model transferred from a Drosophila protein at
91% MH1 identity, not a human measurement.

## Where it acts

SMAD sites are distributed across promoters and enhancers with no CpG-island preference for the
CAGAC form, while 5GC clusters are by definition GC-rich and promoter-biased. What matters more is
that SMAD occupancy is almost entirely conditional. Smad3 ChIP-seq in three different cell types
recovers three largely non-overlapping site sets, each co-occupied by that cell type's
lineage-determining factor: OCT4 in embryonic stem cells, MYOD1 in myotubes, PU.1 in pro-B cells.
In other systems the recurring partners are FOXH1 and other forkhead proteins, RUNX1/2, AP-1
(JUN/FOS), TEAD, and the repressors TGIF1, SKI and SnoN. Named composite elements include the
activin-responsive element of the Mix.2 promoter (a forkhead site next to a SMAD site) and the
BMP-responsive elements of the Id1 and Smad7 promoters. In practice a SMAD peak set looks like the
partner's peak set with a weak SBE enrichment layered on top.

## Biology and disease

TGF-beta/BMP signaling through SMADs controls epithelial growth arrest, extracellular matrix
production, epithelial-mesenchymal transition, regulatory T cell induction, bone and cartilage
formation, and left-right and dorsoventral patterning. Smad3-null mice die within months from
impaired mucosal immunity with defective T cell responses to TGF-beta. SMAD4 was identified as
DPC4, a tumor suppressor homozygously deleted at 18q21 in roughly half of pancreatic
adenocarcinomas; germline SMAD4 mutations cause juvenile polyposis and, with an overlapping
phenotype, hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia. SMAD4 and SMAD2/SMAD3 are also recurrently
mutated in colorectal cancer, and loss of SMAD signaling converts TGF-beta from a growth
suppressor to a driver of invasion and immune evasion. SMAD9 mutations cause a form of pulmonary
arterial hypertension, consistent with the BMP9/BMPR2 axis.

## Reading a hit

Treat an isolated SBE match as essentially no evidence. GTCT or AGAC occurs about once every 128
bases on either strand, so a 4-bp core appears tens of millions of times in the human genome; even
the 8-bp palindrome GTCTAGAC is expected tens of thousands of times by chance. A SMAD hit becomes
meaningful only in one of three forms: several CAGA repeats within a short window, a cluster of
5GC motifs, or an SBE within a few base pairs of a validated partner site (a forkhead, RUNX,
AP-1 or TEAD motif). The second problem is that ChIP-derived SMAD motifs in these collections are
contaminated by indirect binding almost by construction, since SMAD complexes are recruited by
lineage factors. Every HOCOMOCO SMAD2 model here rests on ChIP-seq only (evidence code P), and
wild-type SMAD2 cannot bind DNA directly, so those matrices describe the composition of SMAD2
peaks rather than SMAD2's own specificity. Finally, do not use a hit to name a paralogue. CAGAC
does not mean TGF-beta rather than BMP, because SMAD1/5 bind CAGAC-type sites too and SMAD3/4 bind
GC-type sites; the original "TGF-beta uses CAGAC, BMP uses GC" division does not survive the
structural and genome-wide data.
families.caveats: The lowest-confidence family in this batch. A 4-bp SBE is not a finding; even the 8-bp palindrome is common by chance. The family has two unrelated consensus sequences (CAGAC-type and 5GC-type), so conflicting database entries may both be right, and paralogues are not separable within either. Most SMAD ChIP peaks are explained by a partner's motif, not by an SBE, and all HOCOMOCO SMAD2 models here are ChIP-only while full-length SMAD2 cannot bind DNA directly. The CIS-BP SMAD9 model is transferred from Drosophila. Use SMAD hits only as supporting evidence alongside a partner site or experimental occupancy.

families.name: DMRT (DM domain)
families.def: DM element, palindromic ACAWTGTW. DMRT1-3, DMRTA1/2, DMRTB1, DMRTC2.
families.short: DMRT proteins are the DM-domain transcription factors, named after Drosophila Doublesex and C. elegans MAB-3, the sexual regulators in which the domain was found. Humans have seven well-studied genes, DMRT1, DMRT2, DMRT3, DMRTA1, DMRTA2, DMRTB1 and DMRTC2, plus DMRTC1 paralogues. The DM domain is not a classical zinc finger: two zinc ions are chelated by an intertwined arrangement of cysteines and histidines that cannot be split into independent fingers, and the module ends in a recognition helix. The proteins bind a pseudopalindromic element built from two ACA/TGT half-sites, canonically ACAWTGTW, as dimers and higher-order oligomers. DMRT1 is required for testis differentiation and sustains it after birth; it is the sex-determining gene in chicken, and the 9p24 region containing it is deleted in human 46,XY sex reversal.
families.long:
## The factors

The DM domain was identified in Drosophila Doublesex (DSX) and C. elegans MAB-3 and is conserved
across animals. Vertebrates have a small family: the seven human genes usually discussed are
DMRT1, DMRT2, DMRT3, DMRTA1 (DMRT4), DMRTA2 (DMRT5), DMRTB1 (DMRT6) and DMRTC2 (DMRT7), with
additional DMRTC1 paralogues that also have measured binding. Outside the DM domain the proteins
share almost no sequence, so the family is defined by its DNA-binding module and not by any
common architecture. That module is structurally unusual. Rather than the independent zinc
fingers of C2H2 or GATA proteins, the DM domain chelates two zinc ions through an intertwined
set of cysteine and histidine ligands that cannot be separated into discrete fingers, followed by
a C-terminal recognition helix and a basic tail. DMRT proteins do not bind as simple monomers:
the crystal structures of human DMRT1 on DNA show tetrameric, trimeric and dimeric modes on the
same kind of site, and ChIP with exonuclease treatment indicates that several of these modes are
used in cells. Expression is restricted. DMRT1 is essentially gonad-specific (Sertoli cells and
germ cells); DMRT2 acts in somites; DMRT3 is in spinal interneurons and gonad; DMRTA2 is in
developing cortex; DMRTB1 and DMRTC2 are germ-cell proteins.

## The motif

The element is a pseudopalindrome assembled from two trinucleotide half-sites that are reverse
complements of one another, ACA and TGT, separated by one or two variable bases. Written as the
literature usually does, the core is ACAWTGTW; the equivalent forward-strand rendering with the
half-sites in the other order is TGTWACA, and this is what the data consensus here,
AATGTAACAA, represents. The two are the same element, not a disagreement. Information is
concentrated on the two ACA/TGT triplets; the spacer base and the flanks are weakly constrained,
which is why individual database models range from a bare six-base TGTADC to a full 13-base
AATGTATCAATTT. Structurally, the early NMR work on the DSX DM domain described contacts in the
minor groove of an undistorted duplex, whereas the later crystal structures of DMRT1 showed two
adjacent antiparallel recognition helices inserted into a widened major groove making
base-specific contacts; the current picture is major-groove reading with minor-groove
stabilization, and this shift is worth knowing when reading older descriptions. In vitro
selection across six of the seven vertebrate proteins returned sites resembling the DSX site for
all of them, differing only in efficiency and in preference at individual positions. The family
is correspondingly cohesive here (0.86 across 20 motifs) and no paralogue is separable by
sequence. Some DMRT models drift toward pure AT-richness: the Vierstra archetype
AC0092:DMRT/HOXB is an ATATATT-like model shared with HOXB, and its nearest neighbours lie
outside the family, a reminder that AT-rich DM sites and AT-rich homeodomain sites are hard to
tell apart.

## Where it acts

DMRT1 occupancy in mouse testis is largely promoter-proximal and promoter-distal in roughly equal
measure, with thousands of sites, and the strongest targets are genes of the male pathway
(SOX9, PTGDS) and genes that DMRT1 must keep off (FOXL2, and the retinoic-acid-responsive meiotic
initiator STRA8). DMRT1 works with and against other gonadal regulators: it opposes FOXL2 and
ESR1/ESR2 in the ovarian program, and cooperates with SOX9 and SF1/NR5A1 in the testis. DMRT3
acts in the spinal cord in circuits that coordinate limb movement. Because the factors are
tissue-restricted, the genomic distribution of DM sites is much broader than the set that is
ever occupied: in a cell that expresses no DMRT protein, the sequence is inert.

## Biology and disease

Dmrt1-null mice have severely dysgenic testes, and postnatal loss of DMRT1 in Sertoli cells
reprograms them toward granulosa cells with activation of FOXL2 and ESR2, so DMRT1 is needed
continuously, not just at the sex-determining step. In chicken, the Z-linked DMRT1 is the male
sex-determining gene, and knockdown feminizes male gonads. In humans, deletions of distal 9p
that remove DMRT1 cause 46,XY gonadal dysgenesis and sex reversal, and point mutations in
residues that contact DNA have the same effect; common variants near DMRT1 are associated with
testicular germ cell tumor risk. Outside sex determination, a premature stop codon in horse
DMRT3 underlies the ability to perform alternate gaits, and the same mutation modeled in mice
disturbs spinal circuit function.

## Reading a hit

The element is short and AT-rich in its flanks, so chance matches are common and the AT-rich
tails are readily confused with homeodomain and other minor-groove AT binders. A match cannot
be assigned to a paralogue: the seven vertebrate DM proteins select nearly the same sequence in
vitro, and most models in these databases come from HT-SELEX or methyl-HT-SELEX on isolated
domains, which measure intrinsic specificity and cannot distinguish family members. The strongest
interpretive constraint is expression: DM sites are only meaningful in tissues where a DMRT
protein is present, which for DMRT1 means gonad. Note also that the JASPAR mouse Dmrt1 matrix
MA1603.2 (TACAAAGT) is an outlier here, with nearest neighbours outside the family, so a hit
scored against that specific model deserves a second look.
families.caveats: The informative part of a DM site is two ACA/TGT triplets separated by one or two bases, so an effective width of about seven bases plus AT-rich flanks: chance matches are frequent. All seven vertebrate paralogues select nearly identical sequences in vitro, so a hit identifies the family, never the member, and expression is the only practical discriminator. AT-rich renderings of the site overlap homeodomain space, which is visible in the Vierstra AC0092:DMRT/HOXB archetype. Most models here derive from in vitro selection on isolated DM domains, which supports the sequence preference but says nothing about genomic occupancy. The JASPAR mouse Dmrt1 model MA1603.2 does not match the family consensus.

families.name: Chromatin regulators without a classical DBD
families.def: Motifs attributed to cofactors, readers and writers that have no sequence-specific DBD of their own: BPTF, PHF1, PHF21A, DPF1/2, MYSM1, SETBP1, TOPORS, GATAD2A, ZFPM1, ZZZ3, GLYR1, TCF20, SP140L, NAIF1, ARID1A.
aka: Chromatin regulators without a classical DBD
ChIP-derived motifs of readers and writers
families.short: A deliberate holding bucket, and the place to learn why a ChIP-derived motif may not belong to the protein it is labelled with. The twenty motifs here are attributed to chromatin readers, writers and scaffolds that have no sequence-specific DNA-binding domain: BPTF, PHF1, PHF21A, DPF1, MYSM1, SETBP1, TOPORS, GATAD2A, ZFPM1, ZZZ3, GLYR1, MTF2, TCF20, SP140L, NAIF1 and ARID1A. Cohesion is 0.38, the lowest in the atlas, and six models are explicitly flagged as resembling another family. The clearest case is ZFPM1/FOG-1, which binds GATA-1's zinc finger rather than DNA, yet carries a GATA motif. Read this page as a warning list.
families.long:
## The factors

Curation of the human transcription factors draws a line between proteins that carry a recognised sequence-specific DNA-binding domain and the much larger set of chromatin-associated proteins that reach DNA only through partners. Everything in this family is on the wrong side of that line. BPTF is the largest subunit of the NURF remodelling complex, a PHD-finger and bromodomain histone reader. PHF1 and MTF2 are Polycomb-like accessory subunits of PRC2. DPF1 is a BAF subunit with a double PHD finger, GATAD2A (p66alpha) a NuRD subunit, ZFPM1 is FOG-1, and ZZZ3 belongs to the ATAC acetyltransferase complex, where its ZZ-type zinc finger binds the histone H3 N-terminus. GLYR1 is a nucleosome-destabilising PWWP protein, PHF21A is BHC80 of the LSD1-CoREST complex, MYSM1 a histone H2A deubiquitinase, and ARID1A the BAF subunit whose ARID domain binds DNA with no sequence preference. SETBP1, TCF20, TOPORS, SP140L and NAIF1 are scaffolds and modifiers.

Several do touch DNA - SETBP1 through AT-hooks, ZZZ3 through a Myb/SANT-like region, SP140L through a SAND domain, DPF1 through a Kruppel-like zinc finger - so "no classical DNA-binding domain" is not "no DNA contact". What none has is a demonstrated, discriminating, sequence-specific site. MTF2 is the instructive exception: it binds DNA directly and recruits PRC2 to CpG islands, but what it reads is helical shape, not sequence.

## The motif

A ChIP-seq experiment reports where a protein is crosslinked, not what it recognizes. If the protein is carried to chromatin by a sequence-specific partner, de novo motif discovery on its peaks returns the partner's motif, reproducibly, and the result is then filed under the wrong name. This is not a rare accident: non-targeted transcription factor motifs are a systemic component of ChIP-seq datasets, active promoters generate false-positive "phantom peaks" independent of the antigen, and high-occupancy target regions accumulate signal for many proteins at once. A survey of 208 chromatin-associated proteins in one human cell type found exactly that pattern.

The atlas exposes it mechanically, through the resembles flag and by comparing each model's best within-family match against its best out-of-family match. Six models are flagged, and the cases are concrete:

ZFPM1 (FOG1.H14CORE.0.I.C) reads TTATCt, is flagged as resembling GATA, and has an out-of-family similarity of 0.98. FOG-1 was characterised in 1997 as a multitype zinc finger protein that acts as a cofactor for GATA-1 by binding GATA-1's own zinc finger. It does not bind DNA sequence-specifically. The motif is GATA's. GATAD2A gives the same answer from another complex: its P66A model, tCTTATCTcthtthhnatctt, is flagged as resembling GATA, and its out-of-family similarity (0.858) exceeds its within-family one (0.813) - NuRD is recruited to GATA sites, and the motif came along for the ride. ARID1A's TTTTATtGg is ChIP-only, graded C, flagged as resembling the posterior HOX family, and scores 0.944 against another family; the ARID domain of BAF subunits binds DNA without sequence specificity. PHF1 (tCGG) and NAIF1 (CGTA) are flagged as resembling the CpG readers and are essentially CpG dinucleotides. MTF2's CCCGaCGg is flagged as resembling MTF1 - a different protein with a similar name - at 0.98.

Three more deserve naming. The family's highest-information model, Vierstra archetype AC0442 labelled TOPORS with function "Unknown", is a 17-base-pair, 31.5-bit consensus TCCCAAAGTAGCTGGGA that closely matches a segment of the Alu consensus: it reads as repeat sequence, not a factor site. SP140L's tACGTcA is a fragment of the canonical CRE, TGACGTCA. DPF1 is the genuine near-miss: its HOCOMOCO and CIS-BP models (CaCCTATAG, CTATAGGtG) have in vitro selection support and agree at 0.97, but their best out-of-family similarity is 0.996 and the Vierstra archetype carrying them is labelled DPF/ZBTB and classed as C2H2 - so even here the model cannot be assigned to DPF1 rather than a ZBTB protein. The rest (SETBP1's A-rich aCgvaaAAaaaA, TCF20's gAdTataT, GLYR1's four-base AAAT, PHF21A's rcaaAaAcA, BPTF's AtAACA at 5.4 bits) are short and uninformative; SETBP1's is consistent with its AT-hooks, which give affinity without specificity.

## Where it acts

Wherever the recruiting factor acts. GATAD2A and ZFPM1 signal at GATA sites in erythroid and megakaryocytic cells; PRC2 accessory subunits at CpG islands; BAF and NURF subunits at active promoters and enhancers, which is also where phantom peaks and high-occupancy regions live. The useful statement is always about the complex and its recruiter, not about a sequence.

## Biology and disease

These are important genes. PHF21A disruption in the Potocki-Shaffer region causes intellectual disability with craniofacial anomalies; de novo SETBP1 mutations cause Schinzel-Giedion syndrome; ARID1A is among the most frequently mutated genes in human cancer, and TCF20 and BPTF are established disease genes too. None of that makes their motif models usable. Clinical importance and motif quality are independent.

## Reading a hit

Do not attribute a hit in this family to the labelled protein. Instead, use the entry backwards: if a scan returns a hit for one of these names, identify which real family the model belongs to and read that entry. For ZFPM1 and GATAD2A, go to GATA. For PHF1 and NAIF1, go to MBD_CXXC. For ARID1A, go to the posterior HOX family. For SETBP1 and PHF21A, go to HMGA and read what an AT-hook does. Check TOPORS against repeat annotation. And apply the general rule beyond this page: whenever a motif is attributed to a cofactor, reader, writer or remodeller, ask whether the ChIP experiment that produced it was measuring the protein or its recruiter.
families.caveats: Nothing in this family should be scanned with the intention of finding sites for the named protein. These are chromatin proteins without sequence-specific DNA-binding domains, and their models are best explained as the motifs of the sequence-specific factors that recruit them, as phantom peaks over active promoters, or as repeat sequence. Cohesion is 0.38, the lowest in the atlas; six of twenty models are flagged as resembling another family, and several score higher against other families than within this one. The NAIF1 model is a Gallus gallus transfer at 74 percent domain identity. Even DPF1, the only member with in vitro support and internal agreement, is 0.996 similar to a ZBTB C2H2 model and cannot be attributed.

families.name: HIF / ARNT
families.def: Hypoxia response element (A/G)CGTG. HIF1A, EPAS1/HIF2A, HIF3A, ARNT, ARNT2.
families.short: The hypoxia response element is the site read by HIF, a heterodimer of an oxygen-labile alpha subunit (HIF-1alpha, HIF-2alpha/EPAS1, HIF-3alpha) and the constitutive beta subunit ARNT (HIF-1beta) or its paralogue ARNT2. Both partners are bHLH-PAS proteins. The element is an asymmetric E-box half-site pair: ARNT reads the 3' GTG and the alpha subunit reads a 5' half that is usually TAC or GAC, giving the five-base core (A/G)CGTG, most often written in context as ...TACGTGC... When oxygen is plentiful the alpha subunits are prolyl-hydroxylated and destroyed by the VHL ubiquitin ligase, so occupancy of these sites is a direct readout of oxygen availability. HIF drives erythropoietin, VEGFA and the glycolytic genes, and the pathway is constitutively active in VHL-mutant kidney cancer.
families.long:
## The factors

HIF is an obligate heterodimer of one oxygen-regulated alpha subunit and one constitutive beta subunit. The alpha subunits are HIF-1alpha (*HIF1A*), HIF-2alpha (*EPAS1*) and HIF-3alpha (*HIF3A*, which produces several splice isoforms, some of them dominant-negative); the beta subunits are ARNT (also called HIF-1beta) and the brain- and kidney-enriched paralogue ARNT2. All are bHLH-PAS proteins: a basic helix-loop-helix domain followed by PAS-A and PAS-B. Alpha-subunit prolines are hydroxylated by the PHD enzymes, creating the binding site for the VHL ubiquitin ligase; a separate asparagine hydroxylation by FIH blocks p300/CBP recruitment (Kaelin and Ratcliffe 2008). HIF-1alpha is close to ubiquitous; HIF-2alpha is enriched in endothelium, kidney interstitium, lung and sympathoadrenal tissue. ARNT is the shared partner of the whole bHLH-PAS class: it also dimerizes with AHR, SIM1/2 and NPAS factors, and forms homodimers. Loss of *Arnt* in mice is embryonic lethal around E10.5 with defective angiogenesis and placental vascularization (Maltepe et al. 1997). HIF-1 was first defined as the hypoxia-inducible activity at the erythropoietin enhancer (Semenza and Wang 1992) and then identified as a bHLH-PAS heterodimer (Wang et al. 1995).

## The motif

The core is (A/G)CGTG, conventionally written RCGTG. Unlike the palindromic E-box CACGTG, the HIF site is an asymmetric pair of half-sites: selection experiments assign the 3' half-site GTG to ARNT, while the 5' half comes from the partner (AHR prefers T(C/T)GC and SIM prefers GT(G/A)C, so ARNT is the constant element in all of them) (Swanson et al. 1995). For HIF the 5' half is usually TAC or GAC, so the full site reads TACGTGC or GACGTGC. One substitution, C to T at the first position, is therefore all that separates an HRE from a canonical E-box. Crystal structures of mouse HIF-2alpha-ARNT and HIF-1alpha-ARNT bound to an HRE show ARNT spiraling around the outside of the alpha subunit; the DNA-reading head rotates and extends and cooperates with a distal PAS domain, and cancer-associated alpha-subunit mutations map to residues that establish DNA binding (Wu et al. 2015). Systematic measurements across the family find 12-15 bp footprints in which flanking-base preferences, not the core, distinguish members that share a core (Bersten et al. 2026). The consensus computed from the 19 members here is ACGTGc, core plus a 3' C preference, matching the compiled consensus HRE (Wenger et al. 2005). Nothing in the sequence distinguishes HIF-1alpha from HIF-2alpha (Smythies et al. 2019). Two entries need care: JASPAR EPAS1 (MA2325.1) is written GCACGTAC, the reverse complement of GTACGTGC, so it is the same site on the other strand; JASPAR Arnt (MA0004.1) is an ARNT-homodimer palindrome, not an HRE.

## Where it acts

RCGTG is expected several million times per strand in a 3-Gb genome, and only a small fraction is ever occupied. Chromatin is the dominant filter: occupancy is enriched roughly 20-fold at DNase-hypersensitive sites that were already open in normoxia, irrespective of distance from promoters (Schodel et al. 2011). Confirmed sites number in the hundreds to low thousands per cell type and often lie far from the genes they regulate. The two isoforms partition consistently: HIF-1 is biased toward promoter-proximal sites and HIF-2 toward promoter-distant sites, each with a cell-type-specific repertoire that does not redistribute with hypoxia severity or duration (Smythies et al. 2019). Because the core contains a CpG, HREs cluster with CpG-rich promoters and are sensitive to DNA methylation. Functional HREs generally need neighboring sequence, historically called the HIF ancillary sequence, and commonly co-occur with CREB/ATF, SP1 and AP-1 sites (Wenger et al. 2005).

## Biology and disease

HIF targets include *EPO*, *VEGFA*, the glucose transporter *SLC2A1*, *LDHA*, *PDK1* and *CA9*, coordinating oxygen delivery with a shift to glycolysis. Biallelic *VHL* loss in clear-cell renal carcinoma leaves HIF-2 constitutively active, which made the PAS-B pocket seen in the HIF structures a drug target (Wu et al. 2015; Kaelin and Ratcliffe 2008). Somatic gain-of-function *EPAS1* mutations that block hydroxylation cause paraganglioma with polycythemia (Zhuang et al. 2012), and *EPAS1* carries the strongest selection signal in Tibetan high-altitude adaptation (Yi et al. 2010). The pathway is also the target of prolyl-hydroxylase inhibitors used for renal anemia.

## Reading a hit

An RCGTG match on its own licenses almost no conclusion: five informative base pairs occur millions of times, and the great majority are never bound. Treat it as a candidate only in accessible chromatin, and preferably with hypoxia-responsive expression nearby. A hit cannot tell you which alpha subunit bound, and it barely distinguishes HIF:ARNT from the other ARNT complexes: AHR:ARNT prefers GCGTG, SIM:ARNT GT(G/A)CGTG, and ARNT homodimers the palindromic CACGTG, so the discriminating information sits in one or two weakly constrained positions. Evidence is skewed: eight of the ten HOCOMOCO models here are ChIP-only (letter P) at grade B or C, supporting "this region was occupied in cells" rather than "this protein binds this sequence"; the one HT-SELEX model, ARNT2.H14CORE.2.S.C, is a palindromic CACGTGAC of the kind an ARNT2 homodimer makes. The CIS-BP ARNT entry M01719_2.00 is transferred from mouse at 100% DNA-binding-domain identity: safe, but not a human measurement. The Vierstra archetype AC0072:HIF1A/ARNT is named after the factors whose motifs clustered together and is not a claim that HIF1A and ARNT can be told apart.
families.caveats: The core is only five informative base pairs, so chance matches vastly outnumber real sites and a hit is close to uninformative without chromatin or expression evidence. HIF-1alpha and HIF-2alpha share one consensus and cannot be distinguished by sequence; neither can HIF:ARNT be cleanly separated from AHR:ARNT, SIM:ARNT or ARNT homodimers, since all read CGTG with differences at one or two flanking positions. Most HOCOMOCO models here are ChIP-only at grade B or C, so they reflect occupied regions and may include indirect binding; ChIP peaks lacking any RCGTG are well documented. The ARNT entries in JASPAR and CIS-BP include palindromic E-boxes that are homodimer, not HIF, motifs, and one JASPAR entry is written on the opposite strand.
