families.name: HNF4
families.def: DR1 with strong 5' extension. HNF4A, HNF4G, NR2C1/2 (TR2/TR4).
families.short: HNF4A and HNF4G are nuclear receptors that bind DNA only as homodimers, on a DR1: two hexameric half-sites in the same orientation separated by exactly one base pair. Their preferred half-site drifts away from the superfamily's AGGTCA towards AG(G/T)CCA, which is why the databases render the HNF4 motif as CAAAGTCCA, or at full length as a 13 bp DR1. That drift is real specificity: the HNF4-specific binding motif is bound by HNF4A and not by other nuclear receptors tested in vivo. The same family here also holds NR2C1 and NR2C2 (TR2/TR4), whose models are generic AGGTCA DR1s and are not distinguishable from RXR or COUP-TF. HNF4A is the central regulator of hepatocyte, islet and intestinal gene expression and the MODY1 gene.
families.long:
## The factors

HNF4A (NR2A1) and HNF4G (NR2A2) are C4 double-zinc-finger nuclear receptors, discovered as a liver-enriched activator and immediately recognised as a steroid-receptor-superfamily member (Sladek et al. 1990). HNF4A is expressed in hepatocytes, pancreatic islet beta cells, intestine, kidney proximal tubule and stomach; HNF4G overlaps, weighted towards intestine and stomach. Unlike most of the superfamily they do not use RXR: HNF4A recognises its target genes exclusively as a cooperative homodimer (Lu et al. 2008). Fatty acyl-CoA thioesters have been proposed as ligands, but HNF4 is usually treated as constitutively active, regulated through coactivators and isoform choice (P1 versus P2 promoters).

This family also contains NR2C1 (TR2) and NR2C2 (TR4), broadly expressed orphan receptors that homodimerize and heterodimerize with each other. They are grouped here because their motif models are DR1 elements in the same frame, not because they are HNF4 paralogues. The family holds 18 models in total (JASPAR 6, HOCOMOCO 6, CIS-BP 4, Vierstra 2).

## The motif

The architecture is a DR1: two hexamers on the same strand with a single base between them, generically AGGTCAxAGGTCA (Khorasanizadeh and Rastinejad 2001). HNF4 departs from that hexamer. Its models read AGKCCA-A-AGTCCA at full length (CIS-BP M08219, HOCOMOCO HNF4A.H14CORE.0 gGtyCAAAGTcC, JASPAR MA1494.2 ggGTCCAAAGGTCA), and the short JASPAR models for both paralogues (MA0114.5, MA0484.3) give only the 9 bp core CAAAGTCCA, covering the spacer and the 3' half-site.

Protein-binding microarrays comparing HNF4A, RXRA and COUP-TFII resolved this into a named element: the HNF4-specific binding motif, H4-SBM, xxxxCAAAGTCCA. ChIP data indicated the H4-SBM is bound by HNF4A and not by ten other nuclear receptors in vivo, and the specificity maps to Asp69 and Arg76 in the DNA-binding domain, a residue combination unique to HNF4 among human nuclear receptors. The same study reported a previously unrecognised polarity in the classical DR1 for HNF4A, RXRA and COUP-TFII homodimers (Fang et al. 2012). The 2.0 A structure of the HNF4A DBD on the HNF1A promoter element shows the cooperative homodimer and the contacts that give this element its strong 5' extension (Lu et al. 2008).

So the family splits into two unequal halves. HNF4A and HNF4G carry the AGTCCA-flavoured signature and are partly distinguishable from the rest of the superfamily - but not from each other, their models being 0.999 similar. NR2C1 and NR2C2 models are either the bare hexamer AGGTCA (four of the eighteen models here) or a generic AGGTCAxAGGTCA DR1, and are not distinguishable from RXR homodimers or COUP-TF. That is why the family's data consensus is GgTcAAAGGTCA, the generic DR1, rather than the H4-SBM quoted above, and why the family's medoid model (HOCOMOCO NR2C2.H14CORE.1.PS.A) matches motifs outside this family better than inside it, 0.985 against 0.86. The disagreement is not an error in either source: it reflects a family that contains one receptor pair with a private motif and one without.

## Where it acts

HNF4A occupies promoters and enhancers across the hepatocyte, islet, intestinal and renal gene programs. Promoter-occupancy mapping in human liver and pancreatic islets placed HNF4A in tissue-specific circuits with HNF1A and HNF6/ONECUT1 (Odom et al. 2004), and combining protein-binding microarrays with expression and ChIP data extended the human target list (Bolotin et al. 2010). HNF4 motifs are among the most enriched in liver open chromatin and co-occur with HNF1A/HNF1B, FOXA1/FOXA2, CEBPA/CEBPB, ONECUT1 and NR5A2 sites. On the NR2C side, the best-characterised sites are DR1 elements in the embryonic and fetal beta-type globin promoters, where the TR2/TR4 heterodimer forms the core of a repressor complex (Tanabe et al. 2002).

## Biology and disease

Heterozygous HNF4A mutations cause maturity-onset diabetes of the young type 1 (Yamagata et al. 1996), and some of the same alleles cause transient neonatal hyperinsulinism and macrosomia. Germline Hnf4a-null mouse embryos die during gastrulation. Liver-specific deletion in adult mice causes hepatic lipid accumulation, low serum cholesterol and triglycerides and raised serum bile acids, traced to reduced apolipoprotein B and microsomal triglyceride transfer protein and to reduced basolateral bile-acid transporters (Hayhurst et al. 2001). HNF4A is required for intestinal and hepatic differentiation, and its loss or isoform switching is seen in hepatocellular carcinoma and colorectal cancer. TR2/TR4 repression of the fetal globin genes makes NR2C1 and NR2C2 candidate targets for induction of fetal hemoglobin in sickle-cell disease and beta-thalassemia.

## Reading a hit

This family contains the one place in the nuclear receptor superfamily where a matrix does come close to naming a receptor. A clean CAAAGTCCA or full AGTCCA-type DR1 is reasonable evidence for HNF4A or HNF4G, given that the H4-SBM was bound by HNF4A and not by ten other nuclear receptors tested (Fang et al. 2012). It still does not separate HNF4A from HNF4G; use expression, since the two rarely overlap strongly outside intestine and stomach. A generic AGGTCAxAGGTCA hit tells you much less: RXR homodimers, PPAR:RXR, COUP-TF/NR2F and TR2/TR4 all use DR1. Scale matters too: a 9-mer like CAAAGTCCA occurs on the order of 10^4 times per haploid genome by chance, comparable to the number of HNF4A ChIP peaks recovered in liver, so the motif alone over-calls heavily outside hepatic and intestinal chromatin. Finally, one CIS-BP model labelled NR2C2 in this family, M07990 (abcaCTTCCGGGtC), contains a CTTCC/GGAA core and its nearest neighbours across all four databases are ETS motifs; the family data flags it with altFamily ETS_EHF. Treat it as indirect or misassigned rather than as evidence that TR4 binds an ETS site.
families.caveats: Two different things live in this family. An HNF4-flavoured site (CAAAGTCCA, or a DR1 whose half-sites read AGTCCA) is genuinely informative for HNF4A/HNF4G, though it cannot separate those two paralogues. A generic AGGTCAxAGGTCA DR1 - which is what the NR2C1 and NR2C2 models here are, four of them being the bare hexamer - is shared with RXR homodimers, PPAR:RXR and COUP-TF, and the family's own medoid matches other families better than its own. One CIS-BP model labelled NR2C2 (M07990) is an ETS-like matrix flagged as belonging elsewhere. A 9-mer occurs roughly 10^4 times per genome, so pair hits with liver or intestinal accessibility data.

families.name: MEF2
families.def: AT-rich CTA(A/T)4TAG. MEF2A/B/C/D.
families.short: MEF2 sites are bound by the four MADS-box factors MEF2A, MEF2B, MEF2C and MEF2D, which act as obligate dimers. The element is an A/T-rich decamer, CTA(A/T)4TAG, and is easy to confuse with ordinary AT-rich sequence: the information sits almost entirely in the flanking CTA and TAG. MEF2 and SRF share the MADS fold but not the site - SRF requires the CC and GG of a CArG box where MEF2 requires TA and TA. The four paralogues have the same sequence preference and overlapping expression, so which one acts at a given element is decided by cell type and by chromatin rather than by DNA. MEF2 factors drive muscle differentiation, cardiac morphogenesis and activity-dependent programmes in neurons.
families.long:
## The factors

MEF2A, MEF2B, MEF2C and MEF2D each carry a MADS box - a 56-58 residue domain shared with SRF and with the plant and yeast MADS proteins - immediately followed by a MEF2-specific extension of about 30 residues. The two regions together form the DNA-binding and dimerisation surface; MEF2 proteins bind only as homodimers or as heterodimers among themselves. The crystal structure of the MEF2A core on DNA at 1.5 A resolution and an NMR structure of the same complex showed that MEF2 lacks the N-terminal extension SRF uses, and that the MEF domain C-terminal to the MADS box adopts a conformation substantially different from the equivalent region in SRF and yeast MCM1 - the structural basis for a different sequence preference and a different degree of DNA bending within one fold. All four genes are broadly expressed with different emphases: MEF2A and MEF2D are near-ubiquitous, MEF2C is prominent in brain, cardiac and skeletal muscle and in B lymphocytes, MEF2B in germinal-centre B cells. Activity is regulated post-translationally rather than by abundance: class IIa histone deacetylases (HDAC4, HDAC5, HDAC7, HDAC9) bind the MADS/MEF2 domain and repress it until calcium-CaMK signalling drives their nuclear export, and p38 MAPK, ERK5, sumoylation and the corepressor CABIN1 tune the same surface.

## The motif

The consensus was determined by selecting optimal sites with anti-MEF2A antibodies from muscle, heart and brain extracts: 5'-CT(A/T)(A/T)AAATAG-3', now generally written CTA(A/T)4TAG or YTA(A/T)4TAR, a 10-bp near-palindrome. Each MADS monomer reads one half, contacting the bases through an antiparallel coiled coil of two alpha-helices laid in the widened major groove, with basic residues gripping the flanking phosphates. Because the centre is a run of A and T, essentially all the sequence information lives in the outer CTA and TAG - which is why an A/T-rich stretch with the wrong flanks scores poorly, and why MEF2 sites are easy to over-call in AT-rich genomes. That same selection experiment found that MEF2 complexes from brain extracts imposed additional constraints outside the decamer, a tissue effect that has never been resolved into a distinct PWM. The four paralogues are not separable: in these databases the JASPAR and CIS-BP models for MEF2A, MEF2B, MEF2C and MEF2D are nearly identical (family cohesion 0.86), and no in vitro study has reported a usable difference. One real complication is visible in the data. Alongside the canonical CTATTTTTAG models sits a second flavour - CCAAATATGG, CCNAATTTGGAA and similar - which comes almost entirely from HT-SELEX and methyl-HT-SELEX experiments and which is, read literally, a CArG box: CC plus an A/T core plus GG. These entries have lower label agreement (0.6-0.7) and their nearest non-MEF2 neighbours are MADS-box motifs from SRF. Whether this is a genuine secondary MEF2 specificity or an artefact of selection is unsettled; either way, scanning with those models partly scans for SRF.

## Where it acts

MEF2 motifs are enhancer elements, not promoter elements, and are depleted from CpG islands - unsurprising for an A/T-rich site. In differentiating muscle they mark the same enhancers as the myogenic bHLH factors MYOD1 and MYF5, and MEF2-E-box pairs are the canonical muscle enhancer architecture; MEF2 does not have a named composite element of its own but the MEF2-plus-E-box arrangement is close to one. In neurons MEF2 sites mark activity-regulated enhancers; in cardiomyocytes they co-occur with GATA4, NKX2-5, TBX20 and SRF sites. Paralogue occupancy is largely redundant where two MEF2 proteins are co-expressed, and which paralogue compensates at a given site depends on the local chromatin environment.

## Biology and disease

MEF2 factors are required for differentiation rather than for lineage specification. Mef2c-null mouse embryos fail cardiac morphogenesis, with a single ventricular chamber and absent right ventricle, and die around E9.5. In neurons, activity-dependent MEF2 activation restricts excitatory synapse number, so MEF2 acts in synapse elimination rather than formation. In humans, MEF2C haploinsufficiency - by 5q14.3 microdeletion or point mutation - causes severe intellectual disability with stereotypic movements, epilepsy and absent speech. MEF2B is somatically mutated in roughly 11% of diffuse large B-cell lymphomas and 12% of follicular lymphomas; the mutations increase MEF2B activity, either by disrupting its interaction with the corepressor CABIN1 or by escaping inhibitory phosphorylation and sumoylation, and deregulate the proto-oncogene BCL6. MEF2D fusions define a subtype of B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia, and MEF2A variants have been reported in coronary artery disease.

## Reading a hit

The main risk here is the base composition of the genome, not the paralogue problem. An A/T-rich decamer is common in intergenic and intronic DNA, so scan with a model that actually constrains the CTA and TAG flanks and check the flanks in the match itself; a hit on a poly-A or poly-T stretch with soft flanks is almost certainly noise. A hit identifies MEF2, not MEF2A versus MEF2B, MEF2C or MEF2D - there is no reported sequence-level discrimination, and expression plus chromatin decide the occupant. Be explicit about which model you used, because the collections contain two incompatible flavours: canonical CTA(A/T)4TAG models, and CArG-like CCAAATATGG models from in vitro selection whose nearest neighbours are SRF motifs. If a putative MEF2 hit came from the second kind, consider SRF as an equally good explanation. The ChIP-derived MEF2A and MEF2C models here are grade B and reflect occupancy in specific cell types; because MEF2 sits beside E-boxes at muscle enhancers, E-box information can leak into ChIP-derived MEF2 models and vice versa.
families.caveats: Two distinct problems. First, base composition: the site is an A/T-rich decamer whose only real information is the CTA and TAG flanks, so AT-rich sequence throws false positives unless the flanks are genuinely constrained - inspect them in every hit. Second, the databases carry two incompatible model flavours for this family: canonical CTA(A/T)4TAG, and a CArG-like CCAAATATGG form from HT-SELEX whose nearest neighbours are SRF motifs. A hit from the second kind is as consistent with SRF as with MEF2. No model separates MEF2A, MEF2B, MEF2C and MEF2D, so report MEF2-family and let expression and chromatin decide the member.

families.name: CUX (CUT homeodomain)
families.def: ATCGAT / ATCRAT. CUX1, CUX2, SATB1, SATB2.
families.short: CUX1, CUX2 and the SATB proteins SATB1 and SATB2 bind DNA with two kinds of domain at once: CUT repeats, each an independent ~70-residue DNA-binding module, plus a homeodomain. The combination shifts the preferred site away from the generic TAAT core of other homeodomain proteins toward ATCGAT, usually embedded in a longer near-palindrome such as TAATCGATTA. CUT repeats also bind CCAAT boxes, which is how CUX1 earned its older name, CCAAT displacement protein. SATB1 and SATB2 use their CUT-like domain differently, recognizing AT-rich matrix-attachment regions rather than ATCGAT. CUX1 is a haploinsufficient tumor suppressor in myeloid and other cancers, and SATB1 and SATB2 organize chromatin over long distances in T cells and bone.
families.long:
## The factors

Four human proteins make up this family. CUX1 (also CDP, CUTL1, CASP, Clox) and CUX2 each carry three evolutionarily conserved 73-residue CUT repeats followed by a CUT-type homeodomain. SATB1 and SATB2 carry a CUT-like domain of two repeats plus a homeodomain, and additionally an N-terminal ubiquitin-like dimerization domain, so they act as oligomers. CUX1 is broadly expressed and produces multiple isoforms by alternative splicing and proteolytic processing, which changes how many CUT repeats a given isoform contains and therefore how it binds DNA. CUX2 is largely neural. SATB1 is highest in thymocytes and T cells; SATB2 is expressed in osteoblasts, cortical neurons and intestinal epithelium, where it is used clinically as a lineage marker.

## The motif

The defining feature is that the homeodomain does not work alone. In vitro selection with the mammalian Cut proteins returned the palindromic consensus (t/a)(a/t)tATCGATTAt(t/c)(t/g)(t/a) - an ATCGAT core with a homeodomain ATTA motif adjacent - and showed that CUT repeat 2 binds DNA independently of the homeodomain, preferring CCAAT boxes and an ATTA core, and that the repeat and the homeodomain interact even without DNA, greatly increasing the affinity of the pair. A separate study of CUT repeats 1 and 3 found broad, overlapping specificities, binding as dimers, with flanking sequence contributing measurably, and concluded that the native human Cut-like protein prefers a site with an ATCGAT core flanked by G/C-rich sequence rather than one built around ATTA. Both pictures are visible in the pooled data here: the family consensus is TaATCGATa, JASPAR gives CUX1 TAATCGATA and CUX2 TaATCGATa, HOCOMOCO HT-SELEX models give TATCGATTA, and two Vierstra archetypes recover tandem ATCGAT (ATCgATaannttATCGAT) and, strikingly, CCAATAATCGAT - a CCAAT box abutting the homeodomain site, exactly the arrangement the biochemistry predicts. ATCGAT contains a CpG, and because CpG is depleted several-fold in the human genome outside CpG islands, exact matches are considerably rarer than a naive 6-mer calculation suggests; they are also candidates for methylation-sensitive binding. Note that the SATB1 models in this family look different: the ChIP-derived HOCOMOCO entries read ataATtAwtAcTAATAAtt and tACTAATAATtA, and the JASPAR model CTAATAA - AT-rich rather than ATCGAT.

## Where it acts

CUX1 and CUX2 sites occur in promoters, where CUT-repeat binding to CCAAT elements displaces CCAAT-box activators, and in enhancers of differentiation genes. SATB1 and SATB2 bind base-unpairing regions - AT-rich stretches with an ATC sequence context, one strand rich in A, T and C but not G - that occur in matrix- or scaffold-attachment regions. SATB1 anchors such regions into a cage-like nuclear structure and recruits chromatin remodelling activity to regulate genes tens of kilobases away, most clearly across the T-helper-2 cytokine locus and the MHC class I region. So although the two halves of this family share a domain architecture, they occupy different kinds of sequence: CUX hits tend to be discrete ATCGAT-containing sites, SATB hits broad AT-rich regions.

## Biology and disease

Inactivating CUX1 mutations behave as haploinsufficient tumor-promoting events across cancer types, and CUX1 lies in the commonly deleted 7q22 region of myeloid malignancy. SATB1 overexpression reprograms gene expression to promote breast tumor growth and metastasis in xenograft models. Heterozygous disruption of SATB2 causes cleft palate and, more broadly, the SATB2-associated syndrome; SATB2 immunohistochemistry is standard in distinguishing colorectal from other adenocarcinomas. Mouse Cux1 mutants show hair follicle and immune defects, and Satb1-null mice have a severe block in thymocyte development.

## Reading a hit

A TAATCGATTA-type match is reasonably specific because ATCGAT is CpG-containing and therefore uncommon, but it does not distinguish CUX1 from CUX2, whose models are the same. Do not use an ATCGAT hit as evidence for SATB1 or SATB2: their functional target is an AT-rich base-unpairing region, and the SATB1 motifs in these databases are ChIP-derived (P grade) AT-rich models that may partly reflect the sequence composition of matrix-attachment regions rather than a crisp binding site. Also be careful with short fragments: four CIS-BP and Vierstra members of this family reduce to ATCG or ATTG, which is too short to be informative. Finally, one Vierstra archetype in this family is labelled CUX/ONECUT, a reminder that ATCGAT is shared with the ONECUT factors covered separately.
families.caveats: CUX1 and CUX2 are indistinguishable from sequence. SATB1 and SATB2 belong to the same domain family but do not share the ATCGAT preference; their models here are ChIP-derived, AT-rich, and better understood as matrix-attachment/base-unpairing regions than as a defined site, so do not infer SATB binding from an ATCGAT hit or vice versa. ATCGAT is also the preferred core of the ONECUT factors, and one Vierstra archetype in this family is explicitly labelled CUX/ONECUT, so an ATCGAT hit cannot be assigned to CUX over ONECUT without expression context. Several members reduce to 4-bp fragments that carry almost no information.

families.name: ONECUT (HNF6)
families.def: TATTGATTT. ONECUT1/2/3.
families.short: ONECUT1 (HNF6), ONECUT2 and ONECUT3 bind DNA with a single CUT domain joined to a divergent homeodomain, and the two modules together read TATTGATT, often followed by a run of T. The same proteins also bind ATCGAT, the core preferred by the CUX proteins, and both forms appear across JASPAR, HOCOMOCO and CIS-BP. This is the most internally consistent family in the CUT class: cohesion is 0.92 and the three paralogues cannot be told apart from sequence. ONECUT1 is a liver, pancreas and biliary factor whose loss disrupts bile duct and endocrine pancreas development and causes human diabetes; ONECUT2 has become a target of interest in treatment-resistant and neuroendocrine prostate cancer.
families.long:
## The factors

Three human genes: ONECUT1 (HNF6, HNF-6alpha), ONECUT2 (OC-2) and ONECUT3 (OC-3). ONECUT1 was identified as a liver-enriched factor with an architecture no other homeodomain protein had at the time - a single CUT domain rather than the three CUT repeats of CUX1, followed by a homeodomain of a novel type. The ONECUT homeodomain differs from the canonical fold at positions that normally contact DNA, and it depends on the CUT domain for high-affinity binding, so the functional unit is bipartite. ONECUT1 is expressed in hepatocytes, biliary epithelium, pancreas and parts of the nervous system; ONECUT2 overlaps in liver and pancreas and is also expressed in retina and prostate; ONECUT3 is the least studied and is largely neural. The three are partly redundant, most clearly in retina, where Onecut1 and Onecut2 together, but neither alone, are required for early retinal cell fates.

## The motif

The crystal structure of the bipartite DNA-binding domain of ONECUT1 bound to the HNF6 site of the transthyretin promoter shows the CUT domain and the homeodomain engaging adjacent stretches of the duplex, and the comparison with the DNA-free protein and with the OCT1 POU domain explains how the same protein can bind DNA in two distinct modes that use different coactivators. That structural duality shows up directly in the motif data. One set of models reads TATTGATT with a 3' T-rich extension - HOCOMOCO HNF6.H14CORE.0.PM.A gives TATTGATT, ONEC3.H14CORE.0.S.B gives TATtGATTT, and the JASPAR ONECUT1 and ONECUT3 models are the reverse complements AAATCAATA and AAAAATCAATAa. A second set reads ATCGAT, sometimes doubled: HNF6.H14CORE.2.S.B gives tATCGATcGAT, ONEC2.H14CORE.2.S.B gives TATCGATCG, and the JASPAR ONECUT2 model is GATCGATA. A ChIP-derived ONECUT2 model even resolves into six tandem ATTGAT repeats at 28 bits, which reflects clustered sites rather than a single long element. The pooled consensus is TATTGATT with cohesion 0.92, the highest in the CUT class. No position distinguishes ONECUT1, ONECUT2 and ONECUT3.

## Where it acts

ONECUT1 sites sit in liver and pancreas promoters and enhancers. Genome-scale location analysis of human liver and pancreatic islets put ONECUT1/HNF6 alongside HNF1A and HNF4A on a largely overlapping set of promoters, with the three factors binding each other's genes, so an ONECUT hit in a hepatic or islet regulatory region very often sits within a few hundred base pairs of HNF1 and HNF4 sites. In the developing pancreas, ONECUT1 acts upstream of NEUROG3. Because the informative core is about 8 bp and AT-rich, exact TATTGATT matches are expected on the order of 10^5 times in 3.1 Gb; the ATCGAT form is rarer, since CpG is depleted several-fold in the genome outside CpG islands. Tandem arrangements of ATTGAT, as in the archetype and ChIP-derived models, are a more distinctive signal than a single copy.

## Biology and disease

Hnf6-null mice fail to form a normal biliary tract, with gallbladder agenesis and abnormal intrahepatic bile ducts, and show disrupted pancreatic endocrine differentiation through loss of Ngn3 expression. In humans, biallelic and heterozygous ONECUT1 variants cause diabetes, ranging from neonatal diabetes with pancreatic hypoplasia to a MODY-like presentation, placing ONECUT1 in the same clinical territory as HNF1A, HNF1B and PDX1. ONECUT2 has emerged as a driver in prostate cancer: it suppresses the androgen receptor program and promotes neuroendocrine differentiation, and it is the target of active inhibitor development in castration-resistant and neuroendocrine disease. In retina, combined loss of Onecut1 and Onecut2 depletes horizontal cells and alters retinal ganglion cell production.

## Reading a hit

A TATTGATT match, and especially a tandem ATTGATTGAT arrangement, is good evidence for a ONECUT factor, but it cannot say which of the three; the in vitro models are interchangeable. An ATCGAT-only match is genuinely ambiguous between ONECUT and CUX, and one Vierstra archetype is labelled CUX/ONECUT for exactly that reason - resolve it with expression data, not with the motif. Evidence quality here is good: the HOCOMOCO A-grade models HNF6.H14CORE.0.PM.A and ONEC2.H14CORE.1.PM.A carry methyl-HT-SELEX (M) support, so the sequence claim does not rest on ChIP alone. Be cautious with the 28-bit tandem-repeat model, which will only match clustered sites and will miss ordinary single occurrences.
families.caveats: The three ONECUT paralogues share one motif, so a hit identifies the family only; use tissue expression to guess which one. ONECUT and CUX both prefer ATCGAT, and one Vierstra archetype is labelled CUX/ONECUT, so an ATCGAT-only match cannot be assigned between the two families. The TATTGATT core is short and AT-rich, giving roughly 10^5 expected chance matches genome-wide, so a single hit without footprint or expression support is weak. One ChIP-derived ONECUT2 model is a six-fold tandem repeat and behaves very differently from the single-site models - check which model produced your hit before interpreting its score.

families.name: TCF/LEF (HMG box)
families.def: WNT response element CTTTGWW. TCF7, TCF7L1, TCF7L2, LEF1.
families.short: TCF/LEF proteins are the DNA-binding end of the canonical Wnt pathway. Humans have four: TCF7 (TCF-1), TCF7L1 (TCF-3), TCF7L2 (TCF-4) and LEF1. Each binds DNA through a single SRY-type HMG box plus an adjacent basic region, reading the minor groove of the Wnt response element CTTTGWW and bending the helix sharply. None activates transcription on its own: an N-terminal domain recruits beta-catenin, which supplies the coactivators, and without nuclear beta-catenin the same proteins repress through TLE/Groucho. Wnt response elements control intestinal crypt renewal, hair follicle and limb development, and T cell differentiation; they are constitutively occupied in APC-mutant colorectal cancer, and an intronic variant at TCF7L2 is the largest-effect common risk allele for type 2 diabetes.
families.long:
## The factors

Four human genes encode TCF/LEF proteins: TCF7 (originally TCF-1), TCF7L1 (TCF-3), TCF7L2
(TCF-4) and LEF1. Each carries one HMG box of the same SRY-related, sequence-specific type used
by SOX proteins, together with an adjacent basic region. The HMG box binds entirely in the minor
groove and bends DNA sharply; the LEF-1 solution structure showed the box in a widened minor
groove of a markedly distorted helix, with the basic region lying across the narrowed major
groove and adding to recognition. Because of that geometry these proteins were first described
as architectural factors that bring proteins at flanking sites into contact, the original
example being Ets-1, RUNX and ATF/CREB at the TCR-alpha enhancer. Transcriptional output comes
from partners rather than from the HMG box: an N-terminal domain binds the armadillo repeats of
beta-catenin, whose groove accommodates the extended TCF peptide, and without nuclear beta-
catenin the same proteins repress through TLE/Groucho and histone deacetylases. Alternative
splicing produces "E-tail" isoforms of TCF7 and TCF7L2 carrying a 30-residue cysteine clamp
(C-clamp), a second and independent DNA-binding module. TCF7 and LEF1 are highest in T
lymphocytes and progenitors, TCF7L1 is broad and prominent in embryonic stem cells, and TCF7L2
is broad with high levels in intestine, pancreatic islets and brain.

## The motif

The Wnt response element, also called the TCF binding element, is written CTTTGWW (W = A/T),
most often CTTTGAT or CTTTGAA, and AWWCAAAG on the opposite strand. The medoid of the 18 models
collected here is AGATCAAAG, the reverse complement of CTTTGATCT; the databases differ in which
strand they display, not in what they measured. Cyclic selection with full-length LEF-1 and
TCF-1E gave the extended element TYYCTTTGATSTT. The invariant part is the CTTTG pentamer, where
the HMG box inserts into the minor groove; the two positions after it are read with help from
the basic region and from residues C-terminal to the box, and site selection on Tcf1 showed the
functional element to be about 12 base pairs, not the 6-8 usually assumed for an HMG box. E-tail
isoforms additionally bind a GC-rich helper element, RCCG, near the core. The C-clamp does not
change which WRE is recognized, but it restricts occupancy to sites carrying the extra block,
and that is visible here: the two longest models (HOCOMOCO TCF7L1, CAGCGCCTCGATGT, 18.0 bits;
Vierstra AC0308 LEF/TCF, CAGCGCCCCGATG, 17.4 bits) pair a GC-rich block with the core instead of
extending the AT-rich flanks. All four proteins give the same motif - cohesion 0.84, the
tightest family in the HMG class - so sequence cannot separate TCF7, TCF7L1, TCF7L2 and LEF1,
and the archetypes are named "LEF/TCF" and "TCF7L/LEF". The boundary that does matter is with
SOX: the reverse complement of CTTTGWW is WWCAAAG, and the SRY/SOX consensus is WWCAAWG,
identical except that SOX tolerates T where TCF/LEF requires A.

## Where it acts

Wnt response elements are predominantly distal. Genome-wide mapping of TCF7L2 in colorectal
cancer cells placed most occupied sites well away from transcription start sites, often in
clusters of several elements per responsive gene, and recovered the CTTTG core as the enriched
motif. Canonical targets include AXIN2, LGR5, ASCL2, SP5, NKD1, CDX1, MYC and LEF1 itself. In
intestinal epithelium TCF7L2 sites co-occur with CDX2, HNF4A, GATA6 and SOX9 sites; in T cells
TCF7 sites co-occur with RUNX and GATA3. With two degenerate positions, CTTTGWW is expected on
the order of 1.5 million times in a 3.1 Gb double-stranded genome, so the element is not what
limits output - nuclear beta-catenin level, chromatin state and the presence of a C-clamp helper
site are.

## Biology and disease

TCF/LEF proteins convert Wnt signaling into transcription. Beta-catenin was shown to bind LEF-1
and convert it into an activator, and the Drosophila experiment with Armadillo and dTCF
established that this is the pathway's output step. In colorectal cancer with APC loss, beta-
catenin accumulates and forms a constitutive complex with TCF7L2 that holds Wnt targets on;
activating CTNNB1 mutations produce the same result. LEF1 is required for hair follicle, tooth
and limb development; TCF7 for thymocyte development, and TCF1 marks the stem-like CD8 T cell
population that responds to checkpoint blockade; TCF7L1 restrains differentiation in embryonic
stem cells. The intronic TCF7L2 variant rs7903146 was identified as a common risk allele for
type 2 diabetes and remains the largest-effect common variant for that disease, acting through
islet function.

## Reading a hit

A CTTTGWW match identifies a Wnt response element, not which TCF/LEF protein uses it: all four
are identical on DNA. Choosing among them needs expression data; deciding whether the site is
active needs evidence about beta-catenin. The bigger practical hazard is the SOX family:
CTTTGTT-type sequences satisfy both consensuses, several HOCOMOCO SOX models (SOX4, SOX11,
SOX13, one SOX2 model) read CCTTTGTT, and there is no sequence-only way to resolve them - an AT-
rich flank leans SOX, a GC-rich RCCG block leans an E-tail TCF. The element is common enough to
occur by chance more than a million times, so isolated matches are weak evidence. Three of the
seven HOCOMOCO models here are ChIP-only; prefer the HT-SELEX and methyl-HT-SELEX models when
the question is whether a protein binds a sequence. Finally, do not read the GC-rich block of
the long TCF7L1 models as a WRE - it is the helper site, and alone it is not a TCF/LEF motif.
families.caveats: Good confidence that a CTTTGWW match is a Wnt response element; none at all about which of TCF7, TCF7L1, TCF7L2 and LEF1 binds it, since all four share one motif (cohesion 0.84) and the archetypes are named "LEF/TCF". The element overlaps the SOX consensus at all but one position, so CTTTGTT-type hits cannot be assigned to TCF/LEF rather than SOX from sequence alone. Roughly 1.5 million matches are expected by chance genome-wide. Occupancy depends on nuclear beta-catenin and, for E-tail isoforms, on a nearby GC-rich helper site; the GC block in the longest TCF7L1 and LEF/TCF models is that helper, not the core element.

families.name: SNAIL / SCRATCH
families.def: E-box CAGGTG. SNAI1-3, SCRT1/2.
families.short: The SNAIL/SCRATCH proteins - SNAI1 (Snail), SNAI2 (Slug), SNAI3 (Smuc), SCRT1 and SCRT2 - are C2H2 zinc-finger repressors that read the E-box CAGGTG, the same 6 bp core that basic helix-loop-helix activators use. They carry no HLH domain; specificity comes from four or five zinc fingers, and repression from an N-terminal SNAG peptide that recruits LSD1/CoREST. SNAI1 and SNAI2 repress E-cadherin and drive epithelial-mesenchymal transition in gastrulation, neural crest migration, fibrosis and carcinoma; SCRT1 and SCRT2 do related work in neurons. SCRATCH sites carry an extra CAAC, giving the only sequence feature that separates part of this family. SNAI2 deletion causes Waardenburg syndrome type 2D and piebaldism.
families.long:
## The factors

Five human proteins fall in this family: SNAI1 (Snail), SNAI2 (Slug), SNAI3 (Smuc) and the more distant SCRT1 and SCRT2 (Scratch). All are small, 250-330 residue proteins with four to five C-terminal C2H2 zinc fingers and an N-terminal SNAG domain - a short, highly conserved peptide that docks into the substrate pocket of the histone demethylase LSD1 and so brings the LSD1/CoREST corepressor complex to DNA. They bind DNA as monomers; there is no dimerization interface, and no HLH or leucine zipper. SNAI1 is labile, phosphorylated by GSK3-beta and degraded by beta-TrCP, which makes its protein level a signaling readout rather than a transcriptional one. SNAI1 and SNAI2 are expressed in mesoderm, neural crest, and in mesenchymal and carcinoma cells; SNAI3 is largely restricted to hematopoietic tissue and muscle; SCRT1 and SCRT2 are neural. The superfamily is ancient - Snail and Scratch orthologues are present throughout bilaterians, with the SNAG domain a vertebrate/arthropod-shared feature - and the Drosophila Snail protein that gave the family its name performs the same kind of repression in dorsoventral patterning.

## The motif

The defining site is the E-box CAGGTG (CACCTG on the other strand). It was mapped for Drosophila SNAIL by random-site selection as 5'-(G/A)(A/T)(G/A)A-CAGGTG-(C/T)AC-3', with a highly conserved 6 bp core; the same study noted that the core is identical to the bHLH binding core and that SNAIL bound CAGGTG far better than other CANNTG boxes. Vertebrate SNAI1/2/3 models agree: HOCOMOCO and JASPAR render them gCAGGTG, ggCAGGTGc or gCACCTGT, 10-14 bits, and they are mutually indistinguishable (pairwise similarities 0.95-0.99). The SCRATCH paralogues are the exception worth knowing: SCRT1 and SCRT2 models are consistently GCAACAGGTG, 16-18 bits, with a 5' CAAC that adds real information and separates them from the SNAI models (best similarity to a SNAI motif only 0.80-0.84). Structurally the fingers contact the major groove over the core; because the flanks in the SNAI models are weak, essentially all the discriminating power is in the six core bases plus, for SCRATCH, the upstream CAAC. The family data also contains a Vierstra archetype, AC0083:SNAI/TCF:bHLH, in which SNAIL motifs cluster with TCF (E-protein) motifs and the cluster is labelled bHLH - a direct demonstration that these C2H2 motifs are not separable from bHLH motifs by sequence.

## Where it acts

SNAI sites are classically proximal-promoter elements. The human CDH1 promoter carries three E-boxes, including the E-pal element, and both SNAI1 and SNAI2 bind them; other epithelial targets (CLDNs, OCLN, KRT8) follow the same pattern. Beyond promoters, SNAI1 occupies thousands of enhancers in mesenchymal cells. CAGGTG contains no CpG, is not CpG-island-restricted, and occurs on the order of a million times in the human genome by chance, so genome-wide occupancy is chromatin- and cofactor-limited. SNAI factors co-occur with ZEB1/ZEB2 on the same boxes (the two families cooperate sequentially in EMT, with SNAI1 induction preceding ZEB1), with TGF-beta-driven SMAD complexes, and with LSD1/CoREST and PRC2. SCRT1/SCRT2 act at neuronal promoters, where SCRT2 represses miR-25.

## Biology and disease

Snai1-null mouse embryos die during gastrulation with a mesodermal layer that fails to complete EMT and retains E-cadherin. Snai2-null mice are viable with pigmentation and hair defects, and in humans heterozygous or homozygous SNAI2 deletions cause Waardenburg syndrome type 2D and piebaldism, a neural crest phenotype. SNAI1 also blocks the cell cycle and confers resistance to apoptosis, which is part of why EMT and proliferation are often anticorrelated. Sustained SNAI1 expression in kidney tubular epithelium produces a partial EMT that drives renal fibrosis and is reversible in mice. In carcinoma, SNAI1 and SNAI2 are induced at invasive fronts and correlate with loss of E-cadherin, but the degree to which a complete EMT occurs in human tumors, and its necessity for metastasis, remains disputed; consensus guidelines now favor describing hybrid intermediate states and caution against inferring EMT from any single marker.

## Reading a hit

A CAGGTG hit tells you that an E-box is present, not which protein family reads it. The candidate list includes the bHLH factors (TCF3/4/12, MYOD, TWIST, NEUROD, MAX, USF), ZEB1/ZEB2, INSM-related repressors and ZBTB18, alongside SNAI1-3. E-box does not mean bHLH. Within this family, SNAI1, SNAI2 and SNAI3 cannot be told apart from sequence; a hit identifies "a SNAIL-family site" at best. SCRT1/SCRT2 are the one real discrimination available: if the match extends to GCAACAGGTG, SCRATCH becomes the better guess, and the neural expression restriction helps. Evidence codes matter here. The HOCOMOCO SNAI1, SNAI2, SCRT1 and SCRT2 models are grade A with PSM evidence, meaning they are supported by ChIP-seq plus HT-SELEX and methyl-HT-SELEX, so "this protein binds this sequence" is on firm in vitro ground. SNAI3 rests on HT-SELEX alone at grade C, and the JASPAR SNAI2 (MA0745.3) and SCRT1 (MA0743.3) matrices are ChIP-seq-derived from ReMap, where indirect binding through a partner on the same E-box cannot be excluded.
families.caveats: The core is 6 bp, CpG-free, and shared with bHLH activators as well as with ZEB, INSM and ZBTB18, so an unqualified CAGGTG match supports "E-box" only; expect roughly a million chance occurrences genome-wide. SNAI1, SNAI2 and SNAI3 are indistinguishable from each other. SCRT1/SCRT2 are separable only because of the 5' CAAC extension. One Vierstra archetype in this family (AC0083:SNAI/TCF:bHLH) merges SNAIL with E-protein motifs and is labelled bHLH, which should be read as a statement about clustering, not about biology. ChIP-derived matrices here (JASPAR SNAI2, SCRT1) can reflect a partner bound to the same box.

families.name: Myogenic bHLH (MyoD)
families.def: Muscle E-box CAGCTG with AT-flank preference. MYOD1, MYF5, MYF6, MYOG, MSC, MYOR.
families.short: The four myogenic regulatory factors — MYOD1, MYF5, MYF6 (MRF4) and MYOG — plus the related repressor MSC (musculin/MyoR) are class II basic helix-loop-helix proteins restricted to the skeletal muscle lineage. They bind DNA as heterodimers with the ubiquitous class I E-proteins TCF3, TCF4 and TCF12, reading the E-box CAGCTG with a preference for A/T-rich flanks (AACAGCTGTT). MYOD1 was the first transcription factor shown to reprogram cell identity: transfecting it alone converts fibroblasts into myoblasts. Whether a myogenic bHLH activates muscle genes depends less on where it binds than on three residues in its basic region — the "myogenic code" — so an occupied E-box and an active one are not the same thing.
families.long:
## The factors

Four myogenic regulatory factors (MRFs) define this family: MYOD1, MYF5, MYF6 (MRF4) and MYOG (myogenin). The atlas also places MSC (musculin, also called MyoR and ABF-1) here, on motif similarity. All are class II bHLH proteins of about 68 residues in the DNA-binding domain, and all work as heterodimers with the broadly expressed class I E-proteins TCF3 (E12/E47), TCF4 and TCF12; MYOD1 can homodimerise in vitro, but the heterodimer is the active species in cells. MYOD1 and MYF5 act as determination factors and are largely interchangeable for that job, while MYOG and MYF6 act later in differentiation. Expression is restricted to the skeletal muscle lineage: MYF5 in early somitic and satellite-cell progenitors, MYOD1 in activated myoblasts and satellite cells, MYOG and MYF6 in differentiating and mature fibres. MSC is the odd member — a muscle-restricted bHLH that antagonises MyoD rather than cooperating with it, so a site assigned to this family can be an activating or a repressing site depending on which protein is present. MYOD1's historical importance is that transfecting it alone converts fibroblasts into myoblasts, the first demonstration that one transcription factor can switch cell identity.

## The motif

The core is the E-box CANNTG, and the myogenic version is CAGCTG, usually written with its A/T-rich flanks as AACAGCTGTT. The data agree: the representative model is the Vierstra archetype `AC0075:MYOD/MYOG:bHLH` with consensus AACAGCTGTC, and JASPAR MSC, MYF6 and CIS-BP MYOG models all read AACAGCTGTT. Each monomer reads one CAN half-site through a basic-region glutamate and arginine, which is why CA...TG is fixed while the central two bases are loosely specified. Binding-site selection with MyoD and E2A complexes showed exactly this: both recognise CA--TG but differ in their flanking and internal preferences, consistent with independent half-site recognition.

The interesting part of the myogenic story is not the sequence but three residues in the protein. Replacing MyoD's helices or loop with the equivalent *Drosophila* achaete-scute sequence leaves both DNA binding and muscle-gene activation intact; replacing the basic region preserves DNA binding but abolishes activation. Transferring just three MyoD residues (Ala114, Thr115 and Lys124) into E12 confers myogenic specificity. The crystal structure of the MyoD bHLH-DNA complex then showed that Ala114 and Thr115 are buried at the protein-DNA interface, not exposed for coactivator contacts, and may instead fix the conformation of Arg111. So the "myogenic code" is a DNA-proximal effect, and binding is necessary but not sufficient: functional selection of transcriptionally active MyoD sites recovered sequences resembling real muscle promoters rather than the optimal in vitro binding site.

Two caveats about CAGCTG follow from this. First, genome-wide comparison of MYOD and NEUROD2 found CAGCTG shared between them, with CAGGTG (CACCTG on the other strand) as the MYOD-preferred motif and CAGATG as the NEUROD2-preferred one, and only the factor-specific sites tracked with transcription. JASPAR's MYOD1 MA0499.3 is indeed a GCACCTGTC-type model. Second, none of the four MRFs is distinguishable from the others: cohesion is 0.88 and the family is one motif.

## Where it acts

MRF sites sit in distal muscle enhancers and promoters — the MCK enhancer, the myogenin promoter, desmin, myosin heavy-chain and troponin loci — and are AT-rich rather than CpG-island-associated. Genome-wide, MYOD1 occupies far more sites than it activates, including many in non-muscle chromatin, and occupancy is largely limited to E-boxes that are already accessible; the cell's chromatin state, not the motif, picks the target set. Characteristic co-occurring motifs are MEF2 (an A/T-rich site often within a helical turn or two of the E-box in muscle enhancers), SRF/CArG, TEAD/MCAT, SIX and PBX/MEIS; MYOD1 also binds with PBX1 at some promoters. A "muscle E-box pair" of two CAGCTG sites is common in MRF-dependent enhancers but has no fixed spacing rule.

## Biology and disease

Mice lacking both *Myod1* and *Myf5* form no skeletal muscle and no myoblasts, whereas single mutants are near-normal, showing the two are redundant determination factors. *Myog*-null mice reach birth but have a severe deficit of differentiated fibres and die perinatally. MSC/MyoR was identified as a muscle-restricted bHLH that inhibits MyoD-driven myogenesis. In human disease, the MRFs are both markers and drivers of rhabdomyosarcoma: MYOD1 and MYOG immunostaining is diagnostic, and a recurrent somatic MYOD1 p.Leu122Arg substitution defines an aggressive subset of embryonal/spindle-cell tumours. That mutation is instructive for motif work — it lies in the basic region and redirects MYOD1 to MYC consensus sequences, converting a differentiation factor into a proliferative one.

## Reading a hit

A CAGCTG match with A/T flanks is consistent with an MRF site but cannot name the factor, and cannot separate MRFs from E-protein homodimers, ASCL1/2, NHLH1/2, ATOH8, TCF21 or TWIST2, all of which give CAGCTG models. The A/T flank preference is real but worth only a bit or two. The strongest in vitro support in this family is `MYOD1.H14CORE.1.PSM.A` (grade A, ChIP plus HT-SELEX plus methyl-SELEX), so "MyoD binds CAGCTG" is well grounded; the MSC label is shakier, because the HOCOMOCO in vitro model `MUSC.H14CORE.0.SM.B` reads CATATGGT, a NeuroD/Atonal-type site, and is flagged as matching the TWIST/HAND family instead. One CIS-BP MYF5 model is inferred from the mouse protein (90% DBD identity), which is benign but should be noted. Because CAGCTG is one of the commonest six-mers in the genome, treat an isolated hit as a hypothesis requiring muscle expression, accessibility or conservation.
families.caveats: CAGCTG is among the most frequent six-mers in mammalian genomes and is read by E-protein homodimers, ASCL1/2, NHLH1/2, ATOH8, TCF21 and TWIST2 as well as by the MRFs, so a match places a site in the broad class II bHLH space rather than in muscle. The four MRFs share one motif and cannot be distinguished; nor can the activator MYOD1 be distinguished from the repressor MSC, whose in vitro model in HOCOMOCO is a CATATG site that clusters with TWIST/HAND instead. Binding also does not imply activation: the myogenic code governs activation, not affinity. Muscle-lineage expression and open chromatin are required to make a hit meaningful.

families.name: TEAD
families.def: MCAT element GGAATG. TEAD1-4.
families.short: The four human TEAD proteins (TEAD1-4, formerly TEF-1, TEF-4, TEF-5 and TEF-3) bind the MCAT element GGAATG, read on the other strand as CATTCC. The DNA-binding TEA domain is a three-helix bundle with a homeodomain-like fold, and two TEADs load cooperatively onto tandem MCAT sites. TEADs have no activation domain of their own: they are the DNA-binding platform for the Hippo pathway coactivators YAP and TAZ, and for the VGLL proteins that compete with them. The motif is therefore the readout of Hippo signaling status on chromatin. TEAD sites drive muscle gene expression, trophectoderm specification and organ size control, and are central to YAP-driven cancers.
families.long:
## The factors

Four human genes, TEAD1, TEAD2, TEAD3 and TEAD4, share an N-terminal TEA (also called ATTS) DNA
binding domain and a C-terminal YAP-binding domain. TEAD1 (TEF-1) and TEAD3 (TEF-5) are broadly
expressed with enrichment in muscle and placenta, TEAD2 (TEF-4) in neural and embryonic tissue,
TEAD4 (TEF-3) in skeletal muscle, trophectoderm and many carcinomas. TEADs bind DNA as monomers
but load cooperatively onto tandem sites via a loop in the TEA domain. They carry no intrinsic
transactivation domain, so their output depends entirely on which partner occupies the
YAP-binding domain: YAP or TAZ (WWTR1) when Hippo signaling is off, or a VGLL protein
(VGLL1-VGLL4) competing for the same surface. Structures of the YAP-TEAD, TAZ-TEAD and VGLL1-TEAD
complexes show how the same interface is reused. TEADs are also palmitoylated on a conserved
cysteine in a hydrophobic central pocket; this auto-palmitoylation is required for stability and
for YAP/TAZ binding, and it is the target of the current generation of TEAD inhibitors.

## The motif

The literature name is the MCAT (muscle CAT) element, GGAATG, equivalently CATTCC on the opposite
strand; older papers also call it the Sph motif or the GT-IIC element of the SV40 enhancer. Six
bases carry essentially all the information, with the GGAAT core most constrained. The solution
structure of the TEA domain showed a three-helix bundle with a homeodomain fold, and revealed that
the L1 loop is what allows two TEAD molecules to load cooperatively onto tandemly duplicated MCAT
sites. That explains the pattern in this family's data: single-site models span 6-9 columns with
10-13 bits, while the most informative models (up to 21 bits) are tandem pairs such as
CATTCC-N(2)-CATTCC, which represent the cooperative arrangement rather than a longer monomer
footprint. Database models divide simply into the forward-strand rendering (GGAATG, GGAATGT) and
the reverse rendering (ACATTCC, CATTCCA); they are the same motif and the family is one of the
most cohesive in these collections. No TEAD paralogue is distinguishable from another by sequence.
An in vitro microarray study also found that the isolated TEA domain binds a broader set of
sequences than the sites recovered with the full-length protein, so the narrow GGAATG consensus
partly reflects constraints outside the DNA-binding domain.

## Where it acts

TEAD/YAP sites are overwhelmingly enhancer elements, not promoters. YAP-TEAD complexes occupy
thousands of distal enhancers and act largely through enhancer-promoter contacts and release of
paused RNA polymerase; TEAD motifs are among the most enriched motifs in the accessible chromatin
of proliferating and mechanically stimulated cells. The classic promoter-proximal cases are
muscle: MCAT elements in the cardiac troponin T, beta-myosin heavy chain and smooth muscle
alpha-actin promoters. Recurrent co-occurring motifs are AP-1 (JUN/FOS), which forms functional
composite TEAD-AP-1 enhancers in many YAP-driven contexts, plus RUNX, MYOD E-boxes in muscle, and
CDX2/GATA3 in trophectoderm. Because GGAATG is only 6 bp, chance matches are extremely numerous;
occupancy is set by chromatin state and by whether YAP/TAZ are nuclear.

## Biology and disease

TEAD4 specifies the trophectoderm lineage in the mouse preimplantation embryo, and its activity is
restricted to outer cells by Hippo signaling through LATS and YAP, making this the earliest known
cell-fate decision read out through a TEAD motif. In muscle, MCAT elements coordinate the
cardiac and smooth muscle differentiation programs. A missense mutation in TEAD1 that weakens its
interaction with YAP and TAZ causes Sveinsson chorioretinal atrophy, a dominant retinal
degeneration, and is the clearest human germline TEAD disease. In cancer, TEAD activity is the
effector of Hippo pathway loss: NF2 (merlin) inactivation in mesothelioma and schwannoma, LATS1/2
loss, and YAP1 or WWTR1 fusions all converge on TEAD-driven transcription, and YAP1-TFE3 and
TAZ-CAMTA1 fusions in epithelioid hemangioendothelioma retain the TEAD-binding function.
Small-molecule inhibitors of TEAD auto-palmitoylation selectively suppress NF2-deficient
mesothelioma in preclinical models and have entered clinical testing. VGLL4 acts as a tumor
suppressor by competing with YAP for the same TEAD surface.

## Reading a hit

GGAATG is 6 bp and occurs on the order of a million times in the human genome, so an isolated
match is close to meaningless. Three things upgrade a hit: a tandem pair of MCAT sites within
about 15 bp, which is the cooperative binding arrangement; an adjacent AP-1 site, which marks the
functional TEAD-AP-1 composite enhancers; and open chromatin in a cell with nuclear YAP or TAZ. A
hit never identifies a paralogue; TEAD1 through TEAD4 share one matrix, and in most tissues more
than one is expressed. Equally important, a TEAD motif hit says nothing about the direction of the
output, because the same site is bound by TEAD with YAP/TAZ (activating) or with VGLL4
(repressing), and TEAD occupancy in the absence of a coactivator does little. ChIP-derived TEAD
motifs are reasonably trustworthy here: HOCOMOCO grade-A models for TEAD1-4 combine ChIP-seq with
in vitro selection (evidence codes PS or PSM), so direct binding is independently supported. The
converse caution applies to the reverse: YAP and TAZ ChIP-seq recovers the TEAD motif even though
YAP and TAZ do not touch DNA, a textbook case of a coactivator "having" the motif of the protein
that recruits it. If a database entry attributes GGAATG to YAP1, WWTR1 or a VGLL protein, that is
indirect binding.
families.caveats: GGAATG carries about 6 bits, so single hits are expected by chance and are not evidence on their own; tandem MCAT pairs and neighboring AP-1 sites are what make a hit credible. TEAD1-4 share one matrix and cannot be separated by sequence. A hit does not indicate activation: the same site is used by TEAD-YAP/TAZ and by repressive TEAD-VGLL4 complexes, and TEAD without a coactivator is largely inert. Any GGAATG motif attributed to YAP1, WWTR1/TAZ or a VGLL protein is indirect, since those proteins do not contact DNA. TEAD's own models are supported by in vitro selection as well as ChIP-seq.

families.name: IRX (TALE, Iroquois)
families.def: ACA-rich TALE sites. IRX1-6.
families.short: IRX1 through IRX6, with the related factor MKX (Mohawk), form the Iroquois branch of the TALE homeodomain superclass - homeodomains carrying three extra residues between helices 1 and 2. Unlike most homeodomain proteins they do not read a TAAT core. Their recognition unit is a short ACA, and the functional site is an inverted repeat of it, so models in these databases range from the half-site CATGT up to long palindromes such as ACATGnnnnnCATGT. The IRX genes sit in two clusters, IRX1/2/4 and IRX3/5/6, and pattern the heart, limb, kidney and nervous system. IRX3 is best known outside developmental biology as the gene connected by long-range enhancer contacts to the obesity-associated variants inside FTO.
families.long:
## The factors

The Iroquois genes are one of the five branches of the TALE superclass, which is defined by a three-amino-acid insertion between helices 1 and 2 of the homeodomain. Humans have six, arranged in two clusters that arose by duplication: IRX1, IRX2 and IRX4 on chromosome 5, and IRX3, IRX5 and IRX6 on chromosome 16. Each protein carries a TALE homeodomain plus a C-terminal Iro box. MKX (Mohawk) is an IRX-related TALE homeodomain protein assigned to this family in the motif data; it acts as a repressor and recruits the Sin3A/HDAC corepressor complex. Iroquois proteins form homodimers and heterodimers, which is part of how a very short recognition core is turned into a usable site. Expression is broad but regional: IRX1/2/4 and IRX3/5 are prominent in heart, limb bud, kidney, lung and neural tube, with IRX4 largely ventricle-specific; MKX is expressed in tendon and the precursors of skeletal muscle, cartilage and bone.

## The motif

This family is the clearest example in the atlas of a homeodomain that has abandoned the TAAT core. In vitro site selection with *Drosophila* Mirror defined an Iroquois-binding sequence recognized by the other fly Iroquois proteins and by vertebrate IRX factors, and used in vivo to mediate repression. Bacterial one-hybrid selection with the mouse MKX homeodomain gave a monomeric core of just three bases, A-C-A, and the minimal Mohawk response element in the Mkx promoter is a conserved inverted repeat of that core - the same architecture the human IRX models show. Because the reverse complement of ACA is TGT, the inverted repeat is ACA-TGT, most compactly ACATGT, which is itself palindromic. The databases capture this at several spacings: CIS-BP M05319 gives tACAtGaatattCaTGTa and HOCOMOCO IRX3.H14CORE.2.S.C gives ACAtGnaaaaaCATGTa (ACATG and CATGT separated by five to seven bases), the Vierstra archetype AC0476 gives ACacGawaawtCaTGT, AC0460 gives the tandem ACAtgACA, and the shortest models collapse to the half-site CATGTt or aACATG. The pooled consensus is therefore the half-site CATGTt with cohesion 0.77 - a number that reflects spacer variability, not disagreement about the core. Two methyl-HT-SELEX models for IRX3 and IRX5 instead read ACGCGTaA, a CpG-containing palindrome, so methylation status may matter for a subset of sites. IRX1-6 are not distinguishable from one another by sequence.

## Where it acts

IRX sites occur in developmental enhancers rather than housekeeping promoters, and because the core is 3 bp the useful signal is always the paired arrangement plus its spacing. An exact ACATGT is expected on the order of 10^6 times in 3.1 Gb, so single-half-site matches should not be acted on. The longer palindromic forms with a 5-7 bp AT-rich spacer are much more discriminating. The best-documented regulatory context is the FTO/IRX3 locus, where obesity-associated variants in FTO introns make long-range functional contacts with the IRX3 promoter, so IRX3 rather than FTO is the effector gene. In heart, Irx3 and Irx5 act on conduction-system and repolarization genes and have both cooperative and antagonistic roles, giving a regional readout from the same motif.

## Biology and disease

Irx3/Irx5 double mutants in mouse have cardiac morphogenetic defects and abnormal postnatal cardiac physiology, and Irx4 loss affects ventricular identity. Homozygous loss-of-function mutations in human IRX5 cause Hamamy syndrome, with craniofacial anomalies and impaired germ cell migration attributable to reduced SDF1/CXCL12. Variants in the FTO first intron act on IRX3 to influence body mass, and IRX3 and IRX5 have also been implicated in adipocyte browning. Mkx-null mice have tendon hypoplasia, and MKX loss de-represses Sox6 and shifts skeletal muscle away from slow fiber gene expression.

## Reading a hit

Treat a bare CATGT or ACATG match as noise: 5 bp is not enough, and CATG is also the core of several unrelated motifs. What is interpretable is a paired ACATG...CATGT arrangement, ideally with the AT-rich spacer the high-information models show. The hit identifies the Iroquois branch, not a paralogue - all six IRX models are the same. Two members of this family in CIS-BP are cross-species transfers, one from *Drosophila melanogaster* at 98% DNA-binding-domain identity and one from mouse, and both are extremely low information (aAACA and AcA); do not treat them as independent human evidence. The MKX model here is graded A in HOCOMOCO with integrative and in vitro support but is still only five informative bases.
families.caveats: The recognition core is three bases, so short matches are essentially uninformative and only paired ACATG...CATGT arrangements with their AT-rich spacer are worth interpreting. IRX1-6 share one model, so a hit identifies the Iroquois branch and never a paralogue. Two CIS-BP members are inherited from non-human proteins (one from Drosophila at 98% DBD identity, one from mouse) and carry almost no information. Spacer length varies between models, so scores depend heavily on which matrix you used. Because the CATG core is shared with unrelated motifs, expect a high false-positive rate without footprint or expression support.

families.name: CDX / PDX / anterior gut HD
families.def: TTTATG / CTTTAT. CDX1/2/4, PDX1, and related ParaHox factors.
families.short: This family groups the caudal-related factors CDX1, CDX2 and CDX4 with PDX1, all encoded by ParaHox genes - an ancient cluster that is the evolutionary sister of the Hox cluster. The CDX proteins read TTTATG, usually extended to TTTATGGC, a site distinct enough to be recognizable. PDX1 is a different case: its in vitro motif is plain TAATTA, indistinguishable from the generic Q50 homeodomain site, so PDX1 specificity in vivo comes from partners rather than from the sequence it prefers. CDX2 patterns the posterior gut and is the standard immunohistochemical marker of intestinal epithelium; PDX1 is required for pancreas development and its loss causes pancreatic agenesis and MODY4.
families.long:
## The factors

Four human proteins: CDX1, CDX2 and CDX4, the vertebrate relatives of *Drosophila* caudal, and PDX1 (also IPF1, IDX1, STF1), the vertebrate Xlox gene. All four are ParaHox genes. The ParaHox cluster - Gsx, Xlox/PDX1 and Cdx - is an evolutionary sister of the Hox cluster, which explains why these proteins carry ordinary 60-residue three-helix homeodomains with the same helix 3 recognition chemistry as HOX proteins, and no second DNA-binding domain. CDX1 and CDX2 are expressed throughout the intestinal epithelium, CDX2 most strongly and persisting into adulthood; CDX4 is largely embryonic, with a role in hematopoiesis; PDX1 is restricted to the pancreatic buds and then to beta cells, duodenum and antral stomach. Unlike most families in this group, specificity here does not come from an extra domain in the same polypeptide - it comes either from the extended site that the CDX homeodomain itself prefers, or, for PDX1, from a protein complex.

## The motif

The CDX site is written in the literature as TTTAT(G/A) and in these databases as an extended TTTATGGC, equivalently GCCATAAA on the other strand. CDX2 and CDX1 HT-SELEX models both read TTTATggC, CDX4 gives TTTTATGaC, and the JASPAR models for CDX1, CDX2 and CDX4 render the reverse complement GC(a)ATAAAA. The 5' TTTAT is the homeodomain core - the same TAAT-type element every Q50 homeodomain reads, here with a 3' extension - and the discriminating information sits in the GGC/TGC that follows. Methyl-HT-SELEX models for CDX1, CDX2 and CDX4 instead read TTTACGAC, a CpG-containing variant, so a subset of CDX sites is methylation-sensitive. The pooled consensus is TTTATggC with cohesion 0.84. PDX1 is the exception, and it is worth being explicit about it: the A-grade HOCOMOCO model PDX1.H14CORE.1.PSM.A reads cTAATtA and JASPAR MA0132.3 reads TAATTA - a bare Q50 homeodomain site with no extension at all. The nearest neighbours of those models across all four databases lie in the anterior HOX/Q50 groups, and the data flags them as such. A second PDX1 model, the ChIP-derived PDX1.H14CORE.0.P.B, reads TGATTgATGg, whose nearest neighbours are in the TALE family; that is almost certainly the PBX half-site, because PDX1 works in a trimeric complex with PBX1b and MEIS2/MRG1 on the elastase enhancer, so PBX-type sequence is expected in PDX1 ChIP peaks. Neither flagged model means the database entry is wrong; both mean the label is more specific than the sequence.

## Where it acts

CDX sites sit in intestine-specific promoters and enhancers - sucrase-isomaltase, lactase-phlorizin hydrolase, the CDX1 and CDX2 genes themselves - and in posterior HOX cluster enhancers, where CDX factors feed into anteroposterior patterning. The site is 6-8 bp and AT-rich, so exact TTTATGGC matches are expected in the 10^4-10^5 range in 3.1 Gb and most are not occupied. PDX1 sites are concentrated in beta-cell enhancers, for insulin, GCK and SLC2A2, and in acinar enhancers, where PDX1 acts with PBX1 and MEIS2; PDX1 also co-occurs with NKX6-1, NKX2-2, NEUROD1, FOXA2 and the HNF factors, so an islet regulatory element typically carries several of these motifs together. Because CDX and PDX1 are expressed in adjacent but different gut segments, genomic context and tissue usually resolve which factor is plausible.

## Biology and disease

Cdx2 heterozygous mice show homeotic shifts of the axial skeleton and develop intestinal tumors with gastric-type mucosa, and Cdx2 is required for intestinal identity. In humans, CDX1 and CDX2 are ectopically expressed in intestinal metaplasia of the stomach and in gastric carcinoma, and CDX2 immunohistochemistry is routine for identifying intestinal-lineage adenocarcinoma. Ectopic CDX2 perturbs HOX gene expression in murine progenitors and is associated with acute myeloid leukemia. PDX1 loss is severe: Pdx1-null mice fail to form a pancreas, a homozygous frameshift in human IPF1/PDX1 causes pancreatic agenesis with neonatal diabetes, and heterozygous mutations cause MODY4.

## Reading a hit

A TTTATGGC-type match is reasonable evidence for a CDX factor, but it cannot distinguish CDX1, CDX2 and CDX4, whose models are interchangeable; use expression, since CDX2 dominates in adult intestine. Do not use this family's PDX1 models as evidence for PDX1 specifically. TAATTA matches every Q50 homeodomain in the genome, so a TAATTA hit is a homeodomain hit and nothing more, and the ChIP-derived TGATTGATGG model is better read as a PBX/TALE site that happens to lie in PDX1 peaks. In practice, a PDX1 claim should rest on islet chromatin data and co-occurring beta-cell motifs, not on the motif alone. Four of the 17 members of this family are flagged as having nearest neighbours in another family, all four of them PDX1 or short TAAT models - this is a systematic pattern here, not a one-off.
families.caveats: CDX1, CDX2 and CDX4 share one motif; a hit identifies the CDX group, not a member. PDX1 is the real hazard: its in vitro motif is plain TAATTA, indistinguishable from the whole Q50 homeodomain group, and its ChIP-derived model reads a PBX/TALE half-site, consistent with PDX1 acting in a complex with PBX1 and MEIS2. Four of 17 members of this family have nearest neighbours in the HOX/Q50 or TALE families, all of them PDX1 or bare TAAT models, so treat PDX1 matches as unassignable without islet chromatin evidence. CDX sites are short and AT-rich, so chance matches are common.

families.name: ETV2 / ETV6-type
families.def: ETS sites with tandem GGAA repeats favoured by ETV2 and the ETV6 repressor.
families.short: ETV2 (ER71), ETV6 (TEL) and ETV7 (TEL2) are ETS-domain proteins that read the same GGA(A/T) core as the rest of the family. ETV2 is a transient activator required for the specification of blood and endothelium; ETV6 and ETV7 are repressors, and ETV6 spreads repression by polymerizing through its PNT/SAM domain. They are grouped here because their motif models cluster together, not because they share a distinct binding preference: ETV2's selected sequence is the ordinary class I ETS site and ETV6/ETV7 differ from it only marginally. What does recur among these models is arrangement - several are two GGAA cores in tandem or head-to-head. ETV6 is one of the most frequently rearranged genes in leukemia, most famously as ETV6-RUNX1 in childhood B-lineage acute lymphoblastic leukemia.
families.long:
## The factors

Three genes sit in this family. ETV2 (also ER71 or ETSRP) is a transient transcriptional activator
expressed in a narrow window in nascent mesoderm and hemogenic endothelium and essentially silent
in adult tissues. ETV6 (TEL) and ETV7 (TEL2) are transcriptional repressors; ETV6 is broadly
expressed, ETV7 more narrowly and largely in hematopoietic cells. All three carry one ETS domain of
about 85 residues, the family's winged helix-turn-helix fold, and bind DNA as monomers. ETV6 and
ETV7 additionally carry a PNT domain (a SAM domain) that self-associates head-to-tail into an
open-ended polymer, so one DNA-bound ETV6 molecule can nucleate a long repressive assembly; the
polymer interface and its regulation have been mapped biophysically. ETV6 also has an
autoinhibitory element that damps its DNA binding. It is worth stating plainly that this family is
not a biochemical class. Systematic profiling of every human and mouse ETS protein put ETV6 and
ETV7 in a small subclass of their own (class IIb) and did not group ETV2 with them; ETV2's
preference is the ordinary class I preference.

## The motif

The consensus is ACCGGAAGT - the same nine-mer as ETS class I, read the same way, by two invariant
arginines in recognition helix H3 that hydrogen-bond the two guanines of GGA, with wing and turn
lysines contacting the flanks. The in vitro models differ only at the margins: JASPAR's HT-SELEX
model for ETV2 (MA0762.2) is ACCGGAAAT, with A rather than G immediately 3' of the core, while the
ETV6 (MA0645.2) and ETV7 (MA1708.2) HT-SELEX models are plain CCGGAAGT and CGGAAGTG. There is no
sequence that belongs to this family and not to ETS class I. What is distinctive in part of the
collection is arrangement rather than composition: three models here are doubled sites - CIS-BP
M02990 (CCGGAAGCGGAAGT), CIS-BP M04712 (CGGAAGTACTTCCG) and the ETV7 in vitro model
(CCCGGAAGTACTTC) - that is, two ETS cores in tandem or head-to-head. That is consistent with
ETV6's ability to polymerize and with the reported preference of these factors for repeated GGAA,
but doubled and repeated GGAA matrices also occur in ETS class I, where the EWS-FLI1 fusion's GGAA
microsatellite matrices live, so a tandem arrangement does not on its own assign a motif here.

## Where it acts

ETV2 binds enhancers of endothelial and hematopoietic genes during a short developmental window,
acting downstream of BMP, Notch and Wnt signals. ETV6 and ETV7 occupy ETS sites at promoters and
enhancers and repress them, recruiting corepressors rather than activating. The functional point
this family illustrates is competition: because ETV6, ETV7, ERF and ETV3 read the same sequence as
ETS1, ERG, FLI1 and GABPA, the output of a given ETS site depends on which family member happens to
occupy it, not on the sequence. That is also why sites bound by these repressors are not
distinguishable in a scan from sites bound by activators. Notably, the genome-wide footprint
archetypes derived from DNase data contain no archetype for this family: every archetype whose name
includes ETV clustered instead with ELF, ELK or ETS archetypes that are assigned elsewhere in this
atlas.

## Biology and disease

Etv2-null mouse embryos fail to make blood and endothelium, placing ETV2 at the top of the
hematoendothelial program; the gene is now widely used to force endothelial fate in reprogramming
experiments. Mice lacking Tel/Etv6 die around mid-gestation with a yolk sac angiogenic defect and
intra-embryonic apoptosis, and ETV6 is required for adult bone marrow hematopoiesis. ETV6 is among
the most frequently rearranged genes in human leukemia: the t(12;21) fusion ETV6-RUNX1 (TEL-AML1)
is the most common recurrent fusion in childhood B-lineage acute lymphoblastic leukemia, and ETV6
has many other partners including kinases. Germline heterozygous ETV6 mutations cause autosomal
dominant thrombocytopenia with predisposition to hematologic malignancy.

## Reading a hit

This is the family in this atlas where the label deserves the least weight. The motifs assigned
here are not separable from ETS class I, and the data say so directly: for 15 of the 16 models in
this family, most of the nearest neighbours across the four databases are labelled with a different
family, usually ETS class I, and for 14 of them the single best match anywhere is a motif
rather than a motif from this family - including the CIS-BP model that this atlas picks as the
family's representative. One JASPAR entry, the heterodimer model ETV2::FIGLA (MA1941.2), is flagged
outright as belonging with class I. Practical consequences: read a hit as "an ETS site"; use
expression to decide the factor, remembering that ETV2 is effectively absent outside early mesoderm
and engineered endothelial systems, so an ETV2 call in an adult tissue dataset is far more likely a
generic ETS site; and do not try to tell ETV6 from ERF or ETV3, all repressors reading the same
sequence. Four of the seven JASPAR models here are CAP-SELEX heterodimers (ETV2::HOXB13,
ETV2::FIGLA, ETV2::DRGX, ETV2::FOXI1) in which much of the matrix is a HOX, bHLH or FOX site rather
than an ETS site.
families.caveats:
Treat the family label as provisional. Its separation from ETS class I is largely a
clustering outcome: 15 of 16 models here have most of their cross-database nearest neighbours
labelled with another family, usually class I, 14 match a motif outside the family better than any
inside it, and one JASPAR entry (ETV2::FIGLA) is flagged as belonging with class I. The published classification also does not support the grouping - ETV6 and ETV7
form their own small subclass while ETV2 behaves like a class I factor. No genomic-footprint
archetype corresponds to this family. Four of seven JASPAR models are CAP-SELEX heterodimers whose
matrices are partly a HOX, bHLH or FOX site. A hit therefore means "an ETS site"; which of ETV2,
ETV6, ETV7, ERF or ETV3 is bound has to come from expression and ChIP data.
