families.name: Atypical / composite homeodomain
families.def: Homeodomains in unusual architectures: ZHX1-3, ZFHX2/3, HOMEZ, TSHZ1-3, ADNP, HDX, HMBOX1, PROX1-like, HHEX, POU-less HD archetypes.
aka: ZHX / ZFHX / HOMEZ / TSHZ / HMBOX / HHEX group
families.short: This family collects homeodomains that do not behave like homeodomains. Instead of one small domain in a compact protein, these factors bury one to five divergent homeodomains inside large multidomain proteins, usually alongside many C2H2 zinc fingers: ZHX1-3, ZFHX2 and ZFHX3, HOMEZ, TSHZ1-3, HMBOX1, HDX, HHEX, and the SATB-type CUT-plus-homeodomain proteins. Several were discovered as something else entirely, an AT-rich enhancer-binding protein, a telomere repeat-binding protein, a chromatin scaffold protein. Their motifs are correspondingly heterogeneous: there is no single family consensus, several database models carry almost no information, and where a good motif exists it may be read by the zinc fingers rather than by the homeodomain. Useful as a bucket, not as an identifier.
families.long:
## The factors

What unites these proteins is architecture, not sequence preference. Domain annotation gives the flavour.
ZHX1 and ZHX3 are 873 and 956 residues with five annotated homeobox regions each plus two C2H2 zinc
fingers; ZHX2 has four homeoboxes. ZFHX3, originally named ATBF1, is 3,703 residues carrying four
homeodomains and 23 zinc fingers; ZFHX2 is 2,572 residues with three homeodomains and 12 zinc fingers.
HOMEZ is a 550-residue protein with three homeodomains and a leucine-zipper-like region and no zinc
fingers at all. TSHZ2 and TSHZ3, vertebrate teashirt proteins, have five zinc fingers and a single
homeodomain annotated as atypical. HDX has two homeodomains; HMBOX1 has one, embedded in a POU-like
arrangement. HHEX is the outlier in the other direction, a 270-residue protein with a single homeodomain,
but it homo-oligomerises through a proline-rich region rather than working as a monomer. SATB1 and SATB2
pair a divergent homeodomain with two CUT domains. Several of these proteins were characterised before
anyone called them homeodomain factors: ZFHX3/ATBF1 as the AT-motif binding factor of the human
alpha-fetoprotein enhancer, HMBOX1 as HOT1, a direct double-stranded telomere repeat-binding protein,
SATB1 as a matrix-attachment-region binding protein with "unusual binding site recognition", and ZHX1 as an
NF-Y-interacting repressor.

## The motif

There is no single consensus, and the entry deliberately does not offer one. The three best-supported
models are as follows. HOMEZ, from HT-SELEX, reads TAATCGTTT, about 13 bits: a recognisable TAAT core with
an unusual CGTTT extension, and it is reproduced independently in CIS-BP as TATAATCGTTTT and as a footprint
archetype, so it is probably real. HMBOX1 gives CTAGTTA, equivalently TAACTAG, supported by both in vitro
selection and ChIP; this is a TAAT-like core with an inverted 3' half. Notably it does not resemble the
TTAGGG telomeric repeat that HOT1/HMBOX1 was reported to bind directly, and that discrepancy is not
resolved in the literature. TSHZ2 gives a 15-base CATCAAATGGAATC with high information content and grade A
evidence, and it contains no TAAT core whatever; the most economical reading is that the zinc fingers do
the binding, as they do for *Drosophila* teashirt, and the atypical homeodomain contributes little. The
remaining models are close to empty: ZFHX2 is a bare TAATTA at 5.5 bits, ZFHX3 reduces to AAT at 2.5 bits,
HHEX to AT at 1.9, ZHX1 to AC at 1.3, HDX to a single T. Family cohesion is 0.55, the lowest of the
homeodomain groups, which is the expected signature of a bucket.

## Where it acts

Genuinely varied, and for several members not well mapped. HMBOX1/HOT1 localises to telomeres and
associates with actively processed telomere ends. ZHX proteins act as promoter-proximal repressors in
complexes with NF-Y. ZFHX3/ATBF1 was defined at an AT-rich enhancer element and binds AT-rich sequence
generally, which is one reason its motif carries so little information. SATB1 occupies base-unpairing
regions and matrix attachment regions and organises chromatin loops in T cells rather than acting at a
short consensus. TSHZ3 works at neuronal target genes in cortical projection neurons. The general pattern
is that occupancy for these proteins is determined by protein-protein interaction and by regional DNA
character, AT-richness or repeat content, more than by a short high-information consensus, which is exactly
why motif-based prediction performs poorly for them.

## Biology and disease

Several members have solid human genetics. Somatic mutation and deletion of ZFHX3/ATBF1 occur recurrently
in prostate cancer. Deletion of TSHZ3 causes an autism syndrome with defects in cortical projection
neurons. De novo mutations in ADNP, another large protein with a homeodomain in unusual company, cause a
SWI/SNF-related autism syndrome. HHEX, as PRH/Hex, is required for formation of the vertebrate body axis,
the haematopoietic and vascular systems, liver, thyroid and forebrain, and it can both repress and activate
targets and additionally regulate nuclear export of specific mRNAs. HMBOX1/HOT1 is a positive regulator of
telomere length: depletion shortens and overexpression lengthens telomeres, and it promotes chromatin
association of telomerase. SATB1 controls thymocyte development through higher-order chromatin
organisation.

## Reading a hit

This is the family where a motif hit licenses the least. Of the 13 models, five carry under 6 bits and
three carry under 3 bits, which means they cannot be scanned meaningfully at all; a "hit" for the CIS-BP
ZHX1 or HDX model is not information. The CIS-BP HHEX model is inherited across species: it was measured on
a *Caenorhabditis elegans* protein at 77% DNA-binding-domain identity and transferred to human HHEX, not
measured on the human protein. The CIS-BP ZFHX2 model is a bare TAATTA whose nearest neighbours across all
four databases are Q50 homeodomain motifs, and the ZHX1 model's nearest neighbours are CpG-binding
MBD/CXXC motifs; both are flagged in the underlying data as probably belonging elsewhere. Only HOMEZ,
HMBOX1 and TSHZ2 rest on direct in vitro selection for the human protein, and for TSHZ2 the motif is
probably the zinc fingers' rather than the homeodomain's. Read a hit here as a statement about sequence
composition, and go to expression and ChIP data before naming a protein.
families.caveats: Treat this family as a bucket label, not an identification. Five of the 13 models carry under 6 bits and three under 3 bits, so they are not scannable; matches to them are noise. The CIS-BP HHEX model is transferred from a C. elegans protein at 77% DNA-binding-domain identity rather than measured on human HHEX. The CIS-BP ZFHX2 and ZHX1 models sit closer to Q50 homeodomain and MBD/CXXC motifs respectively than to anything in this family. Only HOMEZ, HMBOX1 and TSHZ2 have credible human in vitro motifs, and the TSHZ2 site contains no TAAT core and is likely read by its zinc fingers. For most members, occupancy is driven by partners and by AT-rich or repeat context, not by the consensus.

families.name: SREBP
families.def: Sterol response element TCACNCCAC plus E-box binding. SREBF1, SREBF2.
families.short: SREBP-1 and SREBP-2 are bHLH-LZ factors made as ER membrane precursors and activated by sterol-regulated proteolysis, so only the cleaved nuclear fragment binds DNA. They are unusual in having dual specificity: a tyrosine replaces the arginine that is otherwise invariant in bHLH basic regions, letting them bind both the palindromic E-box CACGTG and the non-palindromic sterol regulatory element SRE-1, TCACNCCAC. Sites sit in promoters of cholesterol and fatty acid synthesis genes and work with a neighbouring NF-Y CCAAT box or SP1 GC box, which an isolated SRE needs for activity. The pathway controls the LDL receptor, hepatic lipogenesis and the response to statins, and is central to fatty liver disease and insulin resistance.
families.long:
## The factors

SREBF1 and SREBF2 encode SREBP-1 and SREBP-2, basic helix-loop-helix leucine zipper (bHLH-LZ) factors that are unusual in being synthesized as membrane-anchored precursors in the endoplasmic reticulum. SREBF1 produces two isoforms from alternative first exons, SREBP-1a and SREBP-1c (also called ADD1), which differ in the length of their activation domain. Each precursor has two transmembrane segments and is held in the ER by SCAP; when sterols are low, SCAP escorts it to the Golgi, where sequential cleavage by Site-1 and Site-2 proteases releases the N-terminal bHLH-LZ fragment, which enters the nucleus and dimerizes. Regulation is therefore proteolytic rather than transcriptional at the level of DNA binding, and only the cleaved nuclear form is a transcription factor. SREBP-2 is the principal driver of cholesterol synthesis genes, SREBP-1c of fatty acid synthesis genes, and SREBP-1a is a stronger general activator expressed mainly in proliferating cells and cell lines. Both genes are broadly expressed, with SREBF1 highest in liver and adipose tissue. The atlas assigns 12 motifs to this family (4 JASPAR, 5 HOCOMOCO, 2 CIS-BP, 1 Vierstra archetype) over SREBF1 and SREBF2, with cohesion 0.89 - the lowest in the E-box group - and SREBF1 (MA0595.1) as the representative.

## The motif

SREBP has dual DNA-binding specificity, and this is the single most important fact about the family. It binds the canonical palindromic E-box CACGTG, usually with T/A flanks (ATCACGTGAT), and it also binds a non-palindromic, non-E-box element, the sterol regulatory element SRE-1, written TCACNCCAC. Mutagenesis of the LDL receptor promoter identified the nucleotides that make SRE-1 an active element, and biochemistry then showed the structural cause: in SREBP the arginine that is otherwise invariant in the basic region of every bHLH protein is replaced by a tyrosine, and that single substitution is sufficient to add SRE recognition to E-box recognition. The co-crystal of the SREBP-1a bHLH-LZ bound to an E-box showed this tyrosine in a position where an alternative rotamer can accommodate the asymmetric SRE. This is why the atlas cannot give the family one consensus. Roughly half of the assigned models are SRE-type (aTCACCCCAc, or its reverse complement aTGGgGTGAt), including the Vierstra archetype AC0486:SREBF:bHLH; the rest are E-box-type (ATCACGTGAT, ATCACcTGAT, gTCAgGTGAt). The published SRE consensus TCACNCCAC and the data consensus aTCACCCCAc agree, with the databases simply filling the degenerate position with the commonest base, C. The two motif classes are not variants of each other in any alignment sense, and a scan using one will miss the other.

## Where it acts

SREBP sites are promoter-proximal, typically within a few hundred base pairs of the transcription start site of lipid-metabolism genes, and they rarely work alone. An isolated SRE is a weak element; efficient activation requires a co-regulatory factor bound nearby, most often NF-Y at a CCAAT box or SP1 at a GC box. The synergy is direct - SREBP contacts the Btd domain of SP1 and the NF-Y trimer - and mapping SREBP1 together with NFY and SP1 genome-wide confirmed that the three co-occupy a large fraction of SREBP-bound promoters. The canonical composite arrangements are the LDLR promoter (SRE-1 plus SP1 sites) and the HMGCS1 promoter (SRE plus NF-Y). Because the nuclear form is generated by proteolysis, occupancy is switched by sterol depletion, statin treatment, insulin (for SREBP-1c) or feeding rather than by changes in site availability.

## Biology and disease

SREBP-2 activates essentially the whole cholesterol biosynthetic pathway plus the LDL receptor, which is why statin treatment, by lowering hepatic sterols, raises LDLR expression through this pathway. SREBP-1c activates fatty acid and triglyceride synthesis and is induced by insulin and by LXR agonists. Targeted disruption of Srebf1 in mice causes partial embryonic lethality, and surviving animals show elevated SREBP-2 and increased cholesterol synthesis, an example of cross-compensation within the family. In humans the pathway sits at the centre of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, hypertriglyceridemia and insulin resistance, and SREBP-driven lipogenesis is also co-opted by tumours; reviews describe the physiology as convergent but the pathophysiology as divergent between the two genes.

## Reading a hit

Decide first which motif you matched. An ATCACGTGAT hit is a T/A-flanked canonical E-box and is indistinguishable from USF, MITF/TFE, BHLHE41 or CLOCK-BMAL1 sites; it is weak evidence for SREBP on its own. A TCACNCCAC hit is much more specific, because few other human factors read that asymmetric sequence, and it becomes considerably stronger if an NF-Y CCAAT box or an SP1 GC box lies within about 50 bp in a lipid-gene promoter. SREBF1 and SREBF2 cannot be distinguished from each other by sequence, and the SREBP-1a/1c isoforms share one DNA-binding domain entirely. Several HOCOMOCO models here are ChIP-only, and one grade-C model (tCgCGTGA) is a degenerate half-site that should not be used for scanning.
families.caveats: This family has two unrelated motif classes and the databases hold both, so check which one you matched. An ATCACGTGAT E-box hit is shared with USF, MITF/TFE, BHLHE41 and CLOCK-BMAL1 and is weak evidence for SREBP. A TCACNCCAC SRE hit is far more specific, but SREBPs bind it weakly on their own and real elements are usually accompanied by NF-Y or SP1 within about 50 bp. SREBF1 and SREBF2 are indistinguishable by sequence, as are the SREBP-1a and -1c isoforms. Cohesion here is only 0.89 because of the two motif classes, several models are ChIP-only, and one grade-C model is a degenerate half-site not suitable for scanning.

families.name: CLOCK / BMAL1
families.def: Tandem E-boxes CACGTG of the circadian oscillator. CLOCK, ARNTL/BMAL1, NPAS2.
families.short: CLOCK, BMAL1 (gene symbol ARNTL) and NPAS2 are basic helix-loop-helix PER-ARNT-SIM (bHLH-PAS) transcription factors that form the activating limb of the mammalian circadian clock. BMAL1 pairs with CLOCK or with its paralogue NPAS2 and binds the palindromic E-box CACGTG together with a small set of E-box-like variants. The complex reads seven base pairs rather than six, because a flanking A-T pair next to the core contributes to affinity. Strong circadian promoters usually carry two E-boxes in tandem six to seven base pairs apart, and it is the pair, not a single hexamer, that produces rhythmic transcription. Occupancy oscillates once a day and drives Per, Cry, Rev-erb and thousands of output genes. Because CACGTG is also the core read by MYC/MAX, USF and SREBP, sequence alone cannot assign an E-box to the clock.
families.long:
## The factors

CLOCK, BMAL1 (*ARNTL*, formerly MOP3) and NPAS2 (MOP4) are bHLH-PAS proteins: an N-terminal basic helix-loop-helix domain followed by two PAS domains (PAS-A, PAS-B) and a PAC extension. The bHLH contacts DNA; the PAS domains set dimerization specificity and provide cofactor and small-molecule surfaces. Neither subunit binds DNA productively alone. BMAL1 is the obligate partner, heterodimerizing with CLOCK or with NPAS2; BMAL2 (*ARNTL2*) is a lower-abundance paralogue. The crystal structure of the mouse CLOCK:BMAL1 bHLH-PAS region shows an asymmetric, interdigitated assembly with three separate interfaces, so the subunits wrap around one another rather than pairing symmetrically (Huang et al. 2012). CLOCK and BMAL1 are broadly expressed; NPAS2 is enriched in forebrain and some peripheral tissues and can substitute for CLOCK, which is why *Clock*-null mice keep behavioral rhythms (DeBruyne et al. 2006) while *Bmal1*-null mice are arrhythmic in constant darkness (Bunger et al. 2000). This family holds 12 motifs from JASPAR, HOCOMOCO and CIS-BP labeled ARNTL/BMAL1, CLOCK or NPAS2, with none flagged as probably mislabeled.

## The motif

The core is the palindromic E-box CACGTG. Each basic helix enters the major groove and reads one CAC half-site; because the hexamer is its own reverse complement, the two subunits occupy equivalent halves. A structure of the human CLOCK:BMAL1 bHLH domains on a canonical E-box resolved the hydrogen-bond network and showed BMAL1 Ile80 contacting the base pair immediately 3' of the core, so the recognized unit is 7 bp, CACGTGA, with that flanking A-T pair indispensable; the same study measured single substitutions and defined two high-affinity non-canonical boxes, AACGTGA and CATGTGA (Wang et al. 2013). This resolves an apparent split in the databases. The methyl-HT-SELEX models CLOCK.H14CORE.0.M.C and NPAS2.H14CORE.1.M.C recover ACACATGT and ACATGTGT, the CATGTG variant, while the grade-A models BMAL1.H14CORE.0.PSM.A and CLOCK.H14CORE.1.PS.A recover CACGTG with a flanking base. The pooled consensus computed from the members is cCACGTGc; it does not contradict the literature 7-mer, because averaging a strand-ambiguous palindrome symmetrizes the flanks. The other commonly cited variant is the E'-box CACGTT. Functionally rhythmic promoters generally carry tandem E-boxes 6-7 bp apart, and the pair rather than either hexamer confers cell-autonomous rhythmicity (Nakahata et al. 2008); the most information-rich model here, NPAS2.H14CORE.2.S.B, is itself a tandem (CACGTGbnndaCACGTGt, about 21 bits). No member of the family can be told from another by sequence.

## Where it acts

Binding is promoter-biased. ChIP-seq in mouse liver puts most confident sites within a few hundred base pairs of transcription start sites, often in CpG-island promoters, with roughly one to three thousand sites per time point (Rey et al. 2011; Koike et al. 2012). Occupancy itself cycles, peaking once per day ahead of the RNA polymerase II and H3K4me3/H3K9ac rhythms it drives (Koike et al. 2012). Core targets are *Per1*, *Per2*, *Cry1*, *Cry2*, *Nr1d1*/*Nr1d2* and *Dbp*; the wider output program layers E-boxes with D-boxes (DBP/HLF/TEF) and ROREs (ROR/REV-ERB) so that one clock input can generate many output phases (Takahashi 2017). A specific hexamer is expected about 7 x 10^5 times in a 3-Gb genome under uniform base composition; CpG depletion lowers the real count, but matches still outnumber occupied sites by orders of magnitude.

## Biology and disease

CLOCK:BMAL1 was identified as the activator of *Per1* through E-boxes, with the dominant-negative *Clock* mutation lengthening period (Gekakis et al. 1998). *Bmal1* loss abolishes free-running rhythms (Bunger et al. 2000) and produces early-onset aging phenotypes including cataracts, sarcopenia and reduced lifespan (Kondratov et al. 2006). Pancreatic-islet disruption of *Clock* or *Bmal1* causes hypoinsulinemia and diabetes (Marcheva et al. 2010). In humans the clock is implicated in sleep-phase disorders, metabolic syndrome and shift-work-associated disease, though the strongest Mendelian sleep-timing mutations lie in *PER2* and *CSNK1D* rather than in CLOCK or BMAL1 (Takahashi 2017).

## Reading a hit

A CACGTG match by itself says almost nothing about which bHLH protein bound it: MYC/MAX, MXI1, USF1/2, SREBF1/2, TFE3/MITF, ARNT homodimers and HIF:ARNT all read the same or an overlapping core, and several CLOCK/BMAL models in this family have a closer neighbor in another family than within their own. Features that shift the interpretation toward the clock are a tandem pair 6-7 bp apart, an A or T immediately 3' of the core, a promoter-proximal CpG-island location, and rhythmic accessibility or expression of the nearby gene. The hit cannot separate CLOCK from NPAS2, BMAL1 from BMAL2, or either from an ARNT homodimer. Evidence codes matter: the grade-A BMAL1 and CLOCK models carry in vitro support (HT-SELEX and methyl-HT-SELEX), whereas ChIP-only models can reflect tethering to partner factors, and CLOCK/BMAL1 ChIP peaks include many regions with no recognizable E-box.
families.caveats: Treat a hit as "an E-box" first and a clock site only with extra evidence. The core CACGTG is shared with the MYC/MAX, USF, SREBP and MiT bHLH groups and with HIF:ARNT, and in this family several models sit closer to motifs outside the family than inside it. Nothing in the sequence distinguishes CLOCK from NPAS2 or BMAL1 from BMAL2. The non-canonical CATGTG-type models come from methyl-HT-SELEX at grade C and are lower confidence than the grade-A CACGTG models. ChIP-derived versions include indirect binding, so peak-derived motifs are not proof that the tagged subunit touched the DNA. Tandem spacing and rhythmic behavior of the locus are more informative than the match score.

families.name: SPI1 / SPIB / SPIC (PU.1)
families.def: Purine-rich AGAGGAAGTG. SPI1, SPIB, SPIC; EICE composite with IRF.
families.short: SPI1 (PU.1), SPIB and SPIC are the class III branch of the ETS family. They read the same GGA(A/T) core as other ETS proteins but demand a purine-rich 5' flank, giving the hematopoietic PU-box AAAGAGGAAGTG - the one ETS subfamily that a scan can usually tell apart from the rest. SPI1 is required for macrophage, neutrophil, dendritic cell and B-cell development; SPIB acts in B cells and plasmacytoid dendritic cells; SPIC specifies red pulp macrophages. PU.1 also nucleates the ETS-IRF composite element (EICE), GGAAGTGAAAC, by recruiting IRF4 or IRF8 to DNA it has already bound. Reduced PU.1 dosage causes acute myeloid leukemia in mice, and SPI1 fusions occur in high-risk pediatric T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia.
families.long:
## The factors

Three human genes - SPI1 (PU.1, Spi-1), SPIB (Spi-B) and SPIC (Spi-C) - form the SPI subfamily.
Each carries one ETS domain of about 85 residues with the family's winged helix-turn-helix fold and
binds DNA as a monomer; outside the domain they have acidic and glutamine-rich activation regions
and, in PU.1, a PEST region whose Ser148 must be phosphorylated for cooperative assembly with IRF
partners. Systematic profiling of all human and mouse ETS proteins puts these three in their own
class (class III), the most sequence-distinct group in the family; a tyrosine that sets specificity
at the position immediately 3' of the core in other ETS proteins is replaced by asparagine here.
Expression is hematopoietic and essentially non-overlapping with the rest of the family: SPI1 in
myeloid cells, macrophages, dendritic cells, microglia and B cells; SPIB in B cells and
plasmacytoid dendritic cells; SPIC narrowly in red pulp macrophages and related tissue macrophages.
The first crystal structure of any ETS domain on DNA was PU.1's, which established the
loop-helix-loop mode of DNA contact for the whole family.

## The motif

The site is usually written AAAGAGGAAGTG, and the models grouped here agree on AAAGAGGAAGT. The
invariant part is the same GGA(A/T) core all ETS proteins read, contacted by two invariant
arginines in recognition helix H3 that hydrogen-bond the two guanines, with a wing lysine 5' of the
core and a turn lysine on the opposite strand 3' of it. What sets this family apart is the 5' flank.
Class I ETS proteins prefer ACC immediately 5' of GGA; the SPI proteins prefer purines - AGA, with
a marked preference for G two bases 5' of the core - and tolerate a run of As further out. Because
that difference spans three or four positions rather than one, class III motifs are the only ETS
subfamily that a sequence scan separates from the rest with any reliability. Within the family,
SPI1, SPIB and SPIC are not separable: their models are near-identical, and the Vierstra archetype
that represents them is named for two of the three factors at once (AC0642:SPIB/SPI). Note that
the published PU.1 site contains no CpG, so unlike the class I CCGGAAGT it is insensitive to
CpG methylation. The composite EICE, GGAAGTGAAAC, is a PU.1 site fused to an IRF half-site and is
captured by only one model in this family - the CIS-BP entry M07944, whose consensus AAAGAGGAAGTGAAA
runs from the PU.1 site into the IRF half-site.

## Where it acts

PU.1 sites are found at myeloid and B-lineage promoters and, more heavily, at the enhancers that
define those lineages; the classic example is the macrophage colony-stimulating factor receptor
(CSF1R) promoter, where PU.1 directs macrophage-specific expression. PU.1 behaves as a lineage
"pioneer" in the sense that its binding precedes and is required for much of the accessible
chromatin landscape of myeloid cells, so its motif is enriched in macrophage and B-cell DNase and
ATAC footprints far more than in other cell types. Two named composite elements dominate its
cooperative biology. The EICE (ETS-IRF composite element, GGAAGTGAAAC) was defined at
immunoglobulin light-chain enhancers, where DNA-bound and Ser148-phosphorylated PU.1 recruits IRF4
(originally Pip) or IRF8, raising IRF affinity 20- to 40-fold; the crystal structure of the
PU.1/IRF4/DNA complex shows the DNA bent into an S shape that juxtaposes the two domains across the
central minor groove, and explains why IRF1 and IRF2 are anti-cooperative with PU.1 at the same
element. PU.1 sites also cluster with CEBP, RUNX and GATA sites in myeloid enhancers.

## Biology and disease

Spi1-null mice lack macrophages, neutrophils and B cells and have severely disrupted myeloid and
lymphoid development, the most striking single-gene hematopoietic phenotype among the ETS family.
Dosage matters as much as presence: reducing PU.1 expression to roughly a fifth of normal in mice
causes acute myeloid leukemia, placing SPI1 among the transcription factors whose partial loss is
leukemogenic. SPIC is required for red pulp macrophage development and splenic iron recycling.
In human disease, recurrent SPI1 fusions (STMN1-SPI1, TCF7-SPI1) define a high-risk subgroup of
pediatric T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia, and PU.1 activity is a recurring theme in myeloid
leukemia biology more broadly.

## Reading a hit

A purine-rich AAAGAGGAAGTG match is one of the few ETS hits that genuinely localizes the signal to
a subfamily - but only to the subfamily. SPI1, SPIB and SPIC cannot be told apart by sequence, and
the atlas's representative model for this family is itself named for two factors. The distinction
from class I ETS is real but not absolute: degenerate members of this family, such as HOCOMOCO's
short SPI1.H14CORE.1.S.B model whose consensus is only GGAAGT, will match generic ETS sites, and
the GGAA core alone is expected millions of times per strand in a 3.1-Gb genome. Cell type carries
much of the inference: outside myeloid, B-lineage or microglial contexts a PU-box match is far more
likely to be a chance GGAA than a bound PU.1 site. Two caveats specific to this family: only one of its
twelve models (CIS-BP M07944, AAAGAGGAAGTGAAA) reaches into the IRF half-site, so scanning with the
rest will find the PU.1 half of an EICE without flagging the composite - look explicitly for GTGAAAC
a few bases 3' of the core; and the JASPAR
SPIB model (MA0081.3) is stored on the reverse strand as CACTTCCTCTT, the same site as AAGAGGAAGTG.
families.caveats:
This is one of the few ETS subfamilies a scan can separate from the others, because
its purine-rich 5' flank differs over three or four positions rather than one. It cannot separate
its own members: SPI1, SPIB and SPIC share one motif, and the atlas representative is a Vierstra
archetype named for two of them. Expression usually decides - SPIC is confined to red pulp
macrophages, SPIB to B cells and plasmacytoid dendritic cells - so a PU-box hit outside a
hematopoietic context deserves scepticism. The family is small (12 models) and includes short,
degenerate entries that behave like a generic ETS site. Only one of the twelve models reaches into the IRF half-site of
the EICE composite, so a scan will usually register the PU.1 half-site and miss the element that
gives it specificity.

families.name: ZBTB7A/B/C (LRF)
families.def: GC-rich GACCCCCCCC. ZBTB7A, ZBTB7B, ZBTB7C.
families.short: ZBTB7A, ZBTB7B and ZBTB7C are BTB/POZ zinc-finger proteins that read short GC-rich sites through four C2H2 fingers and repress or reorganize promoters through the dimerizing BTB domain. ZBTB7A, also called LRF, Pokemon or FBI-1, competes with SP1 at GC boxes, represses the ARF tumor suppressor and the fetal hemoglobin genes, and acts more broadly as a promoter-accessibility factor for other transcription factors. ZBTB7B, better known as ThPOK or cKrox, directs CD4 rather than CD8 T-cell fate and has been proposed as the vertebrate GAGA factor. Because the recognition sites are short, GC-rich and shared with the large SP/KLF motif class, hits in this family are easy to obtain and hard to attribute.
families.long:
## The factors

Three paralogues: ZBTB7A (LRF, Pokemon, FBI-1, OCZF), ZBTB7B (ThPOK, cKrox, Zfp67) and the much less studied ZBTB7C (APM-1). Each is 500-600 residues with an N-terminal BTB/POZ domain and four C-terminal C2H2 fingers. The BTB domain homodimerizes and also serves as the corepressor-docking surface, so DNA-bound ZBTB7 proteins arrive as dimers carrying NCoR/SMRT- and HDAC-containing complexes; for ZBTB7B the BTB domain is specifically required for its CD4-lineage function. Expression patterns diverge sharply. ZBTB7A is broadly expressed, with well-characterized roles in hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells, erythroid cells and B versus T lineage choice. ZBTB7B is induced in CD4-committed thymocytes during positive selection and is also expressed in cartilage and skin, where it was first described as c-Krox, a regulator of type I collagen genes. ZBTB7C is expressed at low levels in many tissues and has essentially no dedicated functional literature.

## The motif

The in vitro consensus supported by the matrices here is a short GC-rich element, CGACCACC, or GGTGGTCG read on the other strand. HT-SELEX models for ZBTB7B (JASPAR MA0694.2) and ZBTB7C (MA0695.2), the CIS-BP entries for both, and the Vierstra archetype AC0529:ZBTB7A/ZBTB7B all converge on it, with 10-14 bits over eight positions. Four adjacent zinc fingers would be expected to read about 12 bases, so this consensus is shorter than the domain can in principle cover, and the flanks are weakly specified. Two other renderings circulate and should not be conflated with it. First, ZBTB7A models in HOCOMOCO and CIS-BP extend the same GACC core into a run of cytosines - written GGGGGGGTC or GACCCCYSCC - and the GC-rich "GACCCCCCCC" form is what much of the ZBTB7A literature quotes; whether ZBTB7A genuinely prefers a longer C-run than its paralogues, or whether this reflects the different experiments used, is not resolved by these data. Second, ZBTB7B has been identified as the vertebrate homologue of the Drosophila GAGA factor and reported to associate with purine-rich GAGA sequences, a description that does not match CGACCACC at all. The atlas reports the HT-SELEX consensus because that is what the collections agree on, but a reader should know that three different sequence descriptions exist for this family. Within the family, ZBTB7A, ZBTB7B and ZBTB7C models are 0.96-0.98 similar where they overlap, so the paralogues are not separable by sequence.

## Where it acts

These are promoter factors. ZBTB7A binds a substantial fraction of human promoters and enhancers, including many NF-kappaB p65 targets, and it associates with promoters independently of the client factor; prebinding by ZBTB7A marks which promoters can undergo factor-induced changes in accessibility. On its own it does not activate. ZBTB7A also competes directly with SP1 for overlapping GC boxes - documented at the RB1 promoter, where it displaces SP1 and recruits corepressors - which is a general hazard for interpreting GC-box hits. Because the site is GC-rich and CpG-containing, matches concentrate in CpG-island promoters. Known target loci include CDKN2A/ARF, RB1, MCAM, BCL2L11 (BIM) and the fetal globin genes HBG1/HBG2.

## Biology and disease

Zbtb7a-null mouse embryonic fibroblasts resist oncogene-driven transformation, and ZBTB7A overexpression transforms cells in vitro and in transgenic mice, effects attributable in part to direct repression of ARF; ZBTB7A is overexpressed in several human cancers. In hematopoiesis, ZBTB7A antagonizes Notch to enforce B-cell over T-cell fate, and it is an essential GATA1 target in erythroid development, restraining BIM-dependent apoptosis. ZBTB7A and BCL11A independently repress fetal hemoglobin, making ZBTB7A a target of interest for sickle cell disease and beta-thalassemia therapy. Recurrent ZBTB7A mutations occur in acute myeloid leukemia with t(8;21), where they behave as loss-of-function cooperating lesions. For ZBTB7B, transgenic expression forces MHC class I-restricted thymocytes into the CD4 helper program instead of the CD8 cytotoxic program, and a human multimorphic ThPOK variant has been reported to cause an inborn error of immunity with T-cell defects and fibrosis.

## Reading a hit

This family sits in the most crowded part of motif space. CGACCACC and the GC-rich GACCCCC variants overlap the recognition space of SP1-SP4, the KLFs, MAZ, PATZ1, E2F and other CpG-island factors, and ZBTB7A is documented to compete with SP1 for the same sites, so sequence cannot assign a GC-box hit to this family with any confidence. Within the family, the three paralogues are indistinguishable; the Vierstra archetype AC0529:ZBTB7A/ZBTB7B is explicit that ZBTB7A and ZBTB7B were not resolved. Provenance is mixed. The ZBTB7B and ZBTB7C JASPAR matrices are HT-SELEX, which supports direct binding, and HOCOMOCO's ZBT7B and ZBT7C models carry in vitro evidence codes (SM and S). The ZBTB7A situation is worse: the JASPAR ZBTB7A matrix MA0750.3 is ChIP-seq-derived and reads CCGGAAGTG, an ETS-family site with no resemblance to any other ZBTB7A model in the family and with its best cross-database match in a different family altogether. That matrix should be treated as reporting a co-bound or indirectly bound ETS element, not ZBTB7A's own preference. Finally, ZBTB7A occupancy is common and largely permissive rather than instructive, so even a correct ZBTB7A call says little about whether the promoter is regulated by it.
families.caveats: The sites are eight or fewer informative bases, GC-rich and CpG-island-associated, and overlap SP/KLF, MAZ and E2F motif space; ZBTB7A is documented to compete with SP1 for the same GC boxes. ZBTB7A, ZBTB7B and ZBTB7C cannot be told apart from sequence, and the Vierstra archetype merges ZBTB7A with ZBTB7B by name. Three different sequence descriptions exist in the literature for this family (CGACCACC, GC-rich GACCCCCCCC, and purine-rich GAGA for ThPOK/vGAF), which are not reconciled. Most importantly, JASPAR MA0750.3 for ZBTB7A is a ChIP-derived ETS-like matrix (CCGGAAGTG) unrelated to the rest of the family; do not scan with it as if it were ZBTB7A.

families.name: ROR
families.def: RORE: AT-rich half-site AAAGTAGGTCA. RORA, RORB, RORC.
families.short: RORA, RORB and RORC (RORalpha/beta/gamma) are nuclear receptors that bind DNA as monomers to the ROR response element, or RORE: an AGGTCA nuclear-receptor half-site preceded by a 5-6 bp AT-rich extension, most often written AAAGTAGGTCA. The extension is read by a C-terminal extension of the DNA-binding domain lying in the minor groove, and it is the only feature that distinguishes a RORE from the half-site shared by many other nuclear receptors. ROREs form the second transcriptional loop of the mammalian circadian clock, where RORs activate Bmal1 in competition with the REV-ERB repressors at the same sites. RORgammat, a thymus-restricted RORC isoform, drives the Th17 program and is a drug target in autoimmune disease.
families.long:
## The factors

The ROR (RAR-related orphan receptor) group is encoded by three human genes: *RORA* (NR1F1, RORalpha), *RORB* (NR1F2, RORbeta) and *RORC* (NR1F3, RORgamma; the symbol *RORG* is used for it in HOCOMOCO and in the Vierstra archetypes). Each protein has the standard nuclear-receptor layout — an N-terminal A/B region, a DNA-binding domain (DBD) built from two zinc-coordinating modules, a hinge, and a ligand-binding domain (LBD) ending in an AF-2 helix. Unlike the steroid and RXR-partnered receptors, RORs bind DNA as monomers, using a C-terminal extension (CTE) of the DBD in addition to the zinc modules. Alternative promoters and splicing generate isoforms with different N-termini (RORalpha1-4; RORgamma and the thymus-restricted RORgammat), and these N-termini change DNA-binding behavior rather than just transactivation. Expression differs sharply: *RORA* is broad (cerebellum, liver, many tissues), *RORB* is largely restricted to retina, pineal gland and specific brain regions, and *RORC* is expressed in liver, muscle and skeletal tissue, with RORgammat confined to thymocytes and to T-helper and innate lymphoid subsets. RORalpha and RORgamma are constitutively active in reporter assays, with cholesterol and oxysterol derivatives occupying the LBD pocket.

## The motif

The ROR response element (RORE) is a single nuclear-receptor half-site with a 5' extension, conventionally written as an AT-rich stretch of 5-6 bp followed by RGGTCA. The canonical monomeric site established for RORalpha1 is often quoted as the 11-mer AAAGTAGGTCA; the motif models in this family converge on a slightly shorter 10-mer, A(A/T)NTAGGTCA (the pooled data consensus here is AAbTAGGTCA). Both renderings describe the same element — the discrepancy is only how many of the weakly constrained AT positions a given model retains.

Structurally, the split is clean. The zinc modules place a recognition helix in the major groove of AGGTCA, which supplies most of the information content; the CTE (the A-box/T-box region) lies along the minor groove of the AT-rich 5' extension and is what converts a generic half-site into a RORE. The crystal structure of the closely related REV-ERBalpha DBD plus CTE on a direct repeat, and the structure of the monomeric receptor NGFI-B, both show this arrangement directly. Without the 5' extension the motif is just the half-site shared by dozens of nuclear receptors.

RORs also bind extended sites: HT-SELEX models in this family include ~18-bp tandem arrangements (AAGTAGGTCAGTAGGTCA), i.e. two half-sites in direct repeat with a 2-bp gap. All eleven motifs assigned here collapse onto the same core (family cohesion 0.87), and none is flagged as mislabelled. RORA, RORB and RORC are not distinguishable from sequence.

## Where it acts

ROREs sit in promoters and enhancers, not preferentially in CpG islands. The best-characterized examples are the two ROREs in the *Bmal1* (*ARNTL*) promoter, with further sites at *Cry1*, *Npas2* and *Nfil3*. In immune cells, RORgammat acts through ROREs in the *IL17A*/*IL17F* locus and its conserved non-coding regions, alongside RUNX1, BATF and IRF4. In the circadian cis-regulatory grammar, the RORE is one of three elements — E-box (CLOCK:BMAL1), D-box, and RORE — whose combination sets the phase of a rhythmic promoter; the RORE contributes the late-night/early-morning component. Because the informative part is a 10-mer with several degenerate positions, matches are common: expect on the order of 10^5 hits genome-wide at permissive thresholds, so genomic occurrence alone carries little weight.

## Biology and disease

The *staggerer* mouse, a spontaneous *Rora* deletion, loses cerebellar Purkinje cells and is ataxic, and RNAi and mutant analyses place Rora in the mammalian clock, where loss shortens or destabilizes period. *Rorb* is required for photoreceptor and pineal gene programs. *Rorc*-null mice lack lymph nodes and Peyer's patches and show increased thymocyte apoptosis, and RORgammat is required for the Th17 program, making it a drug target in psoriasis and other autoimmune disease; RORgamma inverse agonists and RORalpha/gamma agonists have both been pursued clinically.

## Reading a hit

A RORE match identifies the family, not the member: nothing in the sequence separates RORA from RORB from RORC. More importantly, it does not separate ROR from REV-ERB. NR1D1 and NR1D2 bind the same RORE and the same 2-bp-spaced direct repeat, and the Vierstra archetype AC0123:NR1D/RORC states this by naming both groups. The two are told apart by tissue, circadian phase and cofactor (coactivator versus NCoR-HDAC3), not by motif.

Second, check that your hit includes the AT-rich extension. A bare AGGTCA is shared with ESRRA, NR5A, NR4A and the RXR heterodimer partners; scanning with the full 10-11-mer is the only way to make the call specific. Third, weigh the evidence code. RORB.H14CORE.0.SM.B rests on in vitro selection (HT-SELEX plus methyl-HT-SELEX) and supports a direct binding claim; RORA.H14CORE.0.P.C is ChIP-only at grade C and its consensus drifts at the 3' end. Finally, ChIP-derived versions of this motif can be contaminated by indirect binding: in mouse liver, most REV-ERBalpha ChIP peaks reflect tethering to HNF6 rather than direct RORE occupancy, and the same mechanism is available to RORs.
families.caveats: Treat a RORE hit as a family-level call, and remember the family boundary is porous: REV-ERB (NR1D1/NR1D2) binds the same element, so a match is really a 'ROR/REV-ERB site' unless expression or phase data break the tie. RORA, RORB and RORC are not separable from sequence — all eleven motifs here collapse onto one core. Matches to the bare AGGTCA half-site are not ROREs; require the AT-rich 5' extension. Prefer the in vitro-derived models (HOCOMOCO evidence S/M, e.g. RORB.H14CORE.0.SM.B) over ChIP-only entries such as RORA.H14CORE.0.P.C, which is grade C. The 10-mer is common enough that occurrence alone is weak evidence.

families.name: NR2E (TLX / PNR)
families.def: AAGGTCA monomeric sites. NR2E1, NR2E3.
families.short: NR2E is a small orphan nuclear-receptor group with two human members: NR2E1 (TLX, the homolog of Drosophila tailless) and NR2E3 (PNR, photoreceptor-specific nuclear receptor). Unusually for the superfamily, they prefer the hexamer AAGTCA rather than the AGGTCA half-site read by most nuclear receptors, a switch traced to a residue in the P-box of the recognition helix; the fuller models add a 5' A/T-rich extension and a tandem repeat of the core. The two factors are almost never co-expressed: TLX maintains neural stem and progenitor cells in the forebrain, while PNR acts in rod photoreceptors with CRX and NRL. NR2E3 mutations cause enhanced S-cone syndrome, a retinal cell-fate disorder.
families.long:
## The factors

NR2E is a two-member orphan group within the nuclear receptor superfamily: NR2E1, usually called TLX (the vertebrate homolog of *Drosophila* tailless), and NR2E3, usually called PNR (photoreceptor-specific nuclear receptor). Both have the canonical receptor layout — a short N-terminal region, a DNA-binding domain (DBD) built from two zinc-coordinating modules with a C-terminal extension, and a ligand-binding domain. No endogenous ligand is established for either, which is why they remain formally orphan. The two are expressed in almost non-overlapping places. TLX is confined to the developing forebrain and to adult neural stem and progenitor cells in the subventricular zone and dentate gyrus, where it maintains the undifferentiated state; PNR is essentially retina-specific, restricted to rod photoreceptors, where it works downstream of NRL and alongside CRX. Neither is broadly expressed, and neither has a large paralogue set — with two genes, this is one of the smallest nuclear-receptor groups in the human genome. TLX represses target genes through the atrophin/LSD1 and HDAC corepressor machinery; PNR can both activate rod genes and repress cone genes, depending on context and partner.

## The motif

The NR2E group is unusual in the superfamily for what it reads. Most nuclear receptors recognize the hexamer AGGTCA; tailless and PNR instead prefer AAGTCA, and the switch has been traced to a subclass-specific residue in the P-box, the part of the recognition helix that reads the core. The consensus given here, AAGTCA with a 5' A/T-rich extension (i.e. AAAGTCAA in the fuller models), reflects that. This is where the literature disagrees with itself, and with some database annotation: the group is frequently described as binding "AAGGTCA monomeric sites", which is the ordinary extended half-site. The difference is one base in the core, and the in vitro selection data assembled here fall on the AAGTCA side, including a tandem form AAGTCAATAAGTCA from HT-SELEX. Both renderings are in print; the shorter core is the better supported one for these two proteins specifically.

The family is loosely cohesive (0.67, low for this atlas). Models split into an AAGTCA-centered set (the HOCOMOCO NR2E1 in vitro entries, JASPAR Nr2e1, two Vierstra archetypes) and a second set centered on GGGATCA/AAAGATCA. One CIS-BP entry labelled NR2E1 (M02394_2.00, GAGGTCA) is flagged here as a probable member of the RXR-heterodimer family instead, and the JASPAR profile Nr2e3 (MA0164.2) has a consensus (AAGCTT) that resembles nothing else in the family. Work reported for NR2E3 indicates it binds only dimeric arrangements, while NR2E1 tolerates both monomeric and dimeric sites — a real difference between the two, but not one you can read off a single match.

## Where it acts

Because both factors are cell-type restricted, so is the useful signal. PNR sites cluster at rod photoreceptor gene promoters and enhancers, typically adjacent to CRX (the OTX-family site) and NRL (a Maf-family site), and PNR physically interacts with CRX through its DBD. TLX sites are found at neural stem cell and cell-cycle genes, including *PTEN* and *CDKN1A*, in forebrain progenitors. Neither motif is CpG-island associated. The bare AAGTCA hexamer is far too short to be informative on its own; at any usable threshold a 6-mer occurs hundreds of thousands of times in the human genome, so only the extended or tandem forms are worth scanning.

## Biology and disease

*NR2E3* mutations cause enhanced S-cone syndrome (Goldmann-Favre syndrome), in which S-cone photoreceptors are overproduced at the expense of rods — a cell-fate disorder rather than a simple degeneration — and also account for a share of autosomal recessive retinitis pigmentosa. The naturally occurring *rd7* mouse carries an *Nr2e3* mutation and reproduces the phenotype, and gene supplementation in that model is an active therapeutic line. Disease-associated substitutions in the NR2E3 DBD impair both dimerization and the interaction with CRX, which is consistent with a dimer-only binding mode. *Nr2e1*-null mice have a defective limbic system, with a hypoplastic amygdala and cortical and hypothalamic abnormalities, aggressive behavior, and impaired maintenance of adult neural stem cells.

## Reading a hit

An NR2E match should be read cautiously. The core is short, the family is only loosely cohesive, and the two members are almost never co-expressed, so context does most of the work: a TLX call in retina or a PNR call in brain is almost certainly wrong regardless of motif score. Nothing in the sequence distinguishes NR2E1 from NR2E3, and the AAGTCA core overlaps the AGGTCA half-site used by much of the nuclear receptor superfamily, so a permissive scan will pull in ESRRA, NR4A, NR5A and RXR-partner sites. Prefer the extended or tandem models, and prefer the HOCOMOCO entries with in vitro evidence codes (`S`, `SM`) over the archetype and ChIP-derived profiles. Treat the two Vierstra archetypes whose consensus is GGGATCA or AAAGATCA as separate observations that happen to be labelled NR2E rather than as confirmation of the AAGTCA site; archetypes are named after the majority of the factor labels that clustered, not after a demonstrated binding protein.
families.caveats: This is a weak family to call from sequence. The core is a 6-mer, family cohesion is only 0.67, and the assigned motifs split into an AAGTCA-centered set and a GGGATCA/AAAGATCA set. One CIS-BP entry labelled NR2E1 is flagged here as belonging with the RXR heterodimers, and the JASPAR Nr2e3 profile does not resemble the rest of the family. NR2E1 and NR2E3 are not separable by motif, but they are nearly non-overlapping in expression, so tissue is the more informative discriminator. Note also that the group is often described as binding AAGGTCA; the in vitro data here favor AAGTCA, one base shorter in the core.

families.name: Thinly characterized small families
families.def: Factors with a measured motif but almost no dedicated literature: MSANTD1/3/4, DNTTIP1, FLYWCH1, FAM200B (= ZBED11), ELYS/AHCTF1, NACC2, and XPA, which is a DNA repair protein rather than a transcription factor. BANP is named in older drafts of this entry, but its only matrix is a joint Vierstra archetype filed under ZBTB_OTHER.
families.short: This is not a motif family. It is a holding pen for small, thinly characterized factors that needed somewhere to go, and it currently holds eleven matrices for nine unrelated proteins: MSANTD1, MSANTD3 and MSANTD4, DNTTIP1, FLYWCH1, FAM200B, ELYS/AHCTF1, NACC2 and XPA. Internal cohesion is 0.47, the lowest of any group in this atlas. Two warnings about the label. The name mentions SCAN and SSX domains, but no SCAN-domain or SSX protein has a motif here; and BANP, named in the definition, is not here either - its only model sits in the other-BTB-zinc-finger bucket. XPA is the central scaffold of nucleotide excision repair, not a transcription factor. The motifs themselves are mostly well supported.
families.long:
## The factors

Nine proteins, eleven models, no shared biology; read the list, not the label, which mentions SCAN and SSX domains that are not represented.

BANP is named in the definition and is the most interesting protein in the set, but its motif is filed elsewhere. The CGCG element was for years an orphan promoter motif, enriched near the start sites of a subset of CpG-island promoters and associated with highly expressed genes; single-molecule footprinting combined with interaction proteomics identified BTG3-associated nuclear protein as its binder. Methylation of the motif repels BANP, confining it to unmethylated CpG islands, and on binding it opens chromatin, phases nucleosomes and activates essential metabolic genes. Structures of BEN domains later showed that oligomerization lets BANP select unmethylated CGCG. Here that motif rides on a Vierstra archetype with a joint ZBTB/BANP label, so it went to the other-BTB-zinc-finger entry instead.

The BEN domain reaches one protein that is here: of nine human BEN-domain proteins, NACC1 prefers CATG-containing sequence, and the NACC2 model here reads ACATGC. DNTTIP1, originally TdT-interacting factor 1, is a subunit of the mitotic deacetylase complex MiDAC; its C-terminal SKI/SNO/DAC-like domain binds DNA and nucleosomes, making it a chromatin-binding module rather than an activator. FLYWCH1 is a FLYWCH-type zinc finger studied as a suppressor of nuclear beta-catenin in colorectal cancer. FAM200B, also called ZBED11, is transposase-derived, of the hAT/ZBED lineage with an RNase H-like fold. MSANTD1, MSANTD3 and MSANTD4 carry Myb/SANT-like DNA-binding domains and almost no documented function. ELYS/AHCTF1 was named a transcription factor when cloned from mouse foetal haematopoietic tissue, then shown to be a nucleoporin that seeds Nup107-160 assembly and doubles as a kinetochore protein. XPA was cloned in 1990 as an excision-repair gene "containing a zinc-finger domain", which is how censuses of putative transcription factors caught it; it is the scaffold of nucleotide excision repair and reads splayed-arm junction geometry, not sequence.

## The motif

There is no consensus: the reported CACTCAc is only the MSANTD3 medoid of eleven unrelated matrices, and cohesion is 0.47.

HOCOMOCO v14 encodes assays in the model name: P is ChIP-seq, S HT-SELEX, M methyl-HT-SELEX, G genomic HT-SELEX, I SMiLE-seq, B protein-binding microarray, and grade A means at least two assay types agreed. Most are good on that scale. FLYWCH1 gives aTTCGAhcCGATTCGA, a 19-bit tandem TTCGA repeat, from PSGB at grade A. FAM200B gives the 13-bp palindrome TGGGTCGCGaCCC, 16 bits, PSGIB grade A, the shape a dimeric domesticated transposase should give. MSANTD4 gives acTTACTACtcg (13.8 bits, SGIB, A), MSANTD1 CACTTAAG (10.8 bits, PSGIB, A), DNTTIP1 GcatGCAC (PSG, A) and NACC2 ACATgc (PSGIB, A). Six of the seven HOCOMOCO models are grade A from up to five platforms, the assay set used by the recent systematic effort on poorly characterized human factors that produced motifs for 177 of 332 candidates. A protein with no literature can still have a well-measured motif.

Three entries are weaker. MSANTD3 appears twice, as JASPAR MA1523.2 and CIS-BP M01259, both reading CACTCAc and both flagged as resembling the NKX homeodomain family at 0.94-0.97, so that hexamer is not separable from an NKX site. ELYS contributes AAAT, 8.5 bits, from PBM alone at grade B, with a best match outside the bucket of 0.99: an AT-rich four-mer indistinguishable from any other AT-rich model. XPA appears twice, as CIS-BP M05827 and the Vierstra archetype AC0333:XPA:Unknown, whose domain label is literally "Unknown"; neither carries an assay label here.

## Where it acts

Unmapped for almost everything here; BANP, filed elsewhere, is the exception, at unmethylated CpG-island promoters near transcription start sites, with binding lost where those promoters are aberrantly methylated in cancer. For the rest, the systematic work on understudied factors found in vitro motifs enriched at cellular binding sites concentrated in promoters, making promoter-proximal the prior. Scan arithmetic matters more than location: ACATGC or CACTCA is expected several hundred thousand times per strand in 3.1 Gb and AAAT tens of millions of times, so the ELYS and MSANTD3 models cannot localise anything, while FLYWCH1's or FAM200B's long matrices are genuinely rare.

## Biology and disease

XPA is the only member with a Mendelian disease of its own, and it is a repair disease: biallelic mutations cause xeroderma pigmentosum group A, with extreme ultraviolet sensitivity and, in severe alleles, neurodegeneration. MiDAC, the complex DNTTIP1 assembles, is essential for mouse embryonic development. MSANTD3 appears as an HTN3-MSANTD3 fusion defining a subset of salivary acinic cell carcinoma. ELYS loss blocks nuclear pore assembly and chromosome segregation. MSANTD1, MSANTD4, FAM200B and NACC2 have no established disease link.

## Reading a hit

Name the matrix, not the family: a hit here is on one of eleven unrelated models. Then triage. If you came for the BANP motif, it is TCTCGCGAGA on archetype AC0312:ZBTB/BANP in the other-BTB-zinc-finger entry, and it matches the ZBTB33/Kaiso archetype at 0.99, so sequence alone will not say which of the two bound - use methylation state and expression. If the hit is XPA, discard it: XPA has no sequence specificity. If it is ELYS AAAT, discard it as AT-rich background. If it is MSANTD3 CACTCA, check the NKX entry first. If it is FLYWCH1, FAM200B, MSANTD1, MSANTD4, DNTTIP1 or NACC2, the matrix is reasonable evidence and the protein is not: treat the site as a candidate for an understudied factor, confirm the gene is expressed, and note that on structure FAM200B belongs with the ZBED entry and the MSANTD proteins with MYB.
families.caveats: This is an administrative holding pen, not a family. Eleven matrices for nine unrelated proteins, cohesion 0.47, the lowest in the atlas; there is no consensus and none should be quoted. The label misleads twice: no SCAN-domain or SSX protein has a motif here, and BANP, named in the definition, has its only model filed under other BTB-zinc-fingers as the joint ZBTB/BANP archetype. XPA is a nucleotide excision repair scaffold that binds DNA by shape, so its two models should not be scanned at all, and the ELYS model is a PBM-only AT-rich four-mer. Conversely, do not dismiss the whole group: six of the seven HOCOMOCO models are grade A from several independent assay platforms.

families.name: EBF / COE
families.def: Palindromic Olf-1/EBF site TCCCNNGGGA, read by a Rel-like DNA-binding domain with a zinc knuckle rather than by a bHLH. EBF1-4 (COE1-3).
families.short: EBF1-EBF4 (COE1-COE4, also Olf-1 and O/E-1 to O/E-3) bind a 10-base palindrome, TCCCNNGGGA, as homodimers. Despite being filed with the bHLH proteins, their DNA-binding domain is a pseudo-immunoglobulin fold structurally similar to the Rel homology domains of NF-κB and NFAT, contacting DNA through two loops and a unique zinc-coordination motif, with each subunit reaching across both half-sites; the HLH they carry is used for dimerisation, not DNA contact. EBF1 is required at the earliest committed step of B-lymphocyte development and shows pioneer-like activity on closed chromatin; EBF2 establishes brown adipocyte identity; de novo EBF3 variants cause a hypotonia-ataxia-developmental-delay syndrome. The motif is long enough that scans for it are relatively clean.
families.long:
## The factors

EBF1, EBF2, EBF3 and EBF4 — also called COE1-COE4, and in the olfactory literature Olf-1 and O/E-1 to O/E-3 — make up the vertebrate COE (Collier/Olf-1/EBF) family. They were discovered twice in the same year: EBF1 as a regulator of the B-cell-specific *mb-1*/*Cd79a* promoter, and Olf-1 as the factor binding a conserved element in olfactory neuron gene promoters. The family is conventionally filed with the bHLH proteins, and the atlas inherits that placement, but structurally it is not one. Crystallography shows that the EBF DNA-binding domain adopts a pseudo-immunoglobulin fold with novel topology that is structurally similar to the Rel homology domains of NF-κB and NFAT, and that it contacts DNA through two loop-based modules plus a unique zinc-coordination motif, the "zinc knuckle", with each monomer reaching across to touch both halves of the palindrome. Biochemistry had already identified that zinc motif and multiple dimerisation and activation domains. The proteins also carry an IPT/TIG domain and an atypical helix-loop-helix with its own novel dimerisation motif — an HLH used for dimerisation, not for DNA contact. The Vierstra archetype covering this family is named `AC0500:EBF:Rel_homology_region_(RHR)_factors`, which reflects the structure better than the bHLH label does. EBF1 acts in B lymphocytes, olfactory neurons, adipocytes, striatal neurons and osteoblasts; EBF2 in brown adipocytes, olfactory epithelium and cerebellum; EBF3 broadly in the central nervous system; EBF4 is the least characterised. They function as homodimers and can heterodimerise with each other.

## The motif

The site is a 10-base palindrome, TCCCNNGGGA: two inverted TCCC half-sites separated by two degenerate positions. The databases' versions fill those central positions in slightly different ways — HOCOMOCO EBF1 reads TCCCCTGGGA, HOCOMOCO EBF3 and JASPAR EBF1 read TCCCCAGGGA/TCCCCAGGGGA, the CIS-BP EBF1 model reads AKTCCCTWGGGAAT with extended flanks — but they are all the same element, and the representative model is the archetype consensus TCCCTGGGGA. Because the palindrome is read symmetrically by a dimer, with each subunit contacting both half-sites, the two central bases are the tolerant ones and the TCCC/GGGA blocks are essentially invariant.

Two practical consequences follow. First, this is an information-rich motif by the standards of a transcription factor site: eight effectively fixed positions rather than the four or five of an E-box. An exact TCCCNNGGGA is expected around 47,000 times in a 3.1-Gb genome, and because the pattern is its own reverse complement that count is not doubled — roughly one site per 65 kb, against roughly one per 4 kb for a six-mer. Scans for this motif are correspondingly cleaner. Second, the motif resembles nothing else in the atlas: the best match of any member to a motif outside the family is 0.93 and typically much lower, while within-family similarities run 0.91-1.00 (cohesion 0.91). The four paralogues are completely indistinguishable from sequence.

One provenance note: the CIS-BP EBF2 model `M03721_2.00` is inherited from a *Drosophila melanogaster* protein (Collier/Knot) at 91% DNA-binding-domain identity. Because COE proteins are deeply conserved and the fly motif (AATTCCCTAGGGAATT) matches the human models closely, this transfer is benign, but it is a transfer.

## Where it acts

EBF1 in B cells binds thousands of sites, mostly at enhancers of the B-lineage programme — *Cd79a*, *Pax5*, *Cd19*, *Igll1*, *Vpreb*, *Blnk*, *Foxo1* — and acts by activation, by repression, and by a transcription-independent poising of chromatin at genes that only become active later. Its C-terminal domain confers pioneer-like activity, letting EBF1 engage closed and nucleosomal chromatin and open it for subsequent factors, which is unusual and consistent with the extended DNA contact area seen in the structure. In B cells EBF1 sites co-occur with E2A/TCF3, PAX5, FOXO1 and RUNX1 motifs. In brown fat, EBF2 occupies and activates the PPARG/PRDM16 thermogenic enhancer programme. In olfactory sensory neurons the same element sits in promoters of olfactory marker and signalling genes.

## Biology and disease

*Ebf1*-null mice arrest B-cell development before the pro-B stage, with no immunoglobulin heavy-chain DJ rearrangement — EBF1 is required at the earliest committed step of the B lineage. EBF2 is required to establish and maintain brown adipocyte identity, and forced EBF2 expression imposes a brown-fat programme. In human genetics, de novo variants in *EBF3*, largely missense changes in the DNA-binding domain, cause a neurodevelopmental syndrome with hypotonia, ataxia, developmental delay and expressive language impairment, reported independently by two groups in the same issue; the mutations reduce DNA binding and transactivation, consistent with a dominant-negative or haploinsufficient mechanism.

## Reading a hit

Because the site is long, palindromic and unlike any other family's, a TCCCNNGGGA hit is unusually trustworthy at the family level: if you find a good match, EBF-family binding is a reasonable hypothesis. What it will not tell you is which EBF, since all four share the motif, and in most tissues only one or two are expressed, so expression data resolve the question that sequence cannot. Two cautions. All three HOCOMOCO models here are ChIP-derived (evidence letter `P`, grade B), so the in vitro support for the recognition sequence comes from the original biochemistry and the crystal structure rather than from SELEX models in the current collection. And the family label "bHLH" is misleading: EBF has an HLH, but it is a dimerisation module, and an E-box search will neither find EBF sites nor be found by them.
families.caveats: The site is long, palindromic and unlike any other family's, so a good match is reasonable evidence for EBF-family binding — unusual in this atlas. It is no evidence at all about which EBF: all four paralogues share one motif (cohesion 0.91) and only expression can separate them. All three HOCOMOCO models here are ChIP-derived (evidence letter P, grade B), so the sequence preference rests on the original biochemistry and the crystal structure rather than on in vitro models in the current collection. One CIS-BP EBF2 model is inherited from a Drosophila protein at 91% domain identity, which is benign but is a transfer. The "bHLH" class label is structurally wrong; do not expect E-box searches to find these sites.

families.name: Estrogen-related receptors
families.def: ERRE TNAAGGTCA extended half-site. ESRRA, ESRRB, ESRRG.
families.short: The estrogen-related receptors ERRalpha (ESRRA), ERRbeta (ESRRB) and ERRgamma (ESRRG) are orphan nuclear receptors with no established natural ligand; their activity is set by coactivators such as PGC-1alpha rather than by a hormone. Unlike most nuclear receptors they bind DNA as monomers, on a single AGGTCA half-site carrying a three-base 5' extension: TNAAGGTCA, usually seen as TCAAGGTCA. The extension is read by a C-terminal extension of the DNA-binding domain in the minor groove, and it is what allows a monomer to bind with high affinity. The three paralogues share one motif and are not distinguishable from sequence. ERR sites sit at nuclear-encoded mitochondrial and oxidative-metabolism genes, at pluripotency enhancers, and in the placenta and inner ear.
families.long:
## The factors

Three paralogues make up subfamily NR3B: ESRRA (ERRalpha, NR3B1), ESRRB (ERRbeta, NR3B2) and ESRRG (ERRgamma, NR3B3). They were found by homology to the estrogen receptor but are not activated by estradiol; no endogenous ligand is established, the ligand-binding pocket is small and largely filled, and transcriptional output is controlled by coactivator availability, chiefly PGC-1alpha and PGC-1beta (Giguere 2008). Architecturally they resemble other nuclear receptors - a C4 double-zinc-finger DNA-binding domain (DBD) and a ligand-binding domain - but they bind DNA as monomers, and can also homodimerize. ERRalpha is broadly expressed with highest levels in heart, kidney, skeletal muscle and brown adipose tissue; ERRgamma is enriched in heart, brain and kidney; ERRbeta is the most restricted, appearing in extraembryonic ectoderm and trophoblast, the inner ear and pluripotent stem cells. Ten motif models fall here (JASPAR 3, HOCOMOCO 3, CIS-BP 3, Vierstra 1), covering all three genes.

## The motif

The ERR response element is an extended half-site, not a repeat. Binding-site selection with ERRalpha defined it as TNAAGGTCA: the canonical nuclear receptor hexamer AGGTCA preceded by three bases, of which the two immediately 5' are almost always AA (Sladek et al. 1997). In practice the models here read TCAAGGTCA or CAAGGTCA, and the family's data consensus is CAAGGTCA.

The 5' extension is functional, not decorative. The solution structure of the ERRbeta DBD bound to its site showed that monomeric high-affinity binding requires base-specific minor-groove contacts from a modified guanosine-binding AT-hook in the C-terminal extension (CTE) that flanks the core DBD; the CTE is stabilized by packing against the DBD surface that other receptors use for dimerization, a pseudo-dimer interface (Gearhart et al. 2003). That is the structural reason why ERRs need three extra 5' bases while a GR or ER dimer needs a second hexamer instead. Dimeric arrangements do occur: the CIS-BP ESRRG model M03412 is two extended half-sites in tandem (AAGGTCAttTcAAGGTCA), the highest-information model in the family at 22 bits.

Spacing and orientation are what separate this family from its neighbours, and they separate it imperfectly. An inverted AGGTCA repeat with a 3 bp spacer is an ERE; direct repeats with 1-5 bp spacers are RXR-heterodimer elements; a single 5'-extended half-site is an ERR element - but it is also the SF-1/LRH-1 response element (SFRE), and the Vierstra archetype in this family is labelled ESRRA/NR5A for exactly that reason. ERRalpha and ERRbeta also bind and activate through consensus EREs, while ERbeta does not reciprocate (Vanacker et al. 1999). The family data marks one CIS-BP model labelled ESRRA (M07988) as a full ERE belonging with ESR. ESRRA, ESRRB and ESRRG themselves are indistinguishable: their models are 0.96-0.99 similar to one another.

## Where it acts

ERR sites are found at both promoters and distal enhancers, with a strong bias towards nuclear-encoded mitochondrial genes: oxidative phosphorylation subunits, TCA cycle enzymes and fatty-acid beta-oxidation genes, where ERRalpha works with PGC-1alpha. The founding example was an ERRE in the promoter of the medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase gene (Sladek et al. 1997). Genome-wide mapping in heart showed ERRalpha and ERRgamma occupying an overlapping program of cardiac metabolic and contractile genes (Dufour et al. 2007). At such promoters ERR elements co-occur with NRF1, GABPA and YY1 sites. In mouse embryonic stem cells Esrrb sits at pluripotency enhancers with OCT4, SOX2 and NANOG, and is itself a direct Nanog target that can substitute for Nanog (Festuccia et al. 2012).

## Biology and disease

The ERRs are best understood as regulators of oxidative capacity. Esrra-null mice are lean, resistant to diet-induced obesity and impaired in cold adaptation; ERRalpha and ERRgamma together are required for the perinatal switch of the heart to fatty-acid oxidation. Esrrb-null embryos die from placental failure with abnormal chorion development (Luo et al. 1997). In humans, recessive ESRRB mutations cause nonsyndromic hearing loss DFNB35 (Collin et al. 2008). ERRalpha expression is associated with poor outcome in breast cancer, where it supports the metabolic and biosynthetic demands of proliferation and interacts with ERBB2 signalling (Deblois and Giguere 2013). ERRgamma has been studied in prostate cancer and hepatic gluconeogenesis, and inverse agonists of ERRalpha are in preclinical development.

## Reading a hit

The practical warning is length. TCAAGGTCA is a 9-mer with roughly eight informative positions, so an exact match occurs on the order of 10^4 times in the haploid human genome by chance alone, and near-matches many times more. A hit therefore carries very little weight on its own, and far less than a 13-15 bp dimeric element would. Measure the 5' extension explicitly: without the AA at positions -2 and -3 you have a bare half-site that anything in the superfamily could touch, and with an inverted second hexamer three bases downstream you have an ERE instead. A match cannot distinguish ESRRA, ESRRB and ESRRG, nor reliably distinguish ERRs from NR5A1/NR5A2, whose element is the same 9-mer. All three HOCOMOCO models here are grade A with combined ChIP, HT-SELEX and methyl-SELEX evidence (PSM), so direct binding to this sequence is well supported; the uncertainty is about which family member and which site is used, not about the sequence.
families.caveats: The ERR element is a 9 bp extended half-site, which is short: expect on the order of 10^4 chance matches per haploid genome, so a hit alone is weak evidence. It does not distinguish ESRRA, ESRRB and ESRRG, whose models are 0.96-0.99 similar, and it does not distinguish ERRs from NR5A1/NR5A2, which use the same TCAAGGTCA element - the Vierstra archetype here is labelled ESRRA/NR5A. Cross-recognition with the estrogen receptor is real, not just a labelling artefact: ERRs activate through consensus EREs, and one CIS-BP model labelled ESRRA in this family is a full ERE flagged as belonging with ESR. Require the 5' AA extension before calling an ERR site.

families.name: NR4A (NUR77/NURR1)
families.def: NBRE AAAGGTCA monomeric half-site and NurRE. NR4A1/2/3.
families.short: NR4A1 (NUR77), NR4A2 (NURR1) and NR4A3 (NOR-1) are orphan nuclear receptors and immediate-early genes: they are transcribed within minutes of serum stimulation, depolarization or antigen-receptor signaling and their proteins turn over quickly. Unlike most nuclear receptors they bind DNA as monomers, to a single AGGTCA half-site carried on an A/T-rich 5' extension, giving the eight-base NGFI-B response element AAAGGTCA. A separate protein surface, the A box, reads those A-T base pairs in the minor groove. The same receptors can also act as homodimers on the everted NurRE and as heterodimers with RXR. Because a monomeric half-site constrains only eight or nine positions, matches are common by chance, and the AGGTCA core is shared with most of the nuclear receptor superfamily.
families.long:
## The factors

The NR4A subfamily has three paralogues: NR4A1 (NUR77, NGFI-B, TR3), NR4A2 (NURR1) and NR4A3 (NOR-1, MINOR). Each has the standard nuclear receptor layout: an AF-1 region, a DNA-binding domain of two C4 zinc modules, a carboxy-terminal extension containing the A box, and a ligand-binding domain. All three are immediate-early genes induced by serum, growth factors, depolarization, antigen-receptor signaling and stress, with short protein half-lives, so levels are low in resting tissue; NR4A1 was cloned as a nerve growth factor-induced transcript. They are orphans in a strong sense: the NURR1 ligand-binding domain has no accessible ligand pocket, its interior filled with bulky side chains, defining a class of receptors that activate without a ligand (Wang et al. 2003). The three paralogues are largely redundant: NR4A1-null mice have normal thymocyte apoptosis (Lee et al. 1995). Ten motifs are collected here across all four sources.

## The motif

The core element is the NGFI-B response element, NBRE, AAAGGTCA, identified by genetic selection in yeast (Wilson et al. 1991). Its structure explains its length. The two zinc modules read the AGGTCA half-site through the major groove as in other nuclear receptors, while a substructure carboxy-terminal to them, the A box, reaches into the minor groove and reads the three A-T base pairs extending 5' of the half-site; this was the first structure of a nuclear receptor bound to DNA as a monomer (Meinke and Sigler 1999). Domain swaps had already shown that NR4A1 and SF-1 (NR5A1) bind by the same monomeric mechanism with distinct 5' requirements: an amino group in the minor groove of the SF-1 sequence and an asparagine in the SF-1 A box (Wilson et al. 1993). The same receptors use two other arrangements: homodimers on the NurRE, an everted pair of NBRE-related octamers with an unusual spacer, which mediates signaling at the POMC promoter (Philips et al. 1997), and heterodimers with RXR on a direct repeat (Perlmann and Jansson 1995). The collected data agree: the pooled consensus is AAAGGTCA, and five models from three databases give exactly that string. The highest-information model, the Vierstra archetype AC0119:NR4A at 25 bits, is GACCTTTAAAGGTCA: two NBRE octamers head to head with no spacer, not the classic NurRE spacing. Two entries need care. JASPAR NR4A2::RXRA (MA1147.2) is an inverted-repeat dimer model whose nearest neighbors sit outside this family, so it describes a heterodimer, not monomer binding. The archetype AC0114:NR4A/NR2C is flagged in the data as probably belonging with the RXR heterodimers: it is a bare aAGGTCA half-site, exactly what one expects to be ambiguous. Nothing distinguishes the three paralogues by sequence.

## Where it acts

NR4A sites behave like those of other stimulus-induced factors: promoters and signal-responsive enhancers, with occupancy tracking induction of the receptor rather than presence of the motif. They act in T cells, neurons, pituitary corticotropes, macrophages, vascular smooth muscle, liver and adipose tissue, so target programs are cell-type specific. A specific eight-mer is expected about 47,000 times per strand in a 3-Gb genome, so tens of thousands of NBRE matches exist and only a small fraction is ever bound. Composite arrangement matters: NurRE-type pairs and NBRE-RXR direct repeats bind more tightly and are the configurations shown to respond to physiological signals, while a lone NBRE is often weak or non-functional.

## Biology and disease

NR4A2 loss abolishes midbrain dopaminergic neurons in mice and the gene has been examined in Parkinson disease (Zetterstrom et al. 1997). Although single knockouts are near-normal, the subfamily as a group limits T cell effector function: deleting all three NR4A genes relieves an exhaustion-like program and improves tumor control by CAR T cells (Chen et al. 2019). In the pituitary, NR4A1 mediates CRH-induced POMC transcription through the NurRE (Philips et al. 1997). The clearest cancer link is structural: extraskeletal myxoid chondrosarcoma is defined by a translocation fusing EWSR1 to NR4A3, converting the receptor into a constitutive activator (Labelle et al. 1995).

## Reading a hit

A monomeric half-site is much harder to call than a spaced dimer; this is the central practical point. A dimeric element such as a DR3, DR4 or DR5 constrains two 6-bp half-sites plus a fixed spacer, 13-15 positions in all, so a scanner can demand a rare pattern and the arrangement itself is evidence. The NBRE constrains only eight or nine positions, of which six are the AGGTCA half-site shared by most of the nuclear receptor superfamily, so all the family-level information lives in the two or three A-T bases of the 5' extension, and there is no spacer to check. One or two substitutions convert a predicted NBRE into an SF-1 element or into one half of a genuine RXR heterodimer site. Prediction of nuclear receptor elements improves substantially when dimer configuration is modeled, which is unavailable here (Sandelin and Wasserman 2005). Treat a hit as "a nuclear receptor half-site" first. Provenance is comparatively good here: NR4A1.H14CORE.0.PSM.A is grade A with ChIP, HT-SELEX and methyl-HT-SELEX support and NR4A2.H14CORE.0.SM.B has both in vitro assays, so AAAGGTCA is well supported as directly bound. The one NR4A3 model, CIS-BP M00818_2.00, is inferred from the mouse protein at 97% DNA-binding-domain identity rather than measured for human NR4A3 (Weirauch et al. 2014).
families.caveats: The sequence identifies a nuclear receptor half-site, not a receptor. AAAGGTCA constrains eight positions, six of which are the AGGTCA half-site used across the superfamily, so tens of thousands of chance matches exist and one or two substitutions turn a predicted NBRE into an SF-1 element or into half of an RXR heterodimer site. Nothing separates NR4A1, NR4A2 and NR4A3. The AAAGGTCA string itself is well supported in vitro (a grade-A HOCOMOCO model with HT-SELEX and methyl-HT-SELEX evidence), but the only NR4A3 model is inferred from mouse, one Vierstra archetype in this family is flagged as probably belonging with the RXR heterodimers, and the JASPAR NR4A2::RXRA entry is a dimer model rather than an NR4A monomer motif. Occupancy requires the receptor to have been induced.
