families.name: REV-ERB (NR1D)
families.def: RevDR2 and RORE-like sites. NR1D1, NR1D2.
families.short: REV-ERBalpha (NR1D1) and REV-ERBbeta (NR1D2) are nuclear receptors that lack the helix-12 activation surface and act only as repressors, recruiting the NCoR-HDAC3 complex and binding heme as a ligand. They read the same DNA as the RORs: an AGGTCA half-site with a 5' AT-rich extension (the RORE, or RevRE), and preferentially a direct repeat of two such sites separated by 2 bp, called RevDR2, on which they bind as homodimers. Together with the RORs they form the second feedback loop of the mammalian circadian clock, alternately repressing and activating Bmal1 at the same sites. Loss of both paralogues disrupts circadian behavior and causes hepatic steatosis and metabolic derangement.
families.long:
## The factors

REV-ERB is a two-member nuclear-receptor group: NR1D1 (REV-ERBalpha, historically EAR-1) and NR1D2 (REV-ERBbeta, historically RVR or EAR-1R). The *NR1D1* gene lies on the opposite strand of, and overlapping, the thyroid hormone receptor gene *THRA*, which is how it acquired the name "Rev-ErbA". Both proteins have the standard receptor architecture — an N-terminal region, a two-module zinc-binding DNA-binding domain (DBD) with a C-terminal extension (CTE), and a ligand-binding domain (LBD) — but with one decisive difference from most of the superfamily: the LBD lacks helix 12 and therefore has no AF-2 surface. REV-ERBs cannot activate transcription. They are dedicated repressors that recruit the NCoR-HDAC3 corepressor complex, and their LBD binds heme as a physiological ligand, so their activity tracks cellular heme and redox state. Both paralogues are widely expressed, with high levels in liver, skeletal muscle, adipose tissue, brown fat, brain and macrophages, and both are strongly rhythmic, peaking in the early rest phase. NR1D1 protein is short-lived and its abundance oscillates far more than that of most clock proteins.

## The motif

REV-ERBs read the same element as the RORs. A single REV-ERB monomer binds an AGGTCA half-site carrying a 5-6 bp AT-rich 5' extension — the RORE, also called the RevRE in the older REV-ERB literature. Higher-affinity binding requires two such sites arranged as a direct repeat separated by exactly 2 bp, the element named RevDR2, on which REV-ERB binds as a homodimer. The literature writes the core of RevDR2 as AGGTCANNAGGTCA; the motif models collected here retain the AT-rich extensions as well and therefore run 14-18 bp, with a pooled consensus of ANTAGGTCAGTAGGTCA. This is not a disagreement about the element, only about how much flanking sequence a model keeps.

The structural basis is well defined. The crystal structure of the REV-ERBalpha DBD plus CTE bound to RevDR2 shows each zinc module inserting its recognition helix into the major groove of AGGTCA while the CTE runs along the minor groove of the AT-rich extension; the 2-bp spacing is what allows a second protein-DNA interface to form next to the classical one, which is why DR2 and not DR1 or DR4 is the preferred repeat. The same CTE-plus-minor-groove mechanism was described for the monomeric receptor NGFI-B.

Neither paralogue is distinguishable from the other, and neither is reliably distinguishable from ROR. The Vierstra archetype AC0123:NR1D/RORC names both groups precisely because their motifs clustered together.

## Where it acts

RevDR2 and RORE sites occur in promoters and enhancers and are not enriched in CpG islands. The canonical target is the *Bmal1* (*ARNTL*) promoter, where two ROREs are occupied by RORs during the day and by REV-ERBs at night; *Cry1*, *Npas2* and *Nfil3* carry the same arrangement. In the circadian cis-regulatory grammar, the RORE supplies the late-night phase component and works in combination with E-boxes (CLOCK:BMAL1) and D-boxes. In liver and macrophages, REV-ERBalpha also occupies thousands of tissue-specific enhancers together with lineage factors; in liver these are predominantly HNF6 sites.

## Biology and disease

REV-ERB is the repressive arm of the second circadian feedback loop. *Nr1d1*-null mice have a shortened free-running period and altered clock gene amplitude; deleting both paralogues disrupts circadian behavior far more severely and deranges lipid metabolism, with hepatic steatosis and altered bile acid and glucose handling. REV-ERBs also gate inflammatory gene expression in macrophages and set the timing of muscle mitochondrial function. Because the LBD binds heme, synthetic REV-ERB agonists and ROR inverse agonists have been developed as metabolic and immunological tools, and REV-ERB agonists shift wheel-running rhythms and reduce fat mass in mice.

## Reading a hit

A RevDR2 or RORE match tells you the site belongs to the ROR/REV-ERB group. It does not tell you which of the four proteins binds it, and the ROR-versus-REV-ERB distinction matters biologically because the two have opposite signs: RORs recruit coactivators, REV-ERBs recruit NCoR-HDAC3. The two loops compete for identical sequence; the discrimination is temporal and cell-type dependent, not sequence-encoded. Treat the family boundary between the `ROR` and `REV_ERB` entries in this atlas as a labelling convention, not a specificity claim.

Two further cautions. A single AGGTCA is not a REV-ERB site — that hexamer is shared with ESRRA, NR5A, NR4A and the RXR heterodimer partners — so score the full extended element, and prefer the tandem form when you have it, since RevDR2 is far less likely to occur by chance than a 10-mer monomeric site. Second, ChIP-derived motifs for this family should be read carefully: in mouse liver most REV-ERBalpha ChIP-seq peaks arise from tethering to HNF6 rather than from direct RORE binding, so ChIP-only models (HOCOMOCO evidence code `P`, e.g. NR1D1.H14CORE.0.P.B) can carry a partner's specificity. The in vitro models here (evidence `SM`) are the ones that support a direct binding claim.
families.caveats: REV-ERB and ROR sites are the same sequence. A hit here is a ROR/REV-ERB call; nothing in the motif separates NR1D1 from NR1D2, or either from RORA/RORB/RORC, and the Vierstra archetype AC0123:NR1D/RORC says so explicitly. Because the two groups have opposite transcriptional sign, that ambiguity is consequential — resolve it with expression and phase data, not the motif. Require the AT-rich extension; a bare AGGTCA is shared across the superfamily. The tandem RevDR2 form is much more specific than the monomeric site. Finally, ChIP-derived models (HOCOMOCO code P) may reflect tethering: in liver, most REV-ERBalpha peaks are HNF6 sites rather than direct ROREs.

families.name: CTCF
families.def: 19-bp core CCASYAGRKGGCRSYR with upstream module; the insulator/loop-anchor motif. CTCF.
aka: TFClass: more than 3 adjacent zinc finger factors
families.short: CTCF is a single, near-ubiquitously expressed protein whose eleven C2H2 zinc fingers read an asymmetric, roughly 15-20 bp GC-rich sequence, often with a second recognition module a few bases upstream. Tens of thousands of these sites act as insulators and as anchors for cohesin-extruded chromatin loops, so they delimit topologically associating domains and separate enhancers from promoters they should not reach. Because the motif is long, information-rich, and read by a well-characterized finger-to-base code solved in two crystal structures, a CTCF match is one of the few motif hits that predicts real occupancy reasonably often. The site is directional: which strand it lies on determines which way a loop is anchored, and convergent pairs of sites are the ones that form loops.
families.long:
## The factors

CTCF (CCCTC-binding factor) is one protein, not a family. The human gene encodes a 727-residue polypeptide with a central array of eleven Cys2-His2 zinc fingers flanked by N- and C-terminal regions that carry no DNA-binding domain. It is expressed in essentially every cell type examined, and it is extraordinarily conserved: the chicken and human proteins are 93% identical in amino acid sequence (Filippova et al. 1996). CTCF binds DNA as a monomer; no dimerization interface is required, and its long-range activity comes from partners rather than from self-assembly. The most important of these is cohesin: a short segment in the CTCF N terminus docks onto the SA2-SCC1 (STAG2-RAD21) surface of human cohesin, and a 2.7 A crystal structure of that complex showed the interaction is specifically needed for CTCF-anchored loops and for positioning cohesin at CTCF sites (Li et al. 2020). CTCF has exactly one paralogue, the testis-restricted CTCFL/BORIS, which carries an almost identical zinc-finger array and is treated as a separate family here.

## The motif

The high-information core is 15 bp. JASPAR's core model (MA0139.2) reduces to RCCASYAGRKGGCRS in IUPAC, which is the sequence most people mean when they write the CTCF consensus; longer ChIP-derived models are also in use (JASPAR MA1929.2 and MA1930.2 span 31 and 33 positions), corresponding to the 33/34-mer that Schmidt et al. (2012) defined from six mammals. The structural basis is unusually well understood. In the Hashimoto et al. (2017) crystal structure, zinc fingers 3-7 each contact three bases of the 15-bp core, with each conserved nucleotide making a base-specific hydrogen bond to a particular side chain; variable positions also make contacts, which is how CTCF tolerates deviation from consensus. Yin et al. (2017) resolved CTCF on protocadherin sites and split the site into four modules: ZF3 reads module 4, ZF4-7 read modules 3 and 2, and ZF9-11 read an upstream module 1, with ZF8 acting as a spacer that absorbs variable distance between modules 1 and 2. Genome-wide, ZF4-7 anchor CTCF at roughly 80% of targets containing the core motif, while ZF1-2 and ZF8-11 read non-conserved flanks (Nakahashi et al. 2013). Two consequences matter in practice. The site is asymmetric, so it has an orientation, and a central asymmetric A is part of what makes recognition directional. CTCF is also sensitive to cytosine methylation at position 2 of the core but insensitive at position 12, a difference the structure rationalizes; across 19 human cell types, 41% of variable CTCF occupancy was attributable to differential methylation concentrated at two positions in the recognition sequence (Wang et al. 2012).

## Where it acts

The first genome-wide survey reported 13,804 CTCF sites (Kim et al. 2007); current ChIP-seq gives tens of thousands per cell type. Sites are GC-rich but are not concentrated in CpG islands the way GC-box promoters are; they are spread across intergenic space, introns and promoter-proximal regions, and lineage-specific expansions have been driven by waves of retrotransposon activity (Schmidt et al. 2012). Occupied sites are enriched at topologically associating domain boundaries, where they often occur in clusters rather than singly, a redundancy that appears to stabilize boundaries over evolution (Kentepozidou et al. 2020). The essential partner is cohesin. Loops form preferentially between CTCF sites in convergent orientation (Rao et al. 2014), and deleting or inverting a single site changes the loops formed (de Wit et al. 2015; Guo et al. 2015) - the observation that motivated the loop-extrusion model (Sanborn et al. 2015; Fudenberg et al. 2016) and that single-molecule work later explained as DNA-tension-dependent, orientation-specific blocking of extruding cohesin (Davidson et al. 2023).

## Biology and disease

CTCF was defined functionally as the protein required for enhancer-blocking by vertebrate insulators (Bell et al. 1999) and for methylation-sensitive imprinting control at the H19/Igf2 locus. Acute degradation of CTCF abolishes CTCF-CTCF loops and TAD insulation while leaving A/B compartments intact, separating those two layers of genome folding (Nora et al. 2017). In disease, CTCF/cohesin-binding sites are recurrent somatic mutation hotspots in several cancers (Katainen et al. 2015); in IDH-mutant glioma, hypermethylation disrupts a CTCF boundary and allows an enhancer to activate PDGFRA (Flavahan et al. 2016); and germline monoallelic CTCF variants cause an autosomal dominant neurodevelopmental disorder affecting brain, growth and craniofacial development (Valverde de Morales et al. 2023).

## Reading a hit

This is the one family in the atlas where a position-weight-matrix match genuinely carries predictive weight: sites that match the consensus more closely are occupied more often and more constitutively (Plasschaert et al. 2014). Even so, only a fraction of genomic matches are bound in any one cell type, and occupancy is conditional on the methylation state of the CpG at core position 2. Report the strand: a CTCF hit without an orientation is half an answer, because loop anchoring depends on it. A hit cannot distinguish CTCF from CTCFL, which share the zinc-finger array. Finally, check which matrix matched. Two Vierstra archetypes labelled for CTCF are not the CTCF motif at all - AC0214:CTCF/ZNF is a poly-T model (tTTTTgTTTTT) and AC0174:CTCF/ZNF is a short C-rich model (tGCCCCCT, 8.4 bits) - and a hit to either says nothing about CTCF. The genuine CTCF models, including the ChIP-derived HOCOMOCO core model (CTCF.H14CORE.0.P.B, ChIP evidence, grade B), agree with each other and with two independent crystal structures, so the label itself is not in doubt.
families.caveats: Trust a strong CTCF hit more than almost any other motif in this atlas, but not unconditionally. Only some matches are occupied in a given cell type; occupancy depends on the methylation state of the CpG at core position 2, and a site bound in one lineage may be free in another. The hit cannot tell CTCF from CTCFL/BORIS. Orientation is part of the result, not an afterthought. A single site is weak evidence for a domain boundary, since boundaries are usually clusters of sites. And confirm which matrix matched: two Vierstra archetypes carrying the CTCF label are poly-T or short C-rich models that have nothing to do with the CTCF core.

families.name: Estrogen receptors
families.def: ERE: inverted AGGTCA repeat, GGTCAnnnTGACC. ESR1, ESR2.
families.short: The estrogen receptors ERalpha (ESR1) and ERbeta (ESR2) are estradiol-activated nuclear receptors that bind DNA as homodimers on the estrogen response element, a 15 bp inverted repeat of the hexamer AGGTCA with a 3 bp spacer: AGGTCAnnnTGACCT, usually quoted as its 13 bp core GGTCAnnnTGACC. The element differs from the glucocorticoid-type half-site by only two base pairs, and the same 3 bp spacing and dimer geometry are shared with the steroid receptors, so the half-site sequence rather than the architecture is what marks it as estrogenic. ESR1 and ESR2 cannot be told apart by sequence. These sites drive the estrogen program in breast, uterus, bone and liver, and they are the regulatory target of tamoxifen, aromatase inhibitors and fulvestrant.
families.long:
## The factors

Two paralogues: ESR1 (ERalpha) and ESR2 (ERbeta), subfamily NR3A. Both have an N-terminal AF-1 region, a C4 double-zinc-finger DNA-binding domain (DBD), a hinge and a ligand-binding domain that binds 17beta-estradiol and, with different consequences, tamoxifen, raloxifene and fulvestrant. They bind as homodimers and can form ERalpha/ERbeta heterodimers. ERalpha is the dominant form in breast epithelium, uterus, liver, adipose, bone and hypothalamus; ERbeta is lower and more restricted, with ovarian granulosa cells, prostate, colon and some immune cells the usual examples, and much of its biology remains contested (Hewitt and Korach 2018). Nine motif models fall in this family (JASPAR 2, HOCOMOCO 4, CIS-BP 2, Vierstra 1), all labelled ESR1 or ESR2.

## The motif

The estrogen response element (ERE) is an inverted repeat of AGGTCA with three intervening bases: 5'-AGGTCAnnnTGACCT-3', frequently written as the 13 bp core GGTCAnnnTGACC. It was first defined functionally in the 5' flanking region of the Xenopus vitellogenin A2 gene (Klein-Hitpass et al. 1986) and reviewed in detail by Gruber et al. (2004). The crystal structure of the ERalpha DBD bound to a consensus palindrome showed a symmetrical dimer reading two 6 bp half-sites separated by three base pairs, and explained how the receptor discriminates its own half-site from the glucocorticoid half-site, which differs by only two base pairs (Schwabe et al. 1993). Three residues in the first zinc finger decide which of the two half-sites a receptor reads, and swapping them interconverts glucocorticoid and estrogen specificity (Umesono and Evans 1989).

Spacing is the other half of the rule. A 3 bp spacer with the half-sites pointing at each other is an ERE; the same AGGTCA hexamers arranged as direct repeats separated by 1-5 bp are elements for RXR heterodimers instead, and a single extended half-site with a 5' A/T extension is an ERR or NR5A element. The models here are consistent with this: the data consensus is AGGTCAcvnTGnCCt, a 15 bp inverted repeat whose 3' half-site is noticeably more degenerate than the 5' half in ChIP-derived matrices. Common variants are EREs with one or two mismatches, ERE half-sites flanked by SP1 or AP-1 sites, and no ERE at all where ERalpha works by tethering to AP-1 or SP1.

ESR1 and ESR2 are not distinguishable: their models are 0.86-1.00 similar and the Vierstra archetype in this family, AC0122, is labelled ESR/ESRRA because estrogen and estrogen-related receptor motifs cluster together. The confusion runs both ways and is partly biological rather than a labelling error: the CIS-BP ESR1 model M07985 is an extended monomeric half-site (cCAAGGTCA), an ERR-type element, and the family data flags it as belonging with ESRR, while a CIS-BP ESRRA model is a full ERE. ERRalpha and ERRbeta do activate transcription through consensus EREs, whereas ERbeta activity is restricted to the ERE (Vanacker et al. 1999).

## Where it acts

Near-consensus 15 bp EREs are abundant: a genome-wide screen found roughly 70,000 across the human and mouse genomes, enriched near transcription start sites, with only about 1% conserved in the flanking regions of orthologous genes (Bourdeau et al. 2004). Actual ERalpha occupancy is far smaller and mostly distal: genome-wide mapping in MCF-7 cells placed authentic binding sites predominantly in enhancers rather than promoters (Carroll et al. 2006). FOXA1 is required for most of that occupancy and reprogramming FOXA1 redistributes ERalpha (Hurtado et al. 2011); GATA3, TFAP2C and PGR also shape it. ER binding sites differ between tumours and that differential binding tracks clinical outcome (Ross-Innes et al. 2012). Many peaks contain only a half-site, consistent with indirect or tethered recruitment.

## Biology and disease

EREs carry the estrogen response in mammary and uterine epithelium, bone remodelling, hepatic lipid handling and hypothalamic feedback on gonadotropins. Esr1-null mice are infertile with hypoplastic uterus and anovulatory ovaries; Esr2-null mice have milder, largely ovarian phenotypes. About three quarters of breast cancers are ER-positive and are treated by blocking the receptor or depleting its ligand. Acquired ESR1 ligand-binding-domain mutations, chiefly Y537S and D538G, are recurrent in endocrine-resistant metastatic breast cancer and make the receptor constitutively active (Robinson et al. 2013); because they do not change the DBD, the motif itself is unaltered, and the consequence is where and how much the receptor binds rather than what it binds.

## Reading a hit

A full 15 bp ERE is a reasonably specific signal for the estrogen/ERR branch, but it cannot tell ESR1 from ESR2, and it overlaps with ERRalpha and ERRbeta, which bind consensus EREs. Check the spacing and orientation before naming anything: AGGTCA inverted with a 3 bp gap is an ERE, direct repeats are RXR-heterodimer elements, and a lone AGGTCA with a 5' AA is an ERR element. With about 10 informative positions, exact consensus 13-mers occur on the order of 10^3 times per haploid genome and near-matches tens of thousands of times, so most hits are not bound in any given cell. Two of the four HOCOMOCO models here are bare half-sites (AGGTCA, TGACCT) and all four are ChIP-derived (evidence code P), which in this family means they can include tethering signal; there is no in vitro (S/M) model for either receptor in this set. A ChIP peak with no ERE is expected, not anomalous.
families.caveats: A full inverted-repeat ERE is among the more specific nuclear receptor signals, but it marks the estrogen/ERR branch rather than a receptor: ESR1 and ESR2 are indistinguishable by sequence, and ERRalpha and ERRbeta bind consensus EREs too. One CIS-BP model labelled ESR1 in this family is actually an extended ERR-type half-site and is flagged as such. All four HOCOMOCO models here are ChIP-derived, with no in vitro entry for either receptor, so they may carry signal from tethered recruitment via AP-1 or SP1; conversely, many genuine ER peaks contain only a half-site. Near-consensus EREs number in the tens of thousands genome-wide, so pair a hit with accessibility or ChIP evidence.

families.name: NF-Y (CBF)
families.def: CCAAT box. NFYA, NFYB, NFYC.
families.short: NF-Y is a heterotrimer of NFYA, NFYB and NFYC that binds the CCAAT box, one of the most frequent elements in eukaryotic promoters. NFYB and NFYC carry histone-fold domains and pair like H2A/H2B, gripping the DNA backbone and bending it; NFYA supplies the only sequence-specific contacts, inserting an alpha helix into the minor groove to read CCAAT. All three subunits are required for binding, so the three gene symbols describe one molecular entity and one motif. NF-Y is ubiquitous, sits at a fixed distance upstream of transcription start sites, and helps open chromatin for cell-type-specific factors. NF-YA is overexpressed and alternatively spliced in several cancers.
families.long:
## The factors

NF-Y, also called CBF and historically CP1, is an obligate heterotrimer. NFYB and NFYC each
contain a histone-fold domain (HFD) and first dimerize with each other; the NFYB/NFYC dimer then
recruits NFYA, and only the complete trimer binds DNA. Yeast HAP2, HAP3 and HAP5 are the
orthologues of NFYA, NFYB and NFYC respectively, and the conservation is high enough that subunits
are interchangeable across large evolutionary distances. NFYA exists as two major splice isoforms,
long and short, differing in the glutamine-rich activation region; the short isoform is enriched
in embryonic stem cells. NFYB and NFYC are encoded by single genes with essentially constitutive
expression, so NF-Y activity is regulated largely through NFYA levels and isoform choice. Because
all three subunits are needed, a motif labelled NFYA, NFYB or NFYC in these databases refers to
the same complex and the same site; the three-way split in this family's data (nine models across
three symbols) reflects which subunit was tagged in an experiment, not three specificities.

## The motif

The consensus is the 5-base CCAAT box, generally quoted with flanking preferences as CCAATCA or,
on the reverse strand, TGATTGG; databases here report both renderings plus CCAATCAG and CATTGGCC.
The crystal structure of NF-Y on a 25-bp CCAAT oligonucleotide explained the division of labor.
The NFYB/NFYC histone-fold dimer binds the sugar-phosphate backbone over about 25 bp, mimicking
the H2A/H2B-DNA interaction in a nucleosome and bending the DNA, but makes no base-specific
contacts. NFYA contributes the specificity: a short alpha helix inserts deeply into the minor
groove and reads the CCAAT bases directly. This architecture explains two features of the motif.
First, information is concentrated on five bases with modest preferences a few positions to each
side, giving models of 10-14 bits, and the flanking positions matter partly because they set the
DNA's bendability rather than because they are read. Second, NF-Y has nucleosome-like,
non-sequence-specific affinity in addition to its specific contacts, which is why it behaves like
a chromatin protein as well as a transcription factor. Not every CCAAT box is an NF-Y site: the
element was long used as a generic label, and several unrelated families were grouped under
"CCAAT-binding protein", including the C/EBPs and NFI/CTF. Those are different proteins with
different folds.

## Where it acts

NF-Y is the most positionally constrained factor in this batch. Its CCAAT boxes sit
overwhelmingly in core and proximal promoters, classically between 60 and 100 bp upstream of the
major transcription start site, and frequently in bidirectional promoters. ChIP-on-chip and later
genome-wide work showed that a substantial minority of NF-Y sites nonetheless lie outside core
promoters. NF-Y is bound to a large fraction of cell cycle gene promoters (cyclin A, CDC25C, CDK1)
often together with E2F factors, to the Y box of MHC class II promoters where it binds
cooperatively with the RFX complex about 15-20 bp away, to the CCAAT boxes of heat shock gene
promoters, and to the globin promoters. It recruits histone acetyltransferases including GCN5/PCAF
and p300, contacts TBP, and imposes H3K4 trimethylation through Ash2L. In embryonic stem cells NF-Y
is required to maintain identity and opens chromatin for lineage-determining factors, which makes
it one of the clearest examples of a ubiquitous factor acting as a chromatin accessibility
provider rather than a specificity determinant.

## Biology and disease

NF-Y is essential: loss of NFYA or of the histone-fold subunits is lethal in cells and in mice, and
NF-Y regulates cell cycle progression, cholesterol and lipid metabolism genes, and the
endoplasmic-reticulum stress and heat shock programs. Because the CCAAT box is so widespread, the
downstream consequences are broad rather than tissue-specific. In disease, the clearest links are
quantitative: NF-YA is overexpressed, and its isoform ratio shifted, in breast cancer and in lung
adenocarcinoma, and NF-YA is required for proliferation of epithelial ovarian cancer cells through
EZH2 upregulation. NF-YA splice isoform status has been reported as a prognostic variable in low
grade endometrial cancer. There is no well-established Mendelian disease caused by NFYA, NFYB or
NFYC mutation, which is consistent with the complex being required in every cell.

## Reading a hit

A CCAAT match is 5 bp of information and occurs roughly a million times in the human genome, so a
hit in isolation is not evidence. What makes a CCAAT hit credible is position: an NF-Y site 60-100
bp upstream of an annotated transcription start site, ideally with a preferred flank (CCAATCA or
its reverse complement TGATTGG), is a reasonable prediction, while the same 5-mer in an intron or
a distal enhancer is usually noise. The paralogue problem is unusual here and easy: there are no
paralogues to separate, because NFYA, NFYB and NFYC are three subunits of one complex. Treat all
three labels as synonyms for NF-Y. The main real confusion is with other families historically
called CCAAT-binding. C/EBP factors bind ATTGC-containing palindromes, not CCAAT, and NFI/CTF,
whose old name is literally "CCAAT box transcription factor", binds TTGGC(N5)GCCAA; its GCCAA
half-site contains a CCAAT-like string and will cross-score on loose CCAAT models. If a scan
returns both NF-Y and NFI matches at the same position, they are competing explanations. Finally,
note that every HOCOMOCO model in this family is ChIP-only (evidence code P, grade B) and the
label agreement scores are correspondingly moderate; the structural and biochemical evidence for
NFYA reading CCAAT is strong, but these particular matrices are peak-derived.
families.caveats: CCAAT is 5 bp and occurs about a million times in the genome, so only position makes a hit credible: NF-Y sites cluster 60-100 bp upstream of transcription start sites. NFYA, NFYB and NFYC are subunits of one obligate trimer, so the three labels denote one motif, not three specificities, and only NFYA makes base contacts. The recurring confusion is with other families once called CCAAT-binding: NFI/CTF's GCCAA half-site and C/EBP sites will cross-score on loose CCAAT models and are competing explanations, not corroboration. All HOCOMOCO models here are ChIP-derived (grade B), though the structure independently confirms CCAAT reading.

families.name: BED-type zinc finger
families.def: hAT-transposase-derived BED fingers. ZBED1 (hDREF, TATCGATA), ZBED2/4/5.
families.short: BED fingers are zinc-coordinating DNA-binding modules named for the two proteins in which they were first recognized, Drosophila BEAF and DREF, and they are shared with the hAT superfamily of DNA transposases. Vertebrate ZBED genes arose from at least two independent domestication events of hAT elements, so this is a second family of transposase recognition modules turned into host transcription factors. Nine motifs cover four proteins. Only ZBED1, the human DREF orthologue hDREF, has a strong and reproducible site: all four of its models converge on TATCGCGACAT, a relative of the Drosophila DNA replication-related element TATCGATA. ZBED2, ZBED4 and ZBED5 contribute short, weaker and partly conflicting models.
families.long:
## The factors

The BED finger was described in 2000 as a small zinc-binding DNA-binding domain found in two otherwise unrelated groups of proteins: chromatin boundary-element-binding proteins, of which the Drosophila factors BEAF and DREF gave the domain its name, and hAT-superfamily transposases. Vertebrate ZBED genes are the domesticated descendants of the transposase side of that split. A phylogenetic survey showed they derive from at least two independent domestication events in jawed vertebrate ancestors and form two monophyletic clades: one containing ZBED2, ZBED3, ZBED4, ZBEDX and ZBED6, the other containing ZBED1, with ZBED5 separate again and related to Buster DNA transposons. The family is an unusually clear demonstration that one class of transposon-derived protein module can be recruited repeatedly and independently into quite different host regulatory pathways.

Four proteins carry motifs here. ZBED1 is hDREF, the human orthologue of Drosophila DREF, a 694-residue protein that shares only about 22 percent identity with the fly factor; it self-associates through its hATC domain, and that self-association is required both for nuclear accumulation and for DNA binding. ZBED2 is expressed in keratinocytes and aberrantly in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma. ZBED4 is a cone photoreceptor and Muller cell protein of the human retina. ZBED5 is the Buster1-derived member. ZBED6, the best-known domesticated ZBED of all - it is encoded inside an intron of ZC3H11A and represses IGF2 - contributes no motif to this family and is not filed here.

## The motif

ZBED1 dominates the family. Its CIS-BP, JASPAR, HOCOMOCO and Vierstra models all read essentially the same eleven to twelve base pairs, TATCGCGACAT, with pairwise similarities of 0.98 to 1.00 and 17 to 19 bits of information - by some distance the best-supported site in this entry, and the source of the family consensus. Its relationship to the fly element is informative but not exact: Drosophila DREF binds as a homodimer to the palindromic DNA replication-related element TATCGATA, while the human in vitro models centre on a TATCG core followed by CGACAT. In human cells, hDRE-like sequences were found within 200 base pairs upstream of the transcription start site in 22 of 79 ribosomal protein genes, and hDREF binds them both in vitro and in chromatin.

The remaining models are short and much weaker. ZBED2 gives CGAAACC in JASPAR and CGAAaCt in HOCOMOCO, which agree with each other (similarity 0.92) but carry only about 10 bits. ZBED5 gives the six-base GGwACC. ZBED4 is the problem case: HOCOMOCO reports acCaGAACCAg while JASPAR reports CCCGCcCCGC, and the two are unrelated. Independent in vitro selection with recombinant Zbed4 recovered poly-G tracts and GC-box core signatures, which supports the JASPAR model and not the HOCOMOCO one. Overall family cohesion is 0.57, and that number is misleading: it reflects four nearly identical ZBED1 models plus three unrelated short models rather than a graded family.

## Where it acts

ZBED1/hDREF sites sit in promoters of proliferation-associated genes, prominently ribosomal protein genes, where they act as positive elements; hDREF expression and ribosomal protein gene expression both rise from late G1 into S phase, and knocking hDREF down reduces both ribosomal protein transcript levels and proliferation in normal human fibroblasts. ZBED2 acts at promoters co-occupied with IRF1, where it behaves as a sequence-specific repressor of interferon-stimulated genes by antagonising IRF1-mediated activation. ZBED4's sites, on the present evidence, are G-rich and GC-box-like and therefore fall in the same promoter-proximal compartment as the SP/KLF factors.

## Biology and disease

hDREF is required for normal proliferation, and its self-association mutants fail to enter the nucleus. ZBED2 is preferentially expressed in the squamous molecular subtype of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma and is associated with inferior survival; it represses the pancreatic progenitor programme, enhances motility and promotes invasion, and blunts the growth arrest that follows interferon signalling. ZBED4 is expressed in cones and Muller glia of human retina but only in Muller cells in mouse, a species difference worth remembering before transferring mouse data. ZBED6, outside this family, regulates IGF2 and muscle growth and explains a major porcine growth quantitative trait locus - the textbook example of a domesticated transposon becoming a physiologically important repressor.

## Reading a hit

Trust the ZBED1 model and treat the rest with caution. TATCGCGACAT is eleven informative base pairs and will be genuinely rare, so a good match in a promoter, particularly a ribosomal protein or other growth gene promoter, is a reasonable ZBED1/hDREF call. The short ZBED2, ZBED4 and ZBED5 models are six to ten base pairs and will match constantly; they need expression and occupancy evidence before they mean anything. For ZBED4, prefer the GC-rich JASPAR model over the HOCOMOCO one, and note that a GC-box-like match cannot be attributed to ZBED4 rather than to any SP/KLF factor. Finally, a BED-finger hit does not distinguish the domesticated factor from an active hAT transposase carrying the same recognition module.
families.caveats: Only ZBED1 has a reproducible, information-rich site; the other three members contribute short models of six to ten base pairs that will match frequently by chance. ZBED4 is internally inconsistent: the HOCOMOCO model (acCaGAACCAg) and the JASPAR model (CCCGCcCCGC) are unrelated, and published in vitro selection favours the GC-rich JASPAR version, so the HOCOMOCO ZBED4 model should be treated as unsupported here. The family cohesion figure of 0.57 is an artefact of four near-duplicate ZBED1 models sitting beside three unrelated ones. ZBED6, the best-studied domesticated ZBED, contributes no motif and cannot be scanned for. Nothing in a BED-finger match separates a domesticated ZBED from an active hAT transposase.

families.name: HNF1
families.def: GTTAATNATTAAC palindrome. HNF1A, HNF1B.
families.short: HNF1A and HNF1B are the only two members of this family, and they bind an unusually long 13-bp near-palindrome, GTTAATNATTAAC, as an obligate dimer. Each subunit contributes an atypical homeodomain carrying a 21-residue insertion, paired with a POU-specific-like domain that was only recognized once the protein-DNA structure was solved. Because the dimer is rigid, the spacing between the two half-sites is fixed and the resulting motif carries about 15-16 bits of information - among the most specific sites of any homeodomain-related family. The two factors drive liver, pancreatic islet, kidney tubule and intestinal gene expression, and heterozygous loss of either causes a distinct form of monogenic diabetes (MODY3 for HNF1A, MODY5 with renal cysts for HNF1B).
families.long:
## The factors

The family has exactly two human members: HNF1A (historically TCF1, LFB1) and HNF1B (TCF2, vHNF1). Both are modular. An N-terminal dimerization domain of roughly 32 residues forms an intertwined four-helix bundle in the dimer; a central region provides an atypical POU-specific-like fold; and the DNA-contacting homeodomain carries a 21-amino-acid insertion in the loop between helices 2 and 3 that no other homeodomain has. Dimerization is obligate for high-affinity binding, and HNF1A and HNF1B form homodimers as well as heterodimers, so the two proteins compete for and share the same sites. The dimerization domain is stabilized by the cofactor DCoH/PCBD1. Expression is restricted and partly complementary: HNF1B appears earlier and more broadly in the developing pancreas, liver and kidney, while HNF1A dominates in adult hepatocytes, pancreatic islets, renal proximal tubule, stomach and intestine.

## The motif

The site is the 13-bp near-palindrome GTTAATNATTAAC. Each GTTAAT half-site is read by one homeodomain, and the central position carries essentially no information, which is why the databases render it as an N. The cocrystal of HNF1A residues 83-279 with a high-affinity promoter showed two identical protein molecules on one site and revealed a second domain structurally similar to POU-specific domains that could not be predicted from the amino acid sequence; atypical elements in both domains create a stable interface, distinguishing HNF1A from the flexible POU-homeodomain proteins whose linker allows half-sites to be rearranged. That rigidity is the whole story of the motif: the half-site spacing cannot vary, so the site is long, palindromic and highly informative. All four collections agree closely - JASPAR MA0046.3 and MA0153.2, the HOCOMOCO A-grade models HNF1A.H14CORE.0.PS.A and HNF1B.H14CORE.0.PS.A, two CIS-BP models and the Vierstra archetype AC0650 all give GTTAATNATTAAC at 13-16 bits, and family cohesion is 0.86. HNF1A and HNF1B are not distinguishable from sequence. One JASPAR entry labelled Hnf1A (MA1991.2) instead reads cCTTTGATcT; its nearest neighbours across all four databases lie in the TCF/LEF family, and CTTTG(A/T)T is the canonical TCF7/LEF1 site, so that model should not be used as an HNF1 motif.

## Where it acts

HNF1 sites sit in the promoters of tissue-specific genes - albumin, alpha-1-antitrypsin, fibrinogen, phenylalanine hydroxylase, pyruvate kinase, and many transporters of the renal proximal tubule - and a systematic survey of vertebrate sequence found them concentrated in such promoters rather than spread through the genome. Genome-scale location analysis in human liver and pancreatic islets placed HNF1A on a large set of promoters shared extensively with HNF4A and ONECUT1/HNF6, with the three factors binding overlapping target sets and each other's genes, so HNF1 hits very often occur in clusters with those motifs rather than alone. Arithmetically the site is rare: with 12 informative positions, an exact 13-mer match is expected only a few hundred times in 3.1 Gb, which is orders of magnitude below a typical 6-8 bp transcription factor site.

## Biology and disease

Heterozygous loss-of-function mutations in HNF1A are the most common Mendelian cause of diabetes mellitus (MODY3), and the mutational hotspot in the DNA-binding region was the reason for solving the protein-DNA structure. Mutations in HNF1B cause MODY5, generally with extrapancreatic features - renal cysts and dysplasia, genital tract malformations and pancreatic hypoplasia - described as renal cysts and diabetes syndrome. Hnf1a-null mice develop hepatic dysfunction, phenylketonuria from loss of phenylalanine hydroxylase, and a renal Fanconi syndrome, which maps neatly onto the human phenotypes. Biallelic HNF1A inactivation also defines a recognized molecular subtype of hepatocellular adenoma.

## Reading a hit

Of all the families in this atlas that derive from a homeodomain, this is the one where a sequence match is most informative. A full GTTAATNATTAAC is long enough that chance matches are rare, and finding one in a hepatocyte, islet, renal tubule or intestinal regulatory region is reasonable evidence of real HNF1 occupancy. Two limitations. First, the hit cannot tell you whether HNF1A, HNF1B or a heterodimer is responsible; use expression, since the two genes are expressed in overlapping but not identical tissues. Second, do not call a single GTTAAT half-site an HNF1 site - on its own it is a generic TAAT-type homeodomain core shared with most of the superfamily. The A-grade HOCOMOCO models carry HT-SELEX (S) support, so the claim that these proteins bind this sequence in vitro is solid and does not rest on ChIP alone.
families.caveats: The two members are indistinguishable from sequence, so a hit means HNF1A, HNF1B or a heterodimer. The full 13-bp palindrome is specific enough that false positives are uncommon, but half-site-only matches (GTTAAT) are generic homeodomain cores and should not be reported as HNF1. One JASPAR model labelled Hnf1A (MA1991.2) is a TCF/LEF-type site (CTTTGAT) and is flagged as such by its nearest neighbours; avoid it. Evidence for the canonical motif is in vitro as well as ChIP-based, so the sequence claim is well supported. Occupancy is still tissue-restricted: outside liver, islet, kidney and gut, a match is unlikely to be bound.

families.name: GFI1 / GFI1B
families.def: AATC core, TAAATCAC(A/T)GC. GFI1, GFI1B.
families.short: GFI1 and GFI1B are six-fingered C2H2 zinc-finger repressors of blood cell development that bind a well-defined AATC-core site, TAAATCAC(A/T)GC. Only fingers 3, 4 and 5 make the sequence-specific contacts; repression comes from the N-terminal SNAG peptide, which docks into LSD1 and pulls in the LSD1/CoREST complex. GFI1 acts in granulocyte, T-cell and hematopoietic stem cell programs, GFI1B in erythroid and megakaryocyte programs, and the two proteins bind indistinguishable sequences, so a motif hit identifies the pair rather than one member. Dominant-negative GFI1 mutations cause severe congenital neutropenia; dominant-negative GFI1B mutations cause gray platelet syndrome. The site is AT-rich, information-dense and unusually specific for a C2H2 motif.
families.long:
## The factors

Two paralogues: GFI1 (growth factor independence 1) and GFI1B, each about 330-420 residues, with six C-terminal C2H2 zinc fingers and a 20-residue N-terminal SNAG domain. Gfi-1 was found as the target of provirus integration in rat T-cell lymphoma lines that had been selected for interleukin-2-independent growth, which is how it got its name. The SNAG peptide is the repression module: it inserts into the substrate-binding pocket of the histone demethylase LSD1 (KDM1A) and thereby recruits the LSD1/CoREST/HDAC complex to GFI-bound sites, so both proteins work as sequence-specific adaptors for a chromatin-modifying machine rather than as intrinsic repressors. They bind DNA as monomers; the two paralogues share the same DNA-binding surface but differ outside it, and they are largely non-overlapping in expression. GFI1 is expressed in hematopoietic stem cells, granulocyte-monocyte progenitors, T cells and inner ear sensory cells; GFI1B in erythroid and megakaryocytic cells. Because they cross-repress each other's genes, their expression domains are largely exclusive despite identical sequence preference.

## The motif

The site was defined by random-oligonucleotide selection with recombinant GFI1 as TAAATCAC(A/T)GCA, with an AATC core whose bases are the most sensitive to mutation; methylation interference and mutant probes confirmed the internal hierarchy, and deletion mapping showed that only zinc fingers 3, 4 and 5 are needed for sequence-specific binding - three adjacent fingers reading roughly nine bases of major groove, which matches the length of the informative region. The family data agrees closely. JASPAR renders GFI1 as AAATCACTGC and Gfi1B as AAATCACAGC; the Vierstra archetype AC0241:GFI/GFI1B reads AAATCACWGC; and the HOCOMOCO grade-A models are written GCTGTGATTT, which is the reverse complement of the same site rather than a different motif. At 12-15 bits this is one of the more informative C2H2 motifs, and the AT-rich AATC core is distinctive enough that false positives are less of a problem than for E-box or GC-box families. Two entries in the data are less useful: a CIS-BP GFI1 model reduced to AATC alone (2.6 bits) and a second Vierstra archetype, AC0394:GFI, reading ATATCAC, which matches the main GFI cluster poorly (0.72). One long HOCOMOCO GFI1B model, AGTGVNNTGCAGTGATTT, looks like two core sites in opposite orientation separated by a variable spacer; whether that reflects a genuine dimeric arrangement or a selection artifact is not settled, and the single-site models are the safer default. GFI1 and GFI1B motifs are 0.96 similar and cannot be separated from sequence.

## Where it acts

GFI sites sit in promoters and enhancers of lineage-restricted blood genes rather than in CpG islands; the motif is AT-rich and therefore under-represented in CpG-island promoters. The best-validated target is ELANE (ELA2, neutrophil elastase), which GFI1 represses in granulocyte progenitors; GFI1 and GFI1B also bind their own and each other's regulatory regions, producing a cross-antagonistic circuit that helps keep the myeloid and erythroid programs apart. Genome-wide, GFI1 co-occupies myeloid enhancers with PU.1/SPI1, RUNX1, and the LSD1/CoREST complex, and GFI1B with GATA1 and TAL1 in erythroid and megakaryocytic cells. Because occupancy depends on LSD1 recruitment, GFI-bound sites are typically nucleosome-depleted regions marked by H3K4 methylation that is then removed.

## Biology and disease

Gfi1-null mice have severe neutropenia with an accumulation of atypical immature myeloid cells and heightened inflammatory responses. In humans, heterozygous dominant-negative GFI1 mutations (the recurrent N382S substitution in zinc finger 5) cause severe congenital neutropenia and derepress ELA2, tying the human disease directly to loss of DNA binding. Gfi1b-null mouse embryos die around midgestation with arrested erythroid and megakaryocytic differentiation, and in humans a dominant-negative GFI1B truncation causes gray platelet syndrome, with macrothrombocytopenia and platelets deficient in alpha-granules. Both genes appear in leukemia: GFI1 levels modulate the course of myeloid leukemia and a low-expression GFI1 variant is associated with acute myeloid leukemia risk, while GFI1B is recurrently affected in myelodysplastic contexts. The clinical genetics of both genes are dominated by dominant-negative alleles rather than simple haploinsufficiency, which is consistent with a protein that occupies sites and recruits a corepressor.

## Reading a hit

This is one of the better-behaved families in the C2H2 world. The AATC-core site is long, AT-rich and information-dense, so a strong match is meaningful and unlikely to be a coincidence in a short query. What a match does not tell you is which paralogue: GFI1 and GFI1B read the same sequence, and the Vierstra archetype name AC0241:GFI/GFI1B is an explicit statement that the two were not separable. Use expression to decide - a granulocyte or T-cell context favors GFI1, an erythroid or megakaryocytic one GFI1B. Evidence types are mostly good: HOCOMOCO GFI1 and GFI1B core models are grade A with PSM evidence (ChIP plus HT-SELEX plus methyl-HT-SELEX), and JASPAR MA0038.3 for GFI1 is HT-SELEX, so the in vitro basis is solid. Two entries warrant care: JASPAR MA0483.2 is a ChIP-seq-derived matrix for mouse Gfi1B, so it carries both a cross-species and an indirect-binding caveat, and the 4 bp CIS-BP GFI1 entry is too degenerate to scan with usefully.
families.caveats: The motif itself is trustworthy - long, AT-rich, 12-15 bits, defined in vitro by site selection and reproduced by HT-SELEX - so a strong match is usually a real GFI-family site. What it cannot do is name the paralogue: GFI1 and GFI1B motifs are 0.96 similar and one Vierstra archetype merges them by name. Resolve the ambiguity with cell type, not sequence. Avoid the 4 bp CIS-BP GFI1 entry (AATC, 2.6 bits), which will match everywhere, and treat the mouse ChIP-derived JASPAR Gfi1B matrix as the weakest member. The extended double-site HOCOMOCO GFI1B model should not be assumed to represent obligate dimeric binding.

families.name: ZNF143 / THAP11 (SBS)
families.def: SPH/SBS element ACTACAATTCCC, bound by ZNF143 and by THAP11 (Ronin) with HCFC1; also ZNF76.
families.short: The SPH element, also called the SBS, is a promoter element read by three proteins that are not close relatives. ZNF143 (originally Staf) and its paralogue ZNF76 are C2H2 zinc-finger activators; THAP11 (Ronin) uses an unrelated THAP zinc-coordinating domain and occupies the same sequence in a complex with the coactivator HCFC1. The site sits close to transcription start sites at thousands of CpG-island promoters, where it drives small nuclear RNA genes transcribed by RNA polymerase II and III and a large set of protein-coding genes, prominently nuclear-encoded mitochondrial and ribosomal ones. The element was once presented as a sequence-specific anchor for chromatin loops; that role has since been retracted, but its promoter activity is well supported.
families.long:
## The factors

ZNF143 was cloned as Staf, the selenocysteine tRNA gene transcription-activating factor, a zinc-finger protein that activates an RNA polymerase III promoter; it was soon shown to work on polymerase II promoters as well, including the U6 snRNA gene, whose enhancer-like distal region contains the same element (there called SPH). The DNA-binding region is a tandem array of seven C2H2 zinc fingers, with a separate N-terminal activation domain. ZNF76 is the close paralogue and has essentially the same in vitro specificity. THAP11/Ronin is unrelated in fold: its DNA-binding domain is a THAP domain, a zinc-coordinating domain of transposase ancestry that reads adjacent major and minor grooves, and it binds the element as part of a complex with HCFC1 (HCF-1). ZNF143, THAP11 and HCFC1 occupy overlapping sets of promoters, and the three are individually essential; ZNF143 is deeply conserved in vertebrates, and zebrafish carry two znf143 paralogues.

## The motif

The functional element is bipartite and about 18 base pairs long. The half that carries most of the information is written TCCCAYAATGCA; upstream of it, separated by nothing or a base or two, sits the ACTACAA box, giving the composite form that the ChIP-derived matrices in this family read as ACTACAATTCCCAGCATG (reverse complement CATGCTGGGAATTGTAGT); the element is more often quoted in the literature in the shortened form ACTACAATTCCC used above. The two halves are contacted by different parts of the finger array, which is why databases built from different assays capture different portions of the site. In this family, the in vitro matrices — the HT-SELEX/methyl-SELEX ZNF76 matrix and JASPAR MA0088.2 (ZNF143) and MA1716.2 (ZNF76) — cover the TCCCACAATGCA half, in the opposite orientation, while the ChIP-derived HOCOMOCO matrices and the CIS-BP ZNF143 matrix carry the full bipartite word including ACTACAA. The family-level dataConsensus, CGGGGCATGCTGGGAADTGTAG, is the complete site read on the minus strand, which is why it looks unlike the ACTACAATTCCC form given above. ZNF143, ZNF76 and THAP11 are not distinguishable from sequence: their matrices are each other's nearest neighbours across all four databases.

## Where it acts

This is a promoter motif, not an enhancer motif. Occurrences concentrate within roughly 100-200 base pairs of transcription start sites in CpG islands, often at divergent promoter pairs, and the element is one of the small number of words enriched at bidirectional promoters. It is also a fixture of the type 3 polymerase III promoters (U6, tRNA-Sec, and related small RNA genes), where it works together with the SNAPc complex and the PSE. At protein-coding promoters the element coincides with HCFC1, YY1 and GABP occupancy, making it part of a recurring core-promoter module rather than a stand-alone site. Overlapping ZNF143, THAP11 and Notch1 sites at the same promoters have been described, so occupancy can be competitive. Tens of thousands of matches to the full motif exist in the human genome, but the strongly occupied subset is in the low thousands and is largely invariant between cell types.

## Biology and disease

Depletion of ZNF143 is lethal in cells and in mouse embryos. Degron experiments place its direct output on nuclear-encoded mitochondrial genes and ribosomal genes: loss causes severe mitochondrial dysfunction and blocks proliferation and differentiation, and it acts by stimulating transcription initiation at promoters it occupies directly, activating most and repressing some. THAP11/Ronin knockout arrests mouse embryos before implantation and is required for embryonic stem cell self-renewal, and mutations in HCFC1 and THAP11 cause an inborn error of cobalamin metabolism with ribosomopathy features. ZNF143 has been reported as overexpressed in several cancers, but the mechanistic claims that received most attention were architectural rather than oncogenic.

The architectural story is the important caution here. ZNF143 was reported to occupy chromatin-interaction anchors and to provide sequence specificity for promoter loops, with and without CTCF, and later to mediate CTCF-bound promoter-enhancer loops in haematopoietic stem cells. Two 2025 degron studies overturned this. Acute depletion of ZNF143/ZFP143 in mouse and human cells changed no loops, and one study showed that a widely used ZNF143 antibody cross-reacts with CTCF, which is how the factor came to be placed at loop anchors in the first place. The current view is that ZNF143 is an essential promoter-proximal transcription factor with an unusually long chromatin residence time and no general looping function.

## Reading a hit

A confident match tells you that you are almost certainly at a promoter, and it tells you the family, not the protein: ZNF143, ZNF76 and THAP11/HCFC1 all read this word and cannot be separated from sequence. If the hit came from a ChIP peak set, check which antibody was used before concluding anything about loops or CTCF, and do not treat co-occurrence with CTCF as evidence of a composite element. Because the site is bipartite, a hit on only the TCCCAYAATGCA half is weaker evidence than a hit spanning both halves, and matrices in this family differ in which half they model; scan with several and compare. The motif is information-rich, so chance matches to the full site are uncommon in a single promoter but not negligible genome-wide.
families.caveats: A match identifies the SPH/SBS element, not a specific protein: ZNF143, ZNF76 and THAP11 with HCFC1 all occupy it, and in vitro data support direct binding for all three. The main hazard is historical rather than motif-based. ChIP-derived ZNF143 peak sets in the literature are contaminated by CTCF cross-reactivity of a common antibody, so any inference from a hit to loop anchoring, CTCF cooperation or three-dimensional architecture is unsafe; the 2025 degron studies found no looping function. Also note that the four databases model different portions of the bipartite site, in opposite orientations, so scores are not comparable across matrices and a partial match may reflect the matrix rather than the sequence.

families.name: OVOL (OVO-like)
families.def: CCGTTA core. OVOL1, OVOL2, OVOL3.
families.short: OVOL1 and OVOL2 are C2H2 zinc-finger repressors, the mammalian counterparts of Drosophila OVO/shavenbaby, that bind a short AT-flanked core, CCGTTA (equivalently TAACGG on the other strand). They act mainly as repressors of the epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, holding epithelial cells in an epithelial state by shutting down ZEB1, ZEB2 and other EMT inducers, and OVOL1 additionally represses its own promoter and MYC. Mouse knockouts show defects in hair follicles, sperm, kidney, mammary ductal morphogenesis and epidermal progenitor arrest. In humans, a promoter point mutation that mis-expresses OVOL2 in corneal endothelium causes posterior polymorphous corneal dystrophy type 1. OVOL1 and OVOL2 share one motif and cannot be separated from sequence.
families.long:
## The factors

The OVOL genes are the vertebrate orthologues of Drosophila ovo/shavenbaby (svb), a single locus whose
alternative transcripts supply two genetic functions: svb for the extracellular projections of epidermal
cells and ovo for female germ-cell survival. Humans have OVOL1 (11q13) and OVOL2 (20p11). A third gene,
OVOL3, is annotated in some species but has no measured motif in these databases and is not represented
here. The proteins carry four C2H2 zinc fingers, of which only about three contribute to specificity,
and they bind DNA as monomers. OVOL1 and OVOL2 are epithelial: skin and hair follicle, kidney, mammary
and corneal epithelium, placenta, and germ cells. Both act predominantly as transcriptional repressors;
OVOL1 represses by competing with the activator MYB at overlapping sites and by recruiting histone
deacetylase activity, and OVOL2 exists in repressor and non-repressor isoforms whose balance sets its
output.

## The motif

The consensus is CCGTTA, usually written with AT-rich flanks, and it appears in these databases in both
orientations: ACCGTTAT (JASPAR OVOL1 and OVOL2) and TAACGGT (HOCOMOCO OVOL2, and the atlas
representative). These are the same element read on opposite strands, so the apparent disagreement
between AT-rich and CG-containing renderings is only a strand convention. The information sits almost
entirely on the six-base core; the flanking A/T positions add affinity but little specificity, which is
why the shortest matrices here carry only about 6 bits.

The site was first defined by random-oligomer selection with the Drosophila OVO zinc-finger array, which
gave a statistically significant 9-bp consensus and showed that the recognition does not follow the usual
zinc-finger contact rules, consistent with the conclusion that some fingers in the array have degenerated
and no longer read bases. Mouse Ovol1 binding sites in genomic DNA converge on the same CCGTTA core, and
cross-species ChIP work in the Drosophila germline finds OVO at genomic CCGTTA motifs, so the core is
conserved from fly to mouse. The permissive hexamer CC/TGTTA is also reported, with high-affinity sites
favouring AT-rich flanks.

OVOL1 and OVOL2 are not distinguishable from sequence. Their matrices in all four databases converge
(family cohesion about 0.89, and the best cross-member similarities exceed 0.98), so a hit identifies the
family, not the member. One Vierstra archetype in this family, ACAGTTACA, is a variant with a different
third position and does not match the others closely; treat it as a separate, weakly supported model.

## Where it acts

OVOL sites are found in promoters and enhancers of epithelial-identity and EMT genes. Documented direct
targets include ZEB1 and other EMT inducers, MYC (repressed by OVOL1 in embryonic epidermal
progenitors), the OVOL1 promoter itself, and in flies the ovarian tumor (otu) promoter, where OVO binds
unusually close to the transcription start site. That proximity to start sites is a recurring feature:
OVO/OVOL sites cluster near TSSs rather than in distal enhancer deserts. In epithelial cells the factors
sit inside a double-negative feedback loop with ZEB1/ZEB2, so OVOL peaks tend to co-occur with ZEB and
SNAI motifs in the same regulatory regions, and with GRHL and KLF4 motifs that mark epithelial promoters.
The core is only 6 bp, so genomic occurrences are numerous in any sequence composition.

## Biology and disease

Mouse Ovol1 (movo1) knockouts are small, make aberrant hairs, show hypogenitalism with reduced fertility
and develop kidney abnormalities; the epidermal phenotype traces to failure of embryonic epidermal
progenitors to arrest and to de-repression of MYC. Ovol2 deletion blocks mammary ductal morphogenesis,
depletes stem and progenitor pools, and lets epithelial cells undergo EMT in vivo; conversely, forced
expression of the repressor isoform of OVOL2 reverts metastatic breast cancer cells toward an epithelial
state. OVOL1 and OVOL2 can both induce mesenchymal-to-epithelial transition in human cancer cell lines.
In human disease, posterior polymorphous corneal dystrophy type 1 is caused by point mutations in the
OVOL2 promoter (c.-307T>C and related variants) that switch the gene on ectopically in corneal
endothelium, and OVOL2 maintains the corneal epithelial program by suppressing EMT. Reports in lung,
colorectal and breast cancer describe both tumour-suppressive and context-dependent pro-tumour effects,
and the literature here is not settled.

## Reading a hit

CCGTTA is six informative bases, so chance matches are frequent: expect many hits per megabase and treat
a single match as weak evidence. Sequence cannot distinguish OVOL1 from OVOL2, and in most epithelial
tissues both are expressed, so ChIP-seq in such a cell will not resolve them either. The evidence base
for this family is comparatively good: the HOCOMOCO OVOL1 and OVOL2 models carry in vitro support
(HT-SELEX and methyl-SELEX), so "this protein binds this sequence" is well established even though
"this sequence was bound by this protein here" is not. Be alert to the reverse-complement rendering
TAACGGT, which is the same site and is easy to mistake for an unrelated motif. A match in an
EMT-associated promoter alongside ZEB or SNAI sites is more interpretable than an isolated hit, but the
direction of effect still has to come from expression or perturbation data.
families.caveats: The informative core is only 6 bp (CCGTTA / TAACGG), so chance matches are abundant and one hit is weak evidence. OVOL1 and OVOL2 share a single motif - cohesion here is about 0.89 with cross-member similarities above 0.98 - so a match identifies the family, not the member, and ChIP in epithelium cannot separate them either because both are usually expressed. The two strand renderings (ACCGTTAT and TAACGGT) are the same element and are often mistaken for different motifs. Evidence quality is good: the OVOL1 and OVOL2 HOCOMOCO models include in vitro HT-SELEX and methyl-SELEX support. The Vierstra ACAGTTACA archetype is a poorly matching variant and should be treated separately.

families.name: USF
families.def: E-box with flanking preference GTCACGTGAC. USF1, USF2, USF3.
families.short: USF1 and USF2 are ubiquitously expressed bHLH-LZ proteins, first purified as the adenovirus major late transcription factor (MLTF), that bind DNA as homodimers and heterodimers. They read a canonical E-box core, but with a characteristic extended palindromic preference, GTCACGTGAC: the T and A flanks are what separate a USF site from a MYC-MAX site, which prefers C and G there. Because both proteins are constitutive, USF motifs turn up in a very large number of accessible promoters and CpG islands in every cell type, making USF one of the most frequently recovered motifs in promoter and footprint analyses. Human genetics links USF1 variants to familial combined hyperlipidemia.
families.long:
## The factors

USF1 and USF2 are ubiquitous basic helix-loop-helix leucine zipper (bHLH-LZ) proteins of about 43 and 44 kDa, originally purified as the factor that stimulates transcription from the adenovirus major late promoter and therefore also called MLTF. They bind DNA as homodimers and as USF1-USF2 heterodimers; besides the bHLH-LZ they carry a USF-specific region (USR) immediately N-terminal to the basic domain that is required for activation but not for binding. A third gene, USF3 (KIAA2018), encodes a much larger protein with a divergent bHLH and no leucine zipper, and is not a simple USF1/USF2 paralogue. Both USF1 and USF2 are expressed in essentially all tissues, which is one reason USF sites appear in so many promoters. In mice, loss of either gene alone is tolerated and the two cross-regulate asymmetrically, with Usf2 loss reducing total USF DNA-binding activity more than Usf1 loss; combined loss was reported to be embryonic lethal. The atlas assigns 8 motifs to this family (2 JASPAR, 3 HOCOMOCO, 2 CIS-BP, 1 Vierstra archetype) over the symbols USF1, USF2 and USF3, with high cohesion (0.94) and USF1.H14CORE.0.PSM.A as the representative.

## The motif

USF reads the canonical E-box CACGTG, but what defines the family in practice is the extended, strongly palindromic form GTCACGTGAC: a pyrimidine-purine flank on each side that USF prefers and that MYC-MAX does not. The bHLH-LZ fold places one basic helix in each half of the major groove, where a conserved histidine, glutamate and arginine read the CAC triplet; the crystallographic analysis of the USF b/HLH/Z domain showed the same recognition geometry as Max, with the leucine zipper fixing dimer choice. Because core contacts are shared across the bHLH-ZIP class, almost all of the discriminating information in a USF model sits in the two flanking positions, and in vitro base-preference measurements confirmed that USF and MYC family proteins differ mainly there rather than in the core. Flanking preference of this kind is largely mediated by local DNA shape rather than by new base contacts. Variants matter: the JASPAR USF1 model MA0093.4 is a CATGTG-type site (GTCATGTGAC), so USF tolerates the class-A-like half-site as well. The central CG of the core is a CpG, so occupancy can be modulated by DNA methylation; the HOCOMOCO USF1 and USF2 models carry both HT-SELEX and methyl-HT-SELEX support. The HOCOMOCO USF3 model is an outlier: its consensus GgCCACGTGGg has MYC-like C/G flanks and its nearest neighbours across the four databases sit outside this family.

## Where it acts

USF1 and USF2 are promoter factors. They occupy tens of thousands of accessible, mostly promoter-proximal and CpG-island regions in essentially every cell type examined, which makes USF one of the most commonly recovered motifs in promoter analyses and in DNase footprint atlases. Because both proteins are constitutive, USF occupancy is not a cell-type marker; the dependence is on accessibility and on methylation state rather than on a tissue-restricted partner. USF sites are frequently found close to TATA-less initiators, in housekeeping and metabolic gene promoters, and in composite arrangements with other promoter-proximal factors. The Vierstra footprint archetype covering these motifs is labelled AC0066:USF/BHLHE:bHLH - that is, USF motifs cluster with BHLHE40/41 motifs and were not separable in the footprint data.

## Biology and disease

USF1/USF2 targets are enriched for lipid and glucose metabolism, stress response and cell-cycle genes, and the pair have been characterized as stress-responsive general regulators rather than as a developmental switch. The clearest human genetic link is metabolic: variants in USF1 are associated with familial combined hyperlipidemia, one of the more common inherited dyslipidemias, in Finnish and subsequently other cohorts. USF3 is a separate story; a germline compound heterozygous poly-glutamine deletion in USF3 has been reported in predisposition to heritable and sporadic epithelial thyroid carcinoma. Because USF binding is methylation-sensitive, USF sites are also discussed in the context of promoter CpG island hypermethylation.

## Reading a hit

A GTCACGTGAC match is better evidence for USF than a bare CACGTG, but it is not proof. MITF, TFE3, TFEB and TFEC prefer exactly the same extended palindrome, and BHLHE41 and CLOCK-BMAL1 models look very similar; a strong T/A-flanked E-box narrows the candidate set to USF plus MITF/TFE plus BHLHE41 rather than to one factor. USF1 and USF2 are not distinguishable from each other by sequence at all, so a hit identifies USF, not a paralogue. Do not read the USF3 model as a USF site: it is MYC-flanked and clusters away from USF1/USF2. Given the number of genomic E-boxes, treat a single hit as a hypothesis.
families.caveats: The extended GTCACGTGAC form is shared with MITF, TFE3, TFEB, TFEC and BHLHE41, so it narrows a hit to a T/A-flanked E-box group, not to USF. USF1 and USF2 are indistinguishable by sequence. The Vierstra footprint archetype that carries these motifs is labelled USF/BHLHE, which is an explicit statement that USF and BHLHE40/41 motifs did not separate. The HOCOMOCO USF3 model has MYC-like CCACGTGG flanks and its nearest neighbours lie outside this family, so it should not be used as a USF site definition. USF occupancy is also methylation-sensitive because the core contains a CpG, so a sequence match says nothing about binding in a methylated promoter.

families.name: ARID / BRIGHT
families.def: AT-rich interaction domain; ARID3A/B, ARID5A/B.
families.short: ARID stands for AT-rich interaction domain, and this family is restricted to the four human ARID proteins that really do read AT-rich sequence: ARID3A (Bright), ARID3B, ARID5A and ARID5B. Eight motifs converge on a five to eight base-pair AT core - ATTAAT for ARID3B, ATTAAA for ARID3A, AATATT for ARID5A - so the whole family occupies one narrow, information-poor patch of sequence space and is very hard to separate from homeodomain TAAT sites or from AT-rich DNA generally. The many other ARID-domain proteins, including ARID1A and ARID1B in BAF and ARID2 in PBAF, bind DNA without sequence preference and are deliberately excluded from this family.
families.long:
## The factors

The domain was discovered twice in the same year. Bright, a B cell-specific trans-activator, was purified as the protein binding the matrix-associating regions flanking the immunoglobulin heavy-chain enhancer and was recognized as defining a new DNA-binding protein family; the Drosophila protein Dead ringer provided the first structure, and its DNA-binding module was named the AT-rich interaction domain. Bright is now called ARID3A. The human genome encodes fifteen ARID-domain proteins in seven subfamilies, but only four are filed here: ARID3A and ARID3B, which together with ARID3C form a subfamily carrying an extended ARID plus a REKLES self-association domain, and ARID5A and ARID5B, the shortest members, which consist of little more than the domain itself.

The exclusion of the rest is deliberate and well founded. Systematic comparison of ARID-family proteins showed that sequence-specific AT-rich binding is a property of the ARID3 and ARID5 subfamilies, while the large ARID-containing subunits of chromatin remodellers - ARID1A and ARID1B in BAF, ARID2 in PBAF, and the yeast Swi1 equivalent - bind DNA with no detectable sequence specificity. Those proteins are chromatin regulators that happen to contain a structurally similar domain; scanning a genome for a motif attributed to them is not meaningful, and where such a model exists in the atlas, as for ARID1A, it is filed in the CHROMATIN bucket instead. ARID4A/4B and the JARID/KDM5 demethylases are likewise absent.

## The motif

All eight models agree on the same thing and none of them says very much. ARID3B reads ATTAAT in CIS-BP and tATTAAT in JASPAR; ARID3A reads ATTAAA in JASPAR and the five-base AThAA in CIS-BP; ARID5A reads AATATTa and tAATATTg. Information content runs from 9.6 to 11.8 bits for the useful models, and the trimmed consensus is a five- to seven-base AT-only core. Structurally this is expected: the ARID fold contacts the major groove of AT-rich DNA through a helix-turn-helix-like core, with flanking regions contributing affinity, and recent work shows that ARID5A uses intrinsically disordered extensions on either side of the core domain for its DNA and RNA recognition rather than achieving specificity within the domain alone.

Two entries should be set aside. The Vierstra archetype AC0374 for ARID5B reads ttdGTATTGT, which is only 0.59 similar to anything else in the family. The CIS-BP model M01661 for ARID5B is the three-base ATa at 3.3 bits and carries no information at all. Four of the five CIS-BP models are transferred from other species - three from Mus musculus, one from Microcebus murinus - but all at 100 percent DNA-binding-domain identity, so the transfers are sound even if the models are short.

Family cohesion is 0.69, which looks respectable, but the discriminating number is the comparison between within-family and out-of-family nearest neighbours: bestOther values run from 0.74 to 0.84, meaning the closest matching model in some other family is nearly as similar as the closest match inside this one. The competitors are obvious - homeodomain families reading TAAT, the HMGA AT-hook models, and any AT-rich model at all.

## Where it acts

Bright/ARID3A was found at nuclear-matrix-attachment regions flanking the immunoglobulin heavy-chain intronic enhancer, and it acts there in a strongly context-dependent way, requiring the right surrounding sequence and partner proteins to activate. ARID5B works at Sox9-regulated genes in chondrocytes, where it recruits the histone demethylase PHF2, and more recently has been shown to coordinate HDAC-mediated repression, so both ARID5 proteins are best thought of as sequence-biased recruiters of chromatin enzymes rather than as classical activators. AT-rich cores of this length are extremely abundant, so in practice the location of a real ARID site is set by chromatin context and partner occupancy, not by the motif.

## Biology and disease

ARID5B is the medically prominent member: common germline variants at the ARID5B locus are among the strongest known inherited risk factors for childhood acute lymphoblastic leukaemia, identified by genome-wide association and repeatedly replicated. Targeted deletion of the mouse orthologue, originally named Desrt, causes growth retardation and abnormal development of the reproductive organs, and Arid5b is required for normal chondrogenesis. ARID5A is an immune regulator that stabilises IL-6 messenger RNA - a reminder that ARID-domain proteins can be RNA-binding as well as DNA-binding. ARID3A/Bright has regulatory roles across human and mouse haematopoiesis, including B cell development and stem cell function.

## Reading a hit

Treat a hit in this family as evidence of AT-rich sequence and little more. A five- to seven-base AT core will occur on the order of a million times in the human genome, and it cannot be distinguished from a homeodomain TAAT site, an AT-hook target, or an AT-rich stretch of no consequence. Do not attempt to assign a hit to a particular paralogue: ARID3A, ARID3B and ARID5A models are mutually similar at 0.89 to 0.98. Require expression and, ideally, occupancy data before calling any ARID site, and be aware that an ARID motif call has no bearing on ARID1A, ARID1B, ARID2 or the KDM5 proteins, whose ARID domains are not sequence-specific.
families.caveats: Every model in this family is a short AT-only core, so a match carries almost no information: expect on the order of a million genome-wide hits and no way to distinguish an ARID site from a homeodomain TAAT site, an AT-hook target or plain AT-rich DNA. Out-of-family nearest neighbours score 0.74 to 0.84, nearly as high as within-family ones. Individual paralogues cannot be separated. Two ARID5B entries are unusable: the CIS-BP model is three bases at 3.3 bits, and the Vierstra archetype disagrees with everything else. Four CIS-BP models are cross-species transfers, though all at 100 percent domain identity. Only ARID3 and ARID5 proteins belong here; other ARID-domain proteins bind DNA non-specifically.
