families.name: TAL1 / LYL1 (hematopoietic)
families.def: E-box CAGCTG/CAGGTG within composite GATA-E-box elements. TAL1, TAL2, LYL1.
families.short: TAL1 (SCL), LYL1 and TAL2 are haematopoietic and endothelial class II basic helix-loop-helix proteins with no intrinsic DNA-binding activity: they bind only as heterodimers with the class I E-proteins E12/E47, TCF4 or TCF12. In blood cells the functional unit is larger still — a pentameric complex in which LMO2 bridges the TAL1-E47 dimer to GATA1 or GATA2 with LDB1 — and it reads a composite element made of an E-box followed about nine base pairs later by a GATA site. TAL1 is required for all primitive haematopoiesis and is the most frequently activated oncogene in T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukaemia. The family is the atlas's clearest example of a motif that is really a composite, and partly a partner's.
families.long:
## The factors

TAL1 (also called SCL), LYL1 and TAL2 are class II bHLH proteins of the blood and endothelial lineages. TAL1 is the founding member, identified through the chromosomal rearrangements that activate it in T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukaemia. None of them binds DNA on its own: binding-site selection showed that TAL1 polypeptides have no intrinsic DNA-binding activity, presumably because they cannot homodimerise, and acquire it only on heterodimerising with a class A (class I) partner — E12, E47, TCF4/E2-2 or TCF12/HEB. In blood cells TAL1 rarely acts as a bare heterodimer either. It sits in a pentameric complex in which the LIM-only protein LMO2 bridges the TAL1-E47 dimer to GATA1 (or GATA2), with LDB1/NLI completing the assembly; a crystal structure of LMO2 bound to the SCL:E47 bHLH heterodimer shows how the bridge is made. Expression: TAL1 in haematopoietic stem cells, erythroid, megakaryocytic and mast lineages and in endothelium; LYL1 in stem, endothelial and myeloid cells; TAL2 is narrowly expressed and poorly characterised. Because all three depend on the same E-proteins and the same partners, there is no expectation that they differ in sequence preference.

## The motif

The TAL1 heterodimer's selected consensus is AACAGATGGT, which decomposes into a half-site read by the class A partner (AACAG) and one read by TAL1 (ATGGT). In erythroid cells, an unbiased search of TAL1 ChIP-seq peaks gave CAGNTG as the preferred E-box, which is why the atlas consensus is written that way; the representative model here is the Vierstra archetype `AC0077:LYL/OLIG:bHLH` with consensus AACAGCTG.

The functional site in blood is not the E-box alone. The LMO2/LDB1 complex binds a bipartite element: an E-box, canonically CAGGTG, followed roughly nine base pairs downstream by a GATA site (WGATAA). This composite E-box-GATA element is the signature of TAL1 activity at erythroid and megakaryocytic enhancers, and it is the reason this family is a textbook case of an indirect or composite motif. The highest-information TAL1 model in HOCOMOCO, `TAL1.H14CORE.0.P.B`, reads TGGNNNNNVCAGATAAG — the 3' end of an E-box, a short spacer, and then AGATAAG, which is the GATA motif. The atlas flags this model as matching the GATA family, and it is right to: viewed as a position weight matrix, most of the information in that "TAL1 motif" is GATA information. A second flagged model, JASPAR TAL1::TCF3 MA0091.2 (ACCATCTGTT), matches the MYOD family instead. So of seven motifs assigned here, the two best known are each closer to another family than to their own label.

There is a further structural limitation: every HOCOMOCO model in this family carries the evidence letter `P` (ChIP-seq) with grade B or C. There is no HT-SELEX or methyl-SELEX model for TAL1 or LYL1 in the collection at all. Cohesion is 0.75 over just seven motifs, the smallest and weakest of the tissue-specific bHLH families here.

## Where it acts

TAL1 occupies thousands of sites in erythroid and megakaryocytic cells, concentrated at lineage-specific enhancers of red-cell and platelet genes rather than at CpG-island promoters. About four fifths of erythroid targets require TAL1's own DNA-binding activity; the remaining fifth, enriched among the highest-affinity peaks, are occupied by a DNA-binding-deficient TAL1, which is direct evidence that some "TAL1 sites" are recruitment sites, not recognition sites. Target sets are lineage-specific: TAL1 occupies largely different regions in erythroid and megakaryocytic cells. Co-occurring motifs are GATA (GATA1 in erythroid cells, GATA2 in progenitors), KLF1, NFE2, RUNX1 and FLI1; simultaneous mapping of GATA1/GATA2, RUNX1, FLI1 and SCL in megakaryocytes showed heavy combinatorial overlap. In T-ALL, TAL1 forms a core regulatory circuit with GATA3, RUNX1 and MYB at large enhancer clusters.

## Biology and disease

*Tal1*/*Scl*-null mouse embryos make no blood: yolk-sac haematopoiesis is absent and the embryos die at mid-gestation, the cleanest demonstration that this factor sits at the top of the haematopoietic hierarchy. In humans, TAL1 is the most commonly activated oncogene in T-ALL, through t(1;14)(p32;q11), through the *SIL-TAL1* interstitial deletion, and through small somatic insertions in a non-coding region upstream of *TAL1* that create a MYB binding site and nucleate a new super-enhancer. LYL1 is activated by t(7;19) in T-ALL. The TAL1-driven circuit in T-ALL is a candidate therapeutic target because it depends on the large enhancer clusters it creates.

## Reading a hit

Little in this family licenses a factor-level conclusion. CAGNTG or AACAGATGGT is an ordinary E-box and matches E-proteins, MYOD-family and NEUROD-family models; the archetype covering LYL1 is named LYL/OLIG because the two could not be separated. If you want evidence of TAL1 complex activity, look for the composite architecture — an E-box and a WGATAA about nine bases apart — and not for the E-box alone. Conversely, if a GATA-like motif is the top hit in a TAL1 ChIP experiment, that is the expected result for the composite element and is not evidence that TAL1 binds GATA sites directly; the same logic applies in reverse to GATA1 experiments recovering E-boxes. Because this family has no in vitro model, "TAL1 binds this sequence" rests on the older biochemistry rather than on the database entries, and the database entries should be read as occupancy models for a multiprotein complex.
families.caveats: Read this family's database entries as occupancy models for a complex, not as recognition sequences. Every HOCOMOCO model here is ChIP-only (evidence letter P, grade B or C); there is no HT-SELEX or methyl-SELEX model for TAL1 or LYL1. The highest-information TAL1 model is essentially the GATA motif with an E-box fragment upstream, which is the composite E-box-GATA element rather than a TAL1 recognition site, and a second widely used model (JASPAR TAL1::TCF3) matches the MYOD family. The bare E-box CAGNTG carries almost no discriminating information. TAL1, TAL2 and LYL1 are not separable from sequence; the archetype covering LYL1 also covers OLIG.

families.name: BHLHE40 / BHLHE41 (DEC1/2)
families.def: Class B E-box CACGTG repressors of the circadian and hypoxia programs.
families.short: BHLHE40 and BHLHE41 - also known as DEC1/STRA13/SHARP-2 and DEC2/SHARP-1 - are bHLH repressors without a leucine zipper that bind the class-B E-box CACGTG and shut down transcription, both by competing for E-boxes with activating dimers such as CLOCK-BMAL1 and by recruiting histone deacetylases without contacting DNA. Their own promoters carry hypoxia response elements, so they couple HIF signalling to the E-box landscape. A BHLHE41 missense change causes familial natural short sleep in humans and mice, BHLHE40 is required for pathogenic T cell cytokine output, and the two together control alveolar macrophage identity. Because they read the same site as circadian activators, the sequence alone cannot tell you whether an E-box is being activated or repressed.
families.long:
## The factors

BHLHE40 and BHLHE41 are two closely related basic helix-loop-helix repressors that have accumulated an unusual number of names: BHLHE40 is also DEC1, STRA13, SHARP-2 and BHLHB2; BHLHE41 is also DEC2, SHARP-1 and BHLHB3. Unlike MYC, MAX, USF and the MiT/TFE proteins, they are plain bHLH proteins with no leucine zipper; they homodimerize, heterodimerize with each other, and contain a C-terminal repression region rather than an activation domain. They were found independently several times - as a retinoic-acid-inducible gene that blocked mesodermal and promoted neuronal differentiation of P19 cells, as neuronal-activity-coupled enhancer-of-split- and hairy-related proteins, and as clock components - which is why the nomenclature is so tangled. Both are broadly expressed and strongly inducible: their promoters contain functional hypoxia response elements and are direct HIF targets, and they also respond to serum, TGF-beta and retinoic acid. That makes them stimulus-driven repressors superimposed on a constitutive E-box landscape. They repress by two mechanisms: competing for E-boxes with activating bHLH dimers, and binding proteins - notably BMAL1 and histone deacetylases - without necessarily contacting DNA. The atlas assigns 7 motifs here (2 JASPAR, 3 HOCOMOCO, 2 CIS-BP) over both symbols, cohesion 0.93, with BHLHE40 (MA0464.3) as the representative.

## The motif

The site is the class-B E-box CACGTG, the same 6-bp palindrome read by MYC-MAX, USF and MiT/TFE, with each CAC half-site contacted by the conserved histidine, glutamate and arginine of one basic region. What is worth noticing in the data is that the two paralogues are described differently by the databases. The BHLHE41 models carry the T/A-flanked extended palindrome GTCACGTGAC or GTCACGTGC - that is, the USF and CLEAR-box form - while the BHLHE40 models are shorter and prefer G/C flanks (GCACGTG, tCACGTGa), closer to the MYC-MAX form. Whether that reflects a real difference in flanking preference between the two proteins or differences in the underlying experiments is not settled by these models alone, and the similarity scores show BHLHE41 models matching other families' motifs about as well as they match BHLHE40's. One HOCOMOCO BHLHE40 model is not a single site at all but a tandem pair, CACGTGnnnvgCACGTGa: two E-boxes separated by three base pairs, which matches the clustered E-boxes typical of circadian target promoters. The Vierstra footprint archetype covering these motifs is labelled AC0066:USF/BHLHE:bHLH, an explicit statement that USF and BHLHE40/41 motifs did not separate in footprint data.

## Where it acts

These factors act at promoter-proximal E-boxes in accessible chromatin, in three recurring contexts: circadian genes, where they sit on the same E-boxes used by CLOCK-BMAL1 in PER and DBP promoters; hypoxia-responsive genes, where they are both HIF targets and themselves repressors, giving a feed-forward loop; and immune and metabolic loci, where BHLHE40 in particular is induced by activation signals. Because a substantial part of their repression is protein-mediated, a fraction of their ChIP signal can be expected at sites they do not contact directly. Their binding does not mark a cell type: both are widely expressed, and what changes is induction level and the time of day.

## Biology and disease

DEC1 and DEC2 were shown to repress CLOCK-BMAL1-driven transactivation of the mPer1 promoter and to shift the behavioural clock, placing them in the negative limb of the mammalian oscillator alongside the cryptochromes. The clearest human genetic result is a BHLHE41 missense change (P384R) segregating with the familial natural short sleep trait; the same substitution shortens sleep in transgenic mice. Immunologically, Bhlhe40-deficient mice show defective T cell activation and develop autoimmune disease, and Bhlhe40 is required for the cytokine output that makes T cells pathogenic in autoimmune neuroinflammation. Both paralogues together control alveolar macrophage self-renewal and identity. They have also been linked to hypoxic repression of specific targets, including the mismatch-repair gene MLH1 and SREBP-1c, and to tumour behaviour, though the direction varies by tissue.

## Reading a hit

A CACGTG hit does not distinguish BHLHE40 or BHLHE41 from MYC-MAX, USF, MITF/TFE3/TFEB, SREBP, HIF-ARNT or CLOCK-BMAL1. In the circadian case this ambiguity is biologically real rather than a technical limitation: the same E-box is an activating element when CLOCK-BMAL1 occupies it and a repressing one when DEC1/DEC2 do, so the sequence alone cannot even tell you the sign of the effect. BHLHE40 and BHLHE41 are not distinguishable from one another by sequence; the apparent flanking difference between their models is not a reliable discriminator. Because both repress partly through protein interaction, a ChIP peak without a motif is an expected outcome here, not necessarily an artifact - and conversely, a motif match is not evidence that repression at that site is DNA-binding-dependent.
families.caveats: A CACGTG match cannot separate BHLHE40/41 from MYC-MAX, USF, MITF/TFE, SREBP, HIF-ARNT or CLOCK-BMAL1, and the Vierstra archetype carrying these motifs is explicitly labelled USF/BHLHE because the two did not separate in footprint data. The two paralogues are not distinguishable from each other; their models differ in apparent flanking preference (T/A for BHLHE41, G/C for BHLHE40) but that difference may reflect the experiments rather than the proteins. Since both repress partly by protein-protein interaction with BMAL1 and HDACs, motif-free ChIP peaks are expected, and a motif match does not establish that repression at that site requires DNA binding.

families.name: BCL6 / BCL6B
families.def: STAT-like TTCCTAGAA bound by the BTB-ZF repressors BCL6, BCL6B.
families.short: BCL6 and its paralogue BCL6B (BAZF) are BTB/POZ zinc-finger repressors that bind a nine-base site, TTCCTAGAA, which is a TTCNNNGAA element of the same class that STAT dimers use. That overlap is not incidental: BCL6 represses interleukin-4-induced, STAT6-dependent genes by occupying sites that STAT6 would otherwise use, so the same sequence can be an activating STAT element or a repressed BCL6 element depending on which protein is present. BCL6 is required for germinal center formation and for follicular helper T cells, and its deregulation by chromosomal translocation or promoter mutation occurs in a large fraction of diffuse large B-cell lymphomas. A hit to this motif is ambiguous between BCL6, BCL6B and the STAT family.
families.long:
## The factors

Two paralogues: BCL6 (also LAZ3, ZBTB27) and BCL6B (BAZF, ZBTB28). Both have the standard BTB-ZF architecture - an N-terminal BTB/POZ domain, a central region with PEST and RD2 repression motifs, and six C-terminal C2H2 zinc fingers. The BTB domain obligately homodimerizes, and the dimer creates a lateral groove at the interface into which the SMRT and NCOR corepressors dock through a short peptide; the crystal structure of that complex explained how one BTB dimer recruits corepressor and provided the target site for the small-molecule BCL6 inhibitors and degraders developed since. Repression is therefore corepressor-dependent and also involves BCOR and HDAC recruitment. BCL6 is expressed at high levels in germinal center B cells and in follicular helper T cells, at lower levels in macrophages and other tissues; BCL6B is expressed in endothelium, some T-cell subsets and neural tissue and is much less studied. The two proteins bind DNA as dimers, and the six fingers give a footprint consistent with a nine- to twelve-base site.

## The motif

The site is written in the literature as TTCCTAGAA, sometimes generalized to TTCCT(A/C)GAA. Parsed as TTC-CTA-GAA it is a TTCNNNGAA element - structurally the same family of sites that STAT dimers occupy as gamma-interferon activated sequences (GAS elements). All the matrices here are consistent with that once strand is taken into account: the HOCOMOCO grade-A BCL6 model reads GCTTTCGAGGAAT and JASPAR MA0463.3 reads GCTTTCGAGGAA, whose reverse complements are TTCCTCGAAAGC, while the BCL6B HT-SELEX models read TGCTTTCTAGGAATTCA, reverse-complementing to TTCCTAGAAAGCA. So BCL6 models favor TTCCTCGAA and BCL6B models TTCCTAGAA; both fit TTCCTNGAA, and the difference at that one central position is the only sequence feature that even hints at a paralogue distinction. It is not enough to act on: the BCL6 and BCL6B models are 0.91-0.97 similar, and the Vierstra archetype for the family is named AC0665:BCL/BCL6B, an explicit statement that the two were not separable. Information content is high for a C2H2 family - the BCL6B matrices reach nearly 30 bits because they include long flanks - but much of that comes from the flanking bases selected in vitro rather than from the core, and long high-information matrices of this kind tend to overfit. One entry in the family contradicts the rest outright: CIS-BP M00227, labelled BCL6, reads TAATTAA and its nearest cross-database neighbors are PRD-like homeodomain motifs. It does not belong with the other BCL6 models.

## Where it acts

BCL6 binds promoters and enhancers of genes that must be held off during the germinal center reaction: DNA damage response and checkpoint genes (TP53, CDKN1A, ATR), differentiation genes (PRDM1), and cytokine and chemokine genes. In T cells it represses the Th1, Th2 and Th17 programs while promoting the follicular helper program. Because the site is a GAS-type element, BCL6 sites overlap physically with STAT sites at shared loci - the germline immunoglobulin epsilon (Iepsilon) promoter is the worked example, where BCL6 occupancy blocks STAT6-driven transcription and IgE class switching. TTCCTNGAA is AT-rich, CpG-free and about nine informative bases, so chance occurrences are frequent; occupancy is set by BCL6 abundance, which is itself tightly controlled by phosphorylation-triggered degradation and by MYC-driven transcription in the germinal center.

## Biology and disease

Bcl6-null mice form no germinal centers, cannot mount high-affinity antibody responses, and develop a lethal inflammatory syndrome with eosinophilia and Th2-skewed cytokine production - a phenotype that connects directly to the STAT6 antagonism. Bcl6 is also required for follicular helper T cell development, and enforced Bcl6 expression drives T cells into that program. In human disease, BCL6 is the most frequently translocated locus in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma: chromosomal rearrangements juxtapose heterologous promoters to the BCL6 coding sequence and prevent its normal downregulation, and point mutations in the BCL6 promoter region have the same effect. BCL6 is also deregulated in follicular lymphoma and in some T-cell lymphomas. The BTB lateral groove has been exploited pharmacologically, with peptide and small-molecule inhibitors and BTB-directed degraders in development. BCL6B has no comparable disease association and is best described as an understudied paralogue.

## Reading a hit

The central caution is the STAT overlap. A TTCNNNGAA match is compatible with BCL6, with BCL6B, and with STAT1, STAT3, STAT4, STAT5A/B and (with the N4 spacing) STAT6; the sequence does not distinguish a repressed BCL6 site from an activated STAT site, and at some loci the same element is both at different times. If your interest is signaling, do not read a BCL6 motif hit as evidence against STAT involvement, or vice versa - the correct inference is that the locus is contested. Within the family, BCL6 and BCL6B are not separable; the slight preference of BCL6 models for a central C and BCL6B models for a central A is within the noise of a single position. Evidence quality is otherwise good: HOCOMOCO BCL6 and BCL6B core models are grade A with PSM evidence, and JASPAR MA0463.3 and MA0731.1 are HT-SELEX, so direct binding is well supported. Two practical exclusions: discard CIS-BP M00227 (TAATTAA), which is a homeodomain-like site mislabelled as BCL6, and be wary of scoring with the full 17-position BCL6B matrix, whose extreme information content comes largely from in vitro-selected flanks that are unlikely to be conserved in real promoters. Cell context is the strongest supporting evidence: a germinal center B cell or follicular helper T cell makes a BCL6 call reasonable.
families.caveats: The site is a TTCNNNGAA GAS element, so a match is ambiguous between BCL6, BCL6B and the STAT family; BCL6 is documented to repress STAT6-dependent genes by competing for overlapping sites, so a hit indicates a contested element rather than a settled assignment. BCL6 and BCL6B motifs are 0.91-0.97 similar and the Vierstra archetype merges them by name. The nine-base core is AT-rich and CpG-free and occurs often by chance. Two specific data problems: CIS-BP M00227 labelled BCL6 is a homeodomain-like TAATTAA site that does not belong in this family, and the 17-position BCL6B HT-SELEX matrix draws much of its information from selected flanks.

families.name: DACH / SKI-family corepressors
families.def: DACH1/DACH2 (DD1 winged-helix, binds forkhead-like sites and competes with FOXM1) and the SKI/SnoN/SKOR corepressors (SKI, SKIL, SKOR1, SKOR2), whose DNA contact comes from a SAND-like motif in the Ski homology domain. Their ChIP motifs often resemble those of the homeodomain partners they are recruited by.
families.short: These are transcriptional corepressors, not classical sequence-specific activators. DACH1 and DACH2 are the vertebrate Dachshund proteins, and SKI, SKIL/SnoN, SKOR1 and SKOR2 are the Ski family; all share a Dachshund homology domain with a winged-helix fold related to forkhead. They work mostly by being recruited: DACH proteins into SIX/EYA complexes and onto forkhead sites where they compete with FOXM1, the Ski proteins onto SMAD complexes to shut down TGF-beta signalling, and SKOR1/SKOR2 onto homeodomain factors such as LBX1. The motifs in this family therefore look borrowed. The best-supported models, TTAATTAC for SKOR1 and SKOR2, are indistinguishable from homeodomain dimer sites, which is what you would expect from proteins that arrive at DNA on someone else's back.
families.long:
## The factors

Two lineages sit in this family because they share one domain. DACH1 and DACH2 are the vertebrate
homologues of *Drosophila* dachshund, a retinal determination gene. Their conserved N-terminal region, the
Dachshund homology domain or DD1, was solved crystallographically and turned out to adopt a winged-helix
fold of the kind used by forkhead proteins, with a surface consistent with DNA binding; a second conserved
region, DD2, mediates protein-protein interaction. The Ski family, SKI, SKIL (SnoN), SKOR1 and SKOR2,
carries a homologous Dachshund homology domain; the crystal structure of the human SKI domain confirmed the
same fold and identified a SAND-like element within it as the likely DNA-contacting surface. None of these
proteins has a homeodomain, a zinc finger or a leucine zipper. All of them function primarily as
corepressors that recruit histone deacetylase and N-CoR complexes to sites chosen by a partner: DACH
proteins into SIX-EYA complexes on SIX target promoters, SKI and SnoN onto SMAD2/3 and SMAD4 complexes at
TGF-beta response elements, and SKOR1 and SKOR2, originally named Corl1 and Corl2, onto the homeodomain
protein LBX1 and related factors in developing neurons.

## The motif

There is no single well-founded consensus, and the two lineages point in different directions. For the DACH
proteins, the functional claim from cell biology is that DACH1 binds forkhead-type sequences and thereby
competes with FOXM1 for its targets; the winged-helix fold of DD1 makes that structurally plausible. The
database models for DACH1 and DACH2, however, are HT-SELEX motifs reading CAATCGTCATAATT and TGACGATTG,
which are not forkhead sites, are the weakest-matching members of this family internally, and should be
treated as provisional. For SKOR1 and SKOR2 the models are much stronger and mutually consistent: in vitro
selection and methyl-selection give TTAATTAC and CTTTAATTAA, around 15 to 16 bits, reproduced in CIS-BP as
TTAATTACAGNT. Read as a homeodomain site, TTAATTAC is a TAAT/ATTA arrangement of exactly the type that
LHX, ALX and ARX homeodomains bind as cooperative dimers, and that is what the data show: the
nearest neighbours of these models outside the family are LHX, ALX and ARX homeodomain motifs, at
similarities of 0.88 to 0.93. Whether the Ski/Dachshund winged helix genuinely prefers this sequence, or
whether the selection experiments captured the preference of an associated homeodomain partner, is not
settled. The family consensus offered here, TTAATTAC, is therefore the observed motif, not a validated
statement about which protein reads it.

## Where it acts

DACH1 occupies promoters and enhancers in complexes with SIX1 and EYA proteins, where the three together
convert a SIX-bound site from repressed to activated via CREB-binding protein, and at forkhead sites where
DACH1 opposes FOXM1-driven proliferative programs. SKI and SnoN are found wherever SMAD complexes are, so
their apparent binding footprint is the SMAD-binding element landscape of TGF-beta and BMP signalling.
SKOR1 and SKOR2 are restricted to specific neuronal lineages: SKOR1 in dorsal horn interneurons with LBX1,
SKOR2 in cerebellar Purkinje cell precursors, where it is a selective marker and drives early
differentiation. The practical consequence is that these factors' genome-wide occupancy tracks the
expression and occupancy of their partners, so composite elements in the useful sense are the partner's
elements: a SIX site, a SMAD-binding element, or an LBX1-type homeodomain site.

## Biology and disease

DACH1 restrains proliferation: it inhibits cyclin D1 and breast tumour growth, binds SMAD4 to attenuate
TGF-beta signalling, and attenuates forkhead signalling. It is downregulated in several carcinomas, and
transcriptome-wide association work identified DACH1 as a kidney disease risk gene contributing to fibrosis,
making it a candidate target in chronic kidney disease. DACH1 and DACH2 act redundantly in Mullerian duct
development. SKI and SnoN are proto-oncoproteins by virtue of repressing TGF-beta growth inhibition, and
SKI mutations cause Shprintzen-Goldberg syndrome. SKOR2/Corl2 is required for early Purkinje cell
differentiation. The SKOR1 locus, formerly LBXCOR1, was one of the three regions identified in the first
genome-wide association study of restless legs syndrome, alongside MEIS1 and BTBD9.

## Reading a hit

Be sceptical in a specific way. A TTAATTAC hit is a good homeodomain dimer site and a poor SKOR
identification: if you scan with the SKOR1 or SKOR2 model you will recover LHX, ALX and ARX sites, and in
this family's own data those motifs are the nearest neighbours. Conversely, if a ChIP experiment on any of
these proteins yields a homeodomain or SMAD or forkhead motif, the most likely explanation is indirect
binding through the partner that recruited them, which is the mechanism these proteins are known for. The
DACH1 and DACH2 models are the weakest members of the family internally and do not match the forkhead-like
specificity that the functional literature describes, so a DACH1 motif hit should not be used as evidence
of DACH1 occupancy. In practice, use expression of the partner, not the motif, to decide whether a DACH or
Ski family protein is plausibly at a locus.
families.caveats: This family's motifs probably belong to other proteins. DACH and Ski family members have no homeodomain, no zinc finger and no leucine zipper; they are corepressors recruited by SIX/EYA, SMAD or homeodomain partners, and their conserved Dachshund homology domain has only a plausible, not a demonstrated, sequence preference. The strongest models here, SKOR1 and SKOR2 reading TTAATTAC, sit among LHX, ALX and ARX homeodomain motifs at 0.88 to 0.93 similarity, which is the expected signature of partner carry-over. The DACH1 and DACH2 models do not match the forkhead-like specificity the functional literature reports and are the weakest members internally. Do not call occupancy for these factors from a motif hit alone.

families.name: TFAP4 (AP-4)
families.def: Palindromic E-box CAGCTG. TFAP4.
families.short: TFAP4 (AP-4) is a single-gene bHLH-LZ family with no close paralogue. Unusually for the class, a second zipper-like dimerization motif restricts it to homodimers, so it does not form the combinatorial heterodimers that dominate the rest of the bHLH class. It binds the palindromic class-A E-box CAGCTG, usually written extended as AACAGCTGAT. TFAP4 is a direct MYC target and represses the CDK inhibitor CDKN1A (p21), placing it in a MYC-driven cell-cycle circuit whose direction is context-dependent - growth-promoting in several carcinomas, tumour-suppressive in B lymphocytes. Because CAGCTG is shared with the E-proteins and with most tissue-restricted bHLH factors, a match is weak evidence for AP-4 specifically.
families.long:
## The factors

TFAP4 (AP-4) is a single-gene family: there is one human TFAP4 protein and no close paralogue, which makes it one of the few bHLH families where the usual paralogue problem does not apply. It is a basic helix-loop-helix leucine zipper protein, but with an unusual architecture. Beyond the bHLH and the adjacent leucine zipper, AP-4 carries a second, more distal zipper-like dimerization motif; biochemical dissection showed that these multiple dimerization surfaces restrict it to homodimers and prevent it from partnering the other bHLH-ZIP proteins. Functionally that puts AP-4 in the opposite position from the E-proteins: it does not form the combinatorial heterodimers that dominate the rest of the bHLH class, so its DNA-binding activity depends on its own expression level rather than on the availability of a partner. AP-4 was discovered as an enhancer-binding factor that cooperates with AP-1 to activate SV40 late transcription in vitro, and it is expressed broadly but at levels that follow proliferative signals, because TFAP4 is a direct MYC target gene. The atlas assigns 6 motifs here (4 JASPAR, 1 HOCOMOCO, 1 CIS-BP), all labelled TFAP4, with cohesion of only 0.77 - the lowest in this batch - for reasons explained below.

## The motif

The AP-4 site is the palindromic class-A E-box CAGCTG, six base pairs, read as two CAG half-sites by the basic region of each monomer in the homodimer. In the general bHLH scheme, CACGTG is the class-B E-box read by the MYC/MAX/USF/MITF group and CAGCTG (and CACCTG) is the class-A E-box read by the E-proteins and by tissue-restricted bHLH factors; AP-4 is a class-A binder that happens to be a bHLH-ZIP. In the databases the motif is usually written extended, AaCAGCTGaT or CAGCTGtT, adding a weak preference for A/T immediately outside the core; that extra information is small and comes mainly from local DNA shape rather than from direct base contacts. The low cohesion score has two concrete causes. First, two of the six models are not CAGCTG at all but CATATG-type CANNTG variants (aaCAtaTGtt in JASPAR MA1570.1, AhCATATG in CIS-BP), so the family contains two different E-box classes. Second, two of the models are JASPAR heterodimer profiles in which the TFAP4 half-site is fused to an ETS half-site - ACCGGAAACAGCTG with FLI1, cCGGAAGCAGsTG with ETV1 - which are composite models of a TFAP4-ETS pair rather than definitions of the AP-4 site itself. Across all four databases, the nearest neighbours of the TFAP4 models are usually motifs labelled with some other factor: label agreement is only 0.1-0.2. That is not an error in the databases; it is a statement that CAGCTG is not an AP-4-specific sequence.

## Where it acts

CAGCTG is a 6-bp palindrome and therefore expected several hundred thousand times in the human genome, and unlike CACGTG it contains no CpG and so is not depleted. AP-4 occupancy is concentrated at promoters of cell-cycle and proliferation genes, overlapping heavily with MYC-responsive promoters, which is unsurprising given that TFAP4 is MYC-induced. It can act as an activator or a repressor at the same class of site; at CDKN1A it is a repressor. The JASPAR composite models suggest AP-4 half-sites adjacent to ETS half-sites as one recurring arrangement, and the founding observation was cooperation with AP-1 at the SV40 late enhancer, so AP-4 sites are best interpreted as part of composite promoter modules rather than as stand-alone elements.

## Biology and disease

AP-4 sits in a MYC-driven cell-cycle circuit. TFAP4 is induced directly by MYC and represses the CDK inhibitor CDKN1A (p21), so MYC can suppress p21 indirectly through AP-4; AP-4 is required for mitogen- and MYC-induced cell-cycle progression, and it attenuates DREAM-complex-mediated repression downstream of p53. The relationship is not uniformly oncogenic: in B lymphocytes, MYC was found to suppress tumorigenesis through TFAP4-dependent restriction of stemness, so the direction of the effect is context-dependent. In solid tumours, elevated TFAP4 has been associated with growth-promoting programs, for example upregulation of FOXK1 in prostate cancer cells. There is no well-established Mendelian disease attributed to TFAP4 in the sources reviewed here.

## Reading a hit

A CAGCTG match is close to uninformative about AP-4 on its own. The same core is the preferred site of TCF3, TCF4 and TCF12, of MYOD and the myogenic bHLHs, of ASCL and NEUROD proteins, of TWIST/HAND, and of many other class-A binders, and it is common enough to occur by chance roughly every few kilobases. Nothing in the flanking preference reliably separates AP-4 from those. Use a CAGCTG hit as "class-A E-box", then argue from expression, from ChIP data and from promoter context. Do not treat the two JASPAR TFAP4::ETS models as TFAP4 motifs; they are composite dimer models. Do not treat the CATATG models as the canonical AP-4 site either.
families.caveats: CAGCTG is the generic class-A E-box: TCF3/TCF4/TCF12, MYOD, ASCL, NEUROD, TWIST and many others read it, and nothing in the flanking preference separates AP-4 from them. The site contains no CpG, so it is not depleted and occurs by chance every few kilobases. Family cohesion is only 0.77 because two of the six models are CATATG-type variants rather than CAGCTG, and two are JASPAR heterodimer profiles in which a TFAP4 half-site is fused to an ETS half-site; those composite models should not be used as AP-4 site definitions. Label agreement for these models is 0.1-0.2, meaning their nearest neighbours across databases usually carry a different factor name.

families.name: NR5A (SF-1 / LRH-1)
families.def: SF-1 response element (T)CAAGGTCA. NR5A1, NR5A2.
families.short: NR5A1 (steroidogenic factor 1, SF-1) and NR5A2 (liver receptor homolog 1, LRH-1) are the mammalian relatives of Drosophila FTZ-F1. Like the NR4A receptors they bind DNA as monomers rather than dimers, occupying one AGGTCA half-site plus a short 5' extension read by a separate protein surface called the A box, which gives the nine-base SF-1 response element TCAAGGTCA. NR5A1 drives adrenal and gonadal development and the steroidogenic enzyme genes; NR5A2 works in liver, pancreas, intestine and the early embryo. The two proteins have indistinguishable motifs but almost non-overlapping tissue distributions, so cell type, not sequence, tells them apart. The element differs from the NR4A site at a single base and is contained inside the NR6A1 direct repeat.
families.long:
## The factors

The subfamily has two human members: NR5A1 (SF-1, Ad4BP, STF-1, ELP) and NR5A2 (LRH-1, FTF, CPF, hB1F), both mammalian homologs of the Drosophila regulator FTZ-F1 (Lala et al. 1992). Their DNA-binding domain is the usual pair of C4 zinc modules plus a carboxy-terminal extension carrying the A box, or FTZ-F1 box, and a terminal helix required for a stable complex on DNA (Little et al. 2006). The ligand-binding domain has a large hydrophobic pocket: crystal structures identify bound phosphatidylinositols, making these receptors phospholipid sensors rather than true orphans (Krylova et al. 2005), although LRH-1 adopts an active conformation with the pocket essentially empty (Sablin et al. 2003). The paralogues occupy largely non-overlapping tissues: NR5A1 in adrenal cortex, gonadal somatic cells, pituitary gonadotropes, spleen and ventromedial hypothalamus; NR5A2 in liver, pancreas, intestine and the preimplantation embryo. Six motifs are collected here, two each from JASPAR, HOCOMOCO and CIS-BP; HOCOMOCO files the NR5A1 model under the symbol STF1.

## The motif

The element is usually written (T)CAAGGTCA, the SF-1 response element or SFRE: one AGGTCA half-site with a short 5' extension, bound by a single receptor molecule. Domain swaps placed SF-1 and NGFI-B (NR4A1) in the same monomeric paradigm, zinc modules on the half-site and A box in the minor groove 5' of it; the SF-1 sequence requires an amino group in the minor groove and the SF-1 A box supplies an asparagine (Wilson et al. 1993). The consequence for sequence analysis is stark: the NR4A element is AAAGGTCA and the NR5A element is CAAGGTCA, a difference of one base. The collected models are tight: both HOCOMOCO models, STF1.H14CORE.0.PSM.A and NR5A2.H14CORE.0.PSM.A, are tCAAGGtCA and the CIS-BP NR5A1 model is CAAGGtCA, so the paralogues cannot be separated by sequence. Three entries need care. JASPAR Nr5A2 (MA0505.3) is written TGACCTTGA, the reverse complement of TCAAGGTCA and so the same element on the other strand. CIS-BP M05589_2.00 is TCAAGGTCATGACCTTGA, 21 bits, a head-to-head pair of SF-1 elements with no spacer; its best within-family similarity is only 0.71, so it is an outlier. And JASPAR NR5A1 (MA1540.3) is the 12-mer AGTTCAAGGTCA, which can be read either as the SF-1 element with an extended 5' flank or as a DR0 pair of AGTTCA and AGGTCA half-sites. That ambiguity is real rather than an artifact: the DR0 bound by NR6A1 is AAGTTCAAGGTCA, and its 3' nine bases are exactly the SF-1 element, so every NR6A1 site contains an SFRE match.

## Where it acts

SF-1 sites sit in promoters of the steroidogenic machinery, including STAR, CYP11A1, CYP17A1, CYP19A1 and HSD3B2, and of hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal genes such as INHA, MC2R and NR0B1/DAX1; SF-1 cooperates with SOX9 at the anti-Mullerian hormone promoter and is antagonized by DAX-1, which binds the protein rather than DNA (Ferraz-de-Souza et al. 2011). LRH-1 acts on bile acid and cholesterol genes such as CYP7A1, CYP8B1 and NR0B2/SHP and on pancreatic and intestinal programs. An eight- to nine-base element is expected tens of thousands of times in a mammalian genome, so almost every match lies in a cell expressing neither receptor. Cell type is the strongest filter here, and an unusually effective one: the two cistromes barely overlap because the tissues do not.

## Biology and disease

Sf1-null mice lack adrenal glands and gonads entirely, undergo male-to-female sex reversal and have an abnormal ventromedial hypothalamus (Luo et al. 1994). The first reported human NR5A1 mutation was a heterozygous DNA-binding-domain change causing 46,XY sex reversal with adrenal failure (Achermann et al. 1999); the spectrum now includes 46,XY differences of sex development without adrenal insufficiency, hypospadias, male infertility and primary ovarian insufficiency (Ferraz-de-Souza et al. 2011). SF-1 is overexpressed, and the gene amplified, in adrenocortical tumors, more frequently in children than in adults (Almeida et al. 2010). Mouse embryos lacking Nr5a2 die early with defects in cholesterol homeostasis (Pare et al. 2004), and common variants at NR5A2 on 1q32.1 are an established pancreatic cancer susceptibility signal (Petersen et al. 2010).

## Reading a hit

A monomeric half-site is much harder to call than a spaced dimer. A DR3, DR4 or DR5 element constrains two half-sites plus a defined spacer, 13-15 positions, and the arrangement is itself evidence; the SFRE constrains eight or nine positions, six of which are the AGGTCA half-site shared across the nuclear receptor superfamily, leaving two or three bases of family-level information and no spacer to check. One substitution turns an SFRE into an NR4A NBRE, and any NR6A1 DR0 contains an SFRE, so a hit may belong to a different family or be one half of a genuine dimeric site. Prediction improves substantially when dimer configuration can be modeled, which is not possible here (Sandelin and Wasserman 2005). The sequence evidence is strong: both HOCOMOCO models are grade A with ChIP-seq, HT-SELEX and methyl-HT-SELEX support, so TCAAGGTCA is well supported as directly bound, unlike the ChIP-only models common elsewhere in this atlas. What a hit cannot do is name the receptor. Use expression: outside adrenal, gonad, gonadotrope and hypothalamus an SF-1 call is implausible, as is an LRH-1 call outside liver, pancreas, intestine and early embryo. Note also that databases report this element on either strand, as TCAAGGTCA or TGACCTTGA.
families.caveats: The motif is well measured but weakly diagnostic. Both HOCOMOCO models carry grade-A in vitro support, so TCAAGGTCA really is bound directly, yet it constrains only eight or nine positions, six of them the AGGTCA half-site used across the nuclear receptor superfamily. One substitution converts it into the NR4A element AAAGGTCA, and every NR6A1 DR0 contains an exact SFRE, so family assignment from sequence alone is unreliable. NR5A1 and NR5A2 have identical motifs; only tissue distinguishes them, which in practice works well because their expression barely overlaps. Watch for presentation differences across databases: one JASPAR model is the reverse complement, one CIS-BP model is a head-to-head pair of elements, and HOCOMOCO files NR5A1 under the symbol STF1.

families.name: NR6A1 (GCNF)
families.def: DR0 direct repeat TCAAGGTCA. NR6A1.
families.short: NR6A1, better known as germ cell nuclear factor (GCNF), is the only mammalian member of nuclear receptor subfamily 6: one gene with no paralogue. It binds a DR0, two nuclear receptor half-sites in direct repeat with no intervening bases, and it does so as a homodimer without an RXR partner. That makes it the odd one out among the orphan receptors here, because a two-half-site element of 13 to 15 base pairs is far more specific than a monomeric half-site. Its best-characterized job is repressing the pluripotency gene Oct4 during differentiation, which it does by recruiting methyl-CpG-binding proteins and DNA methyltransferases. Mouse mutants show posterior truncation, the gene underlies a vertebral-number locus in pigs, and human variants cause an oculo-vertebral-renal syndrome.
families.long:
## The factors

NR6A1 was cloned as GCNF, germ cell nuclear factor, from developing germ cells and is also called RTR (Chen et al. 1994). It is the sole mammalian member of nuclear receptor subfamily 6, so unlike most families here it has no paralogue to be confused with; zebrafish carries two copies (Neelathi et al. 2025). The protein has the standard layout: a DNA-binding domain of two C4 zinc modules with a carboxy-terminal extension, then a ligand-binding domain with no established ligand. It behaves predominantly as a repressor, recruiting methyl-CpG-binding domain proteins and DNA methyltransferases at its best-studied target (Gu et al. 2011). Expression is developmentally restricted: germ cells during spermatogenesis and oogenesis, the early post-implantation embryo, embryonic stem cells and parts of the developing nervous system, with little in adult tissue. Six motifs are collected here from all four sources, all labeled NR6A1; the family is the most internally consistent of the orphan receptor groups.

## The motif

The element is a DR0: two nuclear receptor half-sites arranged as a direct repeat with zero intervening bases. In vitro translated GCNF binds autonomously to a direct repeat of AGGTCA; sequences beyond the core DNA-binding domain are needed for specific binding; antibody-shift experiments place two GCNF molecules on one repeat, so the complex is a homodimer; and no RXR interaction is detectable (Borgmeyer 1997). That homodimeric, two-half-site mode separates NR6A1 from NR4A and NR5A, which bind a single extended half-site as monomers (Wilson et al. 1993). The collected models agree closely. Four of the six, from HOCOMOCO, JASPAR, CIS-BP and the Vierstra archetypes, converge on AAGTTCAAGGTCA or the longer TCAAGTTCAAGGTCA at 15 to 20 bits. One detail is worth stating rather than smoothing over: the measured upstream half-site is the AGTTCA variant, not AGGTCA, so the data consensus AAGtTCAAGgTCA differs from the textbook description of a direct repeat of AGGTCA. The architecture is the same; the databases capture which variant of the upstream half-site is preferred. Two further points matter for scanning. The 3' nine bases, TCAAGGTCA, are exactly the NR5A/SF-1 response element, so every genuine NR6A1 site contains an exact SF-1 match. And one of the two ChIP-only HOCOMOCO models, NR6A1.H14CORE.1.P.C, is nothing more than tCAAGgtCA, a bare half-site indistinguishable from the NR5A motif; the other, NR6A1.H14CORE.0.P.C, is a degenerate aAggtCAAGgtCA.

## Where it acts

The best-characterized site is a DR0 in the proximal promoter of Oct4 (POU5F1). GCNF restricts Oct4 to the germline in the mouse embryo (Fuhrmann et al. 2001), is required to repress Oct4 and other pluripotency genes when embryonic stem cells differentiate in response to retinoic acid (Gu et al. 2005), and initiates promoter DNA methylation there by recruiting MBD proteins and DNMTs (Gu et al. 2011). Occupancy is developmentally gated and largely absent from adult tissue. The element's length changes the arithmetic: a specific 13-mer is expected only about 50 times per strand in a 3-Gb genome, against roughly 47,000 for a specific eight-mer, so a full DR0 match is genuinely rare and the limiting question becomes whether NR6A1 is expressed rather than whether the match is chance.

## Biology and disease

Mouse embryos lacking Gcnf develop an ectopic tail bud and a posterior truncation (Chung et al. 2001) and fail to silence Oct4 outside the germline (Fuhrmann et al. 2001). In domestic pigs, NR6A1 underlies a major quantitative trait locus for the number of vertebrae (Mikawa et al. 2007). In humans, rare heterozygous NR6A1 variants in six families cause an autosomal dominant oculo-vertebral-renal syndrome of colobomatous microphthalmia, missing vertebrae and congenital kidney abnormalities; knockdown of either or both zebrafish paralogues gives abnormal eye, kidney and somite development, rescued by wild-type but not variant mRNA (Neelathi et al. 2025). The vertebral phenotype in both pig and human is consistent with a role in somitogenesis.

## Reading a hit

This family is the encouraging case among the orphan receptors, but only if the hit came from the right model. A match to the full 13- to 15-base DR0 is informative: the pattern is long enough that chance occurrences are rare, and the strongest model, NR6A1.H14CORE.2.SM.B, has HT-SELEX and methyl-HT-SELEX support at grade B, so it is in vitro evidence of direct binding rather than mere occupancy. A match to the two ChIP-only grade-C models is different: one is a bare nuclear receptor half-site and should be reported as such, not as NR6A1. Always check which model produced the hit. Two confusions follow from the sequence. Because the DR0 contains an exact SF-1 element, NR5A scanners will score NR6A1 sites, and a hit that looks like NR5A inside a longer direct repeat may be NR6A1. And a DR0 is not unique to NR6A1: the NR2F/COUP-TF group and RXR heterodimers also bind direct repeats with short spacers, so the arrangement narrows the candidates without naming one. Prediction of nuclear receptor elements is much better when the dimer configuration can be modeled, which here it can (Sandelin and Wasserman 2005). The Vierstra entry AC0133:NR6A is a footprint archetype named after the factor group whose motifs clustered together (Vierstra et al. 2020). Expression is the practical gate: outside germ cells, early embryos and stem cell models, an NR6A1 call needs independent support.
families.caveats: The full DR0 is long enough to be reasonably specific, and the strongest model has in vitro support, so a good 13- to 15-base match is more trustworthy than most nuclear receptor hits. The risk is model choice: two of the six collected models are ChIP-only at grade C, and one of those is just the nine-base half-site tCAAGgtCA, which is identical to the NR5A/SF-1 element. Hits from that model say nothing specific about NR6A1. Conversely, every real NR6A1 site contains an exact SF-1 match, so the two families cross-annotate each other. A direct repeat is not unique to NR6A1 either, since NR2F/COUP-TF and RXR heterodimers also read closely spaced repeats. Note finally that the measured upstream half-site is AGTTCA rather than the textbook AGGTCA, and that expression is confined largely to germ cells and early embryos.

families.name: THAP-type zinc finger
families.def: THAP1, THAP12 and other THAP-type zinc fingers. THAP11 is covered by the ZNF143 entry, whose site it shares.
families.short: THAP-type zinc fingers are C2CH modules whose closest known relative is the site-specific DNA-binding domain of the Drosophila P-element transposase, making this a family of domesticated transposase DNA-binding domains. The atlas files six motifs for two proteins, THAP1 and THAP12. THAP1 recognizes a bipartite site - a GCCATCTT-like half and a GGGCA half separated by a short variable spacer - which the trimmed JASPAR model reduces to GCAGGGCA. Crystallography of the fly THAP domain explains the bipartite pattern: a beta-sheet inserts into the major groove while a basic C-terminal loop reads the adjacent minor groove. THAP1 is the DYT6 dystonia gene. THAP11 is deliberately not filed here; it shares the ZNF143 SBS element and is covered by the ZNF143 entry.
families.long:
## The factors

The THAP domain was defined in 2003 as a roughly 90-residue module whose sequence resembles the site-specific DNA-binding domain of the Drosophila melanogaster P-element transposase, carrying a putative metal-coordinating signature of the form CX(2-4)CX(35-53)CX(2)H. A survey across model animals catalogued about 100 distinct THAP proteins, including the human proapoptotic factors THAP1 and DAP4/THAP0, the transcriptional repressor THAP7, and the Caenorhabditis elegans chromatin protein HIM-17 and cell-cycle regulators LIN-36 and LIN-15B. The domain is therefore one of the clearest cases of molecular domestication: a transposase recognition module retained by the host after the mobile element that carried it was lost, a route to new transcription factors seen repeatedly in animal genomes.

The atlas family itself is small. Six motifs cover two named proteins, THAP1 and THAP12, plus two unnamed Vierstra archetypes labelled only THAP. THAP1 is a ubiquitously expressed nuclear protein encoded at 8p11.21. THAP12 is the protein also known as DAP4 or PRKRIR. THAP11, better known as Ronin, is excluded by design: it binds the same element as ZNF143 and is described in the ZNF143 entry, so a THAP11-labelled motif should be read there, not here.

## The motif

In vitro binding-site selection with the THAP domain of human THAP1 yielded an 11-nucleotide consensus, and single-nucleotide substitutions within it abolished binding; chelating zinc with 1,10-o-phenanthroline also abolished binding, confirming the domain is a zinc-dependent member of the zinc-finger superfamily. The structural basis came from a crystal structure of the fly P-element transposase THAP domain bound to a natural ten-base-pair site. Unlike a C2H2 finger, the THAP domain docks a conserved beta-sheet into the major groove and a basic C-terminal loop into the adjacent minor groove, and sequence analysis of natural and selected sites suggested a shared bipartite TXXGGGX(A/T) consensus for the fly domain and for human THAP1 and THAP9.

The atlas models match that description at two different trimmings. The long models keep both halves: HOCOMOCO THAP1.H14CORE.0.P.B reads gccGCCATcTTbgntvcGGGCa over 22 positions, and CIS-BP M08020 gives CGCCATcTTggnTrhGGGCAg at 21.5 bits. The short models keep only the downstream half: JASPAR MA0597.3 and Vierstra archetype AC0141 are both GCAGGGCA, and a second Vierstra archetype AC0478 is the still shorter tnhGGGCA. Family cohesion is moderate at 0.58, driven entirely by this difference in trimming rather than by disagreement about the site. The remaining motif, CIS-BP M02538 for THAP12, carries 3.8 bits of information and is not usable. Label agreement across databases is very low, between 0 and 0.1, which is what an eight-base-pair GC-containing model will always produce: its nearest neighbours in other databases belong to other families.

## Where it acts

THAP1 occupancy is concentrated at promoters and CpG islands rather than distal enhancers. The best-characterised direct target is TOR1A, the DYT1 dystonia gene, whose promoter THAP1 binds and represses. Because the site includes a GGGCA half that overlaps GC-box-like sequence, matches cluster in the same promoter-proximal, CpG-rich compartment occupied by SP/KLF factors, and mouse work indicates THAP1 acts on that same regulatory space. Note the separation of labour within the wider domain family: the hyperconserved promoter element bound by Ronin/THAP11 together with HCF-1 at genes controlling embryonic stem cell growth is the ZNF143 SBS, not the THAP1 site.

## Biology and disease

Heterozygous THAP1 mutations cause DYT6, an autosomal dominant primary torsion dystonia with prominent cranio-cervical and laryngeal involvement. Many of the pathogenic substitutions fall inside the THAP domain and reduce DNA binding directly, which is why this family is one of the few where a motif model maps onto a molecular disease mechanism. THAP1 represses TOR1A, linking the DYT6 and DYT1 loci in one pathway. DYT6-mutant THAP1 behaves as a cell-type-dependent regulator of the SP1 family, and mouse Thap1 loss produces transcriptional deficits that converge on pathways shared with other dystonic syndromes. Elsewhere in the domain family, Ronin/THAP11 is essential for mouse embryogenesis and for embryonic stem cell pluripotency.

## Reading a hit

Use the long model if you can. GCAGGGCA is eight base pairs of partly GC-rich sequence and will match tens of thousands of times in a 3.1 Gb genome, most of them meaningless; the 22-base-pair bipartite HOCOMOCO model is far more specific because it requires both halves and the spacer. A hit identifies a THAP-domain site, not a protein: the bipartite consensus is shared by THAP1, THAP9 and the fly P-element transposase itself. Condition on a promoter or CpG island context and on THAP1 expression. If your hit instead resembles the ACTACA-containing SBS element, you are looking at THAP11 and should read the ZNF143 entry. Ignore the THAP12 model entirely.
families.caveats: The family carries only six motifs for two proteins, and one of them, CIS-BP M02538 for THAP12, has 3.8 bits and no usable information. The HOCOMOCO THAP1 model is ChIP-only (evidence code P, grade B), so within the atlas there is no in vitro support for it, although independent binding-site selection and a crystal structure of the homologous fly domain support the same bipartite site in the literature. Short GCAGGGCA-style matches are common and largely uninformative on their own. Nothing in the motif separates THAP1 from THAP9 or from the ancestral P-element transposase domain. THAP11 is intentionally absent from this family: its site is the ZNF143 SBS and belongs to that entry.

families.name: ZNF263
families.def: Long GA-rich/GGAGGA repeat motif. ZNF263.
families.short: ZNF263 is a nine-finger C2H2 zinc-finger protein that also carries a KRAB repression domain and a SCAN oligomerization domain. Its binding site is unusually long: genome-wide mapping in K562 cells recovered a roughly 24-nucleotide GA-rich element built from tandem GGAGGA-like units, which differs in several positions from what the zinc-finger recognition code predicted for this protein. Unlike most KRAB zinc-finger proteins it does not sit mainly on transposable elements, and many of its thousands of target sites lie inside transcribed regions rather than at promoters; knockdown both raises and lowers target genes. The GA-rich character makes this motif easy to confuse with purine-rich sites read by ETS and SP1-like factors on the opposite strand.
families.long:
## The factors

ZNF263 is the only member of this family. It combines three modules found in the KRAB zinc-finger protein superfamily: nine tandem C2H2 fingers, a KRAB domain that recruits TRIM28/KAP1 and associated silencing machinery, and a SCAN domain, a protein-protein interaction module that mediates selective homo- and hetero-oligomerization among SCAN-domain zinc fingers. Because of the KRAB domain ZNF263 was expected to be a repressor, but knockdown experiments changed expression of target genes in both directions, so it is better described as a context-dependent regulator. It is broadly expressed. Its nine fingers are the reason the recognized element is so long, and it is one of the relatively few C2H2 proteins for which the whole array appears to be used for base reading rather than for anchoring or for protein contacts.

## The motif

The element is long and internally repetitive. ChIP-seq in K562 cells recovered more than 5000 binding sites and a 24-nucleotide consensus assembled from tandem GA-rich units, written here as GGAGGAGGAGGAGGA and equivalently as CTCCTCCTCCTCCTCC on the complementary strand. Notably, the observed motif differed at several positions from the site predicted for ZNF263 by the zinc-finger recognition code, which was one of the early demonstrations that prediction from finger sequence is not a substitute for measurement. The matrices in this family capture different amounts of the repeat: the ChIP-derived HOCOMOCO matrix spans 20 base pairs (GGGAGGAGGGVGAGGAGGAG), while JASPAR MA0528.3, the CIS-BP matrix and the two Vierstra archetypes cover only seven or eight (GGGAGGA, CTCCTCCC, GTGCTCCC). The short versions are not different motifs; they are windows on the same repeat, and because the repeat is periodic a short matrix will match at many registers within one site, so one genomic element can generate several overlapping matches. There is no half-site and no spacing rule, and no paralogue to confuse ZNF263 with.

What distinguishes this from other purine-rich motifs is length and periodicity. ETS-class motifs are built on a GGA(A/T) core needing the flanking ACCGGAAGT-type context and are much shorter; SPI1/PU.1 reads a purine-rich AGAGGAAGTG with a defined 3' half; ZNF281/ZNF148 and ZBTB7 read C-rich CCCCACCC-type words rather than GA-rich ones; VEZF1 reads CT/GC-rich vascular promoter sites. A genuine ZNF263 element is a long, uninterrupted GGAGGA-type repeat rather than a single core with flanks, so a short GGGAGGA match inside a mixed-sequence promoter more likely belongs to one of the shorter families, while a repeat of 20 base pairs or more is the ZNF263 signature.

## Where it acts

ZNF263 sites are not concentrated at transcription start sites in the way most promoter motifs are. A striking fraction of the ChIP-seq peaks fall within the transcribed region of the target gene, including introns and exons, which is atypical both for a KRAB zinc-finger protein and for a promoter factor. Many targets are expressed at high levels despite the KRAB domain. Reported biology places sites at genes of heparan sulfate and heparin biosynthesis, where ZNF263 regulates the pathway, and at SIX3 in glioblastoma, where an EGFR-ZNF263 axis silences the gene. GA-rich and CT-rich simple repeats of this kind are also enriched in short tandem repeat-based silencer elements, so the sequence class has regulatory functions that are not necessarily ZNF263-dependent. The motif is not a CpG-island signature and has no named composite element.

## Biology and disease

The functional literature is modest, and it is better to say so than to pad it. ZNF263 has been reported as a transcriptional regulator of heparin and heparan sulfate biosynthesis, as the effector of an EGFR-driven axis that epigenetically silences SIX3 in glioblastoma, and as a regulator of adipocyte gene expression in cattle. There is no described knockout phenotype in a mammalian model, no Mendelian disease, and no recurrent somatic driver mutation. Broader surveys of human KRAB zinc-finger proteins place ZNF263 among the members whose targets are not dominated by transposable elements, which distinguishes it from the large group of primate-specific KRAB proteins that control endogenous retroviruses. The motif is considerably better characterized than the biology.

## Reading a hit

Ask how long the match is. A 20-base-pair or longer GA repeat is good evidence for the ZNF263 element; a seven- or eight-base match is weak, because the short matrices in this family are windows on a repeat and because several other families read short purine-rich cores. Expect multiple overlapping hits within one real element and do not count them as independent observations. The primary matrices are ChIP-derived; the single HOCOMOCO matrix carrying in vitro support is the short eight-base version, so the long consensus rests on genome-wide occupancy rather than on purified binding, and indirect binding cannot be excluded for individual peaks. A hit inside a gene body is not a reason to discount it here, since that is where much of the reported occupancy lies. Simple repeats are also prone to mapping and assembly artefacts, so confirm that a hit lies in uniquely mappable sequence before building on it.
families.caveats: Two problems. First, length: the long GA repeat is distinctive, but the short seven- and eight-base matrices in this family match promiscuously and overlap ETS, PU.1 and other purine-rich families on one strand and CT-rich families on the other. Only a match of about 20 base pairs or more should be attributed to ZNF263. Second, evidence: the long consensus comes from ChIP-seq in a single cell line, and the ChIP-derived matrix differs from the sequence predicted by the zinc-finger recognition code, so individual peaks could reflect indirect binding or the intrinsic properties of simple repeats. Because the element is periodic, one real site produces several overlapping matches, which inflates naive hit counts.

families.name: ZNF281 / ZNF148 (ZBP-89)
families.def: GC-rich CCCCACCCC sites. ZNF281, ZNF148, ZNF219.
aka: TFClass: more than 3 adjacent zinc finger factors
families.short: ZNF148 (better known as ZBP-89) and ZNF281 (ZBP-99) are broadly expressed four-fingered C2H2 proteins that bind GC- and GA-rich promoter elements, most often written GGGGGAGGGG or, on the opposite strand, CCCCTCCCCC; longer models add a CCCCACCCC module. Both were cloned as factors that occupy GC-rich elements already known to bind Sp1, and that competition is the point: the same element is a legitimate site for several families. ZNF219 is grouped with them on domain similarity but has no matrix here. The two proteins are not distinguishable from each other by sequence, and only weakly distinguishable from MAZ, PATZ1 and VEZF1. Human ZNF148 truncating variants cause a recognized developmental syndrome.
families.long:
## The factors

ZNF148 was cloned as ZBP-89, an 89-kDa zinc-finger protein, by screening a rat expression library with a multimer of the GC-rich element GGGGCGGGGTGGGGGG that confers epidermal growth factor responsiveness on the human gastrin promoter - an element already known to bind Sp1. The protein was 89% identical to a previously described 49-kDa human factor, ht-beta, and acts as a repressor of that promoter (Merchant et al. 1996). ZNF281 was then cloned as ZBP-99, a second member of the same family, also a GC-box binder and also a repressor, this time characterized on the ornithine decarboxylase promoter; its four Kruppel-type zinc fingers share 91% similarity and 79% identity with those of ZBP-89 (Law et al. 1999). Four fingers predicts a footprint of roughly 12 bp, not the long arrays of CTCF-like proteins. ZNF219 is placed here by domain similarity and assembles with Sox9 to drive chondrocyte differentiation (Takigawa et al. 2010), but contributes no matrix, so everything said about the motif comes from ZNF148 and ZNF281. Mouse orthologs are Zfp148 and Zfp281. Both are broadly expressed and both act predominantly as repressors, frequently at elements that Sp1 also occupies.

## The motif

The two JASPAR profiles are one sequence in opposite orientations: ZNF281 (MA1630.3) is GGGGGAGGGG, ZNF148 (MA1653.2) is CCCCTCCCCC, as is CIS-BP M08321_2.00. The HOCOMOCO models are longer and add a module: ZN281.H14CORE.0.P.B is GGGTGGGGGAGGGG and ZN148.H14CORE.0.P.B is the same 14-mer, placing a GGGTGGGG (CCCCACCCC on the other strand) immediately 5' of the GGGGGAGGGG core. At 20.3 and 19.9 bits these are the most information-rich matrices in the family, and they are also where the CCCCACCCC form of the consensus comes from. One matrix here carries in vitro evidence - ZN281.H14CORE.1.SM.B, from HT-SELEX and methyl-HT-SELEX - and it is instructive: it is a 21-position near-uniform G-run, GGGGGGGGGGGGAGGGDGGGG. In other words, the in vitro data for ZNF281 support "long G-rich tract" rather than a crisp, positionally defined site. Family cohesion is high at 0.90, but that is cohesion among six matrices from two gene labels and does not make the family distinctive. Label agreement runs from 0.2 to 0.4, and for the JASPAR ZNF148 profile the best-scoring neighbor anywhere in the four databases (0.95) lies outside this family, beating its best within-family match (0.88). Concretely: GGGAGGG, the MAZ site, is contained inside GGGGGAGGGG, so MAZ and ZNF281 differ only in the length of the run and its flanks; VEZF1's informative model is the same shape; and the ChIP-derived WT1 models fall in the same cluster. The only sequence-level discriminator available in this neighborhood is against the SP1/KLF GC-box - an A in the middle of the run where the GC-box has a C, GGGAGGG versus GGGCGG (Song et al. 2001) - and even that fails when the match spans a G-rich tract long enough to accommodate both.

## Where it acts

These are promoter-proximal factors, at GC-rich elements in CpG-island promoters - gastrin, ornithine decarboxylase and similar targets - usually shared with Sp1. ZBP-89 is butyrate-inducible and binds GC-rich DNA elements in gastrointestinal epithelium (Essien et al. 2013). Zfp281 in mouse embryonic stem cells occupies the Nanog locus, where its function depends on recruited complexes rather than on the motif: it brings in the NuRD complex to mediate Nanog autorepression (Fidalgo et al. 2012) and recruits Polycomb repressive complex 2 to restrict extraembryonic endoderm potential (Huang et al. 2021). The pattern recurs: the motif places the protein, the partner determines the output.

## Biology and disease

Zfp281 is required for embryonic stem cell pluripotency, acting by both direct activation and direct repression of targets (Wang et al. 2008), and behaves predominantly as a transcriptional repressor in that setting (Fidalgo et al. 2011); it also inhibits somatic cell reprogramming (Fidalgo et al. 2012). ZNF281 is induced by genotoxic stress and contributes to the DNA damage response by controlling expression of the homologous-recombination and non-homologous-end-joining factors XRCC2 and XRCC4 (Pieraccioli et al. 2016), and is reported as an oncogene in colorectal and other carcinomas, in association with epithelial-mesenchymal transition. On the ZNF148 side, conditional deletion of Zfp148 in mice alters tryptophan hydroxylase I expression and impairs mucosal defense against Salmonella typhimurium (Essien et al. 2013). The clearest human link is Mendelian: de novo truncating variants in ZNF148 cause a syndrome of corpus callosum defects, developmental delay, short stature and dysmorphic features (Stevens et al. 2016), since named GDACCF and delineated in a cohort of 22 patients (Szakszon et al. 2024).

## Reading a hit

A match identifies a G-rich promoter element and nothing narrower. ZNF148 and ZNF281 share one motif, so the hit cannot choose between them; ZNF219 has no matrix at all, so a claim about ZNF219 from sequence is pure inference from domain similarity. Three of the six matrices are ChIP-only at grade B, and the one in vitro model is effectively a poly-G tract, which means the family's own evidence does not define a sharp site. Long G-runs are common in GC-rich promoters and in G-quadruplex-forming sequence, so expect chance matches. Most importantly, the neighbors: MAZ and PATZ1 sites are nested inside this consensus, VEZF1's model has the same shape, the ChIP-derived WT1 models cluster here, and the SP1/KLF GC-box is one base away. Which protein occupies a site is answered by ChIP, knockdown or expression - not by a score.
families.caveats: ZNF148 and ZNF281 share a single motif, and ZNF219 - also assigned to this family - contributes no matrix, so nothing can be said about it from sequence. Three of the six matrices rest on ChIP-seq alone at grade B, and the one HT-SELEX/methyl-SELEX model is essentially a 21-base poly-G tract, so the in vitro evidence does not define a sharp site. For the JASPAR ZNF148 profile the best-matching matrix anywhere in the four databases lies outside this family. MAZ and PATZ1 sites are nested inside this consensus, VEZF1's model has the same shape, and the SP1 GC-box is one base away. Treat a hit as G-rich promoter sequence.

families.name: Transposase-derived / TE-binding zinc fingers
families.def: Zinc fingers whose motif is a transposable-element sequence (ZNF91/93 on SVA/L1, ZNF445, ZFP57 on imprinted TGCCGC, ZNF808, ZNF780A).
families.short: A small entry for KRAB zinc fingers whose recognized sequence is itself a piece of a transposable element. The best-documented cases are ZNF91, which binds the VNTR region of SVA elements, and ZNF93, which binds a segment of the 5' untranslated region of primate L1 retrotransposons. Both changed as those element families began to spread, and the L1PA3 subfamily escaped ZNF93 by deleting its binding site. The atlas holds six matrices for three proteins, ZNF93, ZNF808 and ZNF780A; ZNF91 itself has no motif in any of the four source databases. Because these motifs are copies of element sequence rather than compact regulatory words, a match usually tells you which repeat you are inside rather than which protein is bound there.
families.long:
## The factors

All three labelled proteins are KRAB zinc-finger proteins (KZFPs): an N-terminal KRAB domain that recruits TRIM28/KAP1 and through it SETDB1 and H3K9me3 heterochromatin, plus a tandem array of C2H2 fingers. ZNF93 (19p12, formerly ZNF505) is primate-restricted and represses L1 elements roughly 12 to 20 million years old (Forey et al. 2025). ZNF808 (19q13.41) is primate-specific and silences a set of primate-specific transposable elements during pancreas development (De Franco et al. 2023). ZNF780A has almost no functional literature; it appears here because its ChIP-derived motif clusters with the others, and the only concrete report about it is as the partner of a RUNX1::ZNF780A fusion in one case of T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukaemia (Panagopoulos et al. 2023). ZNF91, the fourth gene named in this family's definition, has no motif in JASPAR, HOCOMOCO, CIS-BP or the Vierstra archetypes, so it cannot be scanned for at all; it is covered here because its biology defines the category. ZFP57 and the bulk of the KZFP family have their own entries.

## The motif

There is no family consensus: three proteins, three unrelated sequences, cohesion 0.60. ZNF93 is given as GGCAGCGGCAGCGG in JASPAR (MA1721.2) and as GCAGCAGSGNCTGCTGCTDCC in CIS-BP, a tandem GCAGC/CTGCT repeat rather than a compact site, which is what a long finger array tiling a repeated element looks like. ZNF780A is CWGACBGCCTGCC in CIS-BP and in the matching Vierstra archetype AC0167, but GGCAGGCAGTTAGGGAAG in HOCOMOCO. ZNF808 is GGTCTVTAAAGDGCCTGBT. Median consensus length is 16 bp and median information content 15 bits. More important, the primary literature does not describe these proteins with short consensus words at all: ZNF91 is mapped to the VNTR region of SVA elements (Haring et al. 2021) and ZNF93 to a segment of the L1 5' untranslated region whose deletion in the L1PA3 subfamily released those elements from repression (Jacobs et al. 2014). The matrices here are partial models of long element segments, so scanning for them behaves much like scanning for the element.

## Where it acts

Copies of the target element, usually in heterochromatin. SVA is one of three still-mobile human element families, with roughly 2,800 insertions in the reference genome and about half of those human-specific (Haring et al. 2021); recognizable L1PA 5' untranslated regions number in the thousands. Occupancy is concentrated in early embryonic and pluripotent contexts, where TRIM28 and SETDB1 deposit H3K9me3. Many KZFP-bound element copies remain in closed chromatin in differentiated cells, which is why sites of this kind are systematically missed by accessibility-based assays (Razavi et al. 2026). Where repression is relieved, the same elements can act as cis-regulatory modules for neighbouring genes, the route by which element sequence becomes host regulatory DNA (Imbeault et al. 2017; Davis et al. 2026).

## Biology and disease

Deleting ZNF91 in human embryonic stem cells activates SVA transcription, shifts evolutionarily young SVAs toward activating chromatin marks, mildly upregulates nearby genes, and triggers coordinated upregulation of KZFP genes across their clusters. Deleting ZNF611, another strong SVA binder, does not activate SVAs, so binding and functional repression are not the same thing (Haring et al. 2021). Biallelic loss of ZNF808 causes pancreatic agenesis: the primate-specific elements it normally silences gain regulatory activity during pancreas specification and liver-identity genes are induced instead (De Franco et al. 2023). ZNF93 has been co-opted in cancer, where it limits the mutagenic enzyme APOBEC3B; ZNF93 depletion impairs DNA synthesis, activates replication and damage checkpoints, and provokes proinflammatory phenotypes (Forey et al. 2025). The general pattern, of an arms race followed by domestication, is reviewed by Bruno et al. 2019 and Davis et al. 2026, and the correlation between retroelement load and zinc-finger gene number across vertebrates is quantified by Thomas and Schneider 2011.

## Reading a hit

Check the repeat annotation before interpreting anything. A ZNF93 match inside an L1PA 5' untranslated region mainly tells you the approximate age of that L1 copy; whether ZNF93 is bound there in your cell type is a separate question these matrices cannot answer. Occurrence counts scale with element copy number, so genome-wide enrichment of one of these motifs is usually a statement about repeat content rather than about regulation. The evidence base is thin: the family contributes one HOCOMOCO model, ChIP-only (evidence code P) and graded C, and no member has an HT-SELEX or methyl-SELEX model in HOCOMOCO. ZNF91's absence from all four databases is a hard limitation. And because ZNF93's matrix is essentially a GCAGC repeat, it will also score well on unrelated GCAGC- and CTGCT-rich sequence, including trinucleotide-repeat tracts.
families.caveats: These motifs are transposable-element sequence, so scanning for them is close to scanning for the element: check repeat annotation first, and expect occurrence counts to track element copy number rather than regulatory activity. The family contributes a single HOCOMOCO model, ChIP-only and graded C, and no member has in vitro support there. ZNF91, the best-characterized member of this category, has no matrix in any source database and cannot be scanned. The literature describes the ZNF91 and ZNF93 sites as long element segments, not short consensus words, so these matrices are approximations. Binding also does not imply repression: ZNF611 binds SVAs without silencing them.
